options: 只要我能触摸耶稣的衣裳，我就必得痊愈
只要我大声呼求耶稣，我就必得痊愈
只要我把钱给耶稣，我就必得痊愈
只要我能看见耶稣，我就必得痊愈
questions.explanation: 她心里想：“我只摸他的衣裳，就必痊愈。”

questions.question: 在这段经文中，耶稣展示了哪些方面的能力？
options: 能行走在水面上和变水为酒
能平静风浪和喂饱五千人
能使死人复活、医治疾病和赶出污鬼
能建造圣殿和召集门徒
questions.explanation: 耶稣使管会堂的女儿复活，医治了血漏的女人和两个瞎子，并赶出了一个哑巴身上的鬼。

questions.question: 这段经文对我们今天寻求神的帮助有何启发？
options: 只有有信心的人才能得到神的帮助
我们应该只寻求身体上的医治
神的怜悯和能力超越我们的想象，祂乐意回应信心的祈求
神只帮助那些地位高或有影响力的人
questions.explanation: 无论是管会堂的，还是患血漏的妇人，或是瞎子，他们的信心和恳求都得到耶稣的怜悯与医治，表明神的恩典和能力是向所有寻求祂的人敞开的。

zh.reflection: 你生命中有什么“不可能”的困境，需要凭信心交托给主耶稣，求祂施行大能？
reflectionOptions: 内心深处的恐惧或忧虑
zh.prayer: 主耶稣，感谢祢是大有能力又满有怜悯的神。我的生命中也有需要祢触摸和医治的地方。求祢加添我的信心，让我能勇敢地来到祢面前，把一切的软弱、困境和不可能都交托给祢。愿祢的大能再次彰显在我的生命中。奉主耶稣的名祷告，阿们。
zh.action: 今天，用一句话向耶稣说出你最需要祂医治或帮助的困境。

zh.focus: 耶稣看到百姓的困苦，动了慈心，并指示门徒为收割庄稼祷告。

questions.question: 耶稣在走遍各城各乡时，主要做了哪三件事？
options: 教训人、医治病人、赶鬼
教训人、传福音、医治各样的病症
行神迹、分食物、呼召门徒
洁净圣殿、斥责法利赛人、设立圣餐
questions.explanation: 经文明确指出耶稣在各会堂里教训人，宣讲天国的福音，又医治百姓各样的病症。

questions.question: 耶稣看见许多的人，祂的反应是什么？
options: 感到厌烦
心里忧愁
就怜悯他们
感到愤怒
questions.explanation: 耶稣看见许多人，如同羊没有牧人一般，就对他们动了慈心，怜悯他们。

questions.question: 耶稣说“要收的庄稼多，做工的人少”，这“庄稼”指的是什么？
options: 田里的农作物
等候被医治的病人
需要被拯救的人群
愿意奉献的富人
questions.explanation: “庄稼”在这里比喻那些在困苦流离中，等待福音和牧养的人群。

questions.question: 根据经文，我们面对世上许多需要帮助的人时，最应该做的是什么？
options: 立刻投入大量金钱
批评他们的处境
向庄稼的主求，打发工人出去收庄稼
等待别人去帮助他们
questions.explanation: 耶稣指示门徒，面对巨大的需要，首先要做的就是向庄稼的主祷告，求祂打发更多的工人出去。

zh.reflection: 今天，在你的周围，你看到哪些“如同羊没有牧人”的人群？
zh.prayer: 满有怜悯的主耶稣，我感谢祢看到我的软弱和需要，并为我动了慈心。求祢也打开我的眼睛，让我看见周围那些如同羊没有牧人的人群。求祢感动我为他们祷告，并求庄稼的主差派更多工人出去，也预备我成为祢手中的工人。奉主耶稣的名祷告，阿们。
zh.action: 为身边一位你所知道的、目前正感到迷茫或困苦的人祷告。

zh.focus: 耶稣赐给门徒能力和使命，让他们去传扬天国，并以爱心服事他人。

questions.question: 耶稣召聚门徒后，首先赐给他们什么？
options: 财富和名声
制伏污鬼和医治疾病的权柄
去罗马传道的命令
建立大教会的策略
questions.explanation: 耶稣召聚十二个门徒，赐给他们权柄，能赶逐污鬼，并医治各样的疾病和各样的软弱。

questions.question: 耶稣差遣门徒出去时，特别吩咐他们不要带什么？
options: 金、银、铜钱
额外的衣服
杖和鞋
以上所有都不带
questions.explanation: 耶稣吩咐门徒，出门的时候，不要带金、银、铜钱，也不要带口袋，不要带两件褂子，不要带鞋，也不要带拐杖。

questions.question: 耶稣差遣门徒传福音时，主要让他们传讲什么信息？
options: 关于律法的复杂教导
天国近了
如何变得富有
政治改革的必要性
questions.explanation: 耶稣差遣门徒去传讲的信息是：“天国近了”。

questions.question: 耶稣差遣门徒，并赐给他们能力，这对今天的我们有什么启发？
options: 我们应该只关注自己的属灵成长
我们应该等待特别的异象才去服事
我们也被赋予了传扬福音和服事他人的使命
基督徒不需要与他人分享信仰
questions.explanation: 门徒被差遣去传扬天国和服事他人，今天的基督徒也领受了这份使命，用神赐予的能力去爱和帮助身边的人。

zh.reflection: 今天，你会如何回应耶稣的差遣，在你的生活圈子里传扬天国并服事他人？
reflectionOptions: 关心并帮助一位有需要的人
为社区的属灵复兴祷告
zh.prayer: 亲爱的主耶稣，感谢祢赐给我宝贵的使命和能力。求祢帮助我勇敢地回应祢的差遣，用我的言语和行动传扬祢天国的好消息，并以爱心服事身边的人。愿我的生命能荣耀祢。奉主耶稣的名祷告，阿们。
zh.action: 今天特意为一位你认识但还不认识耶稣的人祷告，求神开启他/她的心。

zh.theme: 耶稣的门徒：挑战与应许
zh.focus: 作为耶稣的门徒，我们会面对挑战，但神应许会与我们同在，赐下当说的话，并看顾我们。

questions.question: 耶稣差遣门徒出去时，用什么动物来比喻他们的处境？
options: 绵羊
鸽子
蛇
狼
questions.explanation: 耶稣说祂差遣门徒“如同羊进入狼群”，预示他们将面临危险和敌意。

questions.question: 耶稣提醒门徒，当他们被交付官府时，不需要担心什么？
options: 如何为自己辩护
食物和住宿
人身安全
家人的安危
questions.explanation: 耶稣告诉他们不需要担心说什么，因为圣灵会在那时赐给他们当说的话。

questions.question: 耶稣在这段经文中主要想要消除门徒的哪种恐惧？
options: 传福音的恐惧
被人拒绝的恐惧
遭遇逼迫甚至死亡的恐惧
缺乏生活必需品的恐惧
questions.explanation: 耶稣多次提到门徒会面临逼迫、仇恨，甚至被杀害，但祂劝他们不要害怕那些只能伤害身体却不能伤害灵魂的。

questions.question: 耶稣在这段经文中赐给门徒什么安慰和应许？
options: 他们将永远不会遇到困难
他们会得到世人的尊敬和喜爱
神知道并看顾他们，甚至连他们的头发都数过了
他们将拥有超自然的能力来战胜所有敌人
questions.explanation: 耶稣应许门徒，天父看顾麻雀，也必看顾他们，甚至他们的头发都被数过，所以他们无需惧怕。

zh.reflection: 今天，在你的信仰旅程中，你最需要放下的惧怕是什么？
zh.prayer: 亲爱的天父，感谢祢差派我成为主耶稣的门徒。求祢帮助我勇敢面对挑战，放下一切的惧怕。我知道祢看顾我，连我的头发都数过了。愿我时刻信靠祢的同在和供应。奉主耶稣的名祷告，阿们。
zh.action: 今天花一分钟思想“不要惧怕”这句话，并把一个你最担忧的事情交给神。

zh.theme: 为福音受苦的代价与奖赏
zh.focus: 跟随基督可能带来家庭冲突，但忠心事奉祂的人必得着丰盛的奖赏。

questions.question: 耶稣说祂来不是要叫地上太平，而是带来什么？
options: 和睦与团结
刀剑
富足与昌盛
智慧与知识
questions.explanation: 耶稣明确地说祂来不是叫地上太平，乃是叫地上动刀兵。

questions.question: 耶稣说“爱父母过于爱我的，不配作我的门徒”这句话的重点是什么？
options: 门徒必须放弃爱自己的家人
门徒对耶稣的爱必须超越一切人际关系
门徒只能爱耶稣，不能爱父母
门徒的家人会阻碍他们与神的关系
questions.explanation: 这句话强调的是，对耶稣的忠诚和爱必须是生命中至高无上的，超越任何其他人际关系，包括最亲密的家人。

questions.question: 耶稣用“背起他的十字架”来比喻什么？
options: 承担家庭的重担
接受神的呼召去传福音
愿意为跟随基督而忍受苦难和牺牲
努力做好事工
questions.explanation: 背起自己的十字架意味着愿意为跟随基督而舍弃自己的生命，忍受艰难甚至死亡，这是一种完全的委身和牺牲。

questions.question: 经文结尾提到，凡因门徒的身份接待他们，或给他们一杯凉水的，会有怎样的结果？
options: 会得到金钱上的回报
会被世人称赞
必得着赏赐
会立刻变得健康
questions.explanation: 耶稣应许，凡因门徒的身份接待他们或服事他们的，必得着赏赐，这赏赐是出于对基督的爱与顺服。

zh.reflection: 今天的经文挑战我们思考，在你跟随基督的生命中，哪些是你可能需要放下或重新排序的爱和忠诚？
zh.prayer: 主耶稣，感谢祢为我舍弃一切。求祢帮助我，使我爱祢胜过一切，愿意为祢的福音付上代价。求祢加添我力量，背起自己的十字架跟随祢。奉主耶稣的名祷告，阿们。
zh.action: 今天，思考一个你愿意为基督而牺牲的小事物，并把它带到祷告中。

zh.focus: 即使在疑惑中，我们也能找到耶稣的肯定，并借此重新认识祂的身份和使命。

questions.question: 当施洗约翰听见耶稣所行的事时，他派门徒去问耶稣什么？
options: 祢是不是那位要来的弥赛亚？
祢为什么不像我们一样禁食？
祢的国什么时候降临？
祢能行更大的神迹吗？
questions.explanation: 施洗约翰的门徒问耶稣：“祢是那位要来的，还是我们等候别人呢？”这表明了约翰对耶稣身份的疑问。

questions.question: 耶稣怎样回应施洗约翰的疑问？
options: 直接宣告自己是弥赛亚
引用旧约先知书的预言，指出自己所行的神迹
责备约翰为什么会怀疑
告诉约翰他不需要知道答案
questions.explanation: 耶稣没有直接回答，而是让门徒回去告诉约翰，瞎子看见、瘸子行走、长大麻风的洁净、聋子听见、死人复活、穷人听见福音，这些都应验了旧约先知对弥赛亚的预言。

questions.question: 耶稣称赞施洗约翰是什么样的人？
options: 一位伟大的哲学家
一位比众先知都大的先知
一位国王的谋士
一位杰出的教师
questions.explanation: 耶稣说：“凡妇人所生的，没有一个兴起来大过施洗约翰的；然而天国里最小的，也比他大。”并称他为比先知大得多的。

questions.question: 从耶稣对约翰疑问的回答中，我们学到关于耶稣身份的什么？
options: 耶稣是一位专注于政治变革的领袖
耶稣的身份需要通过他所行的神迹和所传的福音来认识
耶稣只关心那些身体健康的人
耶稣的使命是建立一个军事强国
questions.explanation: 耶稣通过列举他所行的神迹和所传的福音，来证明自己就是旧约预言中的弥赛亚，他的身份不是用言语直接宣告，而是通过行动显明。

zh.reflection: 你是否曾因人生中的困境或不明白而对神的作为产生疑问？今天，你愿意如何回应耶稣的肯定？
reflectionOptions: 重新相信神的恩典和能力
寻求更多认识耶稣的身份和使命
放下自己的疑问，交托给神
zh.prayer: 主耶稣，当我面对困惑或怀疑时，求祢帮助我定睛在祢所行的奇妙作为上。感谢祢借着祢的言语和行动，向我显明祢是那要来的弥赛亚，是我的救主。愿我的心因认识祢而得着平静和盼望。奉主耶稣的名祷告，阿们。
zh.action: 今天花一点时间，回想耶稣在你生命中曾行过的奇妙作为，并为此感谢祂。

zh.focus: 我们是否像那些不满的孩子，对神的呼召和救恩视而不见？

questions.question: 耶稣用什么比喻来形容他那个世代的人？
options: 在街市上玩耍的孩子
在田间劳作的农夫
建造房屋的工匠
在海上捕鱼的渔夫
questions.explanation: 耶稣将他那个世代的人比作在街市上玩耍的孩子，抱怨同伴不按他们的意愿吹笛或哀哭。

questions.type: 观察人们对施洗约翰的反应
questions.question: 人们如何评价施洗约翰？
options: 他有鬼附着
他是神的使者
他是一位伟大的先知
他是弥赛亚
questions.explanation: 经文指出，施洗约翰禁食不吃不喝，人们却说他有鬼附着。

questions.type: 观察人们对耶稣的反应
questions.question: 人们如何评价人子（耶稣）？
options: 他是禁欲的苦行者
他是一位严厉的教师
他是贪食好酒的人，是税吏和罪人的朋友
他是一位政治领袖
questions.explanation: 人们看见人子又吃又喝，就说他是贪食好酒的人，是税吏和罪人的朋友。

questions.question: 耶稣这段话最想指出什么？
options: 施洗约翰和耶稣的教导方式截然不同
人们对神的呼召常常带着预设和偏见
智慧在世人眼中是愚拙的
悔改和相信福音是艰难的
questions.explanation: 耶稣用这个比喻指出，无论施洗约翰以禁欲方式，还是他自己以亲民方式传讲信息，人们都因自己的预设和偏见而不愿接受。

zh.reflection: 你是否也曾像经文中的人一样，因着自己的喜好或偏见，而忽略了神的恩典和真理？
reflectionOptions: 重新审视对信仰的看法
放下自己的期待，寻求神的心意
zh.prayer: 亲爱的主耶稣，求祢赦免我，有时我像那不满的孩子，对祢的呼召和真理视而不见。求祢打开我的心眼，使我能以谦卑的心领受祢的智慧和恩典。帮助我放下自己的偏见和喜好，真心寻求祢的旨意。奉主耶稣的名祷告，阿们。
zh.action: 今天，思考一个你曾因偏见而拒绝的人或事，并尝试以新的眼光去看待它。

zh.theme: 到我这里来，就必得享安息
zh.focus: 耶稣邀请所有劳苦担重担的人到祂那里去，在祂里面找到真正的安息。

questions.question: 耶稣在本段经文的开头向谁献上感谢？
options: 世上的君王
聪明通达人
天父
门徒们
questions.explanation: 耶稣在本段经文一开始就向天父献上感谢，因为祂将真理向聪明通达人隐藏，却向婴孩显明。

questions.question: 耶稣说祂从天父那里领受了什么权柄？
options: 审判全地的权柄
掌管万有的权柄
认识天父的权柄
赦免罪恶的权柄
questions.explanation: 耶稣指出“一切所有的，都是我父交付我的；除了父，没有人知道子；除了子和子所愿意指示的，没有人知道父。” 这表明祂拥有认识天父并指示人的独特权柄。

questions.question: 耶稣邀请哪一类人到祂这里来？
options: 所有富足有权势的人
所有劳苦担重担的人
所有自以为义的人
所有健康强壮的人
questions.explanation: 耶稣的邀请是向“凡劳苦担重担的人”发出的，承诺他们必得安息。

questions.question: 耶稣说祂的轭是怎样的？
options: 沉重难负
轻省容易
复杂难懂
充满挑战
questions.explanation: 耶稣说：“我的轭是容易的，我的担子是轻省的。” 祂的轭与世上的重担形成对比。

zh.reflection: 你现在生活中，有哪些劳苦或重担需要带到耶稣面前寻求安息？
zh.prayer: 亲爱的主耶稣，感谢祢邀请我到祢这里来，因为祢的轭是容易的，祢的担子是轻省的。求祢帮助我放下生命中的重担，学会祢的样式，在祢里面找到真正的安息。奉主耶稣的名祷告，阿们。
zh.action: 今天花点时间，安静地向耶稣倾诉你心里的一个重担，并求祂赐你安息。

zh.focus: 耶稣是安息日的主，祂的怜悯和医治超越了律法的字面规定。

questions.question: 法利赛人为何指责耶稣的门徒？
options: 他们在安息日工作
他们在安息日不祷告
他们在安息日掐麦穗吃
他们在安息日医病
questions.explanation: 法利赛人指责门徒在安息日掐麦穗吃，认为这是违背了安息日的规定。

questions.question: 耶稣用什么来回应法利赛人对门徒的指责？
options: 引用律法书中的其他例子
直接驳斥他们是伪善的
命令门徒停止掐麦穗
指出他们不明白神的爱
questions.explanation: 耶稣引用了大卫和他的随从在会幕里吃陈设饼，以及祭司在安息日于殿里犯了安息日却算为无罪的例子。

questions.question: 耶稣说祂来是要做什么，而不是要定人的罪？
options: 我喜爱怜恤，不喜爱祭祀
我喜爱知识，不喜爱愚昧
我喜爱公义，不喜爱罪恶
我喜爱律法，不喜爱传统
questions.explanation: 耶稣引用了何西阿书，指出神所喜悦的是怜恤，而不是仅仅遵守献祭的规条。

questions.question: 这章经文最主要教导我们什么？
options: 安息日不再重要，可以随意度过
神的律法是僵硬的，没有例外
怜悯和人的需要超越了律法的字面遵守
只有祭司和先知才能在安息日工作
questions.explanation: 耶稣通过行动和教导表明，神的心意是怜悯和帮助人，这些比机械地遵守规条更重要。

zh.reflection: 你生命中是否有某个方面，你倾向于只看重规条而忽略了爱和怜悯？
zh.prayer: 主耶稣，感谢祢是安息日的主，是充满怜悯的主。求祢帮助我，不只看到律法的字面规定，更要看到祢爱和怜悯的心意。愿我的生命能更多地活出祢的怜恤。奉主耶稣的名祷告，阿们。
zh.action: 今天特意找一个机会，对身边的人表达一份温柔的怜悯，即使这可能让你稍微“不方便”。

zh.focus: 耶稣的权柄来自神，拒绝承认祂就是抵挡圣灵的工作，后果严重。

questions.question: 当那个被鬼附、又瞎又哑的人被治好后，众人有什么反应？
options: 他们感到害怕，立刻逃跑了
他们质疑耶稣的能力，要求更多神迹
他们感到惊奇，并开始猜想耶稣是不是大卫的子孙
他们立刻相信耶稣是弥赛亚，并向他下拜
questions.explanation: 众人对耶稣所行的神迹感到惊奇，并开始思考他是否就是所期待的弥赛亚——大卫的子孙。

questions.question: 法利赛人如何解释耶稣赶鬼的能力？
options: 他们说耶稣是依靠神的灵赶鬼
他们指控耶稣是靠着鬼王别西卜赶鬼
他们认为耶稣使用了某种巫术
他们认为那个人根本没有被鬼附
questions.explanation: 法利赛人将耶稣赶鬼的能力归咎于鬼王别西卜，试图否认耶稣的神性。

questions.question: 耶稣如何驳斥法利赛人的指控？
options: 祂施行了另一个更大的神迹证明自己
祂指责法利赛人内心邪恶，不配知道真理
祂指出他们的指控逻辑不通，因为一个王国或家庭内斗是无法站立的
祂直接否认自己认识别西卜
questions.explanation: 耶稣用一个简单的逻辑驳斥了法利赛人的指控：一个内部分裂的王国或家庭是无法站立的，邪灵不会自相残杀。

questions.question: 耶稣提到“亵渎圣灵”的罪，最主要想强调什么？
options: 所有罪都可以被赦免，除了说脏话
故意将圣灵的工作归咎于撒但，是拒绝认识神赦罪恩典的罪
只要说错一句话，就永远不能得救
圣灵只在特定的时刻工作，不容许人质疑
questions.explanation: 耶稣强调，明知圣灵的工作却故意将其归咎于撒但，是拒绝悔改和认识神赦罪恩典的罪，因此无法得到赦免。
questions.evidence: 马太福音 12:30–32（虽然经文范围是22-30节，但31-32节是紧密相关的解释，此处作为理解经文的延伸点。）

zh.reflection: 你是否曾因为偏见或不愿承认神的真实工作，而错失了亲近神的机会？
reflectionOptions: 承认自己的骄傲和不信
更谦卑地寻求圣灵的引导
为过去拒绝真理而悔改
zh.prayer: 主耶稣，求祢赦免我有时因着自己的偏见、不信或无知，而未能完全认识和接受祢的工作。帮助我有一颗谦卑受教的心，敏锐地察觉圣灵的引导，不将祢的荣耀归给撒但。愿我常在祢的光中，与祢同行。奉主耶稣的名祷告，阿们。
zh.action: 今天花一点时间安静思想，有哪些时候你可能没有完全承认或接受圣灵的工作，并向神悔改。

zh.focus: 我们的言语不仅反映内心，更显明我们的生命方向和与神的关系。

questions.question: 耶稣说哪一种罪不能得赦免？
options: 亵渎圣灵
谋杀
偷窃
说谎
questions.explanation: 耶稣明确指出，亵渎圣灵的罪不能得赦免。

questions.question: 耶稣用什么来比喻人与他所说的话之间的关系？
options: 好树结好果子，坏树结坏果子
盐能调味，光能照亮
迷失的羊需要牧人寻找
建造房屋的根基
questions.explanation: 耶稣用“好树结好果子，坏树结坏果子”来比喻人的言语是内心真实的流露。

questions.question: 根据这段经文，耶稣对我们的言语有怎样的教导？
options: 言语不重要，内心最重要
只要不骂人就好，说什么无所谓
我们的言语是内心光景的反映，并要为之负责
言语只是表达方式，没有实际力量
questions.explanation: 耶稣教导我们的言语是从心里发出来的，并且我们将来要为所说的每一句话负责。

questions.question: 今天这段经文如何提醒你在日常生活中谨慎言语？
options: 提醒我少说话，免得说错
提醒我多说积极正面的话
提醒我言语是心灵的窗户，要省察内心
提醒我只要口头上认罪就可以了
questions.explanation: 言语是内心的流露，当我们省察内心、求神洁净时，我们的言语自然会蒙神喜悦。

zh.reflection: 你觉得自己的言语最能反映你内心哪一方面的真实光景？
zh.prayer: 亲爱的主，感谢祢提醒我言语的力量。求祢洁净我的心，使我口中所出的都是蒙祢喜悦、造就人的话语。帮助我常常省察自己，让我的言语成为祢美好的见证。奉主耶稣的名祷告，阿们。
zh.action: 今天试着少说一句抱怨的话，多说一句感恩的话。

zh.focus: 耶稣教导我们，真正的属灵关系超越血缘，在于遵行天父的旨意。

questions.question: 文士和法利赛人向耶稣求什么？
options: 一个神迹
解释律法
税款问题
医治病人
questions.explanation: 文士和法利赛人要求耶稣显一个神迹给他们看。

questions.question: 耶稣给他们什么神迹作为回应？
options: 将水变为酒
使死人复活
约拿的神迹
平静风和海
questions.explanation: 耶稣提到约拿在鱼腹中三天三夜，并以此预表人子也要在地里三天三夜。

questions.question: 耶稣说谁是祂的弟兄、姐妹和母亲？
options: 那些与祂有血缘关系的人
那些住在拿撒勒的人
那些遵行祂天父旨意的人
那些在圣殿里事奉的人
questions.explanation: 耶稣明确指出，凡遵行天父旨意的人，就是祂的弟兄、姐妹和母亲。

questions.question: 这段经文如何挑战我们对“家人”的传统观念？
options: 血缘关系不再重要
属灵关系优先于血缘关系
只有信徒才能成为真正的家人
我们应该完全放弃家庭责任
questions.explanation: 耶稣在这里强调，属灵的连结——即遵行神旨意——比世俗的血缘关系更为重要，它定义了真正的“家人”。

zh.reflection: 你生命中哪些关系真正反映了遵行天父旨意的“家人”关系？你又如何能加强这些关系？
reflectionOptions: 主动关心非血缘的属灵家人
zh.prayer: 亲爱的天父，感谢祢让我因信耶稣而成为祢家中的一份子。求祢帮助我，每天更深地认识祢的旨意，并靠着圣灵的能力去遵行。愿我的生命能荣耀祢，并与属灵的家人一同成长。奉主耶稣的名祷告，阿们。
zh.action: 今天特意为一位与你没有血缘关系，但因信仰而亲近的弟兄姐妹祷告，并送上一个鼓励的信息。

zh.theme: 撒种的比喻：神国度的奥秘
zh.focus: 神的话语如种子，其生长和结果取决于我们心田的预备。

questions.question: 耶稣是在哪里对众人讲撒种的比喻？
options: 在会堂里
在山上
在屋子里
在海边
questions.explanation: 经文清楚记载耶稣从屋子里出来，坐在海边教导众人。

questions.question: 撒种的比喻中，种子撒在了哪些地方？
options: 石头地、肥沃地、沙地、泥地
路旁、石头地、荆棘里、好土里
田埂、水沟、山坡、谷地
贫瘠地、盐碱地、湿地、耕地
questions.explanation: 撒种的比喻提到种子落在路旁、石头地、荆棘里和好土里。

questions.question: 这个比喻的重点是想说明什么？
options: 撒种的人必须非常勤劳
土地的种类决定了种子是否能生长
神的话语是宝贵的，但人们接受的方式不同
只要撒下种子，就一定会有好收成
questions.explanation: 比喻的重点在于不同听道者对神话语的回应，导致了不同的结果。

questions.question: “有耳可听的，就应当听！”这句话对我们有什么提醒？
options: 要多去听音乐会
要留意周围的噪音
要认真思考并回应神的话语
要听从所有人的建议
questions.explanation: 这句话呼吁听众要警醒，用心领受并回应主所说的话。

zh.reflection: 你觉得你的心田现在更像比喻中的哪一种土？你愿意如何回应神的话语？
reflectionOptions: 承认自己心硬，求主软化
清除生命中的“荆棘”，更专注神
更深地扎根在神的话语中
zh.prayer: 主耶稣，感谢祢用撒种的比喻教导我。求祢帮助我预备好我的心田，除去一切拦阻我领受祢话语的障碍。愿我的心成为好土，使祢的话语在我生命中生根、发芽、结出丰盛的果实。奉主耶稣的名祷告，阿们。
zh.action: 今天花一点时间，安静地思考一节你最近读到的经文，并求圣灵帮助你理解和应用。

zh.focus: 主耶稣用比喻教导，是为了向寻求的人显明真理，而向那些硬心不信的人隐藏真理。

questions.question: 门徒问耶稣的第一个问题是什么？
options: 祢为何用比喻讲道？
天国的奥秘是什么？
谁能明白祢的比喻？
我们能明白祢的比喻吗？
questions.explanation: 门徒直接问耶稣，祢为何用比喻对他们讲道。

questions.question: 耶稣解释说，祂用比喻的目的是什么？
options: 让所有人都能轻易明白天国的道理
鼓励人们用智慧去探索深奥的真理
把天国的奥秘显给门徒，却向外人隐藏
测试听众的理解能力和信心程度
questions.explanation: 耶稣说，因为天国的奥秘只叫门徒知道，不叫外人知道。这是神主权的作为。

questions.question: 耶稣引用了哪位先知的话来解释祂的教导方式？
options: 以赛亚
耶利米
以西结
弥迦
questions.explanation: 耶稣引用了先知以赛亚的话来解释，他们看却看不见，听却听不见，也不明白。

questions.question: 耶稣说门徒蒙福是因为什么？
options: 他们比旧约的先知和义人更有智慧
他们能看见和听见许多先知和义人渴望看见和听见的
他们将成为天国奥秘的唯一传承者
他们能够完全明白耶稣所有的比喻
questions.explanation: 耶稣称门徒是有福的，因为他们能看见和听见许多先知和义人渴望看见和听见，却未能看见和听见的事。

zh.reflection: 今天，你感受到天国的奥秘向你显明了吗？你是否正以谦卑受教的心来寻求神的话语？
reflectionOptions: 我渴望更深地明白神的道
我需要更多时间安静读经祷告
我有时对神的话语感到困惑
zh.prayer: 主耶稣，感谢祢向我显明天国的奥秘。求祢开启我的心眼，使我能看见、能听见、能明白祢的话语。帮助我常常存着谦卑受教的心，不硬着颈项，而是渴慕祢的真理。奉主耶稣的名祷告，阿们。
zh.action: 今天，花五分钟时间，安静地重读今天的经文，求圣灵光照你，使你更深地明白其中的真理。

zh.focus: 神容忍世上的恶，直到收割的时候，祂将亲自审判并分别为圣。

questions.question: 这个比喻是从谁开始撒种讲起的？
options: 一个农夫
一个好撒种的
一个人
一个主人
questions.explanation: 比喻开头说“天国好像人撒好种在田里”，强调是“人”开始撒种。

questions.question: 当主人撒了麦子之后，仇敌做了什么？
options: 把麦子拔起来
撒下稗子
放火烧田
偷走了麦子
questions.explanation: 当人睡着的时候，他的仇敌来，在麦子里撒了稗子就走了。

questions.question: 当仆人询问是否要去拔除稗子时，主人是怎样回答的？
options: 让他们一起长，等到收割的时候
立刻去拔掉，不要耽延
只拔除那些大的稗子
让仆人自己决定怎么做
questions.explanation: 主人吩咐仆人让麦子和稗子一同生长，直到收割的时候，才分别处理。

questions.question: 麦子与稗子的比喻给我们最重要的提醒是什么？
options: 我们应该立即分辨和审判身边的每一个人
神允许恶的存在有祂自己的时间表和最终目的
我们必须自己努力清除世上所有的罪恶
善恶的界限模糊不清，无法区分
questions.explanation: 这个比喻提醒我们，神对恶有祂的忍耐和最终的审判，我们应该信靠祂的时间和智慧。

zh.reflection: 你生命中是否有让你感到困惑或不公的“稗子”，你愿意如何将这些担忧交托给掌管一切的神？
reflectionOptions: 放下自己的判断，信靠神的公义
寻求智慧，在力所能及的范围行善
zh.prayer: 天父，感谢祢是公义和忍耐的主。求祢帮助我，在面对世上的不公和邪恶时，不凭自己的血气行事，而是信靠祢的智慧和最终的审判。愿我能像祢的麦子一样，结出荣美的果实。奉主耶稣的名祷告，阿们。
zh.action: 今天尝试对一个你平时看不惯或觉得不公的人，默默地为他/她祷告。

zh.focus: 神的国度虽然开始微小，却有惊人的成长能力，最终将充满大地。

questions.question: 耶稣将神的国比作什么？
options: 一颗宝石和一座城堡
一颗芥菜种和一点面酵
一座高山和一片大海
一棵大树和一群飞鸟
questions.explanation: 耶稣用芥菜种和面酵来比喻神的国度，强调它微小开始却有巨大影响。

questions.question: 芥菜种的比喻强调了神的国度哪一个特性？
options: 它只对少数人开放
它隐藏在地下不为人知
它从微小开始却成长为巨大
它需要人不断浇灌才能生存
questions.explanation: 芥菜种是最小的种子，却能长成大树，表明神的国度从微不足道开始，最终会大大扩展。

questions.question: 面酵的比喻主要说明了神的国度哪一个特性？
options: 它需要等待很长时间才能发酵
它只是表面上的改变
它能悄无声息地全面渗透和改变
它只影响少数的个体
questions.explanation: 面酵虽然少量，却能使整团面发起来，象征神的国度具有内在的、全面的渗透和改变力量。

questions.question: 这两个比喻共同向我们启示了关于神国度怎样的真理？
options: 神的国度只会吸引富有的人
神的国度是立即可见的巨大力量
神的国度从卑微开始，却有内在的生命力和影响力，最终会完全扩展
神的国度只存在于属灵的层面，不影响现实世界
questions.explanation: 芥菜种和面酵的比喻都强调神的国度虽然初期不显眼，但其生命力和渗透力会使其最终全面扩展和改变世界。

zh.reflection: 神的国度正在你生命中的哪个领域悄悄成长和改变你？
zh.prayer: 亲爱的主耶稣，感谢祢用芥菜种和面酵的比喻，让我明白祢的国度虽然开始微小，却有惊人的生命力和改变力。求祢让这国度也在我心中成长，渗透我生命的每一个层面，使我更多地活出祢的样式。奉主耶稣的名祷告，阿们。
zh.action: 今天特意为一件你觉得“微不足道”但与神国度有关的事情感恩，例如一个微小的善举或一个微弱的祷告。

zh.focus: 天国是如此宝贵，值得我们不惜一切代价去拥有。

questions.question: 在马太福音13:44–46中，耶稣用哪两个比喻来形容天国？
options: 撒网的比喻和稗子的比喻
芥菜种的比喻和面酵的比喻
藏宝的比喻和寻珠的比喻
盖房子的比喻和两个儿子的比喻
questions.explanation: 耶稣用‘藏在田里的宝贝’和‘重价的珠子’这两个比喻来形容天国，强调其无与伦比的价值。

questions.question: 藏宝和寻珠这两个比喻共同强调了天国的什么特质？
options: 天国是人人都能轻松得到的
天国是隐藏的，需要努力才能发现
天国是如此宝贵，值得人倾尽所有去获得
天国只赐给那些有财富的人
questions.explanation: 这两个比喻都表明，无论是偶然发现还是努力寻找，当人认识到天国的价值时，都会愿意付出一切去拥有它。

questions.question: 耶稣在自己的家乡传道时，当地人对他的反应是什么？
options: 他们热烈欢迎并相信他
他们感到惊讶，但拒绝相信他
他们要求耶稣行更多的神迹
他们完全不认识耶稣
questions.explanation: 耶稣的家乡人对他的智慧和能力感到惊奇，却因为他的出身而厌弃他，不肯相信。

questions.question: 耶稣在自己的家乡没有行许多神迹，原因是什么？
options: 因为他能力有限
因为他不希望在熟悉的人面前展示神迹
因为他们的不信限制了神迹的发生
因为神迹只在陌生的地方发生
questions.explanation: 经文清楚指出，耶稣在那里没有行许多神迹，是“因为他们不信”。不信成为接受神恩典的阻碍。

zh.reflection: 天国对你而言是怎样的价值？你是否愿意为它付出代价？
reflectionOptions: 愿意投入更多时间服事
愿意牺牲一些物质享受
zh.prayer: 亲爱的主耶稣，感谢祢用比喻启示天国的宝贵。求祢开启我的眼睛，让我更深地认识天国的价值，并赐我勇气和信心，愿意为跟随祢、拥有天国而付出一切代价。帮助我活出信心，不因世界的眼光而跌倒。奉主耶稣的名祷告，阿们。
zh.action: 今天，花几分钟思想一下，你生活中有什么是比天国更重要的？求神帮助你调整 priorities。

zh.focus: 即便在不公义和艰难的时刻，神依然掌权，我们可以选择信靠祂，并注目于祂的作为。

questions.question: 是谁下令逮捕并监禁施洗约翰？
options: 罗马总督彼拉多
犹太公会
希律安提帕
大祭司该亚法
questions.explanation: 经文清楚指出是分封的王希律安提帕下令逮捕并监禁施洗约翰。

questions.question: 希律王最终决定杀害约翰的原因是什么？
options: 约翰煽动百姓反抗希律的统治
希律的妻子希罗底强烈要求
希律的女儿在宴会上跳舞，使希律起誓
约翰咒诅希律的家庭，激怒了希律
questions.explanation: 希律的女儿在宴会上跳舞取悦了希律，希律便起誓要给她任何她所求的。在希罗底的教唆下，她要求约翰的头。

questions.question: 施洗约翰的门徒在约翰死后采取了什么行动？
options: 他们聚集起来反抗希律王
他们向罗马政府投诉希律的不公
他们来领取了约翰的尸体，把他安葬了，然后去告诉耶稣
他们因恐惧而四散，从此不再传道
questions.explanation: 约翰的门徒来把他的尸体领去埋葬了，然后去把这事告诉了耶稣。

questions.question: 在面对不公或痛苦时，我们可以从约翰的门徒身上学到什么？
options: 立刻寻求报复，以牙还牙
保持沉默，假装什么都没发生
将困境带到耶稣面前，寻求祂的安慰和指引
相信自己的能力，独自解决所有问题
questions.explanation: 约翰的门徒在失去老师后，选择将这件痛苦的事告诉耶稣，这教导我们在困境中要寻求耶稣。

zh.reflection: 你目前生活中，是否有让你感到不公或心痛的处境，需要带到耶稣面前？
zh.prayer: 主耶稣，感谢祢掌管一切，即便在看似不公和黑暗的时刻，祢依然是我们的盼望。求祢帮助我将一切的困境和心痛都带到祢面前，信靠祢的安慰和指引。奉主耶稣的名祷告，阿们。
zh.action: 今天花一点时间，在祷告中将你最近感到困扰或不公的一件事告诉耶稣。

zh.focus: 即使在人看似不可能的困境中，主耶稣也以祂的怜悯和神迹大能供应一切所需。

questions.question: 当耶稣听到施洗约翰被杀的消息后，祂做了什么？
options: 立刻谴责希律王
独自退到旷野去
召集门徒商议对策
公开向群众传讲天国信息
questions.explanation: 耶稣听到施洗约翰被杀后，选择独自坐船退到旷野去，寻求安静。

questions.question: 当耶稣退到旷野时，群众是怎样回应的？
options: 他们跟着门徒回家了
他们不顾一切地从各城步行跟随祂
他们派代表去请祂回来
他们抱怨耶稣抛弃了他们
questions.explanation: 群众得知耶稣去了哪里，就从各城步行出来，追随祂。

questions.question: 面对饥饿的五千人（不包括妇女和小孩），耶稣的门徒建议如何解决，而耶稣又是如何做的？
options: 门徒建议解散群众，耶稣却叫他们给群众吃
门徒建议向附近村庄求助，耶稣却叫他们向群众收取奉献
门徒建议自己去买食物，耶稣却叫他们祷告等候
门徒建议只喂饱小孩和老人，耶稣却叫他们喂饱所有人
questions.explanation: 门徒建议耶稣打发群众散开，让他们自己去买食物，而耶稣却对门徒说“不用他们去，你们给他们吃吧！”

questions.question: 从五饼二鱼喂饱五千人的神迹中，我们最能学到什么？
options: 只要资源足够，就能解决一切问题
我们应该依赖自己而不是神来解决困难
即使微小的奉献，在神手中也能成就大事
神只帮助那些生活优越的人
questions.explanation: 这个神迹表明即使只有微不足道的五饼二鱼，在耶稣手中也能奇妙地喂饱众人，并有剩余。

zh.reflection: 今天你生命中有什么“五饼二鱼”——看似微小却可以献给主，让祂使用成就大事的呢？
zh.prayer: 主耶稣，感谢祢充满怜悯，也满有大能。当我看自己和环境的不足时，求祢帮助我转向祢，相信祢能在看似不可能中成就奇迹。愿我愿意献上我所有的，让祢使用。奉主耶稣的名祷告，阿们。
zh.action: 今天特意为一件你觉得“太小了，没用”的事情祷告，求主使用它。

zh.focus: 在人生的风浪中，即使感到恐惧或困惑，依然可以信靠耶稣，因为祂掌管一切，并赐下真正的平安。

questions.question: 耶稣在什么情况下催门徒上船渡海？
options: 祂刚行完五饼二鱼的神迹
祂在山上整夜祷告之后
祂正在与法利赛人争辩
祂准备去耶路撒冷
questions.explanation: 耶稣行完五饼二鱼的神迹，就催门徒上船渡海。

questions.question: 门徒看见耶稣在海面上行走时，起初的反应是什么？
options: 立刻认出祂是主
感到非常喜乐
以为是鬼怪，就害怕起来
争论祂是谁
questions.explanation: 门徒看见耶稣在海面上行走，以为是鬼怪，就害怕起来，喊叫起来。

questions.question: 当彼得开始下沉时，耶稣如何回应？
options: 立刻责备彼得的信心不足
伸出手拉住他，并问他为何疑惑
让彼得自己挣扎学习功课
叫其他门徒去帮助彼得
questions.explanation: 彼得因小信而下沉时，耶稣立刻伸手拉住他，并说：“你这小信的人哪，为什么疑惑呢？”

questions.question: 这段经文最主要教导我们什么？
options: 只要有信心，我们就永远不会遇到困难
耶稣的能力只在平静的水面上彰显
即使在最深的恐惧和困难中，耶稣也与我们同在，并能拯救我们
我们可以靠自己的力量胜过一切挑战
questions.explanation: 这段经文表明，即使在狂风大浪和门徒恐惧小信的时刻，耶稣依然同在，并有能力拯救他们脱离危险。

zh.reflection: 今天你生命中的“风浪”是什么？你最需要求主耶稣在哪方面对你说：“是我，不要怕”？
zh.prayer: 亲爱的主耶稣，感谢祢掌管风浪，也掌管我的生命。当我的心被恐惧或担忧笼罩时，求祢让我听见祢的声音：“是我，不要怕！” 帮助我单单仰望祢，经历祢所赐的平安。奉主耶稣的名祷告，阿们。
zh.action: 闭上眼睛，安静地对自己说三遍：“主耶稣，我相信祢与我同在，不要怕。”

zh.theme: 内在的洁净与真正的敬拜
zh.focus: 真正的洁净和敬拜不是外在仪式的遵守，而是内心的纯正和对神诫命的顺服。

questions.question: 法利赛人和文士质问耶稣的门徒什么？
options: 为什么他们不缴纳圣殿税？
为什么他们不按照传统洗手吃饭？
为什么他们不遵守安息日？
为什么他们与罪人一同吃饭？
questions.explanation: 法利赛人和文士问耶稣的门徒为什么不遵守长辈的遗传，饭前不洗手。

questions.question: 耶稣如何反驳法利赛人和文士，指出他们的问题？
options: 祂说他们不明白律法书的真正含义。
祂说他们用自己的遗传废弃了神的诫命。
祂说他们不认识摩西的律法。
祂说他们的心远离神，只是用嘴唇尊敬祂。
questions.explanation: 耶稣指责法利赛人，说他们“用人的遗传废弃了神的诫命”，并以“供献”为例。

questions.type: 理解耶稣对洁净的定义
questions.question: 耶稣说，真正污秽人的东西是什么？
options: 未经洗净的食物
从人口里出来的恶言恶念
与外邦人接触
不献上足够的祭物
questions.explanation: 耶稣教导说，从人口里出来的恶念、杀害、奸淫、苟合、偷盗、妄证、毁谤，这些才污秽人。

questions.question: 这段经文对我们今天追求敬虔生活有什么提醒？
options: 外在的宗教礼仪比内心更重要。
只要行为端正，内心思想不重要。
我们应该更注重内心的纯洁和对神话语的顺服。
我们可以随意解读圣经，只要心是好的。
questions.explanation: 耶稣强调了内心的重要性，指出真正的敬虔在于内心对神的顺服和清洁，而不是外在的仪式。

zh.reflection: 今天，我是否更看重外在的宗教形式，而忽略了内心对神的真实敬拜和顺服？
reflectionOptions: 省察我的动机是否纯正
求神洁净我的思想和言语
zh.prayer: 亲爱的天父，感谢祢教导我真正的洁净来自内心。求祢赦免我有时只看重外在的宗教行为，而忽略了内心的纯正。求祢帮助我，使我口中所说、心里所想的都蒙祢悦纳，让我能以心灵和诚实来敬拜祢。奉主耶稣的名祷告，阿们。
zh.action: 今天，在与人交谈前，花几秒钟祷告，求神洁净你的心和口，使你所说的话是造就人的。

zh.focus: 真正的信心是即使在考验中也能持续向主呼求，并相信祂的怜悯和能力。

questions.question: 这位迦南妇人向耶稣呼求，称呼祂为什么？
options: 神的儿子
大卫的子孙
以色列的君王
天上的主
questions.explanation: 妇人一开口就称耶稣为“主啊，大卫的子孙”，显示她对耶稣身份的认识。

questions.question: 耶稣第一次对妇人的呼求有什么反应？
options: 立刻治好了她的女儿
严厉地斥责了她
一言不发
告诉她要先悔改
questions.explanation: 经文记载耶稣“却一言不答”，这是对妇人信心的考验。

questions.question: 耶稣与迦南妇人的对话，主要教导我们什么？
options: 神只关心以色列人，不关心外邦人
只要足够坚持，就能强迫神做我们想做的事
即使在看似拒绝的情况下，仍要凭信心坚持向神呼求
谦卑的人不需要为自己争取什么
questions.explanation: 尽管耶稣一开始的回应和比喻似乎在拒绝，妇人仍然凭着谦卑和坚定的信心持续呼求，最终得到了医治。

questions.question: 从迦南妇人的榜样中，我们能学到关于祷告的什么功课？
options: 祷告时要先证明自己的配得
祷告不需恒切，一次就够了
即便感受不到立刻的回应，也要凭信心持续交托
只有那些完美无瑕的人才能蒙神应允
questions.explanation: 妇人在面对耶稣的沉默和看似拒绝的比喻时，仍不放弃，持续凭信心呼求，最终她的信心得到了耶稣的肯定和应允。

zh.reflection: 在你的生命中，有没有一个让你持续祷告但尚未看到答案的境况？
reflectionOptions: 为自己的健康状况祷告
zh.prayer: 主耶稣，感谢祢透过迦南妇人的故事教导我信心的宝贵。求祢帮助我在祷告中保持恒切和谦卑，即使面对挑战或看似沉默时，也坚信祢的慈爱和能力。愿我的信心能蒙祢悦纳。奉主耶稣的名祷告，阿们。
zh.action: 今天为你一个持续祷告的需要，再次献上一次充满信心的祷告。

zh.focus: 耶稣不仅能医治各样的疾病，祂也用祂的大能和怜悯来喂饱饥饿的人。

questions.question: 当耶稣来到加利利海边，人们带着哪些病人来找祂？
options: 瞎子、瘸子、哑巴、残疾的
生病的、被鬼附的、癫痫的
发烧的、麻风病人、中风的
老年人、小孩子、妇女
questions.explanation: 经文清楚列出人们带着瞎子、瘸子、哑巴、残疾的和许多别的病人到耶稣那里，耶稣就医治了他们。

questions.question: 当耶稣医治了众人后，群众有什么反应？
options: 感到惊讶，并离开了
感到害怕，不敢靠近
感到愤怒，不相信祂
稀奇，就荣耀以色列的神
questions.explanation: 群众看到哑巴说话，残疾的痊愈，瘸子行走，瞎子看见，就感到稀奇，并荣耀以色列的神。

questions.question: 耶稣为什么决定要喂饱这些群众？
options: 他们跟随了祂三天，没有吃的
他们请求耶稣给他们食物
耶稣想展示祂的神迹大能
耶稣希望他们不要离开
questions.explanation: 耶稣怜悯群众，因为他们已经跟随祂三天，没有吃的，祂不愿让他们饿着离开而中途困乏。

questions.question: 在喂饱四千人的神迹中，门徒们把仅有的食物交给耶稣后，耶稣做了什么？
options: 耶稣直接变出了更多食物
耶稣拿起食物祝谢，擘开，分给门徒，门徒再分给众人
耶稣吩咐门徒去买食物
耶稣让群众自己想办法
questions.explanation: 耶稣拿起门徒仅有的七个饼和几条小鱼，祝谢了，擘开，递给门徒，门徒再分给众人。

zh.reflection: 今天的经文提醒我们耶稣的怜悯与大能。在你生命中，你最需要耶稣在哪一个方面向你施怜悯并显大能？
zh.prayer: 慈爱的主耶稣，感谢祢的怜悯和大能。祢医治病人，喂饱饥饿的人，显明祢是顾念我们的神。求祢今天也在我的生命中施恩，无论是身体、心灵或生活的需要，都求祢以祢的大能来供应和扶持我。奉主耶稣的名祷告，阿们。
zh.action: 找一个安静的时刻，回想耶稣在经文中的作为，并把自己今天最深的需要告诉祂。

zh.focus: 耶稣拒绝行神迹来满足不信者的要求，因他们寻求的不是真理，而是试探。

questions.question: 法利赛人和撒都该人来到耶稣那里，要求祂行什么？
options: 一个神迹来医治病人
一个从天上来的神迹
一个关于末世的预言
一个使死人复活的神迹
questions.explanation: 他们要求耶稣行一个从天上来的神迹，以此来试探祂。

questions.question: 耶稣为什么责备法利赛人和撒都该人？
options: 他们穿着不符合律法
他们不认识摩西的律法
他们能分辨天气，却不能分辨时代的凭据
他们没有按时奉献
questions.explanation: 耶稣指出他们能够看天色辨认天气，却不能理解神在祂身上所做之事的凭据。

questions.question: 耶稣对这个邪恶淫乱的世代，除了什么，不给他们别的神迹？
options: 摩西的神迹
以利亚的神迹
约拿的神迹
以赛亚的神迹
questions.explanation: 耶稣说除了约拿的神迹，再没有别的神迹给他们了，这预示着祂的死亡和复活。

questions.question: 从这段经文中，我们可以学到关于寻求神迹的什么功课？
options: 神迹是信仰的基础，我们必须不断寻求
神迹是神回应祷告的唯一方式
神迹不是用来满足不信者的好奇心或试探
神迹只对那些完全没有信心的人显现
questions.explanation: 耶稣拒绝为满足法利赛人和撒都该人的试探而行神迹，表明神迹的目的是为了显明神的国和祂的权柄，而不是满足人的私欲或不信。

zh.reflection: 在你的生命中，你是否曾以不当的心态寻求神的凭据或印证？
reflectionOptions: 为了满足自己的好奇心
为了逃避面对现实的挑战
zh.prayer: 主耶稣，求祢帮助我有一颗清洁、寻求真理的心。当我面临挑战或疑惑时，愿我能谦卑地寻求祢的心意，而不是试探祢或要求不当的凭据。愿我能分辨祢的作为，并坚心信靠祢。奉主耶稣的名祷告，阿们。
zh.action: 今天，当心里有疑惑时，先安静祷告，求神赐下智慧和信心，而不是急于寻求外在的“神迹”来印证。

zh.focus: 耶稣提醒门徒要警惕法利赛人和撒都该人的教训，因为错误的教导会像酵母一样影响整体。

questions.question: 当门徒忘记带饼时，他们之间在议论什么？
options: 耶稣会如何变出饼来
他们该去哪里买饼
他们为什么没有带饼
耶稣的教导与饼的关系
questions.explanation: 门徒只想着忘记带饼这件事，因此互相议论。

questions.question: 耶稣提醒门徒“要防备法利赛人和撒都该人的酵”，这里的“酵”指的是什么？
options: 他们做的饼
他们的钱财
他们的错误教训
他们的权柄
questions.explanation: 耶稣明确指出“酵”是指法利赛人和撒都该人的教训，这些教训会潜移默化地影响人。

questions.question: 门徒最初误解了耶稣关于“酵”的教导，这表明了什么？
options: 他们完全不理解耶稣的比喻
他们对物质食物的担忧多于对属灵教导的理解
他们以为耶稣在批评他们的记忆力
他们认为耶稣对食物很挑剔
questions.explanation: 门徒的讨论集中在忘记带饼上，表明他们更关注物质的食物，而没有领会耶稣属灵的提醒。

questions.question: 这段经文对今天的我们有什么重要的提醒？
options: 我们应该避免与所有人分享食物
我们必须只吃无酵饼
我们需要警惕错误的教导，并专注于耶稣的真理
我们不应该担心日常的物质需求
questions.explanation: 耶稣的提醒是要我们警惕那些会污染我们信仰和思想的错误教导，并持守祂的真理。

zh.reflection: 今天，你觉得有什么“酵”可能正在悄悄影响你的思想或信仰？
zh.prayer: 亲爱的主耶稣，感谢祢提醒我要警醒，防备那些可能污染我思想和信仰的“酵”。求祢赐给我分辨的智慧，帮助我持守真理，不被世界的各种教训所迷惑。愿我的心单单跟随祢。奉主耶稣的名祷告，阿们。
zh.action: 今天，花一点时间省察自己最近接触到的信息，并求神帮助你分辨哪些是真理，哪些是“酵”。

zh.theme: 你是基督，永生神的儿子
zh.focus: 耶稣是基督，是永生神的儿子，这是神所启示的真理，也是教会建立的根基。

questions.question: 耶稣问门徒，人说他是谁？门徒提到了哪些答案？
options: 施洗约翰、以利亚、耶利米
摩西、大卫、所罗门
先知撒母耳、以赛亚
一个伟大的教师、一位医治者
questions.explanation: 耶稣问门徒时，他们回答说有人认为他是施洗约翰、以利亚，或是耶利米，或是先知中的一位。

questions.question: 彼得是怎样回答耶稣“你们说我是谁”这个问题？
options: 祢是我们的夫子，是伟大的教师
祢是弥赛亚，将要复兴以色列国
祢是基督，是永生神的儿子
祢是一位大有能力的先知
questions.explanation: 彼得清楚地宣告：“祢是基督，是永生神的儿子。”

questions.question: 耶稣称赞彼得的回答，并指出彼得的洞见不是从何而来？
options: 从他自己的智慧而来
从人的教导而来
从肉体和血气而来
从其他门徒那里听来的
questions.explanation: 耶稣明确指出，彼得的洞见不是出于血肉的指示，而是从天父那里领受的启示。

questions.question: 耶稣说他要把他的教会建造在这“磐石”上。这“磐石”指的是什么？
options: 彼得这个人
彼得的信心和忠心
彼得所认信的“祢是基督，永生神的儿子”这个真理
所有使徒的教导
questions.explanation: 耶稣所说的“磐石”是指彼得所宣告的真理——耶稣是基督，是永生神的儿子。教会是建立在这个核心真理之上。

zh.reflection: 你是否也像彼得一样，认识并承认耶稣是基督，是永生神的儿子？这个真理如何影响你今天的生活？
reflectionOptions: 提醒我每天信靠主耶稣
让我对永生和神的同在有更深的盼望
激励我更积极地向人传讲耶稣
zh.prayer: 主耶稣，感谢祢是基督，是永生神的儿子。感谢天父向我启示这个宝贵的真理。求祢帮助我将生命建造在这磐石上，坚定不移地信靠祢，并活出与这真理相称的生命。奉主耶稣的名祷告，阿们。
zh.action: 今天，花一点时间默想“耶稣是基督，是永生神的儿子”这句话，并为此向神献上感谢。

zh.focus: 跟随耶稣意味着舍己、背起十字架，并且为将来的永恒奖赏而活。

questions.question: 耶稣第一次预言自己受难时，祂提到自己必须去哪里？
options: 撒玛利亚
耶利哥
耶路撒冷
加利利
questions.explanation: 耶稣清楚地告诉门徒，祂必须上耶路撒冷去，并在那里受长老、祭司长和文士许多的苦。

questions.question: 当彼得劝耶稣不要受苦时，耶稣如何回应他？
options: 称赞彼得的关心
斥责彼得，称他为撒但
平静地向他解释神的旨意
要求彼得保持安静
questions.explanation: 耶稣转过来对彼得说：“撒但，退我后边去吧！你是绊我脚的；因为你不体贴神的意思，只体贴人的意思。”

questions.question: 耶稣说，如果有人要跟随祂，就必须做什么？
options: 积累很多财富
舍己，背起自己的十字架来跟随祂
避免所有困难和挑战
寻求世人的赞扬
questions.explanation: 耶稣明确指出，跟随祂的条件是舍己，背起自己的十字架来跟随祂。

questions.question: 这篇经文如何提醒我们看待生命的真正价值？
options: 生命的价值在于积累世上的财富和名声
生命的价值在于享受当下，避免一切痛苦
生命的真正价值在于舍弃属世的得失，为永恒的奖赏而活
生命的价值在于别人如何评价我们
questions.explanation: 耶稣教导说，赚得全世界却赔上自己的生命，或用什么来换回生命，都是毫无益处的。这提醒我们生命的真正价值在于基督和永恒。

zh.reflection: 今天你最需要在哪一个方面“舍己，背起十字架”来跟随耶稣？
reflectionOptions: 放下自己的计划，顺服神的旨意
牺牲自己的时间或资源去服事他人
zh.prayer: 主耶稣，感谢祢为我舍命，为我背负十字架。求祢帮助我今天也愿意舍己，背起我的十字架来跟随祢。愿我所做的不是体贴人的意思，而是体贴神祢的心意。奉主耶稣的名祷告，阿们。
zh.action: 今天特意为某个你不想做，但知道是神喜悦的行动，付出一点努力或牺牲。

en.focus: True restoration comes as God turns His people back to Him and shines His favour upon them.

questions.question: How is God addressed at the beginning of the psalm?
options: LORD of hosts
Shepherd of Israel
Righteous Judge
King of the nations
questions.explanation: The psalm begins by calling God the Shepherd of Israel and asking Him to listen and come to save.

questions.question: Which prayer is repeated several times?
options: Give us greater wealth
Destroy every foreign nation
Restore us and let Your face shine
Help us build stronger walls
questions.explanation: The central repeated prayer asks God to restore His people and let His face shine so that they may be saved.

questions.question: What picture is used for the people brought out of Egypt?
options: A vine
An olive tree
A cedar tree
A fig tree
questions.explanation: Israel is pictured as a vine that God brought out of Egypt and planted with care.

questions.question: What is the main message of this psalm?
options: People can change themselves by trying harder
God’s people do not need to pray
Hope for restoration rests in God’s gracious action
Better circumstances automatically restore faith
questions.explanation: The psalmist places his hope in God, asking Him to restore His people and save them again.

en.reflection: In which area do you most need God to turn your heart back to Him today?
reflectionOptions: Return to quiet time with God
en.prayer: Shepherd of Israel, please watch over me. When my heart becomes distant, weak, or confused, turn me back to You. Let Your face shine upon me and renew my hope, strength, and trust in Your saving grace. In Jesus’ name, amen.
en.action: Be still for one minute and pray, “Lord, turn my heart back to You and draw me nearer.”

en.focus: God calls His people to listen because His way brings true provision, protection, and satisfaction.

questions.question: How are the people called to worship God?
options: Shout, sing, and sound the trumpet
Remain completely silent
Pray only in trouble
Worship alone away from others
questions.explanation: The passage calls the people to shout for joy, sing, play instruments, and sound the trumpet.

questions.question: How did God say He had helped Israel?
options: He kept them from the wilderness
He removed the burden from their shoulders
He immediately gave them a throne
He removed every future trial
questions.explanation: God reminds them that He released them from heavy burdens and answered them in distress.

questions.question: What does God warn His people not to do?
options: Plant vines
Speak to enemies
Worship a foreign god
Leave their homeland
questions.explanation: God commands His people to have no other god and not to bow to a foreign god.

questions.question: Why does God call His people to listen?
options: To control every detail
Because His way leads to true provision and satisfaction
Because obedience guarantees no trouble
Because obedience earns His love
questions.explanation: God longs for His people to listen and promises to provide. Obedience is a response of trust in the God who rescued them.

en.reflection: What voice most easily distracts you from listening to God today?
en.prayer: Dear Father, thank You for rescuing and providing for Your people. Give me a willing and attentive heart. Keep me from being carried away by busyness, worry, and other voices. Help me trust that Your way is good and follow You gladly. Amen.
en.action: After reading today’s passage, sit quietly for two minutes and ask God to help you notice His guidance.

en.focus: God values justice and calls those with responsibility to protect the weak and oppressed.

questions.question: What is God doing at the beginning of the psalm?
options: Receiving sacrifices
Judging in the assembly
Leading through the Red Sea
Calling a prophet
questions.explanation: The passage pictures God standing in the assembly and judging whether those in authority act justly.

questions.question: Whom are they commanded to defend and help?
options: The rich and powerful
Distant merchants
The weak, fatherless, poor, and needy
Only their relatives
questions.explanation: God commands them to defend the weak and fatherless and rescue the poor and needy.

questions.question: What wrongdoing does God rebuke?
options: Unjust judgment and favouring the wicked
Too few offerings
Failing to build a city
Ignoring foreign wisdom
questions.explanation: God rebukes unjust judgment and partiality toward the wicked.

questions.question: What does this psalm reveal about God’s heart?
options: He only cares about ceremonies
He is unconcerned about injustice
He values justice and cares for oppressed people
He allows leaders to act however they wish
questions.explanation: God’s justice is seen in protecting the weak, stopping oppression, and calling for fair judgment.

en.reflection: What small action could you take today to care for someone easily overlooked?
en.prayer: God of justice, You care for those who are overlooked, wounded, and oppressed. Remove prejudice and indifference from my heart. Give me compassion, courage, and wisdom to act fairly and show mercy where I have influence. Amen.
en.action: Notice one person who is easily overlooked and show respect through a caring word or practical help.

en.theme: O God, Do Not Remain Silent
en.focus: When God’s people face threats, they may honestly ask Him to act justly and make His name known.

questions.question: What are the enemies plotting?
options: To destroy God’s people as a nation
To worship together
To learn God’s law
To rebuild the walls
questions.explanation: The enemies conspire so that Israel will no longer be remembered as a nation.

questions.question: What does the psalmist ask God not to do?
options: Withhold rain
Hide the temple
Remain silent
Send a prophet
questions.explanation: The psalm opens with a plea that God would not remain silent but would act.

questions.question: What does the psalmist want the nations to know?
options: Israel has the strongest army
The LORD alone is Most High over all the earth
All nations must be identical
People can win by their own strength
questions.explanation: The prayer seeks that people know the LORD’s name and recognise Him as Most High.

questions.question: How does this psalm guide us when facing injustice or threat?
options: Hide our feelings
Take revenge ourselves
Bring fear and anger honestly to God and ask Him to act justly
Pretend nothing is wrong
questions.explanation: The psalmist brings the crisis honestly to God and asks Him to intervene justly so that His name may be known.

en.reflection: When facing misunderstanding, injustice, or pressure, what response do you most need?
en.prayer: Most High God, when I face pressure, injustice, or threat, guard my heart from fear and uncontrolled anger. Help me speak honestly to You and leave judgment in Your hands. Give me wisdom to respond rightly, and let people know that You are Lord. Amen.
en.action: When something makes you angry or anxious today, pause and pray before deciding what to say or do.

en.theme: Blessed Are Those Who Trust You
en.focus: The truly blessed long for God, trust Him, and receive new strength as they journey toward Him.

questions.question: What does the psalmist most deeply long for?
options: A larger house
The courts of the LORD
More praise
A comfortable journey
questions.explanation: The psalmist longs for God’s courts, and his whole being cries out for the living God.

questions.question: Which two birds find a home near God’s altar?
options: Sparrow and swallow
Eagle and dove
Raven and quail
Peacock and crane
questions.explanation: The sparrow finds a home and the swallow a nest, showing security in God’s presence.

questions.question: What happens as they pass through the Valley of Baca?
options: They return home
They lose all strength
It becomes a place of springs, and they go from strength to strength
They no longer need God
questions.explanation: Even through hardship, those whose hearts are set on God receive His provision and renewed strength.

questions.question: Why is one day in God’s courts better than a thousand elsewhere?
options: The building is more beautiful
God Himself is our greatest joy and blessing
No difficulty can occur there
Worshippers are always wealthy
questions.explanation: The psalmist longs not only for a place but for God Himself. Nearness to God is more precious than every other advantage.

en.reflection: What would help you give fuller attention to God today?
en.prayer: LORD of hosts, how lovely is Your dwelling place. Renew my desire for You. Help me seek not only Your gifts but Your presence. Even in difficulty, strengthen me and teach me to trust You. Amen.
en.action: Set aside five minutes today to put other tasks aside and quietly read, pray, and draw near to God.

en.theme: I Will Listen to What God Says
en.focus: God forgives, restores, and speaks peace; His people are called to listen and not return to former foolish ways.

questions.question: What had God done for His people?
options: Forgiven their sins
Made them unable to fail
Removed their need to repent
Ended every conflict
questions.explanation: The psalmist remembers that God had shown favour, restored His people, and forgiven their sin.

questions.question: What does the psalmist ask God to do again?
options: Build a palace
Restore His people so they may rejoice in Him
Make them the wealthiest nation
Take them away from the land
questions.explanation: He asks God to revive and restore His people so that they may rejoice in Him again.

questions.question: What does the psalmist say he will do?
options: Wait for human advice
Count the enemy forces
Listen to what God says
Leave his community
questions.explanation: He chooses to listen because God speaks peace to His people.

questions.question: What does the meeting of love, faithfulness, righteousness, and peace express?
options: God’s character is divided
God’s saving work reveals them together
Peace matters more than righteousness
People need love but not truth
questions.explanation: God’s restoration does not ignore sin or justice. His steadfast love and faithfulness bring true peace.

en.reflection: Which old pattern may God be inviting you not to return to?
en.prayer: God of steadfast love and faithfulness, thank You for forgiving, restoring, and speaking peace to Your people. Give me a quiet heart that listens. Keep me from returning to old foolish ways, and let Your righteousness guide me into Your peace. Amen.
en.action: Before making one decision today, ask, “How would God’s word guide me in this?”

en.focus: In trouble, we may call on the compassionate God and ask Him to teach us to honour Him with an undivided heart.

questions.question: How does the psalmist describe himself?
options: Rich and powerful
Poor and needy
Without any need
Wiser than everyone
questions.explanation: He admits that he is poor and needy and humbly asks God to hear him.

questions.question: What does the psalmist ask God to teach him?
options: How to build an army
How to gain wealth
God’s way, so he may walk in truth
How to avoid responsibility
questions.explanation: He asks God to teach him His way and give him an undivided heart that honours God’s name.

questions.question: How does the psalmist describe God?
options: Compassionate, gracious, and slow to anger
Distant and unwilling to hear
Concerned only for the powerful
Changeable and unreliable
questions.explanation: The passage praises God as compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, and abounding in love and faithfulness.

questions.question: What does it mean to ask God for an undivided heart?
options: To feel only fear
To be gathered from distraction to trust and honour God sincerely
To stop relating to others
To never make decisions
questions.explanation: An undivided heart is one gathered back from distraction to trust, honour, and obey God sincerely.

en.reflection: What most easily divides your attention today?
en.prayer: Compassionate and gracious Lord, please hear me. When I am weak, busy, or anxious, teach me Your way and give me an undivided heart that honours You. Strengthen me to trust Your love and faithfulness even in difficulty. Amen.
en.action: Set aside one distracting thing for ten minutes today and use that time to read Scripture and pray.

en.theme: Let All Peoples Worship the True God
en.focus: God welcomes people from many nations among His people and calls them to worship Him together.

questions.question: What does the passage mention?
options: Wisdom excels folly as light excels darkness.
God has set His foundation on the holy mountain.
God looks for justice and righteousness but finds bloodshed and cries of distress.
God breaks down gates of bronze and cuts through bars of iron.
questions.explanation: God has set His foundation on the holy mountain.

questions.question: Which statement matches today’s passage?
options: The LORD surrounds His people as the mountains surround Jerusalem.
The LORD loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob.
God promises to make a horn grow for David and prepare a lamp for His anointed.
A good name is more desirable than great riches, and favour better than silver or gold.
questions.explanation: The LORD loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob.

questions.question: According to the passage, which statement is correct?
options: The psalmist has calmed and quieted his soul like a weaned child.
People from Egypt, Babylon, Philistia, Tyre, and Cush are also named.
God sets a boundary for the waters so they will not cover the earth again.
He is a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek.
questions.explanation: People from Egypt, Babylon, Philistia, Tyre, and Cush are also named.

questions.question: What is the main truth of this passage?
options: When no human help is found and the spirit grows faint, God remains our refuge and portion in the land of the living.
In difficult circumstances, God’s promise gives hope and comfort, enabling us to remember and keep His word.
God delights in His people and adorns the humble with salvation; praise reminds them that honour and mission come from Him.
God welcomes people from many nations among His people and calls them to worship Him together.
questions.explanation: God welcomes people from many nations among His people and calls them to worship Him together.

en.reflection: In which area is this passage inviting you to respond to God today?
en.prayer: Lord, thank You for speaking to me through “Let All Peoples Worship the True God.” Please plant this truth deeply in my heart. Help me respond today with faith and obedience. Amen.
en.action: Offer God a song or one sentence of praise today.

en.focus: Even in deep darkness, when no answer is visible, we may continue to cry out to God.

questions.question: What does the passage mention?
options: He considered all his labour and found it to be vanity and a chasing after wind.
There is a way that seems right, but in the end it leads to death.
God heard His people’s cry and remembered His covenant for their sake.
The psalmist cries to God day and night.
questions.explanation: The psalmist cries to God day and night.

questions.question: Which statement matches today’s passage?
options: The LORD is near, and all His commands are true.
The psalmist feels like one who has gone down to the pit.
The psalmist considers his ways and turns his feet to God’s testimonies.
Those who seek God wholeheartedly desire not to wander from His commands.
questions.explanation: The psalmist feels like one who has gone down to the pit.

questions.question: According to the passage, which statement is correct?
options: Those who trust in the LORD are like Mount Zion, which cannot be moved.
Friends and loved ones have been taken far from the psalmist.
It is better to take refuge in the LORD than to trust in people or princes.
The beloved’s name is like perfume poured out, so the young women love him.
questions.explanation: Friends and loved ones have been taken far from the psalmist.

questions.question: What is the main truth of this passage?
options: A holy life grows as we treasure God’s word, meditate on His precepts, and delight in His ways.
True praise is not self-promotion but honest recognition from others; faithful friends sharpen one another through truthful counsel.
Even in deep darkness, when no answer is visible, we may continue to cry out to God.
Human days pass and creation changes, but God remains forever and shows mercy to the afflicted.
questions.explanation: Even in deep darkness, when no answer is visible, we may continue to cry out to God.

en.reflection: In which area is this passage inviting you to respond to God today?
en.prayer: Lord, thank You for speaking to me through “A Cry from the Darkness.” Please plant this truth deeply in my heart. Help me respond today with faith and obedience. Amen.
en.action: Be still for two minutes and bring one concern honestly before God.

en.focus: God is incomparable in steadfast love, faithfulness, power, righteousness, and justice.

questions.question: What does the passage mention?
options: God formed the psalmist’s inward parts and knit him together in the womb.
Dead flies spoil perfume, and a little folly can outweigh wisdom and honour.
The psalmist will proclaim God’s steadfast love and faithfulness through all generations.
Human help is vain, but with God His people will act valiantly.
questions.explanation: The psalmist will proclaim God’s steadfast love and faithfulness through all generations.

questions.question: Which statement matches today’s passage?
options: The beloved praises her with beautiful imagery and promises ornaments for her.
There is a way that seems right, but in the end it leads to death.
God rules the raging sea and stills its rising waves.
God’s steadfast love is proclaimed in the morning and His faithfulness at night.
questions.explanation: God rules the raging sea and stills its rising waves.

questions.question: According to the passage, which statement is correct?
options: When Aram and Israel unite against Judah, Ahaz and the people shake like trees in the wind.
The works of the LORD are great and studied by all who delight in them.
Righteousness and justice are the foundation of God’s throne.
God’s word is firmly fixed in heaven forever.
questions.explanation: Righteousness and justice are the foundation of God’s throne.

questions.question: What is the main truth of this passage?
options: God condemns greed, drunkenness, reversing good and evil, self-made wisdom, and bribery; His people must resist distorted values and live by truth.
Long life, children, and wealth remain empty without satisfaction; life is like a shadow, and we must admit how little we know.
God is incomparable in steadfast love, faithfulness, power, righteousness, and justice.
God rules storms, deserts, and fruitful lands; the wise pay attention to His steadfast love.
questions.explanation: God is incomparable in steadfast love, faithfulness, power, righteousness, and justice.

The oppressed shed tears, but they have no comforter.
The people walking in darkness have seen a great light.
The psalmist asks God to do good to those who are good and upright in heart.
questions.explanation: The people walking in darkness have seen a great light.

questions.question: According to the passage, which statement is correct?
options: Because the people reject the gently flowing waters of Shiloah, Assyria comes like an overflowing river.
A child is born for us and is called Wonderful Counsellor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, and Prince of Peace.
Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the LORD, who will reward the deed.
The psalmist asks God to give him life according to His steadfast love.
questions.explanation: A child is born for us and is called Wonderful Counsellor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, and Prince of Peace.

questions.question: What is the main truth of this passage?
options: Wealth cannot automatically bring satisfaction or enjoyment; the ability to enjoy it with contentment is God’s gift.
Covenant love is exclusive, abundant, and mutually giving; it values safety and faithfulness and allows the fragrance of life to bless the beloved.
We must not seek guidance from darkness but return to God’s word; God promises light for those in darkness and a kingdom of justice and peace through the given Son.
The heart and life need diligent cultivation; fair judgment, truthful witness, and steady work prevent neglect and ruin.
questions.explanation: We must not seek guidance from darkness but return to God’s word; God promises light for those in darkness and a kingdom of justice and peace through the given Son.

en.reflection: In which area is this passage inviting you to respond to God today?
en.prayer: Lord, thank You for speaking to me through “Close to God’s Heart.” Help me reject dark guidance, follow Your word closely, and enter the new year in Christ’s light and peace. Help me respond today with faith and obedience. Amen.
en.action: Choose one small action today that puts the passage into practice.

en.focus: Despite repeated rebellion, God's righteous judgment calls His people to repentance, for His lovingkindness never ceases.

questions.question: Through which prophet does God send His message to Jacob (Israel)?
options: Jeremiah
Isaiah
Amos
Hosea
questions.explanation: The passage clearly states that the Lord sent a message against Jacob, and it came through the prophet Isaiah.

questions.question: What was the people's response when God's hand was stretched out to punish them?
options: They humbled themselves and sought God's face
They confessed their sins and turned to God
They were arrogant and refused to turn back
They became fearful and sought help from foreign nations
questions.explanation: The text describes the people's arrogant defiance, saying they would rebuild even better, indicating a refusal to repent.

questions.question: What is God's ultimate purpose in sending messages of judgment?
options: To utterly destroy His people
To display His majesty to the nations
To turn His people back to Him
To prove He is more powerful than idols
questions.explanation: Despite the judgment, the repeated phrase 'His anger has not turned away, and His hand is stretched out still' suggests God's extended hand is an ongoing call for repentance, not just destruction.

questions.question: How does today's passage remind us of the relationship between God's judgment and His love?
options: God's judgment is only for unbelievers, not believers
God's judgment is an expression of His righteousness and a loving call to repentance
God's love means He will never execute judgment
Believers can completely avoid God's discipline through their own efforts
questions.explanation: The passage shows that God's judgment is real and severe, yet the repeated phrase 'His anger has not turned away, and His hand is stretched out still' also implies His desire for His people to return, which is an aspect of His unchanging love.

en.reflection: Today's passage reminds us that God is both righteous and loving. Is there an area in your life where you have been, or are currently, rebellious toward God and need to turn back?
reflectionOptions: Admitting an attitude of pride or complacency
en.prayer: Righteous and loving Heavenly Father, thank You for Your Word which reminds me that You are holy and full of compassion. Please help me to examine my heart. If there is any area of rebellion, illuminate it so I may humbly turn back and trust and obey You more deeply. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Spend a moment reflecting on God's love and His righteousness, then offer a short prayer of repentance for any area the passage has prompted you to turn back from.

en.theme: God Uses Nations, Yet Judges Their Pride
en.focus: God's sovereignty transcends all nations and kings. He uses them to accomplish His purposes but will also judge their pride and evil.

questions.question: How does God refer to Assyria in the passage?
options: His servant
His scourge
The rod of His anger
His prophet
questions.explanation: God calls Assyria 'the rod of my anger,' indicating that Assyria is His instrument to punish nations, including Israel.

questions.question: The king of Assyria boasts about his conquests. What does he attribute his success to?
options: God's help
His own wisdom and strength
A powerful army
The support of allies
questions.explanation: The king of Assyria attributes his conquests to his own wisdom and strength, demonstrating extreme pride and self-reliance.

questions.question: How will God deal with the proud and arrogant Assyria?
options: Elevate Assyria's status
Make Assyria His chosen people
Judge Assyria's pride and bring disaster
Establish an eternal covenant to protect them
questions.explanation: God explicitly states He will punish the pride and arrogance of the king of Assyria, bringing sickness and destruction, like fire consuming thorns and briers.

questions.question: How does this passage remind us to view worldly power and achievements?
options: All authority is absolute and unquestionable
Human achievements are solely due to personal ability, unrelated to God
God is sovereign over all, uses worldly powers, but will also judge human pride
Possessing authority grants the right to do whatever one pleases
questions.explanation: The passage emphasizes God's sovereignty. He uses Assyria as His tool, but when Assyria becomes arrogant and takes credit, God will judge its pride. This reminds us that all authority and achievements come from God and should bring Him glory.

en.reflection: Today, in your life or ministry, are there any achievements or abilities that make you prone to pride or self-satisfaction, making you forget that God is in control?
en.prayer: Almighty Father, You are the Lord of history; all authority and power are in Your hands. Forgive me for any pride or self-satisfaction that arises from my achievements. Help me to constantly humble myself before You, acknowledging that all good things come from You. May I give all glory to You alone. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, offer thanks for one achievement or ability you possess, and intentionally acknowledge it as God's grace.

en.theme: God's Judgment and the Hope of a Remnant
en.focus: Despite allowing judgment upon His people, God preserves a remnant and will ultimately deliver them.

questions.question: After God's judgment on Assyria, whom will the remnant of Israel no longer lean on?
options: The Pharaoh of Egypt
The Assyrians who struck them
The king of Babylon
Their own strength and wisdom
questions.explanation: The passage states that the remnant of Israel will no longer lean on the Assyrians who struck them, but will faithfully lean on the LORD.

questions.question: How will the LORD deal with the power of Assyria?
options: Allow them to continue oppressing Israel
Burn up their forest and fertile land with fire
Enter into a peace treaty with them
Drive them out of Mesopotamia
questions.explanation: The Lord GOD of hosts will lop off the boughs with terrifying power and will cut down the thickets of the forest with an axe, and Lebanon will fall by the Mighty One.

questions.question: In the context of judgment, what is God's ultimate promise for His people?
options: They will never suffer again
They will become a world superpower
A remnant will return and lean on God, though few in number
God will completely revoke all judgment
questions.explanation: The passage emphasizes that even though many will be cut down, a remnant of Israel and the survivors of Jacob will return and faithfully lean on the LORD.

questions.question: How does this passage encourage us when facing difficulties and challenges in life?
options: It encourages us to rely on our own abilities to overcome everything
It reminds us that while God may discipline, He also preserves hope for those who trust Him
It teaches us to completely avoid any form of suffering
It implies that God is indifferent to our lives
questions.explanation: The passage shows that even amidst judgment, God provides hope and salvation for His remnant, encouraging us to trust Him in difficulties.

en.reflection: Is there any situation in your life right now that makes you feel 'cut off' or helpless? How does this passage bring you hope?
reflectionOptions: It reminds me that God is in control and He is my reliance
It helps me believe that God has good plans even in hardships
It encourages me to trust more deeply in God's faithfulness
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for revealing Your justice and mercy in this passage. I know that You are the sovereign Lord, and even in judgment, You preserve hope for me. Please help me not to rely on my own strength when facing life's challenges and uncertainties, but to faithfully and completely lean on You. May my heart always return to You, for You are my salvation. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Find a quiet moment to pray about one thing that is causing you worry or helplessness today, surrendering it completely to God and declaring, “Lord, I lean on You alone!”

en.focus: God will raise up a righteous Messianic King whose reign will bring peace and complete restoration.

questions.question: From whose lineage will the Messianic King arise?
options: Abraham
David
Jesse
Moses
questions.explanation: The passage states that the Messiah will come from the 'stump of Jesse,' who was King David's father.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an attribute described as belonging to or given to the Messianic King?
options: Spirit of the Lord
Wisdom and understanding
Counsel and might
Long life and good health
questions.explanation: The passage lists the Spirit of the Lord, wisdom, understanding, counsel, might, knowledge, and the fear of the Lord, but not long life and good health.

questions.question: What will be the outcome of the Messiah's rule?
options: Only Israelites will prosper
Increased warfare between nations
Restored peace in nature and all nations seeking God
All animals becoming more aggressive
questions.explanation: The Messiah's reign will be characterized by peace, even among animals, and all nations will seek Him.

questions.question: How does the hope in Isaiah 11 comfort or encourage you today?
options: It warns me that the world will get worse, so I should prepare.
It encourages me to strive for a better life for myself and my family.
It shows me that God will ultimately bring complete justice and peace.
It makes me think God only cares about Israel, not me.
questions.explanation: This chapter prophesies the justice, peace, and salvation that the Messiah (Jesus Christ) will bring, offering ultimate hope amidst worldly struggles.

en.reflection: In which areas of your life do you long to see God's justice and peace prevail?
en.prayer: Lord, thank You for promising a righteous King, Jesus Christ. I long for Your kingdom to come and Your will to be done on earth as it is in heaven. Bring Your justice and peace into my life, my family, and my circumstances. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take a minute today to reflect on how Jesus Christ's reign will bring complete justice and peace, and thank God for this hope.

en.theme: The Glory and Salvation of the Messiah's Kingdom
en.focus: God will gather His remnant, establish the Messiah's kingdom, and bring universal salvation and joy.

questions.question: From where will God gather His remnant?
options: Only from Babylon and Egypt
Only from Israelites dispersed among nations
From Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Shinar, Hamath, and the coastlands of the sea
From all Gentile nations that do not know God
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly lists Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Shinar, Hamath, and the coastlands of the sea as places from which God will gather His remnant.

questions.question: What change will occur between Israel and Judah in the Messianic era?
options: They will continue to be enemies
They will unite and no longer envy or oppose each other
Judah will completely absorb Israel
Israel will become a stronger nation
questions.explanation: The text states, “The jealousy of Ephraim will vanish, and Judah’s adversaries will be cut off; Ephraim will not be jealous of Judah, nor Judah hostile toward Ephraim.” This indicates peaceful unity.

questions.question: What is the primary message conveyed in Isaiah 12?
options: Judgment and punishment for enemies
Gratitude and praise for God's salvation and comfort
A warning about future difficult times
A longing for the rebuilding of the temple
questions.explanation: Chapter 12 is filled with praise to God for being their strength, song, and salvation, inviting all to joyfully proclaim His deeds.

questions.question: From this passage, how should we view God's work in history and His future promises?
options: God is only concerned with the restoration of the nation of Israel
God's plan is to gather His people from all corners to establish a kingdom of peace, justice, and salvation
God's power is only demonstrated in His judgment of enemies
God's promises are vague and difficult to understand
questions.explanation: This passage reveals God's plan to gather His remnant from all places, establish a universal Messianic kingdom of peace, and bring joyful salvation, which extends beyond the interests of a single nation.

en.reflection: What new insights or hope does today's scripture give you about God's redemptive plan and His glorious kingdom?
reflectionOptions: Comforted by God's promise to gather His scattered people
Filled with anticipation for the peace and justice of the Messiah's kingdom
A deeper understanding that God's salvation is universal
en.prayer: Dear Lord, thank You for being a faithful God who keeps Your covenant, gathering Your dispersed people and establishing Your glorious kingdom. Help me to praise Your salvation with a joyful heart and to live in a way that reflects Your kingdom, being an agent of peace and justice. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Spend a moment today quietly reflecting on how God has led you back to Him in your own life. Offer thanks for this grace.

en.theme: The Day of the Lord and Judgment on Nations
en.focus: God is the Judge of all the earth, sovereign over history, and His final judgment will surely come.

questions.question: Which nation is mentioned at the beginning of Isaiah 13 as facing judgment?
options: Egypt
Assyria
Babylon
Israel
questions.explanation: The oracle in this chapter concerns Babylon.

questions.question: How will God gather the army to execute His judgment?
options: From the south
From the north
From a distant land, from the ends of the heavens
From the local region
questions.explanation: God will gather His army from a distant land, from the ends of the heavens, to execute judgment.

questions.question: What does “the Day of the Lord” primarily refer to in this passage?
options: A festival of peace and joy
A day when God judges sin and reveals His righteousness
A day when God bestows abundant blessings
A day when people offer sacrifices to God
questions.explanation: “The Day of the Lord” is described here as a dark, cruel, and wrathful day when God will punish wickedness.

questions.question: What is the main message this passage helps us understand?
options: People can change the course of history through their own efforts
God’s judgment on nations is arbitrary and without reason
God is sovereign over history; He is a righteous Judge, and His judgment will be accomplished
Doing good deeds can prevent God's judgment
questions.explanation: The passage emphasizes God’s sovereignty; His judgment is righteous and unavoidable, even for a powerful nation like Babylon.

en.reflection: In light of God’s sovereignty and His future judgment, what do you most need to adjust or trust God with today?
reflectionOptions: Less worry, more trust in the future
Repent of my sins and turn to God
en.prayer: Almighty Father, You are the King who governs history, and Your judgment is righteous and true. Help me to submit to You with reverence and trust Your sovereignty in all things. May my life glorify You and be prepared for Your coming day. In Jesus’ name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Spend one minute today reflecting on God's greatness and His control over all the earth, then meditate on the verse: “For the day of the LORD is near.”

en.focus: God, in His compassion, delivers His people from oppression and exercises absolute sovereignty over all nations.

questions.question: At the beginning of Isaiah 14, to whom does God show compassion?
options: Assyria
Egypt
Israel
Babylon
questions.explanation: The passage clearly states that the LORD will have compassion on Jacob and will again choose Israel.

questions.question: What image is used to describe the fall of the king of Babylon from heaven?
options: A shooting star
Lightning
Day Star, son of Dawn
A large rock
questions.explanation: The prophet uses a taunt to describe the king of Babylon falling like the 'Day Star, son of Dawn' from heaven.

questions.question: What primary attribute of God is revealed through His pronouncements against Babylon and Philistia?
options: His love is exclusively for Israel
His wisdom surpasses all political strategies
His absolute sovereignty and judgment over all the earth and nations
His concern is only with individual moral behavior
questions.explanation: Through prophecies against Babylon and Philistia, God reveals Himself as the supreme ruler who controls history and the destiny of nations.

questions.question: How does this passage encourage you when facing suffering or injustice in the world?
options: It reminds me that God will ultimately bring justice
It motivates me to change the world through my own strength
It teaches me that God is not concerned with worldly affairs
It advises me to simply wait and do nothing
questions.explanation: The passage emphasizes God's sovereignty and judgment over nations, reminding us that even in the face of powerful oppression, God will ultimately bring justice and salvation.

en.reflection: In your life, what situations make you feel oppressed or unjustly treated, that you need to entrust to God, trusting in His ultimate control?
en.prayer: Almighty Father, thank You that You are the Lord who governs all things, and Your compassion and sovereignty never change. When I feel oppressed by circumstances or face injustice, help me to entrust everything to You, believing that Your will shall ultimately be done and Your righteousness will be revealed. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take a quiet moment to pray about one specific situation that causes you stress or feels unjust, declaring God's sovereignty over it.

en.focus: Even in God's judgment against sin, He reserves mercy and hope for those who trust in Him.

questions.question: Which nation is primarily prophesied to face judgment in this passage?
options: Egypt
Assyria
Moab
Babylon
questions.explanation: Isaiah chapters 15 and 16 focus on God's judgment against Moab.

questions.question: What grim scenes are described when Moab faces judgment?
options: Abundant food and joyful celebrations
Collapsed houses and fertile land
Widespread weeping, nakedness, and withered vegetation
Thriving commerce and national prosperity
questions.explanation: The passage describes the people of Moab weeping, shaving their heads, walking naked due to disaster, and the land being desolate with withered vegetation.

questions.question: In the midst of Moab's tragic situation, what unexpected hope does the prophet mention?
options: Moab will seek help from Assyria
Judah will completely defeat Moab
Moab's remnant will seek refuge with a descendant of David
God will utterly destroy Moab without leaving any survivors
questions.explanation: The prophet calls on the remnant of Moab to seek refuge with the king who sits on the throne of David, who judges with faithfulness (referring to the Messiah).

questions.question: How does this passage remind us about God's judgment and mercy?
options: God only judges foreign nations, not His own people
God's judgment on sin is real, but He also provides hope of salvation for those who seek Him
Doing good deeds can prevent God's judgment
God's judgment is random and unpredictable
questions.explanation: While God announces severe judgment on Moab, the passage also implies that those from Moab who turn to the 'tent of David' can find refuge, demonstrating God's mercy even in judgment.

en.reflection: Have you ever felt helpless and sorrowful due to your own weaknesses or the world's turmoil? How does this passage encourage you to look to God's mercy and salvation even amidst judgment?
reflectionOptions: It reminds me of God's justice and holiness
It shows me that there is true hope in Christ
It prompts me to repent more earnestly and seek God
en.prayer: Lord, You are a righteous Judge and a loving Redeemer. When I see the sin and suffering in the world, help me not to despair, but to lean deeper into You. Thank You for providing hope in Christ even in judgment. May I always find rest in Your mercy. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take some time today to reflect on how you can see God's sovereignty and mercy, even in difficult or unjust circumstances.

en.focus: Even in judgment, God reserves hope for His people, calling them to repentance and to turn back to Him.

questions.question: What is prophesied to happen to Damascus in Isaiah 17:1?
options: It will become a beautiful city
It will become a ruin, no longer a city
It will become a powerful military base
It will become a commercial hub
questions.explanation: The text clearly states that Damascus will 'no longer be a city but will become a heap of ruins.'

questions.question: How will the glory of Israel be diminished during judgment?
options: It will greatly increase
It will completely disappear
It will become scarce, like a harvested field
It will be transferred to another nation
questions.explanation: The text uses analogies like 'when the reaper gathers the standing grain, and his arm harvests the heads of grain' and 'like the shaking of an olive tree' to describe the scarcity of Israel's glory.

questions.question: What did Israel forget, according to this chapter, leading to their judgment?
options: They forgot to build strong walls
They forgot their Maker and their Savior
They forgot to make alliances with foreign nations
They forgot agricultural techniques
questions.explanation: The passage indicates that the people 'have not remembered the God of your salvation; you have not considered the Rock of your refuge.'

questions.question: Despite the judgment, what does Isaiah 17 tell us God still preserves for His people?
options: More wealth and power
The possibility of returning to God and salvation
Better relationships with other nations
New idols and ways of worship
questions.explanation: After the judgment, the text mentions that a few will 'look to their Maker and turn their eyes to the Holy One of Israel,' indicating a preserved hope for return.

en.reflection: How is God reminding you today that He is your Maker and Savior? How will you respond?
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for being my Maker and my Savior. Please help me to always remember You and not be swayed by worldly worries or idols. When my heart strays, guide me back with Your love and truth. In Jesus’ name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Spend one minute in quiet reflection today, considering how God acts as your Maker and Savior in your life.

en.focus: God's sovereignty transcends all, and in the end, all nations will bring gifts to Him.

questions.question: What kind of land does the prophet Isaiah mention in verse 1?
options: A nation full of wealth
A land of whirring wings and ships
A region surrounded by high mountains
A desolate land covered by desert
questions.explanation: The passage begins by mentioning “the land of whirring wings beyond the rivers of Cush”.

questions.question: How does God respond to the hasty messengers and nations preparing for war?
options: He intervenes immediately and punishes them
He encourages them to continue fighting
He prunes them before harvest and leaves them to birds and beasts
He sends His messengers to stop them
questions.explanation: God says, “For before the harvest, when the blossom is over and the grape is ripening, he will cut off the shoots with pruning hooks, and prune away and remove the spreading branches. They will be left to the birds of prey, and to the wild animals.”

questions.question: What does this chapter ultimately prophesy?
options: Nations will forever turn away from God
God will only save the people of Israel
All powerful nations will perish
A tall and smooth-skinned people will bring gifts to Mount Zion for the LORD of hosts
questions.explanation: The passage concludes by stating, “At that time gifts will be brought to the LORD of hosts from a people tall and smooth-skinned, from a people dreaded far and wide, a nation mighty and conquering, whose land is divided by rivers—to Mount Zion, the place of the name of the LORD of hosts.”

questions.question: What important lesson about God's sovereignty can we learn from this chapter?
options: God only cares about the destiny of His chosen people
God's power is only evident in warfare
Regardless of worldly turmoil, God remains sovereign and accomplishes His will
Human plans and power ultimately determine everything
questions.explanation: Despite the presence of war and turmoil in the world, God is always in control, and His plans will ultimately be realized, with even the nations turning to Him.

en.reflection: Are there any 'whirring' worldly affairs in your life today that cause you confusion or worry? How can you entrust them to the sovereign God?
reflectionOptions: Pray about a confusing or worrying matter
Remind myself that God is in control
Look up Bible promises about God's sovereignty
en.prayer: LORD of hosts, You are the God who controls all things. In the face of the world's noise and life's challenges, help me to be still and trust in Your sovereignty. May I see You at work in all things and ultimately bring You glory. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take a quiet moment to meditate on a scripture about God's sovereignty (e.g., Psalm 46:10) and apply it to one of your worries today.

en.focus: God's sovereignty extends over all nations, and He has the power to judge, heal, and ultimately draw all peoples to Himself.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 19 begin by describing the LORD's judgment on Egypt?
options: He will send angels to destroy Egypt
He will ride on a swift cloud into Egypt
He will use foreign armies to attack Egypt
He will cause the land of Egypt to dry up
questions.explanation: The text describes the LORD riding on a swift cloud into Egypt, signifying His swift and sovereign judgment.

questions.question: Besides political and social turmoil, what other difficulties are part of God's judgment on Egypt?
options: Plagues and widespread diseases
Famine and floods
Economic collapse and depletion of resources
Breakdown of the education system
questions.explanation: God's judgment on Egypt includes economic collapse (e.g., cut wages) and depletion of resources (e.g., drying up of the Nile, ruin of fishing).

questions.question: What is the ultimate goal of God's judgment on Egypt?
options: To completely destroy Egypt so it disappears forever
To show His favoritism towards Israel
To cause Egypt to know the LORD and turn to Him
To make other nations fear and not oppose Israel
questions.explanation: Despite judgment, the text repeatedly mentions that Egypt will know the LORD, be healed, blessed, and eventually worship God alongside Israel and Assyria.

questions.question: How does this passage encourage us to trust God when facing difficulties or injustices?
options: If we are strong enough, we can overcome all difficulties
God will eventually punish all who don't believe in Him, benefiting us
God is in control; His judgment and healing serve His ultimate good purpose, including drawing all peoples to Himself
We should actively seek revenge on those who harm us
questions.explanation: God's sovereignty transcends all, and His actions (including judgment and healing) have a higher purpose, ultimately to fulfill His redemptive plan and make Himself known to all peoples.

en.reflection: In which area do you most need to surrender a seemingly chaotic or difficult situation to God today, trusting in His control and good purposes?
en.prayer: Almighty God, You are the sovereign Lord over all nations and peoples. When I see chaos and injustice in the world, help me to look to Your sovereignty. I trust that Your judgment and healing serve Your good purposes, ultimately to make Yourself known to all peoples. May Your will be done on earth as it is in heaven. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Find a quiet moment to pray for your nation or a nation you care about, asking God to direct all things according to His will.

en.focus: God delivers crucial messages to His people and the nations through the dramatic actions of His prophet.

questions.question: What unusual action did the prophet Isaiah perform at the Lord's command?
options: Put on his finest robes
Walked naked and barefoot
Fasted and prayed for seven days
Built an altar
questions.explanation: The Lord commanded Isaiah to take off his sackcloth and sandals, and walk naked and barefoot.

questions.question: What did Isaiah's action symbolize or foreshadow?
options: A great victory for Israel
The capture of Egyptians and Cushites by the king of Assyria
The prophet's suffering and death
A peace treaty between Judah and Assyria
questions.explanation: Isaiah's nakedness and barefoot walking were a sign that the Egyptians and Cushites would be led away captive, also naked and barefoot, by the king of Assyria.

questions.question: What would be the reaction of those living in the coastlands when Egypt and Cush faced this fate?
options: They would rejoice greatly
They would be dismayed and ashamed
They would go to help Egypt and Cush
They would turn to the king of Assyria for protection
questions.explanation: Those who had looked to Egypt and Cush for help and glory would be dismayed and ashamed when they saw them taken captive.

questions.question: This passage reminds us where we should place our trust during difficult times. Where should it be?
options: In powerful nations and alliances
In our own wisdom and abilities
Solely in the living God
In miraculous help from prophets
questions.explanation: When earthly dependencies prove futile, we are reminded that true security and help come only from God.

en.reflection: Is there anyone or anything in your life that you are currently relying on, but might ultimately disappoint you?
en.prayer: Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding me through the prophet Isaiah's actions that all earthly reliance can fail. Please help me, in all circumstances, to trust in You alone, for You are the unchanging Rock and my refuge. In Jesus' name, I pray, Amen.
en.action: Spend some quiet time today reflecting on any people or things you might be over-relying on, then confess it to God and ask Him to help you trust Him alone.

en.focus: God's sovereignty governs history, revealing His love and care for His people even amidst judgment.

questions.question: How does the prophet Isaiah describe the vision he saw in verse 1?
options: A vision about the world
A message concerning the desert by the sea
A vision about Babylon
A message concerning Arabia
questions.explanation: The passage begins by identifying it as 'A prophecy concerning the Desert by the Sea,' describing a terrifying vision from the desert.

questions.question: What was the prophet Isaiah's reaction to seeing this vision?
options: Joyful and happy
Extremely distressed and anxious
Confused and bewildered
Indifferent and unmoved
questions.explanation: The prophet describes himself as 'wracked with pain,' 'anguish has gripped me,' and 'my loins ache,' even to the point of being 'too troubled to hear.'

questions.question: Although this passage primarily predicts judgment on nations, how does it reveal God's care for His people?
options: God promises to give His people more land
God foretells the fall of Babylon, which will lead to His people's release
God commands His people to hide to avoid disaster
God provides abundant food for His people
questions.explanation: The prophecy of Babylon's judgment implies freedom for the exiled people of Judah, demonstrating God's care for them.

questions.question: What does this message of judgment remind us of in our lives today?
options: We should only focus on our spiritual lives and ignore world affairs
God is sovereign over history, and He is faithful even in difficulties; we can trust Him
We should fear the future because judgment can come at any time
We can avoid all suffering if we try hard enough
questions.explanation: This passage reminds us that God is sovereign over all things. He reveals His will and cares for His people even in judgment, so we can trust Him in all circumstances.

en.reflection: In today's rapidly changing world, how do you perceive God's sovereignty over history and His faithfulness?
reflectionOptions: Remind myself that God is in control
Pray for my nation and global affairs
en.prayer: Lord, You are the God who governs history and all things. In the midst of the world's chaos and unrest, help me to fix my eyes on Your faithfulness and sovereignty. Thank You for showing Your love and care for Your people even in judgment. May my heart find peace in knowing You. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take a moment to reflect on how God has faithfully led you in the past, and offer Him thanks.

en.focus: When God's people face crisis, their reliance on God versus their own strength determines their outcome.

questions.question: What does the prophet Isaiah call Jerusalem?
options: Holy City of Zion
Valley of Vision
Dwelling Place of God
City of the Great King
questions.explanation: The passage opens by referring to Jerusalem as the 'Valley of Vision,' depicting a tragic scene.

questions.question: What was the people's reaction when the enemy besieged Jerusalem?
options: Fasting and praying for God's help
Weeping and repenting of their sins
Tearing down houses to strengthen walls and storing water
Celebrating with joy, eating and drinking
questions.explanation: In their time of crisis, instead of turning to God, the people indulged in feasting and revelry.

questions.question: How does God describe His judgment upon His people?
options: A minor correction
No atonement until they die
Making them more prosperous
Giving them victory over all enemies
questions.explanation: God explicitly declares that their sin 'will not be atoned for until you die,' indicating the severity of the judgment.

questions.question: What is the main lesson this passage teaches us?
