options: In crisis, people can rely entirely on their own wisdom and ability
God will overlook the sins of His people
In trouble, we should turn to God instead of relying on fleeting worldly pleasures or human methods
As long as the city walls are strong, no enemy can break through
questions.explanation: The passage highlights the people's error in not relying on God, but rather on worldly preparations and pleasures, leading to severe judgment.

en.reflection: In your life, have you ever, like the people of Jerusalem, first sought human solutions or worldly pleasures in times of difficulty, neglecting to turn to God?
reflectionOptions: Admit to relying on self more than God
Reflect more deeply on God's justice
en.prayer: Heavenly Father, You are the sovereign Lord of all. Please forgive me for times when, in difficulty, I first turn to human methods or worldly comforts instead of wholeheartedly seeking You. Help me to rely solely on You, looking to You for salvation and guidance in every circumstance. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Spend five minutes in quiet reflection today. For a recent concern, how much have you relied on God versus yourself or others?

en.theme: God's Sovereignty Over Nations and Trade
en.focus: Even in powerful trade centres, God’s will prevails, bringing judgment upon pride and offering promises of future restoration.

questions.question: Which city-state's destruction is prophesied at the beginning of Isaiah 23?
options: Babylon
Egypt
Tyre
Assyria
questions.explanation: The first phrase of the passage, 'An oracle concerning Tyre,' clearly identifies the subject of the prophecy.

questions.question: How are the merchants of Tyre described?
options: Poor and powerless
Powerful and wealthy, like kings and the honoured of the earth
Lazy and unproductive
Only focused on agriculture, not trade
questions.explanation: The text describes Tyre's merchants as 'princes' and her traders as 'the honoured of the earth,' indicating their great power and wealth.

questions.question: Why did God judge Tyre?
options: Because Tyre failed to pay tribute to Israel on time
Because Tyre refused to ally with Israel
Because of Tyre's pride and excessive reliance on wealth
Because of Tyre's unfavourable geographical location
questions.explanation: God judged Tyre 'to defile all her proud glory and to humble all who are honoured on the earth,' pointing to pride as the reason for judgment.

questions.question: What is Tyre's ultimate fate?
options: Eternal destruction with no possibility of recovery
Annexation by Egypt, becoming its vassal state
To be forgotten for seventy years, then remembered and restored to trade
To become an ally of Israel and be perpetually protected
questions.explanation: The text states Tyre 'will be forgotten for seventy years.' After seventy years, she 'will be remembered like a prostitute,' resuming her trade, but her profits and earnings will be consecrated to the LORD, to provide for those who serve Him.

en.reflection: Is there anything in your life, like Tyre, that makes you proud, overly dependent, or boastful, and that you need to re-evaluate its true value in God's eyes?
en.prayer: Lord, the rise and fall of Tyre remind me that all power and wealth ultimately rest in Your hands. Help me to examine my heart, to remove all pride and excessive reliance on worldly things. May my life be centred solely on You, and may all I possess be used to glorify You and advance Your kingdom. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take a minute today to consider: What is the one thing I am most prone to be proud of? Then pray for God to help you transform that pride into gratitude and trust in Him.

en.focus: Despite the desolation of the world due to sin, God remains in control, His judgment is just, and His kingdom will ultimately be established.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the destruction and desolation of the earth?
options: The earth is laid waste, emptied, and shaken
The earth is burned and turned to ashes
The earth is flooded and becomes a swamp
The earth is covered by plague, and all life perishes
questions.explanation: The passage describes the earth being “laid waste and devastated; he will turn it upside down and scatter its inhabitants. The earth is utterly broken, completely shattered, violently shaken.”

questions.question: Why does the earth and its inhabitants face such a great judgment?
options: Because they did not observe God's festivals
Because they have transgressed the laws, violated the statutes, and broken the everlasting covenant
Because they worshipped idols and abandoned God
Because they fought among themselves and killed each other
questions.explanation: The passage clearly states that the earth is consumed and its inhabitants suffer because they “have transgressed the laws, violated the statutes, and broken the everlasting covenant.”

questions.question: After the desolation and judgment, what does the passage ultimately point to?
options: The earth will remain desolate forever, uninhabited
God will no longer concern Himself with earthly matters
The moon will be confounded and the sun ashamed, for the LORD of hosts will reign on Mount Zion
New nations will rise and establish order again
questions.explanation: Despite the judgment on the earth, the ultimate vision is that “the moon will be confounded and the sun ashamed, for the LORD of hosts will reign on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem.”

questions.question: What is the primary message this passage conveys to us?
options: The world will eventually be destroyed, so we should enjoy life while we can
God's judgment is real and thorough, yet He remains the sovereign King over all
Humans can avoid disaster if they try hard enough
God's love means He will never judge sin
questions.explanation: The passage vividly describes God's judgment on sin and the desolation of the earth, but ultimately emphasizes God's supreme sovereignty as He reigns on Mount Zion.

en.reflection: In the face of worldly turmoil and injustice, how do you trust in the God who ultimately reigns as King?
reflectionOptions: Remind myself God is in control and release worries
Pray for society and nations, asking for God's justice to prevail
Live out righteousness and holiness in my own life
en.prayer: Almighty Father, You are the Lord who controls all things, Your judgments are righteous, and Your kingdom endures forever. In this challenging and uncertain world, help me to firmly trust in Your sovereignty. May Your will be done on earth as it is in heaven. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Spend one minute today meditating on God as the sovereign King over all things, and offer Him thanks and praise for it.

en.theme: Praise for God's Faithfulness and Victory
en.focus: God, through His faithfulness and power, prepares a lavish feast for His people and swallows up death forever.

questions.question: How does the prophet Isaiah express his praise to God in verse 1?
options: Praising His justice and judgment
Praising His wonderful plans and perfect faithfulness
Praising His power and creation
Praising His love and mercy
questions.explanation: Isaiah praises God because He has 'done wonderful things, plans formed of old, in perfect faithfulness,' referring to His reliable plans and promises.

questions.question: What 'wonderful things' does God do in the passage?
options: Changing the course of rivers
Turning strong cities into heaps of rubble
Making the sun stand still
Sending fire from heaven
questions.explanation: God turns a strong city into a pile of rubble and the fortress of foreigners into a ruin, symbolizing His judgment on oppressors.

questions.question: What future does God prepare for His people?
options: A time of war
A society without poverty
A lavish feast, and the swallowing up of death forever
An opportunity to rebuild their homes
questions.explanation: God will prepare a feast of rich food for all peoples on Mount Zion, and He will swallow up death forever and wipe away every tear from every face.

questions.question: What is the main hope this passage offers us?
options: We can change the world if we try hard enough
God's promises will ultimately be fulfilled, bringing complete salvation and eternal joy
Foreign nations will eventually recognize their mistakes
We should focus on earthly success
questions.explanation: The passage emphasizes that God will fulfill His promises, bringing ultimate salvation to His people, including the swallowing up of death forever and wiping away tears, enabling them to rejoice and be glad.

en.reflection: In what moments or aspects of your life do you especially need to remind yourself of God's faithfulness and His ultimate victory?
reflectionOptions: When feeling uncertain about the future
en.prayer: Faithful Lord, I praise You because Your plans are wonderful, and Your promises are perfectly true. Thank You for preparing an eternal hope for me; You will swallow up death and wipe away all my tears. Help me to fix my eyes on Your ultimate victory amidst life's challenges. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take one minute today to quietly reflect on God's faithfulness in your life and give thanks for it.

en.focus: In times of trouble, God’s people find peace and hope by trusting in His righteousness and salvation.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 26:1, what characterizes the 'strong city' that people sing about?
options: Its walls reach to the sky
Salvation is established as its walls and ramparts
It is the strongest city man can build
The city is full of wealth and power
questions.explanation: The passage states that the strong city has salvation established as its walls and ramparts.

questions.question: What is repeatedly emphasized in Isaiah 26:3-4?
options: God's people must strive to fight to gain peace
Trust in the LORD forever, for the LORD God is an everlasting rock
Peace can only be obtained by keeping the law
Peace is bought with wealth and status
questions.explanation: The text clearly states that the LORD keeps in perfect peace those whose minds are steadfast, because they trust in Him. It also emphasizes to trust in the LORD forever, for the LORD God is an everlasting rock.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 26:19, how will God deal with the righteous who have died?
options: They will sleep forever
Their graves will be forgotten forever
Your dead shall live; their bodies shall rise
Their souls will be reincarnated
questions.explanation: The scripture clearly prophesies that God's dead will live again, their bodies will rise, and they will sing, for God's dew is a dew of light.

questions.question: What is the most important comfort and hope you receive from God in today's passage?
options: God will make all my enemies disappear
God will bring me material prosperity
Even in trouble, trusting God brings peace and the ultimate hope of resurrection
God will make my life smooth sailing without challenges
questions.explanation: Isaiah 26 emphasizes that trusting in God brings peace in times of trouble and prophesies the hope of resurrection, both of which are comforts God gives us.

en.reflection: In what areas of your life do you feel uneasy or lack peace? How can you entrust these more to the Everlasting Rock?
reflectionOptions: Let go of anxiety about the future
Stop being overly critical of myself or others
en.prayer: Everlasting Rock, thank You for being my strong fortress. When my heart wavers and I face troubles, help me to steadfastly trust in You, so that I may find perfect peace. Please also remind me how real and precious is the hope of resurrection You have given. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, when a worry arises, pause for a moment and say to God in your heart: “Lord, I trust in You; You are my peace.”

en.focus: God's sovereignty and faithfulness ensure that He will bring complete salvation and restoration to His people after judgment.

questions.question: What does God command His people to do in Isaiah 26:20?
options: Proclaim God's glory to the nations
Go into your rooms and hide yourselves for a little while
Prepare weapons for war
Build high towers to resist enemies
questions.explanation: God instructs His people to go into their rooms and hide themselves for a little while until His wrath has passed.

questions.question: In Chapter 27, what does God use as a metaphor for the powerful enemy He will cut down?
options: Wild beasts of the desert
The Leviathan, the serpent of the sea
Rocks of the mountains
Eagles flying in the sky
questions.explanation: God refers to Leviathan (a sea monster or great beast) as the powerful enemy He will cut down.

questions.question: Despite God's judgment on the world, what is His intention for His people (Israel)?
options: To abandon them forever in foreign lands
To completely forsake them and no longer care
To care for, water, and protect them like a vineyard
To leave them to their own devices, without intervention
questions.explanation: God describes His people as a 'pleasant vineyard' that He Himself will guard, water, and ensure no harm comes to it, making it fruitful.

questions.question: How does this passage encourage us to trust God when facing difficulties and uncertainties?
options: By relying solely on our own strength and wisdom to overcome everything
God will powerfully judge the wicked while tenderly caring for and preserving His people
God is only concerned with judgment, not our personal safety
We can escape God's judgment by hiding away
questions.explanation: The passage shows that God will judge the wicked, but at the same time, He will tenderly care for and protect His people, ensuring their ultimate restoration and fruitfulness. This encourages us to trust in His faithfulness and sovereignty.

en.reflection: What aspects of your current life cause you anxiety or uncertainty? How does this passage remind you that God is still in control and will care for you?
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for being the God who is in control of all things and is faithful to Your covenant. Please help me to fix my eyes on You when facing anxieties and uncertainties in life, trusting that You will bring salvation through Your judgment and will care for and preserve Your children. May my heart find peace and hope in Your promises. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take a quiet moment to recall how God has cared for you in past difficulties, and offer Him thanks.

en.focus: Despite human rebellion, God remains the faithful and reliable cornerstone, and His judgment ultimately serves His redemptive purposes.

questions.question: To whom does the prophet Isaiah pronounce 'Woe' in verse 1?
options: The kings of Assyria
The pharaohs of Egypt
The drunkards of Ephraim
The priests of Judah
questions.explanation: The passage directly addresses the 'Woe to the proud crown of the drunkards of Ephraim, and to the fading flower of its glorious beauty, which is on the head of the rich valley of those overcome with wine!'

questions.type: Observe the description of the rebellious
questions.question: How are the priests and prophets described due to their drunkenness?
options: They became clearer in thought and could see the future
They preached clearly and helped people understand the law
They staggered, erred in vision, and stumbled in judgment
They became more alert and could discern right from wrong
questions.explanation: The text describes them staggering because of wine, erring in vision, and stumbling in judgment, even defiling the table.

questions.question: Amidst this chaos and rebellion, for whom does God lay a tested stone in Zion?
options: For the king of Assyria
For those who seek false covenants
For those who believe, as a sure foundation
For those who scoff at God's word
questions.explanation: Despite the people's rebellion, God promises to lay a precious cornerstone in Zion, a sure foundation for those who believe.

questions.type: Understand the passage's warning and hope
questions.question: What is the main message of this chapter?
options: God's judgment is only for foreign nations, not for His people
Religious rituals alone guarantee God's favor
Human pride, rebellion, and false security lead to judgment, but God remains the faithful foundation
God always judges immediately, never giving a chance for repentance
questions.explanation: The chapter reveals the sin and false security of Israel's leaders, pronounces impending judgment, but also points to God laying a precious cornerstone in Zion, offering sure hope to those who trust Him.

en.reflection: Are there areas in your life where you are relying on your own wisdom or a false sense of security, rather than fully trusting in God?
reflectionOptions: Let go of attachment to material things
en.prayer: Faithful God, I confess that sometimes I, like Ephraim, rely on my own judgment or worldly assurances. Forgive my pride and unbelief. Help me to trust solely in the precious foundation You have laid in Jesus Christ. May my life be securely built upon Your eternal truth. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, take one minute to meditate on Jesus as your 'precious cornerstone' and thank Him for it.

en.theme: God's Firm Foundation and Wise Guidance
en.focus: God lays a tested stone in Zion as a firm foundation for those who trust Him, and He guides all things with His wisdom.

questions.question: What are the characteristics of the 'stone' God lays in Zion?
options: A stone for decoration and beauty
A tested stone, a precious cornerstone for a sure foundation
A stone for building tall towers
A large stone to block access
questions.explanation: The scripture states that God lays a 'tested stone, a precious cornerstone for a sure foundation' in Zion.

questions.question: With what will God judge those who make lies their refuge?
options: With floods sweeping away their walls
With fire consuming their houses
With justice as a measuring line and righteousness as a plumb line
With great earthquakes shaking their foundations
questions.explanation: God declares, 'I will make justice the measuring line and righteousness the plumb line.' This indicates He will judge with His perfect justice and uprightness those who rely on deceit.

questions.type: Understand the meaning of the farmer's parable
questions.question: What is the main point illustrated by the parable of the farmer's work?
options: The farmer's wisdom and effort are key to success
God sends rain on time, ensuring a good harvest
God gives wisdom and teaches people when and how to work to achieve His ultimate purpose
The natural laws of crop growth are unchangeable
questions.explanation: The farmer knows when to plow, when to plant, and how to harvest; this wisdom comes from the LORD of hosts, whose counsel is wonderful and whose wisdom is great. This parable illustrates that God acts according to His wisdom and plan.

questions.question: According to today's scripture, how should we respond to God's firm foundation and wisdom?
options: Build our lives based on our own wisdom and abilities
Seek worldly power and wealth as security
Build our lives and hope on the firm foundation God has laid, and trust in His guidance
Be anxious about the future because God will judge everything
questions.explanation: God has laid a sure foundation in Zion and provides wisdom. We should trust in this foundation and submit to His wise guidance.

en.reflection: In your life, are you building your hope and security on the firm foundation God has laid? How can you trust Him more today?
reflectionOptions: Release worries about the future, trusting God's control
Seek God's wisdom and guidance in a difficult decision
Acknowledge any 'lies' or 'false refuges' you've relied on
en.prayer: Lord, thank You for being my sure foundation and my precious cornerstone. Help me to build my life and all my hopes upon You, rather than on false securities. Grant me wisdom that comes from You, guiding my every step. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take a moment to meditate on the phrase 'a tested stone, a precious cornerstone for a sure foundation,' and offer a prayer of thanks and trust to God.

en.theme: Worship of the Lips, Not the Heart
en.focus: God condemns those who worship Him with their lips while their hearts are far from Him, and promises to do wonderful things.

questions.question: How does the prophet Isaiah refer to Jerusalem at the beginning of the passage?
options: God's holy city
City where David encamped
Daughter of Zion
Capital of the nations
questions.explanation: The passage begins by referring to Jerusalem as “Ariel, the city where David encamped,” foreshadowing siege and distress.

questions.type: Observe God's description of His people
questions.question: How does God describe His people's worship of Him?
options: Wholehearted love and obedience
Worship with their mouths, but hearts far away
Worship filled with joyful praise
Observing the law and fearing God
questions.explanation: God states that His people honor Him with their lips, but their hearts are far from Him; their worship of Him is based on human rules.

questions.question: How will God respond to the people's insincere worship?
options: He will give them more time to repent
He will do wonderful things, causing the wisdom of the wise to perish and the intelligence of the intelligent to vanish
He will immediately bring judgment and destroy them
He will send more prophets to teach them
questions.explanation: God foretells that He will again do amazing things with this people, shocking and astounding, so that the wisdom of the wise will perish and the intelligence of the intelligent will vanish.

questions.question: What does this passage remind us is most important in our worship and service to God?
options: Outward rituals and rules
Sincerity from the heart and reverence for God
Amount of knowledge and eloquence of speech
Reputation and status before people
questions.explanation: God values genuine worship and love from the heart, not merely outward forms without substance.

en.reflection: Is there any area in your life where you say you love God, but your heart is far from Him?
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, please search my heart and forgive me for times when I honor You with my lips but my heart is far from You. May my worship and obedience be from a sincere heart, truly loving You. Help me, Lord, so that my life may genuinely glorify You. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take a moment today to be still before God, ask Him to illuminate your heart for any insincerity, and confess it to Him.

en.focus: God intends to judge those who are hypocritical and self-righteous, but will graciously grant true wisdom and joy to those who humbly seek Him.

questions.question: The prophet Isaiah condemns those who 'hide their plans deep.' What characterizes their actions?
options: They often seek God's guidance
They believe no one can see or know their deeds
They openly confess their transgressions
They actively proclaim God's law
questions.explanation: The passage indicates these people think, 'Who sees us? Who knows us?' believing their plans are hidden.

questions.question: What metaphor does the passage use to describe the flawed relationship between humans and their Creator?
options: Sheep saying to the shepherd, 'You are not my shepherd'
Trees saying to the gardener, 'You did not plant me'
Pots saying to the potter, 'You did not make me,' or 'He has no understanding'
Children saying to their parents, 'You are not my parents'
questions.explanation: The text depicts created beings presuming over the Creator, like a pot questioning the potter's creative authority and wisdom.

questions.question: What surprising changes does God promise for the future?
options: Lebanon will become a fertile field, and the fertile field will seem like a forest
The deaf will hear, and the blind will see
The humble will increase their joy, and the ruthless will vanish
All of the above
questions.explanation: God promises various changes, including the reversal of geographical landscapes, the restoration of senses, and the overturning of social hierarchies, all of which will come to pass.

questions.question: How does this passage remind us to approach God?
options: We can act by our own wisdom and ability, without divine intervention
Outward piety is sufficient, regardless of the heart's condition
We should humbly acknowledge God's sovereignty and trust in His wisdom and actions
God will ultimately fulfill all our worldly desires
questions.explanation: The passage condemns human pride and self-righteousness, emphasizing that only by humbly trusting God can one receive true wisdom, joy, and salvation.

en.reflection: Is there an area in your life where you've tried to hide your thoughts or actions, thinking God doesn't know? How are you willing to bring it before God today?
reflectionOptions: Trust more deeply in God's omniscience and sovereignty
en.prayer: All-knowing God, thank You for being my Creator and Potter. Forgive me for times when my heart and words don't align, or when I've been self-righteous, trying to hide my sins and intentions. Help me to be humble before You, trusting in Your wisdom and power. May my heart truly turn to You and find joy in You. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Spend a quiet moment today to honestly pour out one of your deepest thoughts or struggles to God.

en.theme: Trust in God, Not in Man
en.focus: When people choose to rely on their own wisdom and strength, they stray from God's path; only by trusting in God can they find true rest and salvation.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 30:1 call the people who refuse to listen to the LORD's counsel?
options: A stubborn people
Rebellious children
Foolish masses
Obstinate priests
questions.explanation: The passage begins by identifying those who refuse to follow God's counsel as 'rebellious children'.

questions.type: Observe whom the people seek help from
questions.question: To seek help, the people chose to go down to Egypt and relied on what?
options: Egypt's chariots and horses
Egypt's wisdom and counsel
Egypt's wealth and allies
Egypt's priests and gods
questions.explanation: The people went down to Egypt to seek Pharaoh's protection and trusted in Egypt's horses and chariots.

questions.type: Understand God's evaluation of the people's actions
questions.question: How does God evaluate the people's act of seeking help from Egypt?
options: It was a wise strategy
It demonstrated trust in God
It would bring shame and disgrace
It was a temporary expedient
questions.explanation: God clearly states that seeking help from Egypt would ultimately bring them shame and disgrace, as Egypt could not help them.

questions.type: Understand God's promise of rest and salvation
questions.question: How does God promise that Israel can find rest and salvation?
options: By gathering more military power
By forming alliances with other nations
By returning, being quiet, and trusting in God
By offering more sacrifices
questions.explanation: God states that in returning and rest they would be saved; in quietness and trust would be their strength.

en.reflection: In which area of your life do you often rely on your own strength or that of others, instead of fully trusting God?
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for teaching me that trusting You is the only way. Please forgive me for often relying on my own limited wisdom and strength instead of fully trusting You. Help me to return, be quiet, and trust in You, so that I may receive the true rest and strength You provide. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Spend five minutes today in quiet reflection before God, meditating on the words 'return, be quiet, and trust,' and express your dependence on Him.

en.theme: Waiting for the Lord, He Will Be Gracious
en.focus: God shows grace to those who wait for Him, guiding them and ultimately bringing complete salvation and restoration.

questions.question: Isaiah 30:18 describes the LORD’s attitude towards His people as what?
options: He is angry
He is hiding Himself
He is waiting to be gracious
He is judging the nations
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that the LORD waits to be gracious to His people, and He will have compassion on them.

questions.question: What does God promise to do for His people when they return?
options: Give them more chariots and horses
No longer hide from them, provide teachers and rain
Allow them to build higher walls
Make them a stronger empire
questions.explanation: God promises that He will no longer hide Himself, their teachers will not be hidden, and He will send rain at the proper time, making the land fruitful.

questions.question: How does this passage prophesy God will deal with Assyria (or opposing forces)?
options: Establish an alliance with Assyria
Let Assyria destroy itself
Prepare a great feast for Assyria
Destroy Assyria with fire and wrath, bringing great celebration
questions.explanation: The passage describes the LORD destroying Assyria with fiery indignation, a sweeping rain, hailstones, and a burning breath, with His glorious arm, which will be accompanied by singing and celebration.

questions.question: What is the primary message this passage conveys about God?
options: God only cares about punishing sin
People must be perfect before God shows grace
God is a God of grace and compassion, actively waiting and desiring to save His people
God's power is insufficient to fully defeat all enemies
questions.explanation: The core message of this passage is that God, out of His grace and compassion, actively waits to be gracious to His people and ultimately brings complete salvation.

en.reflection: In which area do you need to learn to actively wait for the LORD today, trusting in His compassion and grace?
reflectionOptions: Waiting for God to resolve a problem
en.prayer: Lord, thank You for being a God who waits to be gracious and is full of compassion. When I am in trouble or anxious, help me to learn to wait for You. I trust in Your promises that You will provide the grace and guidance needed, and ultimately bring complete salvation. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Choose one area where you are waiting for God's answer today. Spend one minute praying to God, entrusting your waiting and hope to Him.

en.focus: Woe awaits us when we choose to rely on human strength or worldly powers instead of fully trusting God.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 31:1, what did those who went down to Egypt for help rely on?
options: God's power
Egypt's horses and chariots
Their own wisdom
The prophets' predictions
questions.explanation: The text explicitly states that they went down to Egypt for help, relying on its horses and numerous chariots, and strong horsemen.

questions.question: How does God view those who rely on Egypt? What will He do to them?
options: Bless them
Ignore them
Stretch out His hand against them and their helpers
Send prophets to advise them
questions.explanation: God says He “will stretch out His hand against the helpers and against those helped; and they will all fall together.”

questions.question: How does the passage contrast the power of Egyptians and God?
options: Egyptians are wiser than God
Egyptians are men, not God; their horses are flesh, not spirit
Egyptian horses are mightier than God's Spirit
God's power and Egyptian power are comparable
questions.explanation: The passage emphasizes that “the Egyptians are men, not God; their horses are flesh, not spirit,” contrasting this with God's omnipotence.

questions.question: What is the main message of Isaiah 31?
options: With enough effort, all difficulties can be overcome
Seeking human help is more effective than seeking God's help
It is foolish to seek worldly help apart from God; salvation comes only by returning to Him
God only helps those who are completely helpless
questions.explanation: The passage warns Israel against relying on Egypt's military power, urging them instead to return to the Lord, as seeking foreign help apart from God leads to woe.

en.reflection: Is there any area in your life where you are currently relying more on human or worldly strength than on God?
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for being the Almighty God; all my strength and help come from You. Please forgive me for times when I rely on human wisdom or worldly means instead of fully trusting You. Help me today and every day to choose to look to You alone, to return to You, and to seek Your face. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, when a situation arises where you feel tempted to rely on yourself or others, pause and pray silently, “Lord, I rely on You alone.”

en.theme: The Righteous King and His Kingdom
en.focus: God promises a righteous King whose rule will bring peace, integrity, and spiritual insight.

questions.question: How are the king and officials described as ruling at the beginning of the passage?
options: With military might and authority
With righteousness and justice
With power and wealth
With wisdom and strategy
questions.explanation: The passage states that 'a king will reign in righteousness and rulers will rule with justice.'

questions.type: Observe the protection of the king and officials
questions.question: What images are used to describe the protection provided by the king and officials?
options: Like a safe harbour and a high tower
Like a shelter from the wind and a refuge from the storm
Like strong walls and a moat
Like a rich feast and cool springs
questions.explanation: They will be 'like a shelter from the wind and a refuge from the storm, like streams of water in a dry place, like the shade of a great rock in a weary land.'

questions.question: What spiritual changes will happen to the people under righteous rule?
options: The wealthy will become more generous
Their hearts will become harder
Their eyes will no longer be closed, and their ears will listen
They will no longer need prophets or teachers
questions.explanation: 'Then the eyes of those who see will no longer be closed, and the ears of those who hear will listen. The mind of the rash will know and understand, and the stammering tongue will be fluent and clear.' This refers to a restoration of spiritual insight and understanding.

questions.type: Understand the perception of the wicked
questions.question: In the righteous kingdom, how will the perception of the 'fool' and the 'scoundrel' change?
options: They will be seen as role models
Their wicked deeds will be overlooked
The fool will no longer be called noble, nor the scoundrel honourable
They will receive more privileges
questions.explanation: The passage clearly states, 'No longer will the fool be called noble nor the scoundrel be highly respected.'

en.reflection: Today, in what areas do you most long to experience God's righteous rule and spiritual renewal?
reflectionOptions: Ask God for clearer spiritual discernment
Ask God to help me act with more integrity
Ask God for wisdom in my words
en.prayer: Righteous King, thank You for Your promised peace and integrity. Please illuminate my heart today, so my eyes are no longer closed and my ears listen to Your truth. Help me to live righteously and kindly under Your rule. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Spend a few minutes today meditating on Jesus Christ as the righteous King who brings us true peace and insight.

en.theme: Living in God's Righteousness and Peace
en.focus: When God's justice is established, His people will experience lasting peace, security, and abundant blessings.

questions.question: To whom does the prophet Isaiah first address his warning and call?
options: Kings of the nations
Complacent women and carefree daughters
Elders of Jerusalem
All residents of Judah
questions.explanation: The passage begins by specifically addressing the 'complacent women' and 'carefree daughters' to listen to the prophet's words.

questions.question: What event is described as leading to the desolation of the land and the abandonment of the city?
options: Long periods of drought and famine
Invasion and siege by enemy armies
God's judgment coming upon the people
Political corruption and public unrest
questions.explanation: The prophet foretells that 'in a little more than a year,' God's judgment will come, causing vineyards to fail, the land to become desolate, and cities to be abandoned.

questions.question: What transformation will occur when the Spirit is poured out from on high?
options: The people will gain military victory
The wilderness will become a fertile field, and the fertile field will seem like a forest, with righteousness and justice dwelling there
Gentile nations will turn to the Lord
Israel will rebuild a powerful nation
questions.explanation: When the Spirit is poured out, the wilderness will become a fertile field, and the fertile field will seem like a forest, and righteousness and justice will dwell there, bringing peace and security.

questions.question: What beautiful future does this chapter ultimately portray for God's people?
options: They will live within high walls, no longer attacked
They will live in peaceful dwelling places, secure homes, and undisturbed places of rest
They will possess great material wealth
They will become rulers over all nations
questions.explanation: Under the outpouring of the Spirit, God's people will live in peaceful dwelling places, secure homes, and undisturbed places of rest, enjoying the quietness and assurance that comes from righteousness.

en.reflection: In what areas of your life do you currently need God's righteousness and the outpouring of the Holy Spirit to experience deeper peace and security?
reflectionOptions: Uncertainty and worry about the future
en.prayer: Righteous God, thank You for being the God of peace. Please pour out Your Holy Spirit upon me, removing all unrest and chaos from my life. May Your righteousness reign in my heart, enabling me to dwell in peaceful habitations, trusting securely in You. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take one minute today to be still, invite the Holy Spirit to fill your heart, and pray about an area of unrest in your life.

en.focus: In times of extreme distress, God is our salvation and strength, and His justice and faithfulness never change.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 33:1, what will be the outcome for those who deal treacherously and destroy?
options: They will gain more wealth and power
They will eventually be punished by God and suffer the consequences
They will receive God's forgiveness and mercy
They will never face retribution
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that those who deal treacherously and destroy will themselves be dealt with treacherously and destroyed.

questions.question: In their deep distress, what do the people ask of God?
options: For God to bring more calamities upon their enemies
For God to make them richer and stronger
For God to be gracious, their arm every morning, and their salvation in times of trouble
For God to help them reconcile with their enemies
questions.explanation: The people cry out to God for grace, asking Him to be their arm every morning and their salvation in times of trouble.

questions.question: What happens when God rises to act and bring salvation?
options: All nations will become stronger
The nations will flee, and the spoil will be gathered
The nations will become more arrogant
All nations will turn to Israel
questions.explanation: When God rises, the nations scatter, and His people are gathered, like locusts swarming.

questions.question: Based on these verses, how is God described?
options: A distant God who does not intervene in worldly affairs
A God who cares only for a select few
A God who is exalted and fills Zion with justice and righteousness
A fickle God who does not keep His promises
questions.explanation: God is described as exalted, filling Zion (Jerusalem) with justice and righteousness, and He is the stability of the times, a rich store of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge; the fear of the LORD is His treasure.

en.reflection: In which area do you most need God to rise up and be your salvation and strength today?
en.prayer: Lord, my God, when I feel trapped or face difficulties, please be gracious to me. Be my arm every morning and my salvation in times of trouble. Rise up in my life and display Your justice and faithfulness. Help me to fear You and trust in Your wisdom and knowledge. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Spend one minute quietly reflecting and entrusting your current difficulties or challenges to God, believing that He is your salvation and strength.

en.focus: Those who trust in God will experience His presence, protection, and abundant provision, while the wicked will face His consuming fire.

questions.question: To whom does God call out at the beginning of the passage?
options: Those who are far off
Those who are near
All sinners
Those who fear the LORD
questions.explanation: God first calls out to 'those who are near,' so they may acknowledge His power.

questions.question: How does the passage contrast those who fear God with the wicked?
options: The wicked will prosper, the righteous will suffer
The wicked face fire, the righteous dwell on high
The wicked are exalted, the righteous are humbled
The wicked gain wealth, the righteous suffer poverty
questions.explanation: The passage states that the wicked will face 'devouring fire' and 'everlasting burning,' while those who walk righteously 'will dwell on the heights.'

questions.question: What do the 'King in His beauty' and 'a land that stretches afar' in verse 17 symbolize?
options: Earthly rulers and empires
God's glorious reign and the rich inheritance He gives His people
Invading enemies and their territories
Israel's wealth and influence
questions.explanation: This describes God's own glorious reign and the peace and abundance He will grant His people, hinting at the hope of the Messiah's kingdom.

questions.question: How does the passage describe God's presence and protection, especially for 'Zion'?
options: Zion will have a mighty army and strong walls
Zion will be an immovable tent, with the LORD as her rivers
Zion will receive tribute and protection from other nations
Zion will experience sickness and poverty, but eventually be saved
questions.explanation: The passage uses images of an 'immovable tent,' 'pegs never pulled up,' and 'cords never broken' to illustrate Zion's stability, and emphasizes that the LORD will be her 'place of broad rivers and streams,' providing protection and abundance.

en.reflection: In which area of your life do you most long to experience God's glorious presence and steadfast protection?
en.prayer: Almighty Father, thank You that You are my King and my Protector. Help me to trust You more deeply today and to live righteously, so I may dwell in Your presence and experience the peace and abundance You provide. May my life glorify Your name. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Pray specifically about one thing causing you worry today, asking God to reveal His presence and protection.

en.focus: God's righteous judgment will come upon all nations, yet He also gives an everlasting promise to His people.

questions.question: Who does the prophet Isaiah call to listen to the LORD's proclamation?
options: The elders of Israel
The kings of Judah
All nations and their inhabitants
All the stars of heaven
questions.explanation: The passage begins by calling on all nations and the people of the earth to pay attention to the LORD's declaration.

questions.question: Upon whom is the LORD's indignation and judgment primarily directed?
options: All His trusting people
All worshippers of foreign idols
All nations and their armies
All inhabitants of Zion
questions.explanation: The LORD's indignation is against all the nations, and His wrath is against all their armies.

questions.question: How is Edom described as it undergoes judgment?
options: It will become more fruitful and fertile
It will become a dwelling place of peace and tranquility
It will become a desolate wasteland, inhabited by wild animals
It will become a center of worship for all nations
questions.explanation: The passage describes Edom becoming a desolate waste, inhabited by thorns, thistles, and various wild animals, never to be traversed again.

questions.question: What is the primary message this passage conveys to us?
options: God only cares about the welfare of Israel, not other nations
People can escape God's judgment by their own strength
God is the sovereign ruler of all nations; His righteous judgment will be fulfilled, and He is faithful to His covenant
Historical events happen randomly and are unrelated to God
questions.explanation: This passage emphasizes God as the judge of all the earth, whose righteous judgment will be fulfilled, and His judgment on Edom signifies His faithfulness in accomplishing His promises and plans.

en.reflection: This passage reminds us of God's justice and sovereignty. In what area of your life today do you most need to trust in God's rule and justice?
reflectionOptions: When feeling offended in a relationship
en.prayer: Almighty Father, You are the sovereign ruler over all nations, and Your righteous judgment will surely come to pass. Please help me to always live with a heart of reverence, trusting in Your faithfulness and promises. May I see Your hand in all things and submit to Your will. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, spend one minute meditating on the phrase, “The eye of the LORD searches, and His Spirit gathers them,” reminding yourself that God is sovereign and knows all.

en.focus: God will transform the desolate wilderness into a paradise, bringing His salvation and glory to His people.

questions.question: Which places does the prophet Isaiah describe as rejoicing and blossoming?
options: Cities and villages
The wilderness and the dry land
Mountains and seas
Gardens and forests
questions.explanation: The passage begins by stating that 'the wilderness and the dry land shall be glad' and 'the desert shall rejoice.'

questions.question: What physical disabilities are described as being healed when the glory of the Lord is revealed?
options: Poverty and hunger
Ignorance and foolishness
Blindness, deafness, lameness, and muteness
Sickness and old age
questions.explanation: The text clearly states, 'Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf unstopped; then shall the lame man leap like a deer, and the tongue of the mute sing for joy.'

questions.question: For whom is the 'Holy Way' prepared?
options: All foreign nations
Political leaders
The redeemed of the Lord
Wealthy merchants
questions.explanation: The passage states that this Holy Way is 'for them' and specifically refers to 'the redeemed of the LORD.'

questions.question: What message does Isaiah 35 convey to those feeling hopeless and distressed?
options: People must try harder to escape their troubles on their own
God's redemption and grace will bring complete transformation, joy, and rest
Only a select few will experience God's salvation
Suffering will never end
questions.explanation: The entire chapter emphasizes God's direct intervention to transform desolation into paradise, heal disabilities, and bring joy and everlasting rest—all manifestations of His redemptive power.

en.reflection: What 'wilderness' or 'dry land' situations in your life today are you willing to surrender to God, trusting that He can bring transformation and joy?
reflectionOptions: Uncertainty or anxiety about the future
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for being the God who can turn a wilderness into a paradise. When my life feels dry and desolate, please fill me with Your glory and salvation. Help me trust in Your mighty power, to rejoice even in difficult circumstances, and to await Your complete fulfillment. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take a moment today to pray about one 'wilderness' situation in your life, asking God to intervene and bring change and hope.

en.theme: Trusting God in Times of Threat
en.focus: When facing overwhelming threats and ridicule, do we rely on human strength or solely on the Almighty God?

questions.question: Who did King Sennacherib of Assyria send to Jerusalem to deliver his message to King Hezekiah?
options: A prophet
A military commander
A diplomat
A scribe
questions.explanation: King Sennacherib of Assyria sent the Rabshakeh, a military commander, with a large army to Jerusalem.

questions.question: How did the Rabshakeh attempt to demoralize the people of Jerusalem?
options: By promising them wealth
By demonstrating the power of siege engines
By ridiculing their trust in God and intimidating them
By inviting them to peaceful negotiations
questions.explanation: The Rabshakeh loudly addressed the people on the wall in Hebrew, ridiculing their trust and resistance as futile, and intimidating them.

questions.question: When the Rabshakeh spoke in Hebrew to the people on the wall, what did Hezekiah's officials ask him to do?
options: Stop speaking
Speak to them in Aramaic
Speak directly to King Hezekiah
Offer terms of peace
questions.explanation: Hezekiah's officials asked the Rabshakeh to speak to them in Aramaic so that the people on the wall, who did not understand that language, would not be intimidated.

questions.question: How does this chapter illustrate the challenge of trusting God amidst severe threats?
options: It encourages reliance on Egyptian help
It emphasizes that only human wisdom can solve problems against powerful enemies
It reveals how the enemy attempts to undermine faith in God and force submission
It shows that a large enough army can overcome any foe
questions.explanation: The Rabshakeh repeatedly mocked the people's trust in the Lord and tried to convince them that God could not save them, thereby undermining their faith.

en.reflection: What 'Assyrian' threats or challenges are you currently facing that make you feel weak or afraid?
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for being my refuge and strength. When facing great challenges in life and inner fears, please help me to look to You alone and not be swayed by the enemy's lies and intimidation. May I, like Hezekiah, entrust everything to You. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, take a minute to be still, express your deepest fears to God, and ask Him to strengthen your faith.

en.focus: When facing overwhelming challenges, our true hope lies in turning to God and trusting in His power and faithfulness.

questions.question: What was King Hezekiah's first action after hearing the threatening words from Rabshakeh, the Assyrian king's envoy?
options: He gathered his army for battle
He sent envoys to seek peace with the Assyrian king
He tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and entered the house of the LORD
He consulted his advisors for strategies
questions.explanation: Hezekiah's immediate response to the Assyrian threat was to humble himself and seek God.

questions.question: What did the messengers sent by King Hezekiah say to the prophet Isaiah?
options: They asked Isaiah to gather the army
They asked Isaiah to pray for the remnant that was left
They asked Isaiah when the Assyrian king would withdraw
They asked Isaiah to prophesy about Israel's future
questions.explanation: King Hezekiah sent messengers to Isaiah asking him to offer a prayer for the nation's distress and the surviving remnant.

questions.question: When King Hezekiah prayed to the LORD, what attributes of God did he emphasize?
options: God's justice and judgment
God's mercy and kindness
God's greatness, uniqueness, and sovereignty
God's wisdom and counsel
questions.explanation: In his prayer, King Hezekiah highlighted that the LORD is the only true God, the Creator of heaven and earth, and the ruler of all kingdoms.

questions.question: What important lesson can we learn from King Hezekiah's actions in the face of the Assyrian threat?
options: In times of trouble, human strength and strategies are most important
Seeking God and His servants is secondary
Even in desperate situations, we should turn to God and trust in His deliverance
God only helps those who have never made mistakes
questions.explanation: Facing an immense threat, Hezekiah did not rely on his own strength but humbly sought God, trusting in His deliverance.

en.reflection: What are the 'Assyrian kings'—the seemingly insurmountable difficulties or challenges—you are facing in your life right now? How will you bring them before God?
en.prayer: Almighty LORD God, I know that You are the only true God, sovereign over heaven and earth. When my heart is overwhelmed with troubles and fear, help me to turn to You and humbly cast my burdens upon You. I trust in Your power to intervene and make a way for me. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, take one minute to quietly reflect on your greatest worry, then, like King Hezekiah, surrender it completely to God in prayer.

en.focus: God keeps His promises, protects His people, and defeats those who defy Him.

questions.question: What message did the prophet Isaiah bring to King Hezekiah from the LORD?
options: The LORD would punish King Hezekiah
The LORD had abandoned Judah
The LORD had heard the arrogant words of the king of Assyria
The LORD wanted King Hezekiah to surrender to Assyria
questions.explanation: The LORD, through Isaiah, informed Hezekiah that He had heard the blasphemous and arrogant words spoken by Sennacherib, king of Assyria, against Him.

questions.type: Observe God's response to the Assyrian king
questions.question: How did the LORD describe what He would do to King Sennacherib of Assyria?
options: Allow him to continue conquering nations
Grant him a triumphant return
Make him return by the way he came, putting a hook in his nose
Make him an ally of Judah
questions.explanation: The LORD declared that He would put His hook in Sennacherib's nose and His bit in his mouth, making him return by the way he came, and ultimately he would be struck down by the sword.

questions.type: Understand the reason for God's deliverance
questions.question: What was the reason the LORD gave for saving Jerusalem?
options: Because Jerusalem's walls were strong
Because of King Hezekiah's and the people's prayers
For His own sake and for the sake of His servant David
Because the Assyrian army was exhausted
questions.explanation: The LORD clearly stated that He would save Jerusalem for His own sake and for the sake of His servant David, not due to any human merit.

questions.question: What important lesson about God's sovereignty can we learn from this passage?
options: God only cares about the powerful
God's power is limited by human capabilities
God is in complete control of history, even over powerful enemies
God only acts in times of extreme emergency
questions.explanation: This passage vividly demonstrates God's absolute control over the Assyrian king and his army, as He mocks Assyria's arrogance and carries out His deliverance according to His own timing and will, proving His supreme sovereignty.

en.reflection: How does this passage encourage you to trust God when facing challenges and seemingly insurmountable difficulties in your life?
reflectionOptions: It reminds me that God is in control
It motivates me to cry out to God in prayer
It helps me see God's faithfulness
en.prayer: Almighty LORD, You are the God who hears prayers and controls all things. Help me, when facing difficulties and challenges, not to look at the power of my circumstances but to simply look to Your promises and Your mighty power. May my heart find comfort and hope in Your faithfulness. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, when a worry or challenge arises, meditate on God's declaration to the king of Assyria: 'I will put my hook in your nose and my bit in your mouth, and I will turn you back by the way you came.' (Isaiah 37:29), and quietly surrender it to God.

en.theme: God Hears Prayer and Reverses Despair
en.focus: Even in seemingly hopeless situations, God hears prayer and acts according to His will to save and heal.

questions.question: What message did the prophet Isaiah convey to King Hezekiah when he was ill?
options: God would grant him a longer life
He would die from his illness and not recover
He would make a full recovery and suffer no more
He would face a major battle
questions.explanation: Isaiah clearly told Hezekiah that he was going to die and would not live.

questions.question: What was Hezekiah's immediate reaction upon hearing the news of his impending death?
options: Angrily rebuked Isaiah
Turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD
Immediately gathered his officials for advice
Accepted his fate and prepared for his death
questions.explanation: Upon hearing the news, King Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and wept bitterly, praying to the LORD.

questions.question: How did God respond to Hezekiah's prayer?
options: God decided not to change His will
God extended his life and healed him
God told him his prayer was too late
God sent an angel to take his life
questions.explanation: God, through Isaiah, told Hezekiah that He had heard his prayer, seen his tears, and would add fifteen years to his life and heal him.

questions.question: What lesson about prayer can we learn from Hezekiah's experience?
options: Prayer can only change minor things, not predestined fate
If we pray, God will always grant our wishes
Even when facing seemingly unchangeable difficulties, we should call out to God in faith
Only the prayers of the righteous are heard by God
questions.explanation: Hezekiah's experience shows that even in seemingly desperate situations, sincere prayer can be heard by God and bring about unexpected turns according to His will.

en.reflection: Is there a seemingly hopeless situation in your life right now that you need to turn to God in earnest prayer, just like Hezekiah?
reflectionOptions: A physical illness or health concern
en.prayer: Heavenly Father, thank You for being a God who hears prayers. Please help me not to lose heart in the face of life's desperate situations, but to humbly turn to You and pour out my heart, just like Hezekiah. I believe Your mercy and power are far beyond my imagination. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, pray for the one thing you feel most helpless about right now. Surrender it completely to God, trusting that He will respond according to His love and will.

en.theme: A Revealed Heart and Coming Judgment
en.focus: King Hezekiah's pride revealed his inner weakness and foreshadowed the judgment Judah would face.

questions.question: What was the main reason for the king of Babylon sending envoys to Hezekiah?
options: Babylon wanted to form an alliance with Judah against Assyria
The king of Babylon heard Hezekiah had recovered from his illness and sent gifts
Babylon hoped Hezekiah could help them build the temple
Babylon wanted to understand Judah's military strength
questions.explanation: The text states that the king of Babylon heard Hezekiah had recovered from his illness and sent him gifts.

questions.question: What did Hezekiah show the Babylonian envoys?
options: All his gold, silver, treasures, armory, and everything he possessed
His newly built temple and the priests' garments
The tablets of the covenant and the book of the Law he received from God
The miraculous healing he received from God
questions.explanation: Hezekiah showed them all the silver, gold, spices, precious oil, his entire armory, and everything found in his treasuries.

questions.question: What prophecy did Isaiah the prophet give concerning Hezekiah's actions?
options: Babylon would live peacefully with Judah
Judah would be blessed because of Hezekiah's wisdom
All of Judah's treasures and descendants would be carried away to Babylon
Hezekiah would become an ally of Babylon
questions.explanation: Isaiah prophesied that all the treasures Hezekiah displayed, and his descendants, would be carried off to Babylon and become eunuchs.

questions.question: What attitude did Hezekiah's response to Isaiah's prophecy reveal?
options: He immediately repented and sought God's forgiveness
He was only concerned that there would be peace and security in his lifetime
He angrily refuted Isaiah's prophecy
He planned to organize an army to resist the Babylonian invasion
questions.explanation: Hezekiah responded, saying, “The word of the LORD that you have spoken is good! For there will be peace and security in my days.” This shows his immediate concern for personal comfort.

en.reflection: Today, what 'treasures' in your life are you tempted to display to others, rather than solely giving glory to God?
en.prayer: Dear Lord, help me to examine my heart and not allow pride to blind my eyes. May everything I possess be used solely to glorify You, and not to show off myself. Grant me a humble heart, so that every choice in my life prioritizes Your will. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, deliberately refrain from mentioning one of your achievements or a valuable possession, and instead thank God for it.

en.focus: God declares comfort and forgiveness to His people, promising His glory will be revealed.

questions.question: What does God say to His people at the beginning of the passage?
options: He will punish them even more deeply
He wants them to wait longer
He will comfort them
He wants them to repent of all sins
questions.explanation: God commands the prophet to speak tenderly to Jerusalem, declaring that her hard service is ended and her iniquity is pardoned.

questions.question: How is God's power and might described in the passage?
options: He is the Creator of all things, with infinite power
He is a warrior who defeats all enemies
He is a Shepherd who gently guides His flock
He is a Judge who punishes the wicked
questions.explanation: The passage describes God as one who comes with power, yet also gently shepherds His flock.

questions.question: What is the core hope this passage offers to God's people?
options: They can achieve wealth through hard work
They can rebuild their homes by themselves
God's forgiveness and the revelation of His glory, along with His presence and care
Foreign nations will never attack them again
questions.explanation: The core hope is that God will pardon their iniquity, His glory will be revealed, and He will personally care for them like a shepherd.

questions.question: How does this passage comfort you today, especially when you feel weary or powerless?
options: It reminds me of the brevity and emptiness of human life
It lets me know that God will eventually punish all injustice
It shows me that God's mighty arm will always sustain me, and He will gently lead me
It encourages me to rely on my own strength to overcome difficulties
questions.explanation: The passage portrays God's power and His tender care for His people, which is the greatest source of comfort and strength when we feel weary or powerless.

en.reflection: In which areas of your life do you currently need God's comfort and tender shepherding?
en.prayer: Loving Lord, thank You for being the God of comfort, who speaks encouraging words to me. When I feel weary or lost, please uphold me with Your mighty arm and shepherd me with Your tenderness. May Your glory be revealed in my life. In Jesus' name, I pray, Amen.
en.action: Spend one minute reflecting on how God gently shepherds His flock as described in Isaiah 40:11, then commit one burden that needs His care to Him.

en.focus: The LORD's wisdom, power, and care surpass everything, making Him our sole reliance and strength.

questions.question: At the beginning of Isaiah 40:12, what does the prophet use to emphasize God's greatness?
options: He created the heavens and the earth
He measured the waters in the hollow of His hand and marked off the heavens with His fingers
He appointed kings and priests
He reduced all nations to dust
questions.explanation: The passage begins by emphasizing that God measured the waters in the hollow of His hand and marked off the heavens with His fingers, demonstrating His control over the universe.

questions.question: What are the nations compared to before God?
options: Fish in the sea
A drop in a bucket and dust on the scales
Wild animals in the forest
Flowers of the field
questions.explanation: Before God, the nations are merely a drop in a bucket and dust on the scales, showing how great God is and how small humanity is.

questions.question: When the passage says, 'He gives strength to the weary and increases the power of the weak,' what is it primarily telling us?
options: We won't be weary if we work hard enough
God only helps those who are physically healthy
God sustains those who rely on Him, granting them strength in their weakness
Weariness and weakness are unavoidable and must simply be endured
questions.explanation: This verse encourages us that even when we feel weary and weak, if we wait upon the LORD, He will renew our strength.

questions.question: How does this passage encourage us in the face of life's difficulties and challenges?
options: It encourages us to overcome them by our own strength
It reminds us that God is almighty and gives strength to those who wait for Him
It teaches us to ignore difficulties and pretend they don't exist
It suggests seeking human help rather than God's help
questions.explanation: The passage emphasizes that God is eternal and all-powerful; He does not grow weary or tired, and He gives strength to those who wait for Him.

en.reflection: What aspect of your life today makes you feel weary or powerless? How are you willing to surrender it to the almighty God?
en.prayer: Eternal Father, You are the Creator, sovereign over all, and the God who gives strength to the weary. I confess my weakness and limitations. When I feel powerless, renew my strength, that I may soar on wings like eagles. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take one minute today to look up at the sky and reflect on God's infinite greatness and His boundless care for you.

en.theme: Do Not Fear, For I Am With You
en.focus: God reminds His people that He is their Creator and Helper, and therefore they have no need to fear.

questions.question: Who does God call to listen to Him at the beginning of the passage?
options: Islands
Nations
Israel
All the earth
questions.explanation: At the beginning, God calls the 'coastlands' and 'peoples' to be silent before Him and prepare to hear His words.

questions.question: How does God address Israel to emphasize their special relationship with Him?
options: My servant, My chosen one
My warrior, My anointed one
My vine, My planted one
My people, My rescued one
questions.explanation: God calls Israel 'My servant Jacob, whom I have chosen,' emphasizing His special covenant relationship with them.

questions.question: What does God assure the people of Israel so they do not need to fear?
options: They will become the most powerful nation
They will have unlimited wealth and resources
God will be with them, help them, and uphold them
All their enemies will immediately vanish
questions.explanation: God promises, 'Do not fear, for I am with you; do not be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you and help you; I will uphold you with My righteous right hand.' This is the fundamental reason they do not need to fear.

questions.question: How does this passage encourage you today when facing challenges and uncertainties?
options: It reminds me to rely on my own strength and wisdom
It makes me believe God is only with me when things are going well
It gives me confidence that God Himself will uphold and help me
It encourages me to avoid difficulties and wait for problems to disappear
questions.explanation: This passage clearly tells us that even in challenges, God promises His presence, strength, help, and upholding, which is the source of our faith.

en.reflection: In which area of your life do you most need God’s presence and help today to overcome fear?
en.prayer: Faithful Lord, thank You for reminding me that I am Your servant, Your chosen one. Facing the challenges and uncertainties of life, please help me to lay aside fear, for You promise to be with me. May I fully trust in Your strength, help, and upholding. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, specifically pray about one thing that causes you anxiety or fear, declaring, 'Lord, I will not fear, for You are with me.'

en.focus: Only the true God can accurately foretell the future, revealing His reality and power through prophecy.

questions.question: What does God challenge the idols of the nations to do to prove their divinity?
options: Perform miracles and wonders
Predict the future and make it happen
Grant wealth and authority
Defeat Israel's enemies
questions.explanation: God challenges the idols to 'declare to us what is to come' and 'declare to us the former things' to prove their divine nature.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the idols that cannot foretell and those who worship them?
options: As detestable to God
As nothing, and their works as empty and worthless
As bringing disaster
As temporarily useful
questions.explanation: The passage clearly states that idols and their worshippers are 'nothing,' and their deeds are 'empty and worthless,' possessing no power.

questions.question: What does God mean in verse 27 when He says, 'I was the first to say to Zion'?
options: God favors the people of Zion
God only speaks to the people of Zion
God first reveals His will and plans to His people
God does not care about Gentiles
questions.explanation: God specifically emphasizes that He declared things first to His people, Zion, showing His care and priority in revelation to them.

questions.question: How does this passage encourage us to trust in God?
options: God will meet all our material needs
God is the true God who controls all, knows the future, and accomplishes His will
God will bless us if we work hard
God will prevent all bad things from happening
questions.explanation: This passage highlights God's ability to foretell the future and bring it to pass, proving He is the one true God, encouraging us to fully trust in His sovereignty.

en.reflection: In your life today, what uncertainties or worries do you have that need the reminder that only God holds the future?
reflectionOptions: The future of my family members
en.prayer: Almighty Father, thank You that You are the true God who governs history, foretells the future, and brings it to pass. Please help me to trust solely in Your omniscience and omnipotence amidst all uncertainties. May my heart find peace in You. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Spend a few minutes today meditating on a scripture that reminds you of God's sovereignty and that His plans will never fail.

en.focus: God chooses and equips His Servant, empowering Him with His Spirit to bring justice, hope, and salvation to the nations.

questions.question: How does God describe His chosen Servant at the beginning of the passage?
options: He in whom my soul delights, and on whom my Spirit rests
He whom I value, possessing great authority
He whom I trust, having infinite wisdom
He whom I love, endowed with extraordinary gifts
questions.explanation: The passage clearly states that the Servant is upheld, chosen, and delighted in by God, and God's Spirit is upon Him.

questions.question: How will this Servant bring justice to the nations?
options: By crying out loudly and making His voice heard in the streets
By breaking a bruised reed and quenching a dimly burning wick
By not crying out or raising His voice, or making it heard in the streets
By conquering nations with force and power
questions.explanation: The Servant acts gently, without crying out, raising His voice, or making it heard in the streets, showing a compassionate and quiet approach.

questions.question: What does God promise the Servant will bring?
options: The establishment of a new empire
Becoming the king of all nations
A light for the Gentiles, opening blind eyes, and freeing prisoners
Great wealth and glory to Israel
questions.explanation: God promises the Servant will be a light to the Gentiles, open the eyes of the blind, and free those in prison, bringing salvation and liberty.

questions.question: Why does God repeatedly emphasize, 'I am the LORD; that is My name'?
options: To remind people that He is the one true God and does not share His glory with idols
To warn nations that He will bring judgment
To show that He is the sovereign ruler of all, omnipotent
To encourage people to believe that His prophecies will come true
questions.explanation: God emphasizes His name, the LORD, and that He will not give His glory to idols, declaring His uniqueness and supreme sovereignty.

en.reflection: How does today's passage help you understand more deeply the character and work of Jesus Christ, the perfect Servant?
reflectionOptions: The salvation He brings to all nations
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for sending Your Servant, the Lord Jesus Christ, who fulfilled Your justice with gentleness and compassion, and became a light for all peoples. Help me to imitate His example, that I too may gently manifest Your love and truth in my life. In Jesus' name, I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, express Christ's love to someone around you through a gentle action or word.

en.theme: God's Call to a Rebellious People
en.focus: Even when His people are deaf and blind to His truth, God still calls them to return, demonstrating His righteousness and power.

questions.question: How does God describe His people in the passage?
options: Blind servants
Deaf messengers
Blind and deaf
Stiff-necked
questions.explanation: The passage repeatedly emphasizes that the people are 'blind' and 'deaf,' despite being God's servants and messengers.

questions.question: Why did God allow His people to be plundered and taken captive?
options: Because God was powerless to protect them
To punish their sin and disobedience
To let them experience the strength of other nations
To test their faith
questions.explanation: The text clearly states that it was because the people would not follow God's ways and disregarded His instruction that He gave them over to their enemies.

questions.question: Despite their rebellion, what does God still reveal to His people?
options: His righteousness and the greatness of His law
His wrath and unchangeable judgment
His disappointment and helplessness
His favoritism towards other nations
questions.explanation: The text says God was 'pleased, for his righteousness’ sake, to make his law great and glorious,' even in judgment, demonstrating His justice and the honor of His law.

questions.question: What does this passage remind us is most important before God?
options: Having wealth and power
Observing all religious rituals
Humbly listening and obeying God’s word
Actively participating in social activities
questions.explanation: God repeatedly rebukes His people for being 'deaf' and 'blind,' implying that what He values most is their obedience and responsiveness to His word.

en.reflection: In what ways might I be like the 'deaf and blind' people today, not truly listening to God's word?
reflectionOptions: Turning a blind eye to certain sins
en.prayer: Lord, open my ears to hear Your voice and open my eyes to see Your works and Your will. Forgive me for times when I am like the 'deaf and blind' people. Help me to humbly obey Your word. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Spend five minutes in quiet today, asking God to reveal areas in your life where you need to listen more acutely to His word.

en.focus: Even in the deepest fears and difficulties, God declares that He is our Creator, Redeemer, and is always with us to deliver us.

questions.question: How does God address His people at the beginning of the passage?
options: My servant
My chosen one
My Israel
Jacob and Israel
questions.explanation: God directly calls out Jacob and Israel by name, emphasizing His personal relationship with them.

questions.question: What does God promise will happen when His people pass through waters and fire?
options: They will not feel any pain
The waters and fire will completely disappear
God will be with them, and the waters will not engulf them, nor will the fire burn them
They will learn valuable lessons from the experience
questions.explanation: God promises that His presence will protect them, so the waters will not engulf them and the fire will not burn them.

questions.question: What identity of God is repeatedly emphasized in this passage?
options: The almighty Judge
The only Saviour and God
The wise Teacher
The Creator of the universe
questions.explanation: The passage repeatedly emphasizes God as 'your Holy One, the Creator of Israel, your King,' and states 'apart from me there is no savior' and 'I am God.'

questions.question: How does this passage help us face fears and uncertainties in life?
options: It tells us fear is normal, but we must overcome it on our own
It reminds us that God is greater than any difficulty, and He is always with us to deliver us
It encourages us to seek help from others instead of facing things alone
It suggests that God will protect us if we do enough good deeds
questions.explanation: The core message is that God is greater than all difficulties; He is our Creator and Redeemer, promising His presence and deliverance in all circumstances.

en.reflection: In which difficulty do you most need God to remind you of His presence and deliverance today?
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for being my Creator and Redeemer. When I feel afraid or face difficulties, please remind me that You are always with me, and the waters will not engulf me, nor will the fire burn me. Help me to trust You alone, for You are my God, and there is no savior besides You. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Find a quiet moment to silently repeat and meditate on: “Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have summoned you by name; you are mine.” (Isaiah 43:1)

en.focus: God reminds His people that He is the Lord of history and the sole Redeemer, promising to pour out His Spirit.

questions.question: How does God refer to Himself in this passage to emphasize His uniqueness?
options: The Holy One of Israel, your Redeemer
The LORD of hosts, Creator of heaven and earth
The Most High, the Almighty Judge
The Eternal God, King over all
questions.explanation: God repeatedly calls Himself 'the Holy One of Israel, your Redeemer,' emphasizing His special relationship with Israel and His power to save.

questions.question: What wondrous past and present deeds of God are mentioned in this passage?
options: Drying up the sea, making a way through the waters
Sending manna from heaven, bringing water from a rock
Giving the Law, establishing the Temple
Raising up kings, overthrowing empires
questions.explanation: God reminds His people that He once dried up the sea and made a way through the waters to lead them out of distress.

questions.question: Upon whom does God promise to pour out His Spirit?
options: Prophets and priests
All who believe in Him
The descendants of Israel and their offspring
Kings and rulers of the nations
questions.explanation: God promises to pour out His Spirit on the descendants of Israel and their offspring, bringing them blessings.

questions.question: How does this passage encourage us when facing life's challenges and difficulties?
options: By working hard, we can overcome all difficulties
By trusting that God is the only Redeemer who will make a way
By relying on our own wisdom and abilities to solve problems
By seeking human help and advice instead of solely relying on God
