en.prayer: Loving Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding me through Jeremiah's courage that You are a righteous God, yet also full of mercy. Help me to have a humble and teachable heart, willing to listen to Your words. When I stray from You, enlighten me so that I may repent in time and return to You, so that my life may receive forgiveness and renewal. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take some quiet time today to reflect if there is anything you need to confess and repent of to God. If so, pray to Him with sincerity.

en.theme: Submit to the LORD, Find Peace
en.focus: God calls His people and the nations to submit to His sovereignty, even if it means accepting temporary hardship, as this is the path to true peace.

questions.question: What did Jeremiah use, by the LORD's command, to symbolize the nations serving the king of Babylon?
options: A golden crown
An iron scepter
Yokes and straps
A torn garment
questions.explanation: The LORD commanded Jeremiah to make yokes and straps and put them on his own neck, symbolizing that the nations would serve Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon.

questions.question: How does the LORD declare His sovereignty over the nations and the king of Babylon?
options: He is the Creator and controls all things
He is the only true God, all others are idols
He is a loving Father who cares for His people
He is a righteous Judge who punishes sin
questions.explanation: The LORD states that He is the one who made the earth, people, and animals, and therefore has the right to give it to whomever He pleases, including making the nations serve the king of Babylon.

questions.question: How did the message of the prophets and priests differ from Jeremiah's message?
options: They encouraged rebellion against Babylon, while Jeremiah urged submission
They predicted peace and prosperity, while Jeremiah predicted destruction
They emphasized the importance of the Law, while Jeremiah emphasized grace
They called for repentance, while Jeremiah called for sacrifice
questions.explanation: The false prophets and priests urged the people not to serve the king of Babylon and predicted the swift return of the temple articles. Jeremiah, however, advised them to submit to avoid perishing by sword, famine, and plague.

questions.question: What does this passage remind us about submitting to God's sovereignty today?
options: God will immediately change circumstances we dislike if we pray enough
Even in difficult situations, submitting to God's will is the path to blessing
We can choose to submit to God only in matters we prefer
God's sovereignty applies only to church matters, not national affairs
questions.explanation: The passage clearly shows that even when facing the seemingly humiliating rule of Babylon, submission to God (accepting this reality) was the only way to survive. This reminds us that in any circumstance, submitting to God's sovereignty and will, even if it means temporary hardship, is the ultimate path to peace and blessing.

en.reflection: In what area of your life might God be calling you to lay down your own will and submit to His today?
reflectionOptions: Forgiving someone who has wronged you
Letting go of a personal plan
en.prayer: Almighty Creator, I acknowledge that You are the sovereign Lord over all. Help me to lay down my own will and desire for control, and learn to submit to Your purposes in every area of my life. Grant me wisdom to discern Your path and courage and faith to follow it. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, pray about one thing you find most difficult to submit to God, asking Him for a submissive heart.

en.focus: A true prophet's message, even if unpleasant, is faithful to God's word; a false prophet's message caters to human desires, offering false peace.

questions.question: What did Hananiah declare in the presence of Jeremiah the prophet?
options: He prophesied that Judah would prosper forever
He declared that the yoke of Babylon had been broken
He warned that Jerusalem would be destroyed
He called the people to repentance towards God
questions.explanation: Hananiah publicly declared before the priests and all the people that God had broken the yoke of the king of Babylon.

questions.question: What was Jeremiah's initial reaction to Hananiah's prophecy?
options: He immediately rebuked Hananiah as a false prophet
He agreed and wished for the prophecy to come true
He remained silent and said nothing
He asked God to immediately punish Hananiah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah responded with “Amen! May the Lord do so,” expressing his hope that Hananiah’s prophecy would be fulfilled, as it would be good news for the people.

questions.question: What key standard did Jeremiah identify for distinguishing between true and false prophets?
options: The volume of their voice
Their popularity among the people
Whether their prophecies of peace and prosperity came true
Whether they wore elaborate clothing
questions.explanation: Jeremiah stated that if a prophet prophesies peace, only when that prophecy comes true will it be known that the Lord has truly sent him.

questions.question: What main truth does this chapter teach us about God's word?
options: God's word always brings immediate peace and comfort
God's word sometimes brings difficult truths but ultimately fulfills His purposes
God's word can be arbitrarily changed by any prophet
God's word is only delivered through respected leaders
questions.explanation: Jeremiah's message from God was difficult, involving captivity and suffering, but ultimately God would break the yoke of Babylon and fulfill His purposes. Hananiah's 'peaceful' message, though pleasant, was false.

en.reflection: In what areas today do you need to be careful not to be misled by messages that sound appealing but do not align with biblical truth?
reflectionOptions: Having unrealistic expectations for the future
Avoiding facing personal issues in my life
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for Your word of truth that helps me discern right from wrong. Open my eyes to hear and accept Your truth, which may sometimes be difficult but is always full of grace. Help me to reject messages that cater to my desires and offer false peace. May I always be faithful to Your holy word. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Read Proverbs 14:12 and reflect on whether you sometimes choose what you think is right, but actually deviates from God's path, seeking 'peace' on your own terms.

en.theme: Seek the Welfare of the City
en.focus: Even in challenging circumstances, God calls His people to seek the welfare of the city where they dwell and trust in His plans.

questions.question: To whom did Jeremiah write this letter?
options: The Judeans exiled to Egypt
The remaining people in Jerusalem
The elders, priests, prophets, and all the people Nebuchadnezzar had carried into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon
All the Israelites living in the land of Canaan
questions.explanation: The letter was addressed to the elders, priests, prophets, and all the people whom Nebuchadnezzar had carried into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon.

questions.question: What did God command the exiles to do in Babylon?
options: Immediately rebel against the king of Babylon
Build houses, plant gardens, marry and have children, and seek the welfare of the city
Wait three years and then return to Jerusalem
Live in isolation and have no contact with the Babylonians
questions.explanation: God commanded them to build houses, plant gardens, marry and have children, and seek the welfare of Babylon, for in its welfare they would find their welfare.

questions.question: What promise did God make to His people in Jeremiah 29:11?
options: They would immediately return to Jerusalem
He would give them plans for welfare and a future with hope
They would become rulers over Babylon
They would no longer experience any difficulties
questions.explanation: God promised that His plans for them were for welfare, to give them a future and a hope, not for evil.

questions.question: How does this passage encourage us to trust God even in less than ideal circumstances?
options: God will immediately change our circumstances to be perfect
We can ignore our surroundings and focus only on our own needs
God has plans for our welfare, and we should seek the good of our community where we are
We should complain and wait until circumstances improve
questions.explanation: Even in the difficult exile in Babylon, God called His people to seek the welfare of the city and trust that He had plans for their future and hope. This reminds us to seek the good of our community in any situation and trust in God's sovereignty.

en.reflection: In your 'Babylon' (the imperfect place where God has placed you now), how can you pray or act for its welfare and peace?
reflectionOptions: Pray for my local community and neighbors
Reach out to someone nearby in need
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You that even in difficult times, You have plans for my welfare. Help me to seek Your will for the peace and good of the environment You have placed me in. May I be a blessing and trust in the future and hope You have prepared for me. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, intentionally pray for your neighbors, colleagues, or the community where you live, asking God to grant them peace and well-being.

en.focus: Even in punishment, God does not forget His covenant with His people, promising to bring them back and heal them.

questions.question: What did God tell Jeremiah to do at the beginning of the passage?
options: Tell the people they would be rejected forever
Write down His words in a book
Prophesy the destruction of all nations
Instruct the people to build the temple immediately
questions.explanation: God commanded Jeremiah to write down the prophecy concerning Israel and Judah, which is about their future restoration.

questions.question: To what place did God promise to bring His people back?
options: The land of Canaan
The land of their fathers
The Promised Land
Babylon
questions.explanation: God promised to bring His people back to the land of their fathers, so they would possess it once again.

questions.type: Understand God's approach to His people
questions.question: How does God describe what He will do to His people?
options: He will reject them forever and have no further relationship with them
He will discipline them but not destroy them completely, eventually healing them
He will punish only foreign nations, not His own people
He will let them rebuild their homes by their own strength
questions.explanation: God clearly states that He will discipline His people, but His punishment is for healing, not utter destruction, ultimately leading to restoration and healing.

questions.question: What is the significance of the promises in Jeremiah 30 for us today when facing difficulties and challenges?
options: If we just try hard enough, God will immediately remove all difficulties
Even in distress, we can trust in God's power to heal and restore, and His love and promises never change
We can complain to God about why He allows difficulties and then choose to give up
It means we don't need to be accountable for our sins, because God will eventually forgive everything
questions.explanation: This passage reminds us that God is faithful, and even in discipline, His love and promises of healing remain. We can find hope in His faithfulness.

en.reflection: What 'wound' or 'distress' in your life currently needs God's healing and restoration?
en.prayer: Lord, thank You for being a faithful and covenant-keeping God, whose heart is for healing and restoration even in discipline. I have many weaknesses and hurts in my life; please heal and restore me according to Your promises, so I may experience Your presence and grace once again. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take some time today to tell God about one area in your life that needs His healing, and trust in His promises.

en.theme: God's Promised Restoration and the New Covenant
en.focus: God's unchanging love for Israel (including Judah and Ephraim) promises to bring them back from exile, establish a new covenant, and lead them to true restoration.

questions.question: How does God describe His relationship with Israel at the beginning of this passage?
options: A strict judge
An everlasting lover
A righteous king
An almighty warrior
questions.explanation: God states, “I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have continued my faithfulness to you.” This shows His eternal and gracious love for Israel.

questions.question: Who does God promise to bring back from the land of the north?
options: Only the people of Judah
Only the people of Ephraim
The blind and the lame, pregnant women and those in labour
All foreign nations
questions.explanation: God promises to bring back the Israelites from the land of the north, including the most vulnerable, such as the blind, the lame, pregnant women, and those in labour.

questions.question: What is the fundamental difference between the 'new covenant' God makes with Israel in this passage and the previous covenant?
options: The new covenant only requires external actions, not inner change
The new covenant requires people to write the law themselves; God is no longer involved
The new covenant involves putting the law within them, writing it on their hearts, so they may know God
The new covenant applies only to priests and Levites
questions.explanation: The essence of the new covenant is that God will put His law within them, write it on their hearts, so that all may know Him, and He will forgive their sin.

questions.question: How does God's everlasting love for Israel and the promise of the new covenant encourage you today in facing life's challenges?
options: It reminds me that I can overcome anything by relying on my own efforts
It makes me think God only loves His chosen people, not someone like me
It motivates me to trust in God's unchanging love and promised grace, finding hope even in difficulties
It assures me that God will immediately solve all my problems if I just pray
questions.explanation: God's unchanging love for Israel and His new covenant demonstrate His faithfulness. This encourages us to trust in His grace and hope, even when facing challenges.

en.reflection: Reflecting on God's everlasting love for Israel and the promise of the new covenant, what part of yourself do you most need to entrust to this faithful God today?
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for loving me with an everlasting love and for preparing the precious new covenant for me. Please write Your law upon my heart, that I may know You more deeply and experience the forgiveness of my sins. May I always experience Your steadfast love and faithfulness, looking to You in every circumstance. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, take a moment to meditate on Jeremiah 31:33-34 and give thanks for God writing His law on your heart.

en.theme: A New Covenant, A New Hope
en.focus: God promises a new covenant with His people, written on their hearts, bringing complete renewal and forgiveness.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 31:23–26, what does the LORD promise will happen to the land of Judah?
options: It will become richer and lead other nations
It will once again be a dwelling of righteousness and a holy mountain
Its population will drastically decrease and be occupied by foreigners
It will suffer harsher punishments until its complete destruction
questions.explanation: God promises that in the land of Judah, people will again say, “May the LORD bless you, O dwelling of righteousness, O holy mountain!” This signifies restoration of holiness and peace.

questions.question: What is the fundamental difference between the 'new covenant' promised by the LORD and the old covenant?
options: The new covenant is only for the people of Judah, not for Gentiles
The law of the new covenant is written on people's hearts, not on tablets of stone
The new covenant requires stricter sacrifices and rituals
The new covenant only brings material prosperity, not forgiveness of sins
questions.explanation: A key feature of the new covenant is that God will put His law within His people and write it on their hearts, so they will all know Him.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is God's most fundamental promise to His people in the new covenant?
options: To give them a stronger army
To grant them more land and wealth
To forgive their wickedness and remember their sins no more
To allow them to fully understand all of God's mysteries
questions.explanation: God explicitly promises, “I will forgive their wickedness and will remember their sins no more.” This is a core blessing of the new covenant.

questions.question: Jeremiah 31:35-37 emphasizes what truth to strengthen the hope of God's people?
options: Israel's future depends on their own efforts
God's promises to Israel are eternal and unchangeable, like the order of creation
God will not reject Israel as long as they obey all His laws
God will decide whether to preserve Israel based on their merits
questions.explanation: God uses the established order of the sun, moon, stars, and the boundaries of the sea as proof that His promises to Israel are as eternal and firm as these natural laws, and He will never reject them.

en.reflection: Are there any areas in your life where you recognize a need for God's personal transformation and renewal, so that His law can be more deeply etched into your heart?
en.prayer: Faithful God of the Covenant, thank You for establishing a new covenant with me, writing Your law on my heart, and forgiving my sins. Help me to know You more deeply each day and let Your truth guide my thoughts and actions. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take a moment today to reflect: Because of Jesus, my sins are forgiven, and God remembers them no more. Thank God for this truth.

en.theme: God's Faithfulness Even in Desperate Times
en.focus: Even in seemingly hopeless situations, God remains faithful to His covenant, and His promises will surely be fulfilled.

questions.question: Under what circumstances was Jeremiah imprisoned?
options: He attempted to flee Jerusalem
He prophesied that Jerusalem would fall to Babylon
He refused to surrender to Babylon
He stole temple treasures
questions.explanation: Jeremiah was confined in the court of the guard because he prophesied that Jerusalem would fall into the hand of the king of Babylon.

questions.question: What did God command Jeremiah to do while he was imprisoned?
options: Plead with the king of Babylon
Write letters to the exiles
Buy a field
Call the people to repentance
questions.explanation: God commanded Jeremiah to buy a field, an seemingly illogical action given the besieged situation at the time.

questions.question: What did Jeremiah say to God in his prayer?
options: Complained that God's command was unreasonable
Questioned God's power
Acknowledged God's greatness and faithfulness but expressed confusion about the immediate predicament
Asked God to immediately save Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Jeremiah acknowledged God as the God of great wonders, who controls all things, while also expressing confusion about the command to buy the field at that specific time.

questions.question: What is the main message about God conveyed in this chapter?
options: God only makes covenants during times of peace
God's power is limited and cannot change difficult situations
God keeps His promises even in desperate situations, and His word never changes
People must be perfect before God will show grace
questions.explanation: Even in the desperate situation where the nation was about to be destroyed, God commanded Jeremiah to buy a field, demonstrating that His future promises would be fulfilled and that He is a faithful, covenant-keeping God.

en.reflection: When facing your own 'impossible' situations or difficulties, how does this passage encourage you to continue trusting in God's promises?
reflectionOptions: It reminds me of God's omnipotence
It helps me release immediate worries
It prompts me to re-examine God's faithfulness
en.prayer: Faithful and covenant-keeping God, thank You for Your unwavering steadfastness in all circumstances. When I find myself in humanly impossible situations, or when I feel confused and discouraged, help me to hold tightly to Your promises. I know You are the God who does great and mighty things, and Your will shall not fail. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Write down one of God's promises that you most need to believe today and place it where you can easily see it.

en.focus: Even in the deepest distress, God promises restoration and a future hope for His people because He is a faithful God who keeps His covenant.

questions.question: How does the Lord respond to Jeremiah's prayer (v. 25)?
options: He rebukes Jeremiah for his lack of faith
He reaffirms His power and the coming judgment on Israel
He immediately promises to save Israel from Babylon
He instructs Jeremiah to flee Jerusalem
questions.explanation: God first emphasizes that He is the Lord, the God of all mankind, for whom nothing is too hard, and then confirms that Jerusalem will fall to the Babylonians due to the people's wickedness.

questions.question: After declaring punishment, what key promise does God make to the people of Israel?
options: They will establish a greater empire
They will be utterly destroyed with no descendants
They will be gathered back from exile and re-establish a covenant with God
They will be elevated to rule over all nations
questions.explanation: God promises to gather them from all the lands where He has driven them, bring them back to this place, and make an everlasting covenant with them, so they will fear Him forever.

questions.question: God's promise to bring His people back to the promised land and treat them well again reflects what aspect of His character?
options: He is a fickle God
He is a God who only cares about punishment
He is a faithful, covenant-keeping God full of mercy and love
He is a God who shows favoritism
questions.explanation: Despite the people's repeated sins, God's promise to restore them in the future and plant them with all His heart and soul demonstrates His unchanging love and covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: What reminder do the promises in this passage offer for our lives today?
options: God will abandon us forever if we sin
God's promises apply only to ancient Israel
Even in desperate situations, we can trust in God's faithfulness and His promise of restoration
We can sin freely because God will eventually forgive everything
questions.explanation: This passage reminds us that no matter how difficult or seemingly hopeless our circumstances, God's faithfulness and His promise of restoration are unwavering, and we can firmly trust in Him.

en.reflection: Is there a seemingly hopeless situation in your life right now where you need to place your hope afresh in God's promise of restoration?
reflectionOptions: A relationship that seems beyond repair
en.prayer: Faithful God, thank You for Your promises of hope even in the darkest times. Help me to trust firmly in Your love and Your power to restore, no matter my circumstances. May my heart find peace and strength in Your unfailing promises. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, pray specifically for one seemingly hopeless situation in your life, asking God to work according to His faithful promises.

en.focus: Even in seemingly hopeless situations, God faithfully promises His people future restoration, and His covenants remain unbroken.

questions.question: What did the Lord say to Jeremiah while he was confined?
options: You will be imprisoned forever
I will tell you great and hidden things
You must flee this city
Repent of your sins
questions.explanation: God promised to show Jeremiah “great and hidden things” that he did not know.

questions.question: How did God promise to heal and cleanse Jerusalem and Judah?
options: Through political alliances
By granting peace and truth
By leaving them to face their enemies alone
By sending a foreign king to rule
questions.explanation: God stated He would “heal” Jerusalem and grant them “abundant prosperity and security.”

questions.type: Understand the strength of God's covenant
questions.question: What does God use to illustrate that His covenant with David and the Levites will never be broken?
options: The stability of mountains and seas
The order of day, night, sun, moon, and stars
The growth of trees on the earth
Human breathing and heartbeat
questions.explanation: God compares the unbroken covenant with David and the Levites to the unbroken covenant of day and night and the fixed laws of heaven and earth.

questions.question: What is the main hope this passage offers us?
options: Hard work alone can change destiny
God only saves those who are perfect
God is still in control and keeps His promises even in the darkest times
All difficulties are God's punishment for people
questions.explanation: Even when the nation was in a desperate state, God declared Himself to be sovereign and faithful to His covenants, promising restoration and the establishment of David’s lineage, offering great hope.

en.reflection: In what seemingly hopeless situation today do you need to trust that God is still in control and can bring restoration?
en.prayer: Faithful God, thank You that even in the darkest moments, Your promises remain steadfast. Please help me to hold onto Your promise of restoration in the seemingly hopeless situations of my life. May I see the great and hidden things that I do not know. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Choose one situation where you feel hopeless, and quietly pray to God, declaring your trust that He can bring healing and restoration.

en.focus: God severely condemns His people for breaking their covenant and oppressing the vulnerable, declaring imminent judgment.

questions.question: Which cities were still holding out when Nebuchadnezzar attacked Jerusalem?
options: Lachish and Azekah
Jericho and Bethel
Gibeon and Mizpah
Hebron and Debir
questions.explanation: The passage states that only Lachish and Azekah remained among the fortified cities of Judah when the king of Babylon was fighting against them.

questions.question: What message did Jeremiah deliver to King Zedekiah?
options: Jerusalem would not be captured
He would die in Babylon
He would be taken captive to Babylon and die there
He would defeat the king of Babylon
questions.explanation: Jeremiah prophesied that King Zedekiah would be taken captive to Babylon, die there, and be burned with spices in his honor.

questions.question: In what way did the people of Judah break their covenant with God?
options: They failed to offer sacrifices on time
They did not observe the Sabbath
They failed to release their Hebrew slaves
They worshipped idols and false gods
questions.explanation: The people had made a covenant to set free all Hebrew slaves but then went back on their word, re-enslaving them, which violated God's law and their sworn promise.

questions.question: Because the people broke their covenant, what did God declare He would do to them?
options: Immediately bless them
Give them over to their enemies to be terrified
Give them more time to repent
Appoint a new king over them
questions.explanation: God declared that He would give them over to terror among all the kingdoms of the earth, and they would face judgment by sword, famine, and plague.

en.reflection: Today's passage reminds us that God values our covenants, especially those concerning justice and compassion. Are there any promises you have not kept, or areas where you need to treat others with greater justice and compassion?
reflectionOptions: Reflect on attitude towards the vulnerable
en.prayer: Righteous Lord, I acknowledge that You are a faithful God who keeps Your covenants, and I ask for Your help to be a person who keeps my promises. Please illuminate any broken vows or unjust actions in my life, whether before You or others. Forgive me and guide me back to Your ways. May my life reflect Your justice and compassion. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, think of one promise you have made but not yet fulfilled (big or small), and make an effort to complete it.

en.focus: True faithfulness and obedience mean consistently following God's commands and resisting the world's temptations.

questions.question: Which family was the prophet Jeremiah commanded to meet?
options: The house of Judah
The house of Levi
The house of the Rechabites
The house of Benjamin
questions.explanation: Jeremiah chapter 35 records that Jeremiah was commanded to go to the house of the Rechabites.

questions.question: What was the reason the descendants of Rechab gave for refusing to drink wine?
options: They were Nazirites
They were priests
Their ancestor Jonadab had commanded them not to drink wine
They wanted to save money on wine
questions.explanation: The descendants of Rechab explained that their ancestor Jonadab had commanded them not to drink wine, build houses, sow seed, plant vineyards, or own any, but to live in tents.

questions.question: What message did God convey to the people of Judah through the story of the Rechabites?
options: Following ancestral traditions is more important than God's law
God prefers those who live in tents and do not drink wine
The people of Judah were less obedient to God's word than the Rechabites were to their ancestor's command
God grants material wealth for obedience
questions.explanation: God pointed out that the descendants of Rechab were so faithfully obedient to a human command, while the people of Judah refused to obey God's commands, which was the message of rebuke.

questions.question: What can we learn from the example of the Rechabites today?
options: We should completely abstain from alcohol and imitate their lifestyle
We should value and obey the teachings of our parents and elders
We must faithfully uphold God's teachings even when facing difficulties and temptations
Only through ascetic practices can we please God
questions.explanation: The Rechabites faithfully kept their ancestor's command even in difficult circumstances, reminding us to be even more faithful in keeping God's commands and not being swayed by the world's temptations.

en.reflection: Today's passage reminds us of the importance of faithfulness and obedience. In which area do you most need to learn from the Rechabites' example when facing the world's temptations?
reflectionOptions: Persisting in daily devotion and prayer
Being more faithful in handling finances
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding me through the example of the Rechabites to be faithful and consistently obedient to Your commands. Please help me to stand firm in Your word amidst the currents of the world and not be led astray by temptations. May my life bring glory to Your name. In Jesus' name, I pray. Amen.
en.action: Think of one spiritual discipline you used to practice faithfully but have become lax in, and restart it today.

en.focus: Despite human resistance or rejection, God's Word carries His authority and purpose, and it will ultimately be fulfilled.

questions.question: At the beginning of Jeremiah 36, what did the LORD command Jeremiah to do?
options: Go to Egypt and preach a message
Write down all His words concerning Israel and Judah
Prophesy the downfall of Babylon
Offer sacrifices for the sins of the people
questions.explanation: God commanded Jeremiah to take a scroll and write on it all the words He had spoken to him concerning Israel, Judah, and all the nations, from the time he was called until that day.

questions.question: What did King Jehoiakim do after hearing the message on the scroll?
options: He repented and tore his clothes
He ordered more scrolls to be copied
He cut the scroll with a knife and threw it into the fire
He had Jeremiah and Baruch imprisoned
questions.explanation: Upon hearing the words read, King Jehoiakim cut the scroll with a knife and threw it into the fire to be burned.

questions.question: Despite King Jehoiakim burning the scroll, what does God's response demonstrate?
options: God gave up on Judah
God's Word can be destroyed and cancelled
God's Word carries eternal authority and cannot be nullified by human actions
God's anger towards Jehoiakim would immediately subside
questions.explanation: God commanded Jeremiah to rewrite the words from the burned scroll, adding even more severe judgment against King Jehoiakim. This shows that God's Word stands firm and cannot be nullified by anyone.

questions.question: How does this chapter encourage us to treat God's Word?
options: We can freely modify or ignore God's Word
We should cherish, obey, and proclaim God's Word, as it carries life-changing power
God's Word is only relevant to the ancient Israelites
Only educated people can understand God's Word
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 36 emphasizes the enduring nature and authority of God's Word. Even in the face of resistance, God's message stands firm and accomplishes His purpose, reminding us to cherish and obey it.

en.reflection: How can you respond more actively to God's Word today, beyond just passively hearing or reading it?
reflectionOptions: Spend more time meditating on a passage
Apply scripture to a specific decision
Share God's Word with someone else
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for giving us Your eternal and unchanging Word. Please help me to receive Your Word with reverence, not just hearing or reading, but also obeying and living it out. May Your Word work its transforming power in my life. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Choose a familiar scripture today. Meditate on it and reflect on its impact on your life, then try to live out its teaching.

en.focus: Even in hardship and persecution, God remains sovereign and delivers His message through His prophet.

questions.question: Whom did King Zedekiah of Judah send to the prophet Jeremiah?
options: High officials of Judah
Zedekiah's son and the elders
His servant Jehucal and the priest Zephaniah
Army commanders and ministers
questions.explanation: King Zedekiah sent Jehucal son of Shelemiah and the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah to Jeremiah.

questions.question: What did Jeremiah decide to do when the Babylonian army temporarily withdrew?
options: Flee to Egypt
Go to his hometown in the land of Benjamin to claim his property
Offer advice to the king
Remain in Jerusalem to continue preaching
questions.explanation: Jeremiah intended to go to his hometown in the land of Benjamin to receive his share of the property while the Babylonian army was temporarily away.

questions.question: What was the reason for Jeremiah's arrest?
options: He was collaborating with the Babylonians
He was attempting to defect to the Chaldeans
He prophesied that the Babylonian army would return to attack Jerusalem
He incited the people to rebel against the king
questions.explanation: Jeremiah was falsely accused of deserting to the Chaldeans, but the real reason was his prophecy that Jerusalem would again be captured by the Babylonians.

questions.question: What important lesson can we learn from Jeremiah's experience about faithfully delivering God's message?
options: Avoid delivering messages that are unpopular
Remain faithful to God's message even when facing persecution
Only speak the truth when circumstances are favourable
Modify God's message for self-preservation
questions.explanation: Jeremiah remained faithful to deliver God's message to the king even while imprisoned and suffering, teaching us to be faithful in difficult times.

en.reflection: In your life today, have you ever felt alone or faced difficulties for standing up for truth or doing what is right?
en.prayer: Dear Lord, thank You for being the God who is in control of all things. Grant me courage and wisdom to be faithful to Your message and truth, like Jeremiah, even when facing misunderstanding or persecution. Help me to trust in Your presence and provision. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Meditate on the verse: “The LORD is my light and my salvation—whom shall I fear?” (Psalm 27:1)

en.focus: Even when facing persecution and hardship, we are to choose to trust God, for He will make a way for us.

questions.question: What did the prophet Jeremiah say that led the officials to accuse him of 'weakening the hands of the soldiers and all the people left in this city'?
options: He advised the people to surrender to the Babylonians
He prophesied the destruction of Jerusalem
He called the people to repent and turn to God
He rebuked the officials for not obeying God's word
questions.explanation: Jeremiah advised that those who remained in the city and surrendered to the Babylonians would live, otherwise they would die by sword, famine, and plague.

questions.question: After the officials handed Jeremiah over to King Zedekiah, how did they treat him?
options: They imprisoned him in the palace
They threw him into a muddy cistern
They banished him from the city
They put him to death
questions.explanation: The officials threw Jeremiah into the cistern of Malkijah, the son of the king, which was in the court of the guard. It had no water, only mud.

questions.question: Who interceded with King Zedekiah to have Jeremiah pulled out of the muddy pit?
options: Jeremiah's companions
An Ethiopian eunuch
Some elders of the city
King Zedekiah's son
questions.explanation: Ebed-Melech the Ethiopian pleaded with the king, pointing out the evil the officials had done to Jeremiah, and received the king's permission to rescue him.

questions.question: What is the main lesson we can learn from Jeremiah's perseverance in speaking God's word despite his plight, and his subsequent rescue?
options: Speaking the truth guarantees no suffering
Obeying God's word can bring hardship, but God will care for and rescue His servants
One should avoid saying things that might cause controversy
God only rescues those with high social status
questions.explanation: Jeremiah suffered persecution, even being thrown into a muddy pit, for proclaiming God's word, yet God used a foreign eunuch to rescue him, demonstrating God's care for His faithful servants.

en.reflection: In your life, have there been moments when you faced difficulty or misunderstanding for doing what was right or speaking the truth?
reflectionOptions: Being criticized for your faith stance
Paying a price for an honest decision
Sacrificing for the good of others
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for being our God who watches over us and rescues us. Grant me courage to faithfully speak Your word and do what pleases You, even when facing difficulties and persecution. I trust that You will make a way for me. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Think of someone who has encouraged you to persevere in your faith and express your gratitude to them today.

en.focus: Even in the most difficult circumstances, God's will is worthy of our trust and obedience.

questions.question: Where did King Zedekiah secretly meet Jeremiah?
options: In the palace garden
At the third entrance to the temple of the LORD
At the camp of the King of Babylon
In the house of Jonathan the scribe
questions.explanation: King Zedekiah brought Jeremiah to the third entrance to the temple of the LORD to speak with him in private.

questions.question: What fear did King Zedekiah express to Jeremiah?
options: That Jeremiah would betray him
That the Judeans would mock him
That the Babylonians would kill him
That Jeremiah would be thrown back into the muddy cistern
questions.explanation: King Zedekiah feared that if he followed Jeremiah's advice, the officials who had thrown Jeremiah into the cistern would hand him over to others, who might then kill him.

questions.question: What did Jeremiah tell King Zedekiah would happen if he did not surrender?
options: The Babylonians would be defeated, and Jerusalem saved
Jerusalem would be burned, and the women and children from the palace taken captive
The Egyptians would come to help them against the Babylonians
King Zedekiah would be crowned the new King of Babylon
questions.explanation: Jeremiah prophesied that if King Zedekiah did not surrender, Jerusalem would be burned by the Chaldeans, and his family would be taken captive.

questions.question: What lesson about obeying God can we learn from King Zedekiah's story?
options: With enough faith, God will always change our circumstances
Obeying God's will sometimes requires us to let go of fear, even if the outcome is uncertain
It's enough to hear God's word without actually doing it
We should only obey God when it is easy
questions.explanation: King Zedekiah failed to fully obey God's will due to fear of human ridicule and opposition. This reminds us that obeying God sometimes requires courage to let go of fear of the unknown and the opinions of others.

en.reflection: In your life, have there been moments when you hesitated to fully obey God's will because of fear of what others might think or the difficulties you might face?
reflectionOptions: Seek prayer support from a spiritual friend
en.prayer: Faithful Lord, thank You for revealing Your will to us in every situation. Please help me to lay down my fear of others and grant me the courage and faith to simply obey You, no matter the outcome. May I understand that Your way is always the best way. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, reflect on an area where you have hesitated to obey God due to fear, and pray for His help.

en.focus: Even in the midst of judgment, God extends His grace and protection to those who are faithful or choose to obey.

questions.question: In what year did King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon capture Jerusalem?
options: The fourth year of Jeremiah's ministry
The ninth year of King Zedekiah's reign
The eleventh year of King Zedekiah's reign
The third year after the walls of Jerusalem were breached
questions.explanation: The text specifies that Jerusalem was captured in the eleventh year of King Zedekiah, on the ninth day of the fourth month.

questions.type: Observe the fate of a character
questions.question: What was the fate of King Zedekiah?
options: He was released by the king of Babylon and continued to rule Judah
He was killed and buried in Jerusalem
His eyes were put out, and he was bound in chains and taken to Babylon
He fled to Egypt and lived out his days there
questions.explanation: King Zedekiah was judged by the king of Babylon at Riblah, his sons were killed before his eyes, and then his eyes were put out, and he was bound with bronze chains and taken to Babylon.

questions.question: After the fall of Jerusalem, which prophet received kind treatment and special care from the king of Babylon?
options: Ezekiel
Daniel
Jeremiah
Isaiah
questions.explanation: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon commanded Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard, to treat Jeremiah well, not to harm him, and to do with him whatever he wished.

questions.question: What important truth does God reveal to us through the experience of Ebed-Melech the Cushite?
options: Bravery alone can change the destiny of a nation
Even in judgment, God remembers and protects those who trust in Him
Foreigners are more likely to receive God's favor than Israelites
God only saves those who are of high status
questions.explanation: Because Ebed-Melech the Cushite trusted in the LORD, his life was spared even though Jerusalem fell. This shows that God will protect those who trust in Him, even amidst judgment.

en.reflection: In your life, how has God shown His grace and preservation in difficult or unexpected circumstances?
reflectionOptions: Experienced healing or comfort during illness
Found reconciliation in a relational conflict
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for being a righteous judge and a gracious protector. Help me to trust You in all circumstances, knowing that You will watch over and preserve those who seek You. May I also show Your grace to others today. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, offer thanks to God for a specific instance of His grace in a difficult situation you have experienced.

en.focus: Even in the chaos and uncertainty after exile, God remains in control and makes a way for His people.

questions.question: Where was Jeremiah when Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, found him?
options: Inside the city of Jerusalem
Among the captives at Ramah
In the king's palace in Babylon
With Gedaliah, the governor of Judah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah was found among the captives who were being held at Ramah before being released by the Babylonians.

questions.question: What significant statement did Nebuzaradan make to Jeremiah?
options: He accused Jeremiah of being a traitor
He acknowledged Jeremiah's message as a fulfillment of the LORD's prophecy
He invited Jeremiah to be a consultant in Babylon
He commanded Jeremiah to go to Babylon
questions.explanation: Nebuzaradan acknowledged that God's word had come to pass, stating that the LORD had brought disaster upon the land because of the people's sins.

questions.question: What choices were given to Jeremiah after his release?
options: He was only allowed to go to Babylon
He was forced to stay in Jerusalem
He could choose to go to Babylon or remain in the land of Judah
He was ordered to seek refuge in Egypt
questions.explanation: Nebuzaradan gave Jeremiah the option to either go to Babylon or stay in Judah and live with Gedaliah.

questions.question: How did God continue to care for His people after Judah’s fall, even through the hands of non-believers?
options: He allowed all the Judeans to go to Babylon
He granted Jeremiah freedom and choices through the Babylonian captain
He enabled Gedaliah, the governor, to build a strong army
He allowed the Judeans to immediately rebuild the temple
questions.explanation: Despite the Babylonians being the invaders, God used their captain, Nebuzaradan, to grant His prophet Jeremiah freedom and choices, even arranging for his provision and dwelling in Judah.

en.reflection: What situation in your life currently feels difficult or chaotic, where you need to trust that God is still in control and making a way for you?
reflectionOptions: A problem in a family relationship
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You that You are still in control amidst all difficulties. Please help me to trust You in chaos and uncertainty, knowing You are making a way for me. May I, like Jeremiah, make wise choices under Your guidance. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Think of one thing you feel helpless about recently, then pray a one-sentence prayer to God: “Lord, I trust You are in control of this situation, and I ask You to make a way.”

en.focus: Even in the most challenging and dangerous times, we can trust in God’s protection and guidance.

questions.question: Who came to Gedaliah at Mizpah in the seventh month, accompanied by ten men?
options: Johanan
Ishmael
Nethaniah
Baalis
questions.explanation: The text clearly states that Ishmael, son of Nethaniah, came with ten men to Gedaliah.

questions.question: How did Ishmael and his companions treat Gedaliah and the Judeans and Chaldeans with him?
options: They dined with Gedaliah and planned for the future
They persuaded Gedaliah to flee to Egypt with them
They struck down Gedaliah and those with him with the sword
They sought Gedaliah's protection from the Chaldeans
questions.explanation: Ishmael and his companions struck down Gedaliah, along with the Judeans and Chaldeans who were with him, using a sword.

questions.question: What internal issues among the people of Israel after the exile does this event reflect?
options: Unity and mutual trust
Steadfast faith in God
Chaos, violence, and a lack of leadership
Loyalty to the Chaldeans
questions.explanation: The series of violent and chaotic events following Gedaliah’s assassination highlights the disorder, distrust, and lack of stable leadership in Judah after the exile.

questions.question: What can we learn from Johanan's courageous pursuit of Ishmael and rescue of the captives?
options: When facing evil, being a bystander is the best option
Individual strength cannot change anything
Even in danger, one should bravely seek justice and protect the vulnerable
Wait for God to intervene personally, without our action
questions.explanation: Despite the danger, Johanan chose to bravely pursue Ishmael and successfully rescued the captives, reminding us to act courageously in the face of injustice and evil.

en.reflection: In today's world, have you ever felt helpless or afraid in situations of chaos or injustice? How does this passage encourage you to trust God and take action?
reflectionOptions: Ask God for peace to overcome fear
Seek wisdom to know when to act
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for being sovereign even amidst chaos and danger. Please help me to trust in Your protection and guidance, even in difficult times. Grant me the courage to stand for justice and protect the vulnerable when needed. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, offer a short prayer for those in your community or country who are experiencing injustice or danger.

en.focus: To truly seek God’s will and commit to obeying His guidance, regardless of the outcome, is key to trusting Him.

questions.question: When the people asked Jeremiah to pray for them, what promise did they make?
options: They would offer abundant sacrifices to God
They would obey everything the LORD their God said
They would stay in the land of Judah and not go to Egypt
They would build altars to worship the LORD
questions.explanation: The people promised Jeremiah that they would obey whatever the LORD their God said.

questions.question: Through Jeremiah, what did the LORD say He would do for the people if they remained in the land of Judah?
options: He would build them up and not tear them down; plant them and not uproot them
He would give them more wealth and land
He would make them the head over all nations
He would protect them from all their enemies
questions.explanation: The LORD promised that if they obeyed and remained in Judah, He would build them up, plant them, and relent concerning the disaster He had inflicted.

questions.question: What consequences did the LORD warn the people about if they disobeyed and insisted on going to Egypt?
options: They would face famine and disease
The sword, famine, and plague would overtake and destroy them in Egypt
They would lose their land and livestock
They would be scattered from their families and become homeless
questions.explanation: The LORD explicitly stated that if they insisted on going to Egypt, the sword, famine, and plague would overtake them there, and they would die in Egypt.

questions.question: How did Jeremiah accuse the people of being in their hearts when they sought God's will?
options: Truly repentant and willing to obey everything
Doubtful and questioning God's power
Deceitful, only seeking the answer they wanted
Full of fear and unable to make a decision
questions.explanation: Jeremiah accused the people of being 'deceitful in your hearts,' pretending to seek God's will when they had already decided to go to Egypt and merely wanted God to approve their plan.

en.reflection: Have you ever, like these people, had a preconceived answer or inclination in your heart when seeking God’s will?
reflectionOptions: Admit I have done this before
Willing to seek God more genuinely today
Realize I am currently doing this
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for being a God who is willing to reveal Your will to us. Please help me to have an honest and submissive heart when seeking Your guidance, without deceit. May my request truly be to understand Your heart and willingly obey. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, pray about a decision you are facing, asking God to reveal His will and committing to obey, no matter the answer.

en.focus: When God's people refuse to obey His commands and seek their own solutions, they face tragic consequences.

questions.question: After Jeremiah finished speaking the words of the LORD, who stood up to contradict him?
options: The priests and Levites
Johanan and all the army commanders
The elders and officials
Baruch and all the scribes
questions.explanation: After Jeremiah finished speaking the words of the LORD, Azariah son of Hoshaiah (also called Johanan), and Johanan son of Kareah, and all the arrogant men stood up to contradict him.

questions.question: These people accused Jeremiah of not speaking God's words, but whose idea was it?
options: His own idea
Baruch’s idea, who incited him
Pharaoh of Egypt’s idea
The Chaldeans’ idea
questions.explanation: They accused Jeremiah of being incited by Baruch son of Neriah, with the purpose of handing them over to the Chaldeans so that they might kill them or carry them away to Babylon.

questions.question: Despite God's clear instruction for them to remain in Judah, what decision did the people ultimately make?
options: They remained in Judah and repented to God
They went to Babylon to find peace
They went to Egypt for protection
They scattered to neighboring nations for refuge
questions.explanation: Johanan son of Kareah and all the army commanders, along with all the people, did not obey the LORD's command to stay in Judah; instead, they took all the remnant and went to Egypt.

questions.question: What did God declare through Jeremiah that the people could not escape, even by fleeing to Egypt?
options: Famine and plague
Pursuit and destruction by the Chaldeans
Slavery by the Egyptians
Internal strife and division
questions.explanation: God clearly stated that the sword, famine, and plague they feared would overtake them in Egypt, and Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon would attack Egypt, set up his throne there, and destroy Egypt.

en.reflection: Is there an area in your life where, despite God's clear guidance, you tend to rely on your own judgment or the world's help?
en.prayer: Heavenly Father, thank You for Your Word that reminds me that true safety and protection are found only in You. Forgive me for times when I fail to trust You and instead seek my own ways or the world's help. Help me to have an obedient heart, listening to Your commands and trusting in Your leading alone. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, pray for one area in your life where you tend not to trust God, asking Him for an obedient heart and faith to trust Him.

en.theme: The Cost of Disobedience and God's Mercy
en.focus: God's people face consequences for persistent disobedience, yet God continues to warn them and call them to turn back.

questions.question: At the beginning of Jeremiah 44, to which Judahites does the word of the LORD come?
options: Only to those in Pathros, Egypt
To all the Judahites living in Egypt, including Migdol, Tahpanhes, Memphis, and Pathros
Only to the Judahites in Jerusalem
To all the Judahites in Babylon
questions.explanation: The word of the LORD came to 'all the Judahites living in Egypt—in Migdol, Tahpanhes, Memphis and Pathros.'

questions.question: God reminded these Judahites that their ancestors and kings of Judah had done what, leading to the desolation of Jerusalem and the towns of Judah?
options: Failed to build sufficient defenses
Lived in the land of Egypt
Burned incense and served other gods
Failed to observe the Sabbath
questions.explanation: God reminded them that their ancestors and kings burned incense and served other gods, which led to the desolation of Jerusalem and the towns of Judah.

questions.question: How did the people respond when Jeremiah warned them to turn from their wickedness in the name of the LORD?
options: They immediately repented and sought God's will
They asked Jeremiah to pray for them
They refused to listen and declared they would continue to burn incense to the Queen of Heaven
They expressed confusion, not understanding why God was angry
questions.explanation: The people refused to listen to Jeremiah, declaring they would continue to burn incense to the Queen of Heaven, believing it brought them prosperity.

questions.question: What is the main teaching of this passage?
options: As long as people have faith, even idolatry can bring blessings
God shows no mercy to disobedient people
Persistent disobedience leads to severe consequences, but God still warns and calls people to return
Human choices do not affect God's plans
questions.explanation: The passage clearly shows that persistent disobedience leads to God's judgment and severe consequences, but even on the brink of judgment, God sends prophets to warn and call people to return.

en.reflection: Today's passage reminds us that God grieves over our disobedience and repeatedly calls us to return. Is there an area in your life where you know you are disobedient but persist, and need to repent to God?
reflectionOptions: Be more faithful in obedience to God
en.prayer: Loving Heavenly Father, thank You for repeatedly reminding me through Your Word that even in my disobedience, You love me and call me to return. Please forgive the deliberate sins in my life. Help me to have an obedient heart, to listen to Your teachings, to turn away from all idols and wickedness, and to serve You alone. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take some quiet time today to reflect: what 'small idol' or 'small persistence' in your life do you need to let go of and confess to God?

en.focus: God reminds His people that disobedience inevitably leads to dire consequences, and His word will surely come to pass.

questions.question: What did Jeremiah tell the people of Judah and Jerusalem?
options: God would bless them because they had finally repented
God had forgiven their sins and would return them to their homeland
God remembered their burning of incense in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem
God could no longer endure their evil deeds of burning incense to other gods
questions.explanation: Jeremiah stated that God could no longer tolerate their evil practices of burning incense to other gods, which led to their land becoming a desolation and a curse.

questions.question: How did the Judeans living in Egypt, especially the women, respond to Jeremiah’s words?
options: They immediately repented and sought God's forgiveness
They agreed with Jeremiah and promised to stop idol worship
They defiantly declared they would continue burning incense to the 'Queen of Heaven,' believing it brought them peace before
They asked Jeremiah to pray for them, so God might change His mind
questions.explanation: They stubbornly declared that they would continue burning incense to the 'Queen of Heaven,' believing that their lives prospered when they did so previously.

questions.question: What did God declare through Jeremiah would happen to the Judeans in Egypt who continued to burn incense and worship idols?
options: They would prosper greatly for their steadfast faith
They would return to the land of Judah and rebuild their homes
They would perish by sword and famine until very few remained
They would become leaders among the Egyptians and be honored
questions.explanation: God declared that those Judeans in Egypt who continued to worship idols would perish by sword and famine, with only a small remnant escaping.

questions.question: What sign did God give the people to prove that His words would surely come to pass?
options: The Pharaoh of Egypt would convert to the Lord
Judah would be rebuilt
Pharaoh Hophra, king of Egypt, would be given into the hand of his enemies, just like King Zedekiah of Judah
The Queen of Heaven would appear, proving her existence
questions.explanation: God gave the sign that Pharaoh Hophra, king of Egypt, would be given into the hand of his enemies, as proof that His words against the people of Judah would surely be fulfilled.

en.reflection: Have you ever, like the people in the passage, known God's will but stubbornly insisted on your own way? In what area do you need to submit more fully to God's word today?
en.prayer: Loving Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding me through Jeremiah that Your word is firm in the heavens and never changes. Please enlighten me to see if there is any disobedience or stubbornness in my life. Help me to let go of my own thoughts and will, and to simply obey Your will. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Spend a moment in quiet prayer today, asking God to reveal any disobedience in your life that is displeasing to Him, and ask Him for strength to obey.

en.theme: Trusting God in Times of Trouble
en.focus: Even in personal distress, we can choose to trust God's plan and find true comfort and hope in Him.

questions.question: What was Baruch's role when he wrote these words?
options: He was building a new city
He was writing down Jeremiah's words
He was repenting of his sins
He was fleeing from his enemies
questions.explanation: The passage states that Baruch was the one 'who wrote in a book all these words at Jeremiah’s dictation'.

questions.question: What emotions did Baruch express in Jeremiah 45:1-3?
options: Joy and gratitude
Pride and self-satisfaction
Weariness and sorrow
Anger and bitterness
questions.explanation: Baruch says, 'Woe is me! For the Lord has added sorrow to my pain; I am weary with my groaning and find no rest.' This indicates weariness and sorrow.

questions.question: How did God respond to Baruch's sorrow and his desire to 'seek great things' for himself?
options: God promised him great wealth and status
God rebuked him for being selfish and refused to help
God reminded him of coming destruction but promised to preserve his life
God encouraged him to continue seeking great things for himself
questions.explanation: God reminded Baruch that He was about to tear down what He had built and uproot what He had planted, and that He was bringing 'disaster on all flesh'. However, He promised to 'give you your life as a prize of war wherever you may go.'

questions.question: What lesson can we learn from God's instruction to Baruch about trusting God in difficult times?
options: God only cares about our personal success and comfort
God has a purpose even in destruction and can preserve those who trust Him
We should strive to create a perfect future for ourselves, not rely on God
God will condemn us when we feel weary
questions.explanation: Despite declaring impending destruction, God promised to preserve Baruch's life amidst the general disaster, showing that even in difficult times, God is sovereign and can protect His servants.

en.reflection: Like Baruch, have you ever felt weary or sorrowful while 'seeking great things' for yourself? How are you willing to surrender these 'great things' to God?
reflectionOptions: Let go of the need to control the future
Stop comparing myself to others and focus on God's call for me
Trust more deeply in God's provision and protection
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding me through Baruch's story that You are sovereign over all things. When I feel weary, sorrowful, or try to achieve great things for myself, please help me to surrender them and trust in Your will and protection. Help me to understand that true peace and security in life come only from You. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, take a few moments to consider what 'great things' you have been striving for, then surrender them to God, saying, 'Lord, my life is in Your hands; please guide me.'

en.focus: Even in judgment, God remains sovereign and offers promises of future restoration to His people.

questions.question: Which nation is the subject of the prophecy in Jeremiah 46?
options: Assyria
Babylon
Egypt
Moab
questions.explanation: This chapter contains a prophecy concerning Egypt, specifically the defeat of Pharaoh Neco's army by Babylon at Carchemish.

questions.question: How does God describe His actions towards Egypt and Babylon in this chapter?
options: God is helping Egypt against Babylon
God is using Babylon as His instrument to judge Egypt
God is indifferent to both nations
God commands Egypt and Babylon to live in peace
questions.explanation: God clearly states that He is using Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, as His instrument to bring judgment upon Egypt.

questions.question: Amidst prophecies of judgment on nations, what special word does God have for His people Israel?
options: He will destroy Israel immediately
He will keep them in perpetual captivity
He promises to save them from afar and bring them back
He will judge them alongside Egypt without hope
questions.explanation: God promises His people Israel that although they will be disciplined, He will ultimately bring them back from captivity and grant them peace.

questions.question: What is the most important lesson we can learn from the judgments and promises in Jeremiah 46?
options: God only cares about Israel, not other nations
God is sovereign over all nations and historical events, and His promises are unfailing
We can avoid all calamities if we try hard enough
God is a harsh judge without grace
questions.explanation: This chapter emphasizes God's sovereignty over all the earth, showing that He judges nations but also keeps His promises to His people, demonstrating His faithfulness.

en.reflection: How do you respond to the truth of God's sovereignty and His unfailing promises when facing difficulties or uncertainties in life?
reflectionOptions: Trust more deeply in His sovereignty
Pray for myself and my loved ones
en.prayer: Almighty God, I worship You because You are sovereign over all nations and events. Even in judgment, Your grace and faithfulness remain. Help me to trust in Your promises no matter my circumstances. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take a moment today to reflect: God is sovereign even when the world is chaotic. Let this truth bring you peace.

en.focus: God's sovereignty controls the destiny of all nations and peoples, and no one can escape His righteous judgment.

questions.question: Jeremiah 47 begins by mentioning 'Philistia.' Before which historical event did this message come?
options: Before Babylon captured Jerusalem
Before Pharaoh attacked Gaza
Before the Assyrian invasion
Before the Exodus of Israel
questions.explanation: The text explicitly states that this is 'the word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the Philistines, before Pharaoh attacked Gaza.'

questions.question: What natural phenomenon is used to describe the disaster coming from the north?
options: A burning fire
A violent earthquake
An overflowing river
Clouds covering the sky
questions.explanation: The prophet Jeremiah uses the image of 'waters rising from the north, an overflowing torrent' to describe the impending disaster that will flood the land.

questions.question: What ultimate fate will the Philistines experience?
options: They will build stronger walls to defend against enemies
They will be utterly destroyed without escape
They will cry out to God and receive His mercy
They will make a peace treaty with the invaders
questions.explanation: The text clearly indicates that God will utterly destroy Philistia; Gaza will be made bald, Ashkelon cut off, with no remnant. This judgment is executed by God Himself.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 47, concerning God's judgment on Philistia, remind us of today?
options: God's judgment is only for ancient pagan nations and irrelevant to us
God is the Lord of history, and His will will ultimately be accomplished
We can escape God's justice by our own strength
We should live in fear and avoid all enjoyment
questions.explanation: This passage shows that God is the sovereign ruler of history. His judgment is not arbitrary but flows from His righteousness, and His will will ultimately be accomplished; no nation can escape it.

en.reflection: Is there an area in your life where you need to acknowledge God's sovereignty, release your need for control, and turn to His justice and mercy?
en.prayer: Almighty Lord, You are the sovereign ruler over all nations and peoples; Your judgment is righteous and true. Help me to always fear You and acknowledge Your sovereignty in my life. May I submit to Your will and live a life pleasing to You. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take one minute today to reflect on and acknowledge God's ultimate sovereignty in one specific area of your life.

en.focus: God is a righteous judge whose judgment on sin is real and thorough, yet He is also a compassionate God who shows mercy.

questions.question: Which nation does the prophet Jeremiah prophesy God's judgment against?
options: Ammon
Moab
Edom
Philistia
questions.explanation: Jeremiah chapter 48 explicitly begins with the word of the LORD concerning Moab.

questions.question: According to the passage, what was one reason for Moab's judgment?
options: They did not keep the law
They worshipped idols and trusted in their wealth and works
They did not help the Israelites
They allied with Egypt
questions.explanation: The text indicates that Moab was judged for trusting in her works and treasures, and also for her pride.

questions.question: The passage repeatedly mentions Moab's 'shame' and being 'put to shame.' What aspect of God's judgment does this reflect?
options: God's hatred for Moab
God's unfairness towards Moab
God exposing Moab's idolatry and false sense of security
God simply punishing them
questions.explanation: Moab's shame arises because their trust in idols and achievements proved futile, revealing their emptiness as God exposed their false confidence.

questions.question: What important lesson can we learn today from God's judgment on Moab?
options: We don't need to worry about God's judgment; it's only for ancient peoples
We can rely on our achievements and wealth for true security and satisfaction
Pride and trust in false idols (whether material things or status) ultimately lead to judgment and shame
God only cares about His chosen people, not other nations
questions.explanation: Moab's example reminds us that placing our security in material possessions, achievements, or anything other than God is empty and will ultimately face God's judgment and shame.

en.reflection: Is there anything in your life today that you are overly relying on or that has taken God's place, causing you pride or complacency?
en.prayer: Righteous Lord, thank You for being a faithful God whose judgment is just and true. Please help me to examine my heart and remove any idols that cause me pride or lead me astray from You. May I rely solely on You and build my security and satisfaction in You alone. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take a moment today to list three things in your life you might be overly relying on, and pray for God to help you place them back in their proper perspective.

en.theme: God's Judgment and Mercy for Moab
en.focus: God's righteous judgment comes upon all pride and irreverence, yet His compassion also offers future hope.

questions.question: How does the prophet Jeremiah characterize Moab?
options: Their wealth
Their pride
Their wisdom
Their military strength
questions.explanation: The text repeatedly mentions Moab's 'pride,' including their arrogance, insolence, and haughtiness.

questions.question: According to the passage, what was a key reason for Moab's judgment regarding their attitude towards the LORD?
options: They built many altars
They allied with Israel
They scoffed at the LORD
They offered sacrifices to the LORD
questions.explanation: The LORD says, 'For he magnified himself against the LORD.' This indicates a lack of reverence for God, even mocking Him.

questions.question: Despite the severe judgment pronounced against Moab, what hope is expressed in the very last verse of the passage?
options: Moab will disappear from the earth forever
The judgment will cease immediately
Moab's captives will be restored in the future
God will no longer punish any nation
questions.explanation: After all the messages of judgment, the passage concludes with God's promise, 'But I will restore the fortunes of Moab in the latter days,' showing His compassion.

questions.question: What important lesson can we learn from God's judgment and ultimate mercy towards Moab?
options: God only cares about His chosen people, not gentiles
Pride and irreverence towards God inevitably bring consequences, but God still has a plan of mercy and restoration
Possessing wealth and military strength can withstand God's judgment
God is a merciless judge who never forgives sin
questions.explanation: Moab's pride and scoffing at the LORD led to judgment, but God's ultimate promise reveals His compassion and redemptive plan beyond judgment.

en.reflection: Today's passage reminds us that pride and irreverence towards God are detestable to Him. Are there areas in your life where you might be exhibiting pride or an irreverent attitude towards God?
reflectionOptions: Repent of my words and actions
en.prayer: Righteous and merciful God, I confess that at times I too harbor pride in my heart or, unknowingly, treat You with irreverence. Please forgive me and help me walk humbly in Your ways, revering Your name. Thank You, for Your mercy endures forever. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take one minute today to reflect on God's grace in your life and offer Him thanks, cultivating a humble heart.

en.theme: God's Judgment and Promise of Restoration
en.focus: God's sovereignty extends over all nations. His judgment will come upon pride and injustice, but He also promises restoration in the latter days.

questions.question: Which nation is Jeremiah primarily prophesying against in this passage?
options: Egypt
Moab
Ammon
Edom
questions.explanation: The passage begins by explicitly stating it is a prophecy concerning the Ammonites.

questions.type: Observe the sin in the passage
questions.question: What was the main sin for which the Ammonites were condemned by God?
options: Idolatry
Disregarding the Sabbath
Taking possession of Gad's inheritance
Murdering prophets
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 49:1 indicates that the Ammonites took possession of Gad's inheritance and settled in their towns.

questions.question: What attributes of God are demonstrated in the prophecy of judgment against Ammon?
options: Unconditional mercy, no judgment
Absolute justice and sovereignty, none can escape
Punishment only for pagans, not for His chosen people
Concern only for Israel, not other nations
questions.explanation: The text shows God as the LORD of hosts, who judges Ammon's wickedness with justice, from which no one can escape, demonstrating His sovereignty over all nations.

questions.type: Understand the hope in the passage
questions.question: Despite the prophecy of judgment, what promise does God give concerning Ammon's future?
options: They will be completely destroyed and never restored
They will become slaves to Israel
In the latter days, God will restore the fortunes of Ammon
They will make a covenant with Israel and worship God together
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 49:6 clearly states, 'But afterward I will restore the fortunes of the Ammonites,' showing God's grace and promise of restoration even amidst judgment.

en.reflection: Are there any areas of pride or injustice in your life that require humble repentance and trust in God's sovereignty?
en.prayer: Almighty Father, You are the sovereign Ruler over all, Your judgments are righteous, and Your promises are faithful. Help me to examine my heart and remove all pride and injustice. May I trust more deeply in Your sovereignty and grace, knowing that even in difficulties, You have a plan for restoration. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Spend some time today reflecting on any pride in your life that prevents you from fully trusting God, and confess it to Him.

en.focus: Even in judgment, God is sovereign and ultimately brings forth promises of restoration.

questions.question: How does the LORD declare He will deal with Edom?
options: Make them a powerful nation
Destroy Edom's wisdom and warriors completely
Allow them to live peacefully with surrounding nations
Grant them abundant harvests
questions.explanation: The LORD declares He will destroy Edom's wise men, leaving them with no understanding, and strike down their warriors.

questions.question: How does the passage describe Edom's pride and self-reliance?
options: They built magnificent cities
They lived in rocky strongholds and thought no one could dislodge them
They possessed a mighty army and chariots
They formed strong alliances with other nations
questions.explanation: Edom was proud because they lived in rocky strongholds, believing themselves secure from attack.

questions.type: Understand the universality of God's judgment
questions.question: God's judgment on Edom reveals His principles for dealing with what kind of people?
options: Only those who worship idols
Only unbelievers who do not know God
All who are rebellious, proud, and self-reliant
Only those who previously attacked Israel
questions.explanation: God's judgment on Edom demonstrates His righteous judgment on all who are proud, self-reliant, and rebellious against His will.

questions.type: Understand the hope in the passage
questions.question: Beyond the message of judgment, to whom does Jeremiah 49:11 offer hope?
options: Edom's orphans and widows
All the exiled Israelites
Jeremiah's family
Those who followed Edom
questions.explanation: Despite the severe judgment on Edom, God promises to preserve their orphans and widows, showing His compassion.

en.reflection: In what area today are you relying on your own wisdom or strength instead of fully trusting God?
en.prayer: Dear Lord, You are the sovereign God whose judgment is righteous and whose mercy endures. Forgive me for times when I rely on my own wisdom and strength instead of fully trusting You. Help me to humbly surrender everything to You, confident in Your care. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take a minute today to think about something you need to release to God, and pray about it.

en.focus: God's judgment on the nations reveals His sovereignty and justice, often intertwined with hope for the future.

questions.question: Which city-state's fate is prophesied at the beginning of this passage?
options: Damascus
Kedar
Hazor
Elam
questions.explanation: The first prophecy in the passage is against Damascus, describing its coming anguish and distress.

questions.question: What specific action do the inhabitants of Kedar and Hazor take when faced with the LORD's judgment?
options: They gather wealth to flee
They seek help from neighboring nations
They flee and hide in deep places
They build strong walls for defense
questions.explanation: The LORD commands an attack on Kedar, and the inhabitants of Hazor are described as fleeing and hiding in deep places.

questions.question: Although Jeremiah 49 primarily speaks of God's judgment, what hope is revealed in the prophecy concerning Elam?
options: Elam will become stronger than before
God will restore the fortunes of Elam's captives
Elam will form an alliance with Israel
Elam will be completely spared from judgment
questions.explanation: After prophesying destruction for Elam, God declares, 'But in the latter days I will restore the fortunes of Elam.' This indicates God's mercy and promise of restoration.

questions.question: How does this passage help us understand the attributes of God?
options: God only cares for His chosen people, not other nations
God is a righteous judge, and His sovereignty extends over all the earth
God always acts immediately in judgment, never offering a chance for repentance
