questions.question: When God promises to restore His people, what response does He expect from them?
options: To remain silent and wait for God to do everything
To turn from their wickedness and ask God to fulfill His promises
To work hard on their own without God's help
To complain about God's delay in acting
questions.explanation: The passage indicates that even though God initiates the promise, He still expects His people to inquire of Him for these things to be done for them, and to turn from all their detestable practices.

en.reflection: In what area of your life do you most need God's Spirit to renew you today, so you are more willing to obey Him?
reflectionOptions: Letting go of a stubborn habit
Loving and forgiving more in a relationship
en.prayer: Faithful God, thank You for promising a new heart and a new spirit. May Your Holy Spirit continue to renew my life today, removing stubbornness and disobedience from my heart, and making me willing to walk in Your statutes. May my life bring glory to Your holy name. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take a quiet moment to pray for one area of your life where you find it hardest to obey God, asking Him for a heart of flesh and His Spirit to renew you.

en.focus: Even in seemingly hopeless situations, God's power can bring full restoration and new life.

questions.question: Where did God lead Ezekiel, and what did he see?
options: A valley full of living people
A valley full of dry bones
A temple under construction
A city besieged by enemies
questions.explanation: The Spirit of the LORD led Ezekiel to a valley filled with very dry bones, showing him the desperate state of Israel.

questions.question: God asked Ezekiel, “Son of man, can these bones live?” How did Ezekiel respond?
options: He immediately said, “Yes, they can.”
He answered, “No, they cannot.”
He replied, “Sovereign LORD, you alone know.”
He remained silent and did not answer.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel humbly deferred to God's sovereignty, saying, “Sovereign LORD, you alone know,” rather than relying on his own judgment.

questions.question: What does the vision of the dry bones primarily symbolize?
options: The physical resurrection of the people of Israel
The permanent dispersion of Israel among the nations
God's restoration of the people of Israel from exile to new life
God's judgment on all unbelieving Gentiles
questions.explanation: God explicitly states that the dry bones represent the whole house of Israel, and He will bring them out of their graves, restore them to the land of Israel, and put His Spirit in them.

questions.question: How does this vision encourage us when facing despair or impossibilities in life?
options: If we try hard enough, we can change anything.
We can rely on our own wisdom to solve problems.
Even in the most hopeless situations, God's power can bring supernatural restoration and life.
We should accept the status quo and give up all efforts.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37 highlights God's power beyond all limitations, showing He can bring dry bones to life. This reminds us that no matter how desperate a situation seems, God can bring miraculous change and new life.

en.reflection: Is there an area or relationship in your life that feels like “dry bones,” almost beyond hope of restoration?
en.prayer: Sovereign LORD, You are the God who brings dry bones to life. I confess that there are situations in my life that seem hopeless, like “dry bones” to me. I ask You to intervene with Your mighty power, bringing new life and Your Spirit. Help me to trust You, knowing that even in the most desperate times, You can do wonders. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take a minute today to quietly surrender a specific area of despair in your life to God, and meditate on the thought: “Sovereign LORD, You alone know, and You can bring dry bones to life.”

en.focus: God promises to gather His scattered people, unite them as one, and dwell among them forever.

questions.question: How many sticks was Ezekiel commanded to take to symbolize the two main parts of Israel?
options: One
Two
Three
Four
questions.explanation: God commanded Ezekiel to take two sticks: one for Judah and his associates, and the other for Joseph and his associates.

questions.question: What does it symbolize when God makes the two sticks into one?
options: The kingdom of Judah will completely absorb the kingdom of Israel
The Israelites will again split into two separate kingdoms
The northern and southern kingdoms will reunite and no longer be divided
All foreign nations will become part of Israel
questions.explanation: The two sticks symbolize the reunification of the northern and southern kingdoms into one nation, no longer divided.

questions.type: Observe the eternal nature of God's promise
questions.question: What is repeatedly emphasized about God's covenant with His people in this passage?
options: It is temporary and can be revoked at any time
It applies only to a few pious Israelites
It is a covenant of peace and an everlasting covenant
It only involves material blessings
questions.explanation: God promises to make a covenant of peace with them, an everlasting covenant, and to set His sanctuary among them forever.

questions.question: What insight does this passage offer for unity in the church today?
options: Unity is impossible because people always have disagreements
Unity requires us to eliminate all cultural differences
True unity is ultimately God's work, achieved through His Spirit and truth
Unity will naturally happen if the church grows large enough
questions.explanation: Just as God promised to unite Israel, unity in the church today is God's work, as He unites us through Christ and dwells among us.

en.reflection: In what areas do you currently experience division or disharmony? How are you willing to respond to God's desire for unity?
reflectionOptions: Pray for unity in the church
Take initiative to reconcile with someone
Let go of personal biases or stubbornness
en.prayer: Faithful God, thank You for Your promise to gather and unite Your people. Please bring about such unity in my life and in Your church. Help me to lay aside division and live in peace, so that Your name may be glorified. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, specifically pray for your church or for a strained relationship you know, asking God to bring unity and harmony.

en.focus: God's sovereignty over all nations will be displayed through His judgment for His holy name, so that all nations will know Him.

questions.question: God's word came to Ezekiel concerning the leader of which nation?
options: Egypt
Babylon
Gog, of the land of Magog
Persia
questions.explanation: The word of the Lord came to Ezekiel, instructing him to set his face against Gog, of the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.

questions.question: What does the passage indicate as Gog's purpose for attacking Israel?
options: To seek a peaceful alliance
To seize plunder and loot
To spread their pagan beliefs
To help Israel against other enemies
questions.explanation: Gog is described as coming up against a 'land of unwalled villages' to 'seize plunder and carry off loot'.

questions.question: What is God's primary purpose in allowing Gog to attack Israel?
options: To punish Israel for its sins
To display His holy name and power to the nations
To test Israel's faith
To make Israel more dependent on foreign allies
questions.explanation: God clearly states that He will make Himself known in the sight of many nations through His judgment on Gog, so that they will know that He is the Lord.

questions.question: What is the most important lesson we can learn about God from this passage today?
options: God only cares about the destiny of the nation of Israel
God does not intervene in worldly political conflicts
Regardless of global turmoil, God is always in control and works for His glory
People can defeat all enemies by their own strength
questions.explanation: This passage powerfully demonstrates that even amidst seemingly chaotic international conflicts, God remains in control and will act according to His will, ultimately making His supreme sovereignty known to all nations.

en.reflection: How does this passage help you to re-examine God's sovereignty and His plan for your life when the world is in turmoil or facing challenges?
reflectionOptions: It reminds me that God is in control, reducing my anxiety
It helps me trust in God's justice and ultimate victory
It inspires me to seek God's guidance and protection
en.prayer: Almighty Father, thank You that You are the Sovereign Lord over all nations and events, and no one can thwart Your purposes. When the world is full of unrest, help me to fix my eyes on You, trusting that You will execute judgment and salvation for Your holy name. May my life also bring glory to Your holy name. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, when you encounter news or events that cause you worry, pause and reflect: 'God is in control!' and pray about it.

en.focus: God will reveal His holy name to all nations through the judgment of nations and the restoration of His people.

questions.question: In God's prophecy against Gog, how does He describe His action towards Gog?
options: He will make Gog wealthy and strong
He will lead Gog to attack Israel
He will establish a covenant with Gog
He will cause Gog and Israel to live in peace
questions.explanation: God explicitly states that He will lead Gog to attack Israel as part of His divine plan.

questions.question: After God defeats Gog, what are the people of Israel required to do?
options: Mourn for Gog for seven years
Bury Gog's bodies and burn their weapons for fuel
Sign a peace treaty with Gog's remaining forces
Collect Gog's treasures and distribute them to neighboring nations
questions.explanation: The text describes Israel spending seven months burying Gog's bodies and seven years burning their weapons for fuel, thereby cleansing the land and demonstrating God's judgment.

questions.question: What is God's primary purpose in defeating Gog?
options: To make Israel a global superpower
To make the people of Israel forget their past sins
To make all nations know that He is the LORD and to manifest His holy name
To completely annihilate Gog's army
questions.explanation: God repeatedly emphasizes that His purpose in defeating Gog is to make Himself known as the LORD to all nations and to manifest His holy name.

questions.question: Why does God say He will no longer hide His face from the house of Israel?
options: Because the people of Israel have become completely holy
Because God is tired of judging them
Because He has poured out His Spirit on them
Because the people of Israel achieved military victory
questions.explanation: God promises not to hide His face from Israel anymore because He has poured out His Spirit on them, which is central to His restoration of their relationship.

en.reflection: Today's passage reminds us of God's faithfulness and the manifestation of His glory. How can you, through your words and actions, help others recognize God's glory and faithfulness in your daily life?
en.prayer: Almighty God, I thank You for being a faithful God who keeps Your covenant, and Your name is greatly to be feared. Please help me to live out Your character in my daily life, so that my life may be a testimony to Your glory, and more people may come to know Your greatness and love through me. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, think of a concrete way to share God's faithfulness or grace in your life with someone around you.

en.theme: Vision of the Temple: Hope in God's Presence
en.focus: God grants His exiled people solid hope for His presence and restoration through the vision of the temple.

questions.question: At what point in time did Ezekiel see this vision?
options: When the Israelites were first exiled to Babylon
Fourteen years after the fall of Jerusalem
On the hundredth anniversary of the temple's completion
After the death of King Nebuchadnezzar
questions.explanation: The text clearly states that the vision occurred “in the fourteenth year after Jerusalem had been captured.”

questions.type: Observe the details of the vision
questions.question: In the vision, which part of the temple did the man first measure with Ezekiel?
options: The altar
The outer gate facing east
The Most Holy Place
The inner sanctuary of the temple
questions.explanation: The man first measured the gate facing east, which is the outer east gate, detailing its dimensions.

questions.question: What was the primary significance of this detailed temple vision for the exiled Israelites at that time?
options: To encourage them to quickly return to Jerusalem to rebuild the temple
To predict a longer period of exile for them
To give them hope concerning God's presence and future restoration
To point out that their past sins led to the temple's destruction
questions.explanation: In the desperate situation of the temple's destruction and the people's exile, God gave such a detailed vision to show them that He had not abandoned them, and His presence and future restoration were certain hope.
questions.evidence: Ezekiel 40:1 (timing), detailed description of the entire vision

questions.question: How does this passage encourage you when you experience 'exile-like' difficulties or disappointments in your life?
options: It reminds me that God's judgment is just
It helps me understand that God is always with me and has a plan for restoration
It encourages me to strive to escape difficulties by my own strength
It tells me that problems will resolve themselves if I just wait
questions.explanation: Like the exiled people, even in the darkest moments, God reveals His presence and future restoration through a vision. This reminds us that no matter our circumstances, God has His plan and hope for us.
questions.evidence: Ezekiel 40:1-2 (context and purpose of the vision)

en.reflection: Is there an 'exile-like' situation in your life where you need to rediscover hope in God's presence and restoration?
en.prayer: Lord, thank You for giving hope in despair. When I feel discouraged or uncertain about the future, please help me to see Your presence and trust in Your plan for rebuilding and restoration. May Your Spirit guide me to look to You in every circumstance. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Spend some time today meditating on the hope God provides in this scripture, and pray to Him to reveal His presence and guidance in the challenges you are currently facing.

en.theme: The Temple Vision: God's Presence and Order
en.focus: God reveals His glorious presence in the Temple to Ezekiel, emphasizing the importance of holiness and order.

questions.question: In the portico of the temple, where were the burnt offerings, sin offerings, and guilt offerings slaughtered?
options: Beside the altar
Beside the pillars
Beside the entrance
Beside the tables
questions.explanation: The passage states there were tables in the portico used for slaughtering these offerings.

questions.question: What was the relationship between the width of the inner sanctuary (Most Holy Place) and the main hall (Holy Place)?
options: The main hall was twice as wide as the inner sanctuary
The inner sanctuary and main hall were of the same width
The inner sanctuary was twice as wide as the main hall
The main hall was half as wide as the inner sanctuary
questions.explanation: The text clearly indicates that both the inner sanctuary and the main hall were twenty cubits wide, showing they had the same width.

questions.question: What is the primary emphasis of God's detailed revelation of the Temple's dimensions and structure?
options: People can build God's dwelling however they wish
God's dwelling requires strict holiness and order
The temple design was for the Israelites to conduct business
These details merely demonstrate God's power
questions.explanation: The meticulous details of the Temple's dimensions and structure underscore God's demand for holiness and order; everything must be built according to His will.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel's vision of the Temple inform our understanding of God's presence with us today?
options: God is only present in magnificent buildings
God requires order and holiness in our lives
We don't need to pay attention to personal life details
Only priests can draw near to God
questions.explanation: This vision reveals God as a holy and orderly God. His presence demands holiness and order in our lives, even though New Testament believers are God's temple.

en.reflection: The Temple vision emphasizes God's holy presence. In what areas of your life today do you need deeper holiness or more order to better reflect God's glory?
en.prayer: Holy Lord, thank You for revealing Your requirements for holiness and order through Ezekiel's vision. Help me to be a dwelling place pleasing to You, glorifying You in my thoughts, words, and actions. May Your presence fill me and guide me to live a holy and orderly life. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Spend five minutes today reflecting on one area of your life where you desire more order or holiness, and pray to God about it.

en.theme: Vision of the Sanctuary and Its Meaning
en.focus: Ezekiel’s vision of the sanctuary reminds us of God’s desire to dwell among His people and provides a way for them to worship Him.

questions.question: To which side of the temple complex was the prophet Ezekiel brought to examine the chambers?
options: East side
South side
West side
North side
questions.explanation: Ezekiel was brought to the 'north side' to examine the chambers and their structure.

questions.question: What was the purpose of the chambers Ezekiel saw?
options: Dwellings for kings
Rooms for priests to eat and store holy things
Meeting halls for the people
Watchtowers on the city walls
questions.explanation: The text clearly states these were 'holy chambers' for priests to 'eat the most holy things' and where 'the most holy things' were stored.

questions.question: What do the detailed measurements and descriptions of these chambers primarily symbolize?
options: God's demand for perfect architectural design
God's strict control over the lives of His people
God's emphasis on holiness and order, and His desire for fellowship
God's preparation of future material wealth
questions.explanation: The precise measurements and divisions of the temple area in the vision emphasize God's holy nature, the boundaries between Him and sin, and His desire to dwell with His people in order.

questions.question: How does the sanctuary depicted in Ezekiel 42 help us understand God's character more deeply?
options: God only cares about magnificent buildings
God is distant and unapproachable to humans
God is holy, orderly, and full of grace, desiring a relationship with His people
God is fickle and unpredictable
questions.explanation: The vision of the sanctuary reveals God's holiness and His emphasis on order, but also His provision for His people to draw near to Him, showing He is gracious and desires to dwell among them.

en.reflection: Today's scripture reminds us of God's holiness and His desire to be with us. In your daily life, how are you practicing drawing near to God and living a holy life?
reflectionOptions: Spending more time in Bible reading and prayer
Being more careful with words and actions
Participating more actively in church service
en.prayer: Holy Lord, thank You for showing me more of Your character and Your love for us through Ezekiel’s vision. Please help me to live a holy life and draw closer to You each day. May my life bring glory to Your name. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Spend 5 minutes today in quiet reflection on God's presence in your life, and ask Him to help you live a holy life in one specific area.

en.theme: God's Glory Returns to the Temple
en.focus: God's glory returns to His Temple, signifying His desire to dwell again with His people and establish norms for worship.

questions.question: From which direction did Ezekiel see the glory of God enter the temple?
options: North
South
East
West
questions.explanation: Ezekiel saw the glory of God enter the temple by the gate facing east.

questions.question: After God's glory entered the temple, what did God say to Ezekiel?
options: His temple will never again be defiled
This is the place of His throne and the place for the soles of His feet
He will judge all rebellious people
He will give new laws and commandments
questions.explanation: God declared that this is the place of His throne and the place for the soles of His feet, where He will dwell among the Israelites forever.

questions.type: Understand the purpose of the temple
questions.question: What was the main purpose for God asking Ezekiel to show the house's design to the house of Israel?
options: So they could build a larger temple
So they might be ashamed of their iniquities
So they could learn new architectural techniques
So they would understand God's majesty and power
questions.explanation: God said to show them the design of the temple so that they might be ashamed of their iniquities and keep all His ordinances.

questions.question: What is the significance for us today that God's glory returned to the temple and established norms for worship?
options: God only dwells with us in specific buildings
We should focus more on external rituals and rules
God is holy, desires to dwell with us, and calls us to live holy lives
We don't need to follow any rules, just worship from the heart
questions.explanation: This shows that God is holy and desires to dwell with His people, calling them to live holy lives in response to Him.

en.reflection: In what area of your life do you most need to invite God's glory to descend, cleanse, and take control today?
en.prayer: Holy Lord, thank You that Your glory returns and desires to dwell with us. Cleanse my heart and remove anything displeasing to You. May my life be a dwelling place for Your glory and presence. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Spend some quiet time today in prayer, inviting God to cleanse a corner of your heart and fill it with His glory.

en.theme: A Call to Holiness and Priestly Duties
en.focus: God calls His servants to live holy lives and faithfully carry out the duties He entrusts to them, to glorify His name.

questions.question: After the eastern gate of the temple was shut, who was permitted to enter or sit there?
options: Ordinary Levites
The Prince of Israel
Any worshipping commoner
Foreign priests
questions.explanation: The text clearly states that only the Prince of Israel could sit inside the eastern gate to eat bread before the LORD.

questions.question: What serious error did the LORD God specifically point out that His people and priests had committed in their past service?
options: They did not offer enough sacrifices
They did not build a magnificent temple
They allowed uncircumcised foreigners, uncircumcised in heart, to enter the sanctuary and defile God's temple
They failed to teach the law to the people
questions.explanation: God severely rebuked them for allowing unclean foreigners to enter and serve in the sanctuary, thereby defiling His temple.

questions.question: The descendants of Zadok were chosen to be priests, distinct from other Levites. What special responsibilities were given to them?
options: Only guarding the temple gates
Managing the temple finances and offerings
Drawing near to the LORD to minister to Him, and teaching the people the distinction between the holy and the common, and the clean and the unclean
Leading the army into battle
questions.explanation: The sons of Zadok were chosen not only to draw near to God and minister to Him but also to teach the people to distinguish between the holy and the common, and the clean and the unclean.

questions.question: What important reminder does this passage offer us today?
options: We should strictly separate social classes and only associate with specific groups
We should strive for outward ritual perfection to please God
God values holiness greatly, and His servants (including believers today) are called to be set apart from the world in word and deed, serving Him faithfully
As long as we believe, we don't need to be concerned about holiness in our lives
questions.explanation: God's requirement for holiness is constant. As New Testament believers, we are called to be a royal priesthood and should live out a life of consecration, faithfully serving God.

en.reflection: Today's passage reminds us that God is holy, and He calls His servants to be holy as well. In what area of your daily life do you feel you most need to live out a more consecrated life to honor God?
reflectionOptions: The media content I consume (what I watch, listen to, and engage with)
My attitude towards money and material possessions
en.prayer: Holy Lord, thank You for choosing me to be Your child and a royal priest. Please help me, by the power of the Holy Spirit, to live a life set apart in my thoughts, words, and actions. May my life bring glory to Your name and be a beautiful testimony of You. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Spend some time today meditating on a scripture about holiness (e.g., 1 Peter 1:15–16) and ask God to help you live a holy life.

en.theme: The Holy Portion and the Prince's Duty
en.focus: God establishes a holy center and righteous governance for His people to ensure His presence and blessings.

questions.question: When dividing the land, which portion did God first set aside as 'holy'?
options: The prince's portion
The portion for the Levites
The sacred portion for the LORD
The land for the common people
questions.explanation: The text states that a portion of land is first to be offered to the LORD as a 'holy portion,' containing the sanctuary.

questions.question: What specific instructions and requirements does God give to the prince of Israel?
options: Increase taxes to build more palaces
Dispossess the people to accumulate personal wealth
Put away violence and oppression, and execute justice and righteousness
Arbitrarily change laws to suit his rule
questions.explanation: God explicitly instructs the prince to 'put away violence and oppression, and execute justice and righteousness; stop dispossessing my people,' which means acting with fairness and justice.

questions.question: What is the primary responsibility of the prince during the festivals?
options: To organize grand feasts for nobles
To provide the sacrifices for burnt offerings, grain offerings, and peace offerings
To announce new laws and regulations
To review the army and display power
questions.explanation: The text indicates that the prince is responsible for providing the animals for 'burnt offerings, grain offerings, and peace offerings' during the festivals, New Moons, Sabbaths, and all appointed feasts.

questions.question: Ezekiel 45 emphasizes holiness and justice. How does this apply to our lives today?
options: Only rulers and priests need to be concerned with justice
God's people should pursue holiness and justice in both personal and public spheres
Observing formal worship is sufficient for us
Justice was only an Old Testament requirement, irrelevant to New Testament believers
questions.explanation: While addressed to Israel's prince and people, the core principle—that God's people should pursue holiness and justice in all aspects of life (personal conduct and communal governance)—remains relevant for us today.

en.reflection: In which area of your life today can you more actively pursue holiness and justice, so that God's presence and blessings may be more evident?
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for being a holy and righteous God. Please help me to live a life of holiness, worthy of You, in my thoughts, words, and actions. Grant me courage and wisdom to actively pursue justice within my sphere of influence, caring for those who are oppressed. May Your will be done on earth as it is in heaven. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, pray about one situation (big or small) that you perceive as unjust, and consider if there's a small, concrete action you can take regarding it.

en.theme: Worship and Service in the Temple
en.focus: God establishes order and holiness in worship and service for His people, reminding them of His presence and grace.

questions.question: What was the specific regulation for the inner court gate facing east on the Sabbath and the New Moon?
options: It had to be completely closed, allowing no one to enter
It had to be opened, and a burnt offering presented
Only the prince was allowed to enter and offer sacrifices
Only the priests and Levites were allowed to enter and offer sacrifices
questions.explanation: The passage clearly states that on the Sabbath and the New Moon, the inner court gate facing east must be opened, and a burnt offering presented.

questions.question: How were the sacrificial meats to be distributed and prepared?
options: All sacrificial meat had to be completely burned and could not be eaten
Priests could eat all sacrificial meat, but the people could not
Priests, Levites, and the people could eat a portion, but it had to be cooked in specific areas
Sacrificial meat could be taken home and eaten freely
questions.explanation: The text mentions specific kitchens for the priests, Levites, and the people to cook sacrificial meat, indicating that the meat was prepared and distributed in designated areas.

questions.question: What is the primary message reflected by these detailed regulations concerning temple worship?
options: God's preference for elaborate rituals and rules
God's strict demands on Israel to punish their past sins
God requires order, holiness, and consecration in the worship of Him
Obeying rituals automatically guarantees God's blessing
questions.explanation: These detailed regulations, whether about the opening and closing of gates or the types and handling of sacrifices, highlight God's demand for order, holiness, and consecration in worship.

questions.question: How can we apply God's emphasis on worship from this passage to our church life today?
options: Churches should reinstate the Old Testament sacrificial system
Order and holiness in church worship are important for focusing our worship on God
Worship is a purely personal act, unrelated to the church community
Any form of worship is acceptable as long as one is sincere
questions.explanation: While we no longer offer animal sacrifices, God's requirements for order and holiness in worship still apply. An orderly and holy worship environment helps congregants draw closer to God.
questions.evidence: Ezekiel 46:1–24 (applying core principles from the text)

en.reflection: Today's passage reminds us that God values order and holiness. In your daily life, in what ways can you better demonstrate reverence and consecration to God?
reflectionOptions: Prepare more thoughtfully for Sunday worship
en.prayer: Dear Lord, thank You for being a holy and orderly God. Please help me to approach worship and service with reverence and consecration. May my life reflect my devotion to You. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take some time today to thoughtfully organize a place that often gets cluttered (e.g., your desk or a corner of a room), reminding yourself that God delights in order.

en.focus: The life-giving water flowing from the temple brings healing and abundance, foreshadowing the vitality of God's salvation.

questions.question: From which direction did Ezekiel see the water flowing from the temple?
options: From under the threshold of the east gate
From under the threshold of the west gate
From under the north wall
From under the south wall
questions.explanation: The text clearly states the water was flowing out from under the threshold of the temple toward the east.

questions.question: How did the depth of the water change?
options: From ankle-deep to knee-deep
From knee-deep to waist-deep
From ankle-deep to waist-deep
From ankle-deep to a river that could not be crossed
questions.explanation: The water progressed from ankle-deep, to knee-deep, to waist-deep, and finally to a river that could not be crossed.

questions.question: What effects did this water flowing from the temple have?
options: It made the sea saltier
It caused trees to wither
It made the Dead Sea fresh, bringing fish and life to its banks
It made the land barren
questions.explanation: This water made the Dead Sea (eastern sea) fresh, leading to an abundance of fish and lush trees along its banks that bore fruit monthly, with leaves for healing.

questions.question: Which kind of healing and nourishment from this river of life do you most need today?
options: Relief from spiritual dryness and weariness
Restoration in strained or broken relationships
Clarity and direction for an uncertain future
Strength and healing for physical ailments
questions.explanation: This life-giving water symbolises God's grace and the work of the Holy Spirit, which can refresh every aspect of our lives, bringing renewal and healing.

en.reflection: What are the 'dead seas' or 'barren places' in your life that you long for God's living water to touch and renew?
reflectionOptions: A persistent worry you can't shake off
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for being the source of life. Let Your living water flow into every corner of my life, healing my dry spirit, renewing my thoughts, and nourishing my soul. May I be like a tree by the river, bearing fruit often, with leaves for healing. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take a moment today to be still and meditate on Jesus as the fountain of living water. Ask Him to pour out His Spirit upon you to refresh your life.

en.theme: Glory and Order of the New City
en.focus: God prepares an ordered dwelling place full of His presence for His people, demonstrating His faithfulness and glory.

questions.question: Which tribe received the northernmost boundary in the distribution of land?
options: Reuben
Dan
Naphtali
Asher
questions.explanation: The tribe of Dan's territory was located at the extreme north, bordering the northern frontier.

questions.question: What was the size of the holy district (the sacred portion) set apart for the LORD?
options: 25,000 cubits long and 10,000 cubits wide
25,000 cubits long and 25,000 cubits wide
50,000 cubits long and 50,000 cubits wide
10,000 cubits long and 10,000 cubits wide
questions.explanation: The holy district dedicated to the LORD was a square, with sides measuring 25,000 cubits.

questions.question: What is significant about the naming of the gates of the new city?
options: They are named after their builders
They are named after the twelve tribes of Israel
They are named after the twelve apostles
They are named after twelve famous mountains in the Bible
questions.explanation: The new city has twelve gates, each named after one of the tribes of Israel, symbolizing God's people within it.

questions.question: What core message does the final name of the new city, 'The LORD Is There,' convey?
options: People can change God's plans at will
God's glory will forever depart from His people
God's perpetual presence with His people is their meaning and glory
Only a few select people can enter this city
questions.explanation: This name emphasizes that God's presence is the most central and important feature of the city, its glory and purpose.

en.reflection: How do you see God’s faithfulness and presence in the glory and order He prepares for His people?
reflectionOptions: My life has hope because of God's presence
God brings order to my chaos
I trust God to faithfully fulfill His promises
en.prayer: Faithful Lord, thank You for preparing such a glorious and ordered dwelling place for Your people. Help me to live in Your presence each day, understanding that You are my 'The LORD Is There'. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, spend one minute meditating on the phrase 'The LORD Is There' and give thanks for it.

en.focus: Even when living in a foreign land and under pressure, we can, by God's grace, faithfully uphold our beliefs and make wise choices.

questions.question: What was happening in Judah, Daniel's homeland, when he and his friends were taken captive to Babylon?
options: A period of peace and prosperity
A widespread famine and disease
It was besieged and conquered by Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon
It formed an alliance with Egypt against Babylon
questions.explanation: The text clearly states that in the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and besieged it.

questions.question: What Babylonian names did Ashpenaz, the chief of the court officials, give to Daniel and his three friends?
options: Belshazzar, Meshech, Abednego, Hananiah
Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, Azariah
Belteshazzar, Shadrach, Meshach, Abednego
Shadrach, Meshach, Abednego, Daniel
questions.explanation: Daniel was named Belteshazzar, Hananiah was named Shadrach, Mishael was named Meshach, and Azariah was named Abednego.

questions.question: What was the main reason Daniel and his friends refused the king's food?
options: They did not like the taste of Babylonian food
They believed the king's food was unhealthy
They wanted to protest the king through fasting
They did not want to 'defile' themselves with the king's food, likely involving religious dietary laws or food offered to idols
questions.explanation: Daniel 'resolved not to defile himself with the royal food and wine,' indicating their refusal stemmed from their faith and commitment to the Law, avoiding pagan practices or unclean foods.

questions.question: From the experience of Daniel and his friends, what can we learn today about maintaining faith in a different culture or under pressure?
options: It's acceptable to temporarily abandon faith principles for survival
It's fine to be unfaithful to God internally as long as it's not public
Even in adverse circumstances, we should, by God's grace, courageously make choices aligned with our faith
Completely isolate ourselves from the mainstream culture to avoid all contact
questions.explanation: Daniel and his friends, in a foreign cultural environment, bravely resolved to uphold their faith principles and sought wise ways to practice them, ultimately receiving God's blessing.

en.reflection: In your daily life, are there times or situations where you find it challenging to uphold your faith principles?
reflectionOptions: Conflicts of values in social circles
en.prayer: Faithful Lord, thank You for the grace and wisdom You displayed through Daniel and his friends. Please help me to stand firm in Your word today, even amidst challenges. Grant me discernment and courage to glorify Your name in all circumstances. In Jesus' name, I pray, Amen.
en.action: In one decision or interaction today, intentionally choose a way that honors God, even if it requires a little courage.

en.focus: Even in seemingly desperate situations, God is in control and willing to reveal mysteries to those who seek Him.

questions.question: What did King Nebuchadnezzar demand of his magicians and enchanters?
options: To build him a new city of Babylon
To interpret his dream, but first to tell him the dream itself
To write a new law governing the whole nation
To predict the future and bring him good fortune
questions.explanation: King Nebuchadnezzar demanded that the wise men not only interpret his dream but, more importantly, first tell him what the dream was.

questions.question: When the king demanded that the magicians and enchanters tell him the dream and its interpretation, what was their response?
options: They immediately told him the dream and its interpretation
They asked the king for more time to think
They stated that no one could meet the king's demand except the gods
They suggested the king consult other wise men
questions.explanation: The wise men responded that no man on earth could possibly tell the king his dream, only the gods, who do not dwell among humans, could do so.

questions.question: What can we learn from the dialogue between the king and the wise men?
options: Human wisdom and ability are limitless
God alone can reveal hidden mysteries
All answers can be found by diligent searching
There are no true mysteries in the world
questions.explanation: This dialogue clearly demonstrates that earthly wisdom cannot reveal divine mysteries; only God Himself can reveal them.

questions.question: After Daniel learned of the king's decree, what request did he make to the king?
options: He asked the king for wealth
He asked the king to pardon the wise men
He asked the king for time, so he could ask God for the mystery
He asked the king to make him the new chief advisor
questions.explanation: Daniel requested time from the king so that he might go to the God of heaven and ask for the revelation of the mystery.

en.reflection: Is there a 'mystery' or a difficult situation in your life today where you feel helpless and need God's special revelation and help?
en.prayer: Almighty Father, You are the God who reveals all mysteries. I confess my limited wisdom, and I often feel helpless facing many unknowns and difficulties. I pray that You would reveal Your will and path to me, just as You did for Daniel. Help me to trust in You in my struggles and seek Your help. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, pray about one area in your life where you feel confused or helpless, asking God to show you His way.

en.focus: God is the revealer of mysteries and the sovereign ruler of all things. He is worthy of all our praise and trust.

questions.question: After hearing the king's demand, whom did Daniel first seek help from?
options: The Babylonian magicians
The palace guards
His companions Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah
Prayed to God alone
questions.explanation: Daniel first went to his house and told his companions Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, seeking their prayer support.

questions.question: What did Daniel and his companions pray for from the God of heaven?
options: For the king to forget his dream
For the king to change his mind about demanding an interpretation
To show mercy so that they would not perish with the rest of the wise men of Babylon
For Daniel to receive a higher position and reward
questions.explanation: They prayed for the God of heaven to show mercy and reveal this mystery so that Daniel and his companions would not perish with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.

questions.question: When Daniel praised God, what attributes of God did he emphasize?
options: God controls time, changing times and seasons
God gives wisdom to the wise and knowledge to the discerning
God reveals deep and hidden things and knows what is in the darkness
All of the above
questions.explanation: Daniel praised God as the one who controls time, gives wisdom, reveals mysteries, and knows all that is hidden.

questions.type: Understand Daniel's declaration to the king
questions.question: Daniel declared to the king who could reveal the king's dream and its interpretation?
options: Only I, Daniel, can do it
No one can do it
Only there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries
The Babylonian wise men will eventually find the answer
questions.explanation: Daniel clearly told the king that no wise man, enchanter, magician, or diviner on earth could reveal this mystery to the king, but only there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries.

en.reflection: Is there any 'mystery' in your life that you feel confused about or need God to reveal? How are you willing to trust God?
reflectionOptions: Pray for wisdom from God regarding a specific difficulty
Learn to wait on God in uncertain matters
Acknowledge your limitations and let God be in control
en.prayer: Almighty Father, You are the God who reveals mysteries and governs all things. Thank You for revealing all deep and hidden things. Help me to trust in Your wisdom and sovereignty in confusion and uncertainty, knowing that You are in control of everything. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, pray about one thing that confuses you, ask God to reveal His will, and trust in His guidance.

en.focus: God controls history, and His kingdom will endure forever, surpassing all earthly, temporary powers.

questions.question: In King Nebuchadnezzar's dream, what materials were mixed together for the feet and toes of the great statue?
options: Gold and silver
Bronze and iron
Iron and clay
Silver and clay
questions.explanation: The feet and toes of the statue were a mixture of iron and clay, symbolizing a divided yet mixed kingdom.

questions.question: When Daniel explained the dream to King Nebuchadnezzar, whose ability to reveal mysteries did he emphasize?
options: The wisdom of the magicians
The magic of the enchanters
The revelation from the God of heaven
The authority of the king
questions.explanation: Daniel clearly stated that only the God of heaven can reveal mysteries and show what will happen in the future.

questions.question: What happened to the great statue when the “stone cut out by no human hand” struck it?
options: It was absorbed by the statue
It struck the feet of the statue, shattering it completely
It became a great mountain and filled the whole earth
It was crushed by the iron feet of the statue
questions.explanation: The stone cut out by no human hand struck the iron and clay feet of the statue, breaking it to pieces. This stone then became a great mountain and filled the whole earth.

questions.question: What does Daniel's explanation reveal about the rise and fall of earthly governments?
options: All governments will last forever
Human wisdom can control the course of history
All earthly powers will ultimately be replaced by God's kingdom
Nations will not fall as long as they are strong
questions.explanation: Both the dream and its interpretation clearly show that all earthly governments are temporary and will eventually be replaced by the eternal kingdom established by God.

en.reflection: In what areas do you need to trust more in God’s ultimate control and await the coming of His eternal kingdom today?
en.prayer: Heavenly Father, You who control history, thank You for revealing mysteries to Daniel and showing me that You are the sovereign God. Help me to trust in Your eternal kingdom amidst the temporary powers and chaos of this world. May Your will be done on earth as it is in heaven. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Meditate for one minute: God's eternal kingdom will ultimately replace all others. Entrust one future concern you have to the God who controls all things.

en.focus: Even in the face of death threats, we can choose to be faithful to God, for He is worthy of our complete trust.

questions.question: How large was the gold image that King Nebuchadnezzar made?
options: Thirty cubits high and three cubits wide
Sixty cubits high and six cubits wide
Ninety cubits high and nine cubits wide
One hundred cubits high and ten cubits wide
questions.explanation: The text states that the image was "sixty cubits high and six cubits wide."

questions.question: When what sound was heard, were all people commanded to fall down and worship the image?
options: The sound of the king's command
The sound of war drums
The sound of all kinds of musical instruments
The sound of the priests' trumpets
questions.explanation: The text mentions the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and all kinds of music as the signal for worship.

questions.question: Why did some Chaldeans accuse Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to the king?
options: Because they had not paid their taxes
Because they had stolen the king's property
Because they did not serve the king's gods or worship the gold image
Because they incited the people to rebel against the king
questions.explanation: The Chaldeans accused the three Hebrews of not serving the king's gods or worshipping the gold image he had set up, which was against the king's decree.

questions.question: What can we learn from these three Hebrew men?
options: Compromise is the way to survive in a pagan culture
One should remain faithful to God even under immense pressure
God's servants do not need to obey earthly laws
We can pretend to worship idols and later ask God for forgiveness
questions.explanation: They showed unwavering loyalty to God, refusing to worship the idol despite facing a death threat.

en.reflection: In your life, are there moments when you need to stand firm in your faith and not compromise with the world?
reflectionOptions: Not conforming to secular culture in my faith
Upholding biblical principles in my morality
Glorifying God in my words and actions
en.prayer: Faithful Lord, thank You for being worthy of my complete worship and loyalty. Grant me the courage and strength to serve and honor You steadfastly, no matter the pressure or temptation. Help me to live in a way that reflects Your character and be a good testimony for You. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, pray for someone you know who is standing firm in their faith, asking God to strengthen them.

en.focus: Even in the fiercest trials, our trust in God can glorify His name and experience His presence.

questions.question: Why was King Nebuchadnezzar furious with Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego?
options: They refused to eat the king's food
They did not attend the king's banquet on time
They refused to worship the gold image the king had set up
They secretly discussed the king's rule
questions.explanation: The king was furious because Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego refused to worship the gold image he had set up.

questions.question: How did the three Hebrews respond to the king's threat?
options: They indicated willingness to compromise but needed time to consider
They pleaded with the king to forgive their ignorance
They firmly stated they would not worship the image, trusting God to save them
They questioned the legality of the king setting up the image
questions.explanation: They told the king that their God was able to save them from the fiery furnace, and even if He did not, they would still not serve his gods.

questions.question: What did King Nebuchadnezzar see when the three Hebrews were thrown into the fiery furnace?
options: The three of them burned to death by the flames
The flames of the furnace were extinguished
A fourth person walking with them, unharmed
Angels pulled them out of the furnace
questions.explanation: The king saw four men walking around in the fire, unharmed, and the fourth looked like a son of the gods.

questions.question: What is the main lesson this story teaches us?
options: Believing in God guarantees freedom from all disasters
God only saves those who perfectly obey His commands
True faith means refusing to compromise one's beliefs, even under threat of death
People need miracles to recognize God's power
questions.explanation: The actions of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego demonstrate that they steadfastly trusted God and refused to compromise their faith, even in the face of extreme threats.

en.reflection: In which area today do you most need to learn from Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego's steadfast trust in God?
reflectionOptions: Seeking God's will in a difficult decision
Releasing worry about an uncertain future
Refusing to compromise on a matter of faith
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for revealing Your power and faithfulness to me in this passage. Please grant me courage, like Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, to trust You steadfastly no matter the circumstances, and to not compromise under the pressures of the world. May my life glorify Your name. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, take five minutes to reflect on a difficulty you are currently experiencing, and pray to God, asking Him to help you fully trust Him in this matter.

en.theme: The King's Dream and God's Sovereignty
en.focus: King Nebuchadnezzar's dream reveals God's supreme rule over all human kingdoms, able to humble the proud and exalt the lowly.

questions.question: What was King Nebuchadnezzar's purpose in writing this letter?
options: To declare the greatness of his empire
To proclaim the signs and wonders that the Most High God had performed for him to all peoples, nations, and languages
To warn his people against rebellion
To record his personal diary
questions.explanation: The king begins his letter by stating his intention to proclaim the great signs and wonders that the Most High God had performed for him to all peoples.

questions.question: What did King Nebuchadnezzar see in his dream?
options: A great golden statue
A tall and flourishing tree whose foliage covered the whole earth
Four great beasts coming up from the sea
A burning fiery furnace
questions.explanation: The king dreamed of a great tree, tall and strong, providing shelter and food for all, until a heavenly watcher commanded it to be cut down.

questions.question: According to the passage, what did the watcher's words in the dream primarily signify?
options: The king would be defeated by his enemies
The king would lose his power and sanity until he acknowledged the Most High's rule
The king would build a new city
The king would become even wealthier and more powerful
questions.explanation: The watcher commanded the tree to be cut down and prophesied that the stump would remain until the king recognized that the Most High rules in the kingdom of mankind and gives it to whom he will.

questions.question: What main truth about God and human power does this dream reveal?
options: Human efforts will always succeed in the end
God is indifferent to earthly affairs
The Most High God rules in the kingdom of mankind, able to humble the proud and exalt the lowly
Wealth and power are the ultimate measures of a person's worth
questions.explanation: The dream clearly shows that God is sovereign, able to give and take away power as He wills, and to teach men to acknowledge His rule.

en.reflection: Nebuchadnezzar's experience reminds us that all authority comes from God. In what area of your life do you most need to fully acknowledge God's sovereignty today?
reflectionOptions: In my personal plans and decisions
en.prayer: Most High God, I acknowledge Your sovereign rule over my life and over all the kingdoms of the world. Help me to humble myself and always recognize that any ability, wisdom, or possession I have comes from You. May my life bring glory to Your holy name. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take a moment today to list three things you have been proud of or taken credit for in the past, and then give glory to God, acknowledging that He is the source of all good things.

en.theme: The Sovereignty of the Most High
en.focus: God is absolutely sovereign; He humbles the proud and exalts the humble.

questions.question: For what reason was King Nebuchadnezzar driven from human society and made to eat grass like an ox?
options: He committed treason against his kingdom
He sinned against his people
He was proud and did not acknowledge the sovereignty of the Most High
He failed to worship God faithfully
questions.explanation: The text clearly states that King Nebuchadnezzar was humbled because of his pride and failure to acknowledge God's sovereignty.

questions.question: After King Nebuchadnezzar's reason returned, how did he respond to God?
options: He began to complain about God's unjust judgment
He built a new temple for God
He praised, honored, and glorified the Most High, whose dominion endures forever
He sought Daniel's help
questions.explanation: Upon his recovery, the king praised, honored, and glorified God, acknowledging Him as the living Most High whose dominion is eternal.

questions.question: What is the most important lesson we learn about God's character from Nebuchadnezzar's experience?
options: God only cares about powerful rulers
God's judgments are inconsistent
God has absolute authority over all kingdoms and can humble the proud
God's love is unconditional
questions.explanation: The king's experience clearly demonstrates that God is the sovereign ruler over all, capable of humbling the proud and making them know His authority.

questions.question: Nebuchadnezzar's experience reminds us of the most crucial attitude to have in life. What is it?
options: To strive for worldly wealth and fame
To rely only on oneself and not seek help
To humbly acknowledge God's supreme sovereignty and glorify Him
To focus solely on one's own feelings and needs
questions.explanation: The king's journey ultimately led him to recognize that in the face of God's supreme sovereignty, one must be humble and glorify Him.

en.reflection: Is there an area in your life where you need to more deeply acknowledge God's supreme authority and sovereignty?
en.prayer: Almighty God, I acknowledge You as the King who rules over heaven and earth, whose dominion endures forever. Please help me to remove pride from my heart and humbly acknowledge Your sovereignty in all things. May my life bring glory to Your name. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, pray to God about an area in your life where you feel proud or struggle to let go, acknowledging His supreme sovereignty over it.

en.focus: When people become arrogant and forget God's sovereignty, divine judgment inevitably follows.

questions.question: What vessels did King Belshazzar command to be brought for drinking wine during his feast?
options: Ordinary gold and silver vessels
Gold and silver vessels plundered from the temple in Jerusalem
Vessels taken from Babylonian temples
Vessels from his father's treasury
questions.explanation: King Belshazzar commanded the gold and silver vessels that his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple in Jerusalem to be brought for drinking wine.

questions.question: What supernatural event occurred while King Belshazzar and his nobles were drinking?
options: A strong wind extinguished all the lamps
A bolt of lightning struck the throne
Fingers of a human hand appeared and wrote on the plaster of the wall
Food and fine wine descended from heaven
questions.explanation: As they were drinking from the temple vessels, the fingers of a human hand suddenly appeared and wrote on the plaster of the royal palace wall.

questions.question: What was the reaction of King Belshazzar and his nobles after seeing the writing on the wall?
options: They were curious and wanted to know who wrote it
They were angry, thinking someone was playing a trick
The king's face changed, his thoughts terrified him, and his nobles were perplexed
They ignored it and continued their revelry
questions.explanation: When King Belshazzar saw the hand writing, his face changed, his thoughts terrified him, his knees knocked together, and his nobles were perplexed.

questions.question: What is the main warning this passage gives us?
options: Having wealth and power is the most important thing in life
We can use any objects as we please, without restriction
God is the supreme ruler, and those who treat Him lightly will be judged
As long as a feast is well-organized, it will earn everyone's respect
questions.explanation: King Belshazzar desecrated sacred vessels, showing his arrogance and forgetfulness of God's sovereignty, which led to divine judgment.

en.reflection: Have you ever, in word or deed, shown disrespect or misused a blessing or spiritual matter given by God?
reflectionOptions: Approach spiritual matters with more humility
en.prayer: Almighty God, I acknowledge that You are the Sovereign Ruler of all. Forgive me for times when I have, through pride or carelessness, treated Your holy name or Your blessings lightly. Help me to live with a humble and reverent heart, always meditating on Your greatness and sovereignty. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, take one minute to meditate on a blessing God has given you and offer Him sincere thanks for it.

en.focus: True wisdom comes from God and allows us to understand divine mysteries.

questions.question: Who did King Belshazzar’s queen recommend to interpret the writing on the wall?
options: A Chaldean astrologer
An Egyptian pharaoh
Daniel
Nebuchadnezzar’s advisor
questions.explanation: The queen remembered Daniel, who possessed the spirit of the holy gods and was able to interpret dreams, explain riddles, and solve difficult problems.

questions.question: According to the queen’s description, what special gift did Daniel possess?
options: Exceptional military skills
Wisdom to interpret mysteries and solve problems
Accumulated great wealth
Proficiency in multiple languages
questions.explanation: The queen emphasized that Daniel had 'the spirit of the holy gods' and could 'interpret dreams, explain riddles, and solve difficult problems,' indicating wisdom from God.

questions.question: What was King Belshazzar’s main purpose in summoning Daniel?
options: To seek Daniel’s political counsel
To promote Daniel to a higher position
To have him interpret the writing on the wall
To learn about the religion of Israel from him
questions.explanation: King Belshazzar summoned Daniel, at the queen's recommendation, to interpret the mysterious writing that no one else could understand.

questions.question: What does Daniel’s story remind us about the source of true wisdom?
options: It comes through diligent study and accumulated experience
It comes by seeking powerful people in the world
It comes through knowing and revering the God who gives wisdom
It comes through noble birth and lineage
questions.explanation: Daniel's wisdom came from 'the spirit of the holy gods' within him, indicating that true wisdom is a gift from God, not from human effort or background.

en.reflection: In what area of your life do you most need God to grant you wisdom today?
reflectionOptions: Understanding and responding to a family member
Encountering a challenge at work or in ministry
en.prayer: Lord of wisdom, I confess my wisdom is limited, and I often cannot see the path ahead. Please grant me wisdom from above, so I can discern right from wrong, make decisions that honor You, and gain insight from You when facing challenges. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Spend one minute today quietly praying for God to grant you wisdom for a specific situation.

en.theme: The End of Pride and the Reward of Humility
en.focus: God is sovereign over all; He exalts the humble and punishes the proud, so that all may know He is the Most High.

questions.question: What offer from King Belshazzar did Daniel refuse?
options: Becoming a high official
Receiving gifts and rewards
Dining with the king
Marrying the king's daughter
questions.explanation: Daniel told the king, 'You may keep your gifts for yourself and give your rewards to someone else,' indicating his refusal of the king's wealth and presents.

questions.question: According to Daniel's accusation, what was King Belshazzar's primary sin?
options: Lust and debauchery
Disregarding God and exalting himself
Mass murder and tyranny
Poor governance leading to hardship
questions.explanation: Daniel pointed out that Belshazzar, though knowing how God dealt with his father Nebuchadnezzar, still exalted himself and did not honor God, but used the temple vessels for drinking and revelry.

questions.question: What was the meaning of the writing on the wall: 'Mene, Mene, Tekel, Parsin'?
options: God will prosper you and make your kingdom secure
Your kingdom has been weighed and given to others
God judges you and grants you wisdom
You will become the ruler of nations
questions.explanation: Daniel explained that the words meant God had numbered Belshazzar's kingdom and brought it to an end, he was weighed on the scales and found wanting, and his kingdom was divided and given to the Medes and Persians.

questions.question: What is the most significant reminder this passage from Daniel offers us today?
options: People can succeed through their own efforts
We should avoid feasts and live an ascetic life
God is the Lord of history and will judge all pride and irreverence
External appearances matter more than internal character
questions.explanation: This passage clearly demonstrates God's judgment on the proud and those who do not honor Him, as well as His sovereignty over history, reminding us to maintain a humble and reverent heart.

en.reflection: Are there areas in your life where pride resides, or where you assume control, neglecting God?
en.prayer: Almighty God, You are the sovereign Lord over all. Help me to remove pride from my heart and to always seek You with a humble and reverent spirit. May I look solely to You and glorify Your name in both good times and bad. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Spend some time today quietly reflecting on areas where you might be exalting yourself over God, and confess these to Him.

en.focus: Even in the face of danger, our faithfulness to God and excellent character can make us a blessing to others.

questions.question: How many satraps did King Darius intend to appoint to govern the whole kingdom?
options: One
Three
One hundred and twenty
One hundred and twenty-three
questions.explanation: The passage clearly states that King Darius appointed one hundred and twenty satraps, and over them, three administrators, of whom Daniel was one.

questions.question: What was the reason for Daniel's promotion?
options: He bribed the king
He was the oldest
He distinguished himself by his exceptional spirit, surpassing other administrators and satraps in wisdom
He was related to the king
questions.explanation: The scripture states that Daniel “distinguished himself among the administrators and satraps by his exceptional qualities. So the king planned to set him over the whole kingdom.” This exceptional quality is rooted in his spiritual excellence and wisdom.

questions.question: What was the attitude of the other administrators and satraps towards Daniel?
options: They greatly admired him
They tried to find grounds for charges against him
They became good friends with Daniel
They were completely indifferent to Daniel
questions.explanation: The other administrators and satraps “tried to find grounds for charges against Daniel in his conduct of government affairs,” indicating their hostility and jealousy towards him.

questions.question: From Daniel's example, how should we view faith in our work and daily life?
options: Faith is only important in church; it doesn't need to be mentioned at work
As long as work performance is good, faith is not important
Our faith should be reflected in excellent character and faithfulness in our work
It's acceptable to compromise faith principles occasionally for promotion
questions.explanation: Daniel's excellent spirit led to his outstanding performance at work, reminding us that our faith should shape our character and be evident in our daily work and life.

en.reflection: Today, how can you glorify God in your work or daily life through excellent character and faithfulness?
reflectionOptions: Treat colleagues or family with greater integrity
Uphold faith principles when facing temptation
en.prayer: Heavenly Father, thank You for granting Daniel such an excellent spirit, enabling him to glorify You in a foreign land. Please grant me wisdom and courage to display faithfulness and excellent character in my work and at home, bringing glory to Your name. In Jesus' name, I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, choose one everyday task that you can do better, and complete it with your best effort as an act of faithfulness to God.

en.focus: Even when facing the threat of death, those loyal to God consider prayer and worship as essential as breathing.

questions.question: On what grounds did Daniel's adversaries request King Darius to issue the decree?
options: For national security
To unify all officials
To test Daniel's loyalty
To display the king's supreme authority
questions.explanation: The adversaries used the pretext of 'upholding the king's decree' but their real intention was to trap Daniel.

questions.question: After the decree was issued, what did Daniel continue to do as usual?
options: He prayed to God for the king's protection
He closed his windows and prayed in secret
He knelt down and prayed, giving thanks to God three times a day
He consulted with his friends on how to handle the crisis
questions.explanation: Even after the decree was issued, Daniel continued his custom of kneeling and praying, giving thanks to God three times a day, without fear.

questions.question: How did King Darius react when he learned Daniel had been accused?
options: He immediately ordered Daniel's arrest
He was deeply distressed and tried his best to rescue Daniel
He was angry that Daniel had disobeyed his command
He gathered his advisors to discuss how to punish Daniel
questions.explanation: Upon learning of Daniel's accusation, King Darius was greatly distressed and made every effort to rescue him.

questions.question: What important lesson does Daniel's story teach us about faithfulness?
options: As long as we obey the law, God will protect us
In all circumstances, we must persevere in worship and prayer to God
Seeking help from others is more important than trusting God
We can temporarily compromise our faith principles to avoid danger
questions.explanation: Even when facing the threat of death, Daniel regarded prayer and worship as non-negotiable principles in his life, demonstrating his complete trust in God.

en.reflection: Today, what faith principle in your life do you need to uphold without compromise?
reflectionOptions: Commit to daily Bible reading and prayer
Be a witness for Christ at work
Forgive someone who has hurt me
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for the example of Daniel. Grant me courage and wisdom to remain steadfast in my loyalty to You amidst the currents of the world. Help me to consider prayer and worshiping You as the very breath of my life, no matter the circumstances. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, intentionally find a quiet moment to kneel and offer a prayer of thanks to God, just like Daniel.

en.focus: Even in the darkest moments, God can deliver His servants and cause His name to be glorified.

questions.question: What did King Darius say to Daniel when he was thrown into the lions' den?
options: May your God save you, Daniel!
May your God, whom you serve continually, deliver you!
May the God you believe in rescue you from the lions!
May the LORD God Himself deliver you!
questions.explanation: King Darius said to Daniel, “May your God, whom you serve continually, deliver you!”

questions.question: How did God save Daniel?
options: He sent an angel to destroy the lions
He made the lions fall asleep
He sent His angel to shut the mouths of the lions
He gave Daniel strength to fight the lions
questions.explanation: Daniel told the king that God sent His angel and shut the mouths of the lions so that they had not harmed him.

questions.question: What decree did King Darius issue to the whole kingdom after Daniel’s deliverance?
options: He commanded everyone to worship Daniel's God
He commanded everyone to fear Daniel's God
He commanded everyone to praise Daniel's God as the living God
He commanded everyone to believe Daniel's God is the only God
questions.explanation: King Darius issued a decree for all people to tremble and fear before the God of Daniel, and to praise Him as the living God, who endures forever.

questions.question: What truth about God can we learn from Daniel's experience?
options: God only saves those who have never made a mistake
God's power is limited by earthly authorities
God is a living God who can deliver those who trust in Him, even in desperate situations
God will always act according to our will if we have enough faith
questions.explanation: Daniel's experience clearly shows that God is a living God, whose power to save is limitless, and He faithfully delivers those who steadfastly trust in Him.

en.reflection: In your life, in which 'lions' den' like desperate situations has God miraculously delivered you? How did this strengthen your faith in Him?
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for being the living God, the God of deliverance. Please help me to trust You steadfastly when I face the 'lions' dens' of life. May my life bear witness to Your mighty power, so that more people may know and praise You. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Share an experience of God's deliverance in your life with a friend or family member today.

en.focus: Even amidst chaos and suffering, God remains sovereign, and His kingdom is eternal and ultimately victorious.

questions.question: What did the first beast Daniel saw in his vision resemble?
options: A lion
A bear
A leopard
A dreadful and terrifying beast with ten horns
questions.explanation: The first beast Daniel saw in his vision was like a lion and had eagles' wings.

questions.question: What were the characteristics of the fourth beast Daniel saw in his vision?
options: Three ribs in its mouth
Four wings
Exceedingly strong, with iron teeth and bronze claws
Ten horns, from which a little horn grew
questions.explanation: The fourth beast was terrifying, with iron teeth and bronze claws, and it had ten horns, from which another little horn later grew.

questions.question: In Daniel's vision, what important truth do 'the Ancient of Days' and 'the Son of Man' represent?
options: The temporary nature of earthly kings' power
God's judgment and eternal reign
Israel will always be ruled by foreign nations
Humans can become gods through effort
questions.explanation: The 'Ancient of Days' represents God's eternality and authority to judge; 'the Son of Man' foreshadows the Messiah (Jesus) who will receive an everlasting kingdom and authority.

questions.question: What comfort and hope do the visions in Daniel 7 offer to believers facing challenges in life?
options: They predict our immediate exemption from all suffering
They remind us that God will destroy all non-believers
They proclaim God's sovereignty and the eternal triumph of His kingdom
They encourage us to strive for earthly power
questions.explanation: These visions, though depicting fearsome earthly powers, ultimately point to God's judgment and His eternal kingdom that will supersede all others, bringing ultimate comfort and hope to believers.

en.reflection: How do you actively live out your trust in God's sovereignty and His eternal kingdom amidst the various confusions and challenges of this world?
reflectionOptions: Entrusting my worries to God in prayer
Focusing more on God's Word and promises
Facing difficulties with a hopeful attitude
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for being the sovereign Ruler over all creation, whose kingdom is eternal and indestructible. When I face the world's chaos and challenges, please help me fix my eyes on You, trusting in Your authority and Your ultimate victory. May Your will be done on earth as it is in heaven. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take a moment today to reflect on God's sovereignty in your life and thank Him for His eternal kingdom.

en.theme: The Sovereignty of the Most High and the Triumph of the Saints
en.focus: Even amidst worldly chaos and evil, God reigns supreme, and His saints will ultimately receive an everlasting kingdom.

questions.question: What was Daniel’s physical reaction after the vision?
options: He felt hungry
He was troubled and his face turned pale
He became very excited
He felt sleepy and tired
questions.explanation: After the vision, Daniel was troubled in his spirit and his face turned pale because of these thoughts.

questions.question: When the angel explained the vision to Daniel, what was repeatedly emphasized about the outcome for the 'saints'?
options: The saints would fight against the nations
The saints would suffer for a time, but would ultimately receive the kingdom forever and ever
The saints would establish a temporary earthly empire
The authority of the saints would gradually diminish
questions.explanation: The angel repeatedly emphasized that despite the power and hostility of the fourth beast, ultimately, 'the holy people of the Most High will receive the kingdom and will possess it forever—yes, forever and ever.'

questions.question: How does this passage offer comfort to believers suffering under evil forces?
options: It suggests that being strong enough will overcome all enemies
It implies God is unaware of evil in the world and cannot intervene
It affirms that evil powers are temporary, the Most High is sovereign, and He will give an everlasting kingdom to His saints
It teaches that evil will simply disappear if one endures
questions.explanation: The text clearly states that though evil powers rage and persecute the saints, 'the court will sit, and his power will be taken away.' Ultimately, 'the holy people of the Most High will receive the kingdom and will possess it forever—yes, forever and ever,' demonstrating God's ultimate sovereignty and justice.

questions.question: In today's world, when facing injustice or evil, how does this passage help us maintain hope?
options: It tells us not to trust any authority
It encourages us to retaliate with violence
It confirms God's ultimate sovereignty and victory, assuring His people an eternal kingdom despite present evils
It teaches us to be indifferent to everything
questions.explanation: The vision and explanation in Daniel 7 remind us in every age that no matter how chaotic the world may seem, the ultimate ruler is not human kings or evil powers, but the Most High. His people will ultimately receive an eternal kingdom, providing steadfast hope in the face of injustice.

en.reflection: In what situation today do you feel God's sovereignty seems distant? How does this passage help you regain hope?
reflectionOptions: Witnessing challenges in the church or faith community
en.prayer: Most High God, I thank You that You are in control of all things, and even amidst the world's chaos and evil, Your plan remains steadfast. Help me to fix my eyes on Your ultimate victory and the eternal kingdom You have prepared for Your saints when facing challenges. May my heart find comfort and strength in Your promises. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, when feeling anxious or disheartened, meditate on Daniel 7:27, reminding yourself of God's ultimate victory and the eternal inheritance of His saints.

en.focus: God reveals future events through visions, reminding us that He is the sovereign Lord of history.

questions.question: In what year did Daniel see this vision?
options: The first year of King Belshazzar's reign
The third year of King Belshazzar's reign
The first year of King Darius's reign
The third year of King Cyrus's reign
questions.explanation: The text clearly states that Daniel saw this vision in the third year of King Belshazzar's reign.

questions.question: What two animals did Daniel see in his vision?
options: A lion and a bear
A leopard and a male goat
A ram and a male goat
An ox and a deer
questions.explanation: Daniel saw a ram and a male goat in his vision.

questions.question: What did the breaking of the male goat's large horn and the growth of four new horns signify?
options: A powerful empire would last forever
A great kingdom would be divided into several smaller kingdoms
A new great leader would rise quickly
A time of peace and prosperity was coming
questions.explanation: The 'great horn' of the male goat represents a powerful king, and its breaking, followed by four new horns, signifies a great empire dividing into four kingdoms.

questions.question: What does the vision in Daniel remind us about our lives today?
options: Humans can control the course of history
God's plans are chaotic and incomprehensible
