God is in control of history, and His will will ultimately be accomplished
We should focus on pursuing worldly power
questions.explanation: Daniel's vision shows God's control over the future, reminding us that no matter how world events unfold, His will is accomplished, and He is the true sovereign over history.

en.reflection: When facing uncertainty in world events or your personal circumstances, how does Daniel's vision help you trust in God's sovereignty again?
reflectionOptions: It reminds me that God is in control, easing my anxiety
It motivates me to pray and seek God more
It helps me see that present difficulties are not the end
en.prayer: Almighty Father, thank You for revealing Your sovereignty over history through Daniel's vision. When I face uncertainty or confusion, help me to trust in Your eternal plan and sovereign control. May my heart find rest and hope in You. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take one minute today to reflect: No matter how the world changes, God is still on the throne. Thank God for this truth.

en.focus: God reveals the course of history and His ultimate sovereignty through visions, assuring that His plans will prevail even amidst suffering.

questions.question: What was a notable characteristic of the male goat Daniel saw in the vision?
options: It had two high horns
It came from the west, moving swiftly without touching the ground
It moved very slowly
It had a golden horn
questions.explanation: Daniel saw the goat coming “from the west across the whole earth, without touching the ground,” indicating its extreme speed.

questions.question: What happened after the large horn on the male goat was broken off?
options: Two larger horns grew in its place
Four prominent horns grew up toward the four winds of heaven
It transformed into a bear
It completely disappeared
questions.explanation: When the large horn was broken, “four prominent horns grew up toward the four winds of heaven” in its place.

questions.question: According to the angel Gabriel, who did the male goat in the vision represent?
options: The king of Persia
The king of Greece
The Pharaoh of Egypt
The king of Babylon
questions.explanation: The angel Gabriel clearly explained: “The male goat is the king of Greece.”

questions.question: What is the primary message revealed by Daniel's vision?
options: Human history happens randomly, without pattern
God is unaware of the course of history
God foreknows and sovereignly controls the development of history, and His plans will ultimately be accomplished
Human power can completely alter God's plans
questions.explanation: This vision reveals God's foreknowledge and sovereignty in history, showing that His plans will unfold in due time, even through the rise and fall of powerful empires.

en.reflection: How does God's sovereignty, as seen in this vision, comfort you when facing the future, especially when you feel uncertain or anxious?
reflectionOptions: It reminds me God is in control
It motivates me to trust God more
en.prayer: Almighty God, You are the Lord of history, and Your plans cannot be thwarted. Thank You for showing me Your supreme wisdom and power through Daniel's vision. Help me to trust You firmly when facing future challenges, knowing that You will accomplish all things according to Your good will. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take a minute to reflect on the fact that God is sovereign over history, and then say to yourself, 'My God is in control, and I can trust Him.'

en.focus: Daniel humbly sought God in prayer during a time of national crisis, confessing the sins of his people.

questions.question: During the reign of which king did Daniel begin his prayer?
options: King Cyrus
King Darius
King Nebuchadnezzar
King Belshazzar
questions.explanation: The text clearly states that Daniel's prayer began in the first year of the reign of Darius the son of Ahasuerus.

questions.question: What specific preparations did Daniel make before he began to pray?
options: Fasting, wearing sackcloth and ashes
Offering burnt offerings and grain offerings
Gathering the elders to pray with him
Reading the Law to the people
questions.explanation: Daniel set his face toward the Lord God to seek Him by prayer and supplications, with fasting and sackcloth and ashes.

questions.type: Understand the content of the prayer
questions.question: How does Daniel describe the God he is appealing to in his prayer?
options: A distant and indifferent God
A God who often changes His mind
A great and awesome God who keeps His covenant of love
A God who only punishes and does not show grace
questions.explanation: Daniel addresses God as “the great and awesome God, who keeps his covenant of love with those who love him and keep his commandments.”

questions.question: How does Daniel’s prayer instruct us to respond when our nation or we as individuals face difficulties?
options: Complain and blame others
Rely solely on human efforts to solve problems
Humbly approach God, confessing sin and seeking His mercy
Pretend everything is fine and avoid confronting problems
questions.explanation: Daniel's example teaches us that in times of trouble, we should come before God with humility and repentance, seeking His help and forgiveness.

en.reflection: Daniel confessed the sins of his people in his prayer. Today, do you need to confess and repent of any sin before God, either for yourself or for a community you belong to?
reflectionOptions: Repent of personal pride or unbelief
Repent of injustice or indifference in a community
Repent of failing to love God and others fully
en.prayer: Almighty Lord, thank You for being the great and awesome God who keeps His covenant of love. Help me to follow Daniel’s example, not relying on my own strength when facing challenges and difficulties, but humbly coming before You. May I always examine my heart, confessing my transgressions and weaknesses to You, and seeking Your mercy and guidance. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take a moment today to specifically confess a sin to God, either for yourself or for a community you care about, and ask for His forgiveness and help.

en.focus: Daniel genuinely confesses the sins of his people and passionately pleads for God's mercy and restoration.

questions.question: What sins does Daniel confess on behalf of the Israelites in his prayer?
options: Only caring for themselves and neglecting neighbours
Failing to offer sacrifices on time
Acting wickedly, rebelling against God, and not obeying His servants
Intermarrying with foreign nations
questions.explanation: Daniel confesses on behalf of the Israelites that they have sinned, acted wickedly, been rebellious, and have not listened to God's servants, the prophets.

questions.question: What is the basis of Daniel's plea for God's favour?
options: The righteous deeds of the Israelites
Daniel's own piety
God's own nature of abundant mercy and righteousness
The fear of God among the nations
questions.explanation: Daniel repeatedly appeals to God based on His 'great mercy' and 'righteousness,' not on any good deeds of the people.

questions.question: Daniel grieves over the desolation of Jerusalem and the sanctuary. What does he ask God to do?
options: Ask God to bring disaster upon their enemies
Ask God to rebuild the walls and the temple
Ask God to hear, forgive, and act quickly for His own sake
Ask God to send angels to help them
questions.explanation: Daniel asks God to hear, forgive, and answer, and to act quickly for His own sake, without delay, because Jerusalem and God's people are called by His name.

questions.question: What important lesson do we learn from Daniel's prayer?
options: God must respond immediately if we confess our sins
Confessing sins for ourselves and our community, and trusting God's mercy, is key to prayer
God's wrath is greater than His mercy
Prayer should only focus on individual needs
questions.explanation: Daniel's prayer highlights the importance of confessing personal and communal sins and placing all hope in God's abundant mercy and righteousness.

en.reflection: Daniel confessed the sins of his nation and people. Today, do you need to confess any sins to God, either for yourself or for your community (e.g., family, church, nation)?
en.prayer: Heavenly Father, I come before You, confessing my sins and the sins of my community (e.g., family, church). We have often rebelled against You and failed to obey Your word. Please forgive us according to Your great mercy and righteousness. Hear our prayer and, for Your own glory, act quickly to restore us. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take a moment today to confess a sin you are aware of (either personal or communal) to God and ask for His mercy and forgiveness.

en.focus: God reveals His grand redemptive plan for Israel and the world to Daniel through Gabriel.

questions.question: Who was commanded to appear to Daniel while he was still praying?
options: An angel named Michael
An angel named Gabriel
A king named Cyrus
A priest named Jeshua
questions.explanation: While Daniel was still praying, the angel Gabriel was commanded to fly swiftly to him.

questions.question: What did Gabriel come to give Daniel understanding about?
options: His personal future destiny
The rise and fall of the Babylonian empire
The vision and dream he had seen
How the people of Israel should rebuild the temple
questions.explanation: Gabriel was sent to give Daniel understanding of the vision and dream he had previously seen.

questions.type: Understand the purpose of the 'seventy sevens'
questions.question: What were the 'seventy sevens' mentioned by Gabriel meant to accomplish?
options: To bring wealth and glory to the people of Israel
To finish transgression, to put an end to sin, to atone for iniquity, to bring in everlasting righteousness, to seal up vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most holy place
To enable the people of Israel to rebuild a strong army and defeat their enemies
To make all gentile nations worship God
questions.explanation: The purpose of the 'seventy sevens' is to deal with sin, bring eternal righteousness, and anoint the most holy place.

questions.question: What is the main message this passage helps us understand?
options: If we pray hard enough, God will immediately solve all problems
God has a clear and grand redemptive plan for His people, and He will accomplish it on time
Human history is entirely determined by chance, without divine intervention
God's plan is only about individuals, not about nations or the world
questions.explanation: God, through Gabriel, reveals His timetable and purpose for the redemption of Israel and the world, showing His sovereignty over all.

en.reflection: God's sovereignty over history and His redemptive plan are powerfully displayed in Daniel 9. How does this impact your current challenges and your hope for the future?
reflectionOptions: Be willing to wait patiently for God's plan
en.prayer: Gracious and wise God, thank You for revealing Your magnificent plan to Daniel, showing me that You are in control of history and have wonderful redemptive arrangements for Your people. Help me to trust in Your wisdom and sovereignty, even when facing uncertainty and challenges, and to follow You faithfully. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Spend one minute reflecting on God's sovereignty and surrender one concern you have to Him today.

en.focus: Even in profound spiritual encounters, we may feel weak and overwhelmed, but God always strengthens us with His presence and grace.

questions.question: Under what circumstances did Daniel experience this vision?
options: He was building the temple
He was fasting and praying
He was imprisoned in Babylon
He was reading the Law
questions.explanation: The passage clearly states that Daniel had been fasting for three weeks by the great river Tigris when he saw this great vision.

questions.question: What were the characteristics of the man Daniel saw in the vision?
options: Clothed in sackcloth, with a face like lightning
Clothed in linen, with a belt of gold from Uphaz
Shining brightly, with a voice like the sound of many waters
Holding a scroll, with feet like burnished bronze
questions.explanation: Daniel describes the man in the vision as clothed in linen, with a belt of gold from Uphaz around his waist, his body like beryl, his face like lightning, his eyes like flaming torches, his arms and legs like the gleam of burnished bronze, and his voice like the sound of a multitude.

questions.question: What was Daniel's reaction, and the reaction of those with him, when he saw the vision?
options: They were all very excited and began to sing praises
They all felt peace and were filled with joy
Only Daniel saw the vision, but he became weak and fell to the ground
All those with him saw the vision and were terrified, fleeing away
questions.explanation: Those with Daniel, though they did not see the vision, were seized with great terror and fled to hide themselves. Daniel himself was left alone, felt all his strength leave him, and fell into a deep sleep with his face to the ground.

questions.question: What does Daniel's reaction to the vision reveal?
options: God only reveals Himself to the strong
Humans naturally feel small and limited in the presence of God's glory
Daniel's faith was insufficient, which is why he was weak
The purpose of the vision was to instill fear and drive people away from God
questions.explanation: Despite being a devout man, Daniel felt extreme weakness and terror in the presence of God's glory, demonstrating God's immense power and holiness, and humanity's smallness.

en.reflection: In your spiritual life, have you ever hesitated to approach God because you felt weak or inadequate? How does this passage encourage you?
reflectionOptions: It reminds me that God is all-powerful, so I need not fear
It helps me to honestly face my weaknesses and seek God's help
It encourages me to keep seeking God even when I feel weak
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for showing me Your glory and power through Daniel’s experience. Lord, when I feel weak, afraid, or inadequate, please help me to still draw near to You. I know You are the God who sustains me. Grant me strength and courage to continue seeking Your face. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take one minute today to be still and invite God into the weakest or most fearful part of your heart, trusting that He will strengthen you.

en.focus: God is sovereign over unseen spiritual battles and strengthens us through His messengers.

questions.question: What was Daniel's initial reaction when he was touched?
options: He immediately understood the vision
He was greatly afraid and fell on his face
He began to pray to God
He asked who touched him
questions.explanation: The text describes Daniel falling on his face, in a deep sleep, indicating extreme fear and weakness when touched by a hand.

questions.question: According to the angel, what caused the delay in Daniel receiving the message despite his prayer being heard?
options: Daniel's faith was not strong enough
God did not want Daniel to know the future too soon
The prince of the kingdom of Persia opposed the angel
The angel needed more time to prepare the message
questions.explanation: The angel told Daniel that from the first day he set his heart to understand, his words were heard, but the prince of the kingdom of Persia withstood him for 21 days.

questions.question: How did the angel encourage Daniel?
options: By telling him that he would succeed if he tried harder
By reminding him that God was with him and calling him 'highly esteemed'
By promising that he would immediately see the vision fulfilled
By telling him that future difficulties would disappear
questions.explanation: The angel repeatedly told Daniel, “O man greatly beloved, fear not, peace be with you; be strong and courageous!” and touched him again to strengthen him.

questions.question: From this passage, how should we view delays in our prayers being answered?
options: Delay means God has not heard our prayers
Delay means we need to pray harder
Delay might be due to unseen spiritual battles, but God is still sovereign
Delay means God is displeased with us
questions.explanation: Daniel's prayer was heard from the very first day but was delayed for 21 days due to spiritual warfare. This reminds us that even if prayers are not immediately answered, God is in control, and we should maintain faith.

en.reflection: In your life, have you ever felt discouraged by prayers that seemed unanswered immediately? How does this passage encourage you to continue trusting God?
reflectionOptions: Remind myself that God is sovereign over all spiritual battles
Seek God's peace and strength in the waiting
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding me through this passage that You are sovereign even in unseen spiritual battles. When my heart feels weak or my prayers seem unanswered, strengthen me, just as Daniel was strengthened, to know that I am highly esteemed by You. May Your peace fill my heart and enable me to continue trusting You. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, pray for a persistent request that has not yet been answered and meditate on the thought: 'My prayer was heard by God from the very first day.'

en.focus: Even amidst the incessant conflicts of earthly kings, God remains in control, fulfilling His purposes.

questions.question: In verse 1, the angel reveals to Daniel that he supported Darius the Mede in the early days of which king?
options: Cyrus of Persia
Alexander of Greece
Darius of Persia
Pharaoh of Egypt
questions.explanation: The angel mentions that in the first year of Darius the Mede, he stood up to support Darius against Cyrus of Persia.

questions.question: The prophecy in Daniel 11 mainly focuses on conflicts between which two entities?
options: Babylon and Assyria
Persia and Greece
The King of the North and the King of the South
Rome and Egypt
questions.explanation: The passage details continuous wars and political schemes between the King of the North and the King of the South (commonly interpreted as the Seleucid Dynasty in Syria and the Ptolemaic Dynasty in Egypt).

questions.question: This passage prophesies the rise and fall of many empires and wars. What does this primarily reveal to us?
options: The course of history is entirely determined by human choices
God is unaware of the development of human history
God's will is accomplished even amidst the strife of nations
The future of the world is completely random and unpredictable
questions.explanation: While the prophecy involves complex political and military events, its core message is that God is in control of history and moves everything according to His will.

questions.question: How does this passage help us in the face of worldly turmoil and uncertainty?
options: It encourages us to actively engage in political struggles
It reminds us that God's sovereignty is our greatest comfort and hope
It suggests we adopt a pessimistic attitude towards the future
It teaches us to ignore various world news
questions.explanation: This passage demonstrates God's detailed foreknowledge and control over history, reminding us that we can trust in His eternal sovereignty amidst any turmoil.

en.reflection: When you see conflict and uncertainty in the world, are you able to place your hope and trust in God's sovereignty?
en.prayer: Almighty God, You are the King who governs history. When I witness the turmoil and unrest in the world, help me to remember that Your will shall ultimately prevail. May my heart find peace and hope in Your sovereign control. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Choose one piece of world news that causes you concern, and pray about it, asking God to oversee everything according to His good will.

en.focus: Even amidst worldly turmoil and evil forces, God remains in control of history and preserves His faithful people.

questions.question: How did the 'contemptible person' described in the passage seize the kingdom?
options: Through military conquest
Through hereditary succession
Through intrigue and flattery
Through popular acclaim
questions.explanation: The passage states that he “will not be given the honor of royalty” but “will come in a time of peace and seize the kingdom by intrigue.”

questions.question: What actions did this 'contemptible person' take regarding the holy land and sanctuary once in power?
options: He rebuilt the temple
He respected local religious customs
He desecrated the sanctuary and abolished the daily sacrifice
He made a peace treaty with the Jews
questions.explanation: He “will abolish the daily sacrifice and set up the abomination that causes desolation,” and “desecrate the sanctuary fortress.”

questions.question: How will those who know God respond when facing persecution?
options: They will seek cooperation with their enemies
They will completely abandon their faith
They will stand firm and instruct many
They will secretly flee and hide
questions.explanation: The passage states that “the people who know their God will firmly resist him” and “those who are wise will instruct many.”

questions.question: How does this passage comfort those who hold onto their faith in difficult times?
options: God promises they will not experience any suffering
God promises they will immediately see evil punished
God will use suffering to refine and purify them until the appointed time of the end
God will send angels to fight directly for them
questions.explanation: The passage mentions that “some of the wise will stumble, so that they may be refined, purified and made spotless until the time of the end,” indicating God has a purpose for allowing suffering.

en.reflection: In today's world, do you sense any challenges from 'evil forces'? How can you, like those who know God, 'stand firm' and 'instruct many'?
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You that You are the God who controls all history and seasons. When I face the world's evil and challenges, please grant me wisdom and courage to stand firm and be faithful to You. Cleanse my heart, so I may be salt and light according to Your will. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, pray for a friend you know who is struggling in their faith, asking God to strengthen them to hold fast to the truth.

en.theme: Defiance Against God and God's End
en.focus: No earthly power, no matter how great, can ultimately thwart God’s plan, for He is sovereign over all.

questions.question: How does this king, who acts as he pleases, view himself and God?
options: He fears God and seeks His will
He exalts himself, considers himself divine, and disregards any god
Although he does not worship God, he respects the gods of other nations
He claims to be God's messenger, acting on God's behalf
questions.explanation: The text states that this king “will do as he pleases. He will exalt and magnify himself above every god and will say unheard-of things against the God of gods. He will prosper until the time of wrath is completed.”

questions.question: Which types of gods does this king disregard, and what does he value instead?
options: He worships only his national idols and not foreign gods
He will show no regard for the gods of his ancestors or for the god desired by women, nor will he regard any god, but will exalt himself above them all. Instead, he will honor a god of fortresses.
He worships only heavenly gods, not earthly gods
He respects all gods, but prioritizes his political allies
questions.explanation: The text explicitly says, “He will show no regard for the gods of his ancestors or for the god desired by women, nor will he regard any god, but will exalt himself above them all. Instead of them, he will honor a god of fortresses; a god unknown to his ancestors he will honor with gold and silver, with precious stones and costly gifts.” The god of fortresses can be understood as military power.

questions.question: What is the ultimate end of this arrogant king?
options: He will conquer the world and establish an eternal empire
He will be defeated by a more powerful king and go into exile
He will die peacefully with glory and wealth
He will come to his end between the seas and the glorious holy mountain, with no one to help him
questions.explanation: Despite his great power and widespread conquests, his ultimate end is that “he will pitch his royal tents between the seas and the glorious holy mountain. Yet he will come to his end, and no one will help him.”

questions.question: What main hope does this passage offer us?
options: People can control their own destiny if they are powerful enough
God helps those who are arrogant to succeed
No matter how arrogant and defiant earthly rulers are, they cannot escape God's ultimate control and judgment
We should completely avoid involvement in politics to avoid being affected
questions.explanation: This passage portrays an exceedingly powerful and arrogant king, yet his ultimate end is that no one will help him. This highlights God's ultimate sovereignty and His control over history, showing that all powers that defy God will come to an end.

en.reflection: In today's world, what phenomena make you feel the pride of humanity and its challenges to God? How do you view and respond to these challenges?
reflectionOptions: Pray for those in authority, asking God to guide them
Trust more deeply in God's sovereignty, not fearing worldly changes
Actively live out Christ's likeness, being salt and light
en.prayer: Lord, You are the God who governs history and all things. In the face of worldly pride and challenges to Your authority, help me to steadfastly trust in You. May my heart not be swayed by the world's clamor, but fixed on Your eternal plan. May Your will be done on earth as it is in heaven. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Meditate for one minute on the phrase 'God is sovereign' and commit one worldly power or event that concerns you to God.

en.focus: Even in the greatest distress, those who trust in God have eternal hope and reward.

questions.question: Who will stand up when the great distress comes at the end of time?
options: A new king
Michael, the archangel
A powerful prophet
Earthly judges
questions.explanation: The passage clearly states that Michael, the great prince, will stand up during the time of distress.

questions.question: When those who sleep in the dust awake, what two different outcomes will there be?
options: Some will find peace, others will continue to sleep
Some will gain wealth, others will suffer poverty
Some to everlasting life, others to shame and everlasting contempt
Some will become kings, others will become servants
questions.explanation: The text states that those who awake will face different destinies: some to everlasting life, others to shame and everlasting contempt.

questions.question: What reward will 'the wise' and 'those who lead many to righteousness' receive?
options: Earthly power
Long life
Shine like the brightness of the heavens and the stars
Exemption from all suffering
questions.explanation: The passage promises that the wise will shine like the brightness of the heavens, and those who lead many to righteousness, like the stars forever and ever.

questions.question: What hope does this passage from Daniel bring to us today as we face the world's challenges?
options: That we can avoid all trouble by trying harder
That God will ultimately prevail and administer justice and reward
That all problems will immediately disappear if we believe
That the future world will be much better than the present
questions.explanation: The passage emphasizes God's ultimate judgment and eternal reward for believers, reminding us that God is sovereign and will justly recompense His servants.

en.reflection: How do the promises in Daniel 12:1–3 strengthen your heart in today's challenging world?
reflectionOptions: It reminds me of God's ultimate sovereignty
It encourages me to continue trusting God
It solidifies my hope in eternity
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for the eternal hope You give me through the prophecies in Daniel. Help me to trust in Your justice and love amidst all tribulations. May I be among the wise, leading many to righteousness, so that my life may shine like the stars for Your glory. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, take a minute to ponder the meaning of 'everlasting life' and 'everlasting contempt,' and give thanks for the path to eternal life.

en.theme: The Final End and Eternal Hope
en.focus: God's words are mysterious, but He promises eternal reward to those who remain faithful to the end.

questions.question: What was Daniel instructed to do with the book?
options: Read it publicly
Conceal and seal it
Burn it
Hand it to the next generation of leaders
questions.explanation: Daniel was told to conceal the words and seal the book until the time of the end.

questions.question: What will be characteristic of those who know God at the time of the end?
options: They will become wealthy
Many will run to and fro, and knowledge will increase
They will build mighty armies
They will be persecuted by everyone
questions.explanation: The text states that at the time of the end, many will go to and fro, and knowledge will increase.

questions.question: What were the wise people told they would do for many?
options: Lead them in battle
Teach them how to become rich
Lead many to righteousness
Help them build magnificent structures
questions.explanation: Those who are wise will shine like the brightness of the heavens, and those who lead many to righteousness, like the stars forever and ever.

questions.question: What promise was given to Daniel?
options: He would live to see the end of days
He would receive earthly wealth and honour
He would rest and then rise to receive his allotted inheritance at the end of the days
He would become king of Israel
questions.explanation: Daniel was promised that he would rest and then rise to receive his allotted inheritance at the end of the days.

en.reflection: As you await the fulfillment of God's promises, how can you live more faithfully and place your eternal hope in Him?
reflectionOptions: Spend daily quiet time in God's Word and prayer
Be more active in sharing the Gospel with others
Serve the church with love and wisdom
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for revealing the mysteries of the end times and for giving us eternal hope. Help me, I pray, not to be consumed by worldly anxieties in my daily life, but to always look to You and faithfully uphold Your Word. May I, like the wise, shine Your light to those around me, bringing more people to You. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take a moment today to reflect on the promise in Daniel 12:13 and thank God for it.

en.focus: Even amidst severe messages of judgment, God reveals His unchanging love and future hope for His people.

questions.question: During which kings' reigns did Hosea receive the word of the LORD for Israel and Judah, respectively?
options: Jeroboam and Ahaz
Joash and Uzziah
Jeroboam and Uzziah
Ahaz and Hezekiah
questions.explanation: Hosea received the word of the LORD during the reign of Jeroboam king of Israel, and during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.

questions.question: What kind of wife was Hosea commanded to marry, to symbolize Israel's relationship with God?
options: A poor but faithful woman
A promiscuous woman
A prophet's daughter
A foreign woman
questions.explanation: God commanded Hosea to marry a promiscuous woman and have children of promiscuity, because it symbolized Israel's great unfaithfulness to the LORD.

questions.question: God gave Hosea's three children special names. What did these names primarily foreshadow regarding God's plan for Israel and Judah?
options: God would bless them with prosperity
God would build a powerful empire through them
God would judge Israel but eventually show mercy to Judah and restore His people
God would allow them to be assimilated by pagan nations
questions.explanation: The three names (Jezreel, Lo-Ruhamah, Lo-Ammi) foreshadowed God's judgment on Israel (Jehu's house), His withdrawal of mercy from Israel, and His declaring them 'Not My People.' However, God also prophesied future mercy for Judah and the eventual restoration of all His people.

questions.question: How do we see God's love and hope within the severe message of judgment in Hosea chapter 1?
options: God promised no judgment if Israel repented
God prophesied judgment through the prophet, but also foretold future restoration and mercy
God punished Israel to demonstrate His justice to other nations
God commanding Hosea to marry a promiscuous woman meant He had completely given up on Israel
questions.explanation: Despite the pronouncements of judgment on Israel (ending Jehu's dynasty, no more mercy, being called 'Not My People'), God also explicitly foretold the future salvation of Judah and the eventual reunification and multiplication of Israel and Judah, who would be called 'children of the living God.' This reveals God's love and ultimate hope even in discipline.

en.reflection: Have you ever felt abandoned or disappointed by God due to your own shortcomings or struggles? How does this passage remind you that even in discipline, God still holds love and hope?
reflectionOptions: Trusting in God's mercy and promises
Confessing my faults and seeking God's help
Reminding myself that God is faithful and His love never changes
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for revealing Yourself through Hosea's life and message as a God who is just yet full of mercy. Please help me, even when I feel disciplined or distant from You, to trust in Your unchanging love and good promises. May my heart always turn back to You. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, take one minute to meditate on the title 'children of the living God' and give thanks for being God's child.

en.focus: God's enduring love for His people remains constant, even when they stray, as He calls them back with grace and compassion.

questions.question: In Hosea 2:1, what is Israel commanded to call God?
options: My Master
My Husband
My Father
My King
questions.explanation: God instructs Israel to call Him 'My Husband' rather than 'My Master,' emphasizing the intimate covenant relationship He desires with them.

questions.question: What blessings does God promise to restore to Israel?
options: Wealth and power
Peace and victory
Vineyards and the Valley of Achor as a door of hope
Mountains and rivers
questions.explanation: God promises to restore her vineyards and make the Valley of Achor a 'door of hope,' symbolizing new beginnings and abundance.

questions.type: Understand God's way of restoring relationship
questions.question: How does God show He will re-establish His covenant relationship with Israel?
options: By punishing all their enemies
By enacting new legal statutes
By speaking tenderly to them and making a covenant of peace
By requiring more sacrifices
questions.explanation: God promises to 'speak tenderly' to win Israel back and make a covenant of peace with them, including with the wild animals and birds, so they may live securely.

questions.question: What is the main message this passage teaches us?
options: God's love is based on perfect human performance
Once people sin, God abandons them forever
God's grace and mercy overcome human unfaithfulness, and He longs to restore His relationship with people
All difficulties will disappear immediately if we call upon God
questions.explanation: Despite Israel's unfaithfulness, God calls them back with love and grace, promising to restore their relationship and bless them abundantly.

en.reflection: Have there been times in your life when you felt distant from God or lost hope? How does this passage encourage you today?
reflectionOptions: It reminds me God never gives up on me
It motivates me to seek closeness with God again
It gives me hope for the future
en.prayer: Heavenly Father, thank You for Your unwavering love and compassion. When I stray or feel disheartened, draw me back with Your tender words. May I call You 'My Husband' and experience the intimate relationship, hope, and abundance You offer. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Find a quiet moment and say to God, “Lord, I desire to turn back to You.”

en.focus: Despite our frequent straying, God's love remains constant, calling us back to Him.

questions.question: What did the Lord command Hosea to do again?
options: Marry a foreign woman
Go and love a woman who is loved by another man and is an adulteress
Rebuke the people of Israel
Pray for the people of Israel
questions.explanation: The Lord commanded Hosea to go and show love to his wife again, even though she was loved by another and an adulteress.

questions.question: What does Hosea's relationship with the adulterous woman symbolize?
options: God's love for the land of Canaan
God's judgment on Egypt
The Lord's love for the Israelites
The covenant between Israel and other nations
questions.explanation: Hosea's relationship symbolizes the Lord's love for the Israelites, even though they turned to other gods and were unfaithful.

questions.question: According to the passage, how will the people of Israel seek the Lord their God in the future?
options: They will make alliances with foreign nations
They will seek other gods in exile
They will seek the Lord their God and David their king
They will build magnificent temples
questions.explanation: In the latter days, the Israelites will return and seek the Lord their God and David their king.

questions.question: What is the main message this passage conveys about God's character?
options: God is a strict judge who never forgives
God is indifferent and does not intervene in human affairs
God is faithful to His covenant, and His love never changes
God only loves those who are completely without sin
questions.explanation: This passage emphasizes God's faithful and unwavering love for His people, even in their rebellion, as He calls them back to Himself.

en.reflection: How does this passage encourage you that even if you have strayed from God, His love remains constant and calls you back?
en.prayer: Faithful God, thank You that even when I, like Israel, often stray from You, Your love never changes. Help me to respond to Your love, truly turn back to You, and experience Your grace and mercy more deeply. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Spend one minute today reflecting on God's unwavering love for you and offer Him thanks.

en.focus: God accuses His people, Israel, for their ignorance and unfaithfulness, revealing the deep roots of their moral decay.

questions.question: To whom does God address His accusation at the beginning of Hosea 4?
options: The nations
The tribe of Judah
The people of Israel
The Assyrians
questions.explanation: Hosea 4:1 explicitly states, “Hear the word of the LORD, O people of Israel.”

questions.question: According to Hosea 4:2, what sins did the people of Israel commit?
options: Theft, fraud, betrayal
Swearing, deception, murder, stealing, adultery, bloodshed
Idolatry, sorcery, lying
Oppressing the poor, breaking the Sabbath, despising the law
questions.explanation: The passage lists “swearing, lying, murder, stealing, and adultery,” noting that “bloodshed follows bloodshed.”

questions.question: Hosea 4:6 indicates that God's people are destroyed for what reason?
options: Lack of wealth
Lack of knowledge
Lack of military strength
Lack of political leadership
questions.explanation: God states, “My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge; because you have rejected knowledge, I reject you from being a priest to me.” This refers to the knowledge and understanding of God’s truth.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the priests of that time?
options: They faithfully taught the law
They led the people to worship idols
They delighted in sin and became corrupt with the people
They diligently sought God's will
questions.explanation: Hosea 4:8–9 reveals that the priests fed on the sins of the people and delighted in their iniquity, and therefore God would punish them according to their ways.

en.reflection: The warning in Hosea 4 reminds us that “lack of knowledge” about God has severe consequences. Today, in what area do you most need to deepen your understanding of God and His Word?
en.prayer: Loving Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding me through Hosea that knowing Your truth is so vital. Please forgive my sins committed out of ignorance, and grant me a heart that hungers for Your Word. Help me to know You more deeply each day and to live a life that pleases You. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Spend 5-10 minutes today reflecting on how you can be more intentional in learning God’s Word to avoid a “lack of knowledge.”

en.focus: God judges His people for their unfaithfulness, but His ultimate purpose is to lead them to return and seek Him.

questions.question: According to Hosea 5:1, which three groups of people is God addressing?
options: Priests, the house of Israel, the king
Priests, prophets, the people
Kings, leaders, commoners
The house of Israel, the house of Judah, foreign nations
questions.explanation: The text clearly states that God is speaking to the priests, the house of Israel (the people), and the king (the leaders) because they have all turned aside from the right path.

questions.type: Observe God's description of the people
questions.question: How does God describe the sin of Israel and Judah?
options: They became rich and arrogant
They have played the harlot and do not know the LORD
They built many altars for idols
They did not keep every commandment in the Book of the Law
questions.explanation: God describes Israel and Judah as playing the harlot through idolatry, turning away from Him, and not knowing Him.

questions.type: Understand the purpose of God's judgment
questions.question: According to this passage, what is the purpose of God's judgment?
options: To utterly destroy His people
To show them that God’s anger is eternal
To make them suffer until they return and seek Him
To punish them so they can never sin again
questions.explanation: The passage indicates that God will strike them until they acknowledge their guilt and earnestly seek Him in their distress, showing that the purpose of judgment is to lead the people to repentance and return to Him.

questions.question: What does this passage remind us to do when God allows us to experience difficulties?
options: Complain about God's injustice
Look for other alternative help
Examine our sins and seek God's mercy and healing
Wait for time to solve the problems itself
questions.explanation: The passage emphasizes that when the people face distress, they will seek God's face and acknowledge their guilt, which is exactly what God desires them to do.

en.reflection: In what areas have you recently felt distant from God, or encountered difficulties in your life? Does this remind you to seek Him more deeply?
reflectionOptions: Diligently read the Bible and pray to draw closer to God
en.prayer: Heavenly Father, thank You for being a righteous Judge and a loving Shepherd. Please shine Your light on me, so I can see any areas in my life where I have strayed from You. When I experience difficulties, help me not to despair, but to earnestly seek Your face, acknowledge my weaknesses, and experience Your healing and restoration. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take some time today to quietly pray to God, asking Him to reveal areas in your life that need to turn back to Him.

en.focus: True knowledge of God involves seeking and living out His steadfast love and justice, rather than mere religious rituals.

questions.question: As Hosea calls the people to 'return to the LORD,' what does he believe God will do for them?
options: He will immediately punish them
He will heal, bind up, and revive them
He will reject them and no longer be with them
He will demand more sacrifices
questions.explanation: The passage begins by calling the people to return, because the LORD, who has 'torn us, will heal us; he has struck us down, but he will bind us up. After two days he will revive us; on the third day he will restore us, that we may live in his presence.'

questions.question: What is the people's love and pursuit of God compared to in the passage?
options: Morning mist and early dew
Winter rains and spring thunder
Hot sun and desert drought
Tall mountains and deep oceans
questions.explanation: The people's love is described as being 'like a morning mist, like the early dew that disappears,' indicating its fleeting and insubstantial nature.

questions.question: What does God desire more than sacrifice and burnt offerings?
options: Strict adherence to all laws
Building magnificent temples
Steadfast love and the knowledge of God
Abundant offerings of gold and silver
questions.explanation: God explicitly states, 'I desire steadfast love and not sacrifice, the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.' This shows His preference for genuine inner attitude and relationship over external rituals.

questions.question: According to this passage, how can we truly know God and live a life pleasing to Him?
options: Just by regularly attending church services
By making more offerings and serving in church
By continuously seeking God, showing steadfast love to others, and truly understanding His heart
By avoiding all mistakes and becoming perfect
questions.explanation: The passage emphasizes striving 'to know the LORD' and that God desires 'steadfast love' and 'the knowledge of God.' This calls us to continuously seek Him, practice love in our lives, and understand His will.

en.reflection: In your daily life, do you sometimes prioritize outward religious forms over a genuine knowledge of God and steadfast love for others? How can you adjust today?
reflectionOptions: Spend more time in quiet prayer, seeking to know God
Actively express steadfast love to someone around you
Reflect on your motives and correct anything misaligned with God's heart
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for revealing Your heart to me, that You value my inner being and actions more than external rituals. Help me to strive to know You, so that my love is not a fleeting mist but enduring steadfast love. May I truly live out Your justice and mercy in my daily life. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, try to express kindness or offer help, in word or deed, to someone you don't usually interact with, practicing 'steadfast love'.

en.focus: God sees the sin and rebellion of His people with a broken heart, yet still calls them to return.

questions.question: When God desired to heal Israel, what did He see instead?
options: Their increasing wealth
Their healing from sickness
Their iniquity exposed
The destruction of their enemies
questions.explanation: The text states that when God desired to heal Israel, He saw their iniquity exposed, with fraud and theft rampant.

questions.question: What metaphor is used to describe Israel's failure to turn to God, instead relying on foreign nations?
options: A flock of lost sheep
An unleavened cake
A cake not turned
A withered tree
questions.explanation: Israel is compared to 'a cake not turned,' meaning they were unknowingly consumed by foreign influences, and not fully devoted to God.

questions.question: According to the passage, despite facing difficulties, what did the Israelites fail to do?
options: Offer sacrifices to Baal
Seek help from Egypt
Return wholeheartedly to the LORD
Fight among themselves
questions.explanation: Although the LORD punished them, they did not 'cry out to me from their hearts' but 'wail on their beds,' and did not 'return to the Most High.'

questions.question: This passage in Hosea reminds us, when we face difficulties, what should be our primary response?
options: Complain about unfair circumstances
Seek worldly solutions
Reflect on our sins and turn wholeheartedly to God
Pretend everything is fine
questions.explanation: The passage repeatedly highlights Israel's rebellion and their failure to turn to God, reminding us that when difficulties arise, we should first reflect on our relationship with God and turn back to Him wholeheartedly.

en.reflection: Have you ever, like the Israelites, sought other solutions in times of trouble, forgetting to turn wholeheartedly to God? What do you most need to confess to God and return from today?
reflectionOptions: Confess worry over an issue instead of trusting God
Confess solving a problem in my own strength
Confess a deep-seated lukewarmness towards God
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for the love and heartbreak revealed in Hosea. Please forgive me for times when, like Israel, I seek other ways in trouble instead of turning wholeheartedly to You. Help me to return today, to fully surrender my thoughts and heart to You. May my life bring glory to Your name. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Find a quiet moment to confess to God one area where you have not fully trusted Him in the past, and ask Him to help you turn back today.

en.theme: The Cost of Breaking the Covenant
en.focus: Israel's self-appointed kings and idol worship, a betrayal of God's covenant, will inevitably lead to divine judgment.

questions.question: How does the prophet Hosea describe Israel's sin at the beginning of the passage?
options: Theft
Deceit
Transgressing My covenant and violating My law
Selfishness
questions.explanation: The passage begins by identifying Israel's sin as 'transgressing My covenant and violating My law.'

questions.question: What actions did the people of Israel take that displeased God?
options: Building too many cities
Offering unacceptable sacrifices, appointing kings for themselves, and making idols
Seeking help from foreign nations
Not observing the Sabbath
questions.explanation: The passage states that Israel 'set up kings without My consent; they chose princes without My approval' and 'they make idols for themselves from their silver and gold, that they may be destroyed.'

questions.question: How will God respond to these actions of the people of Israel?
options: He will fully forgive them without consequence
He will grant them greater blessings
He will allow them to experience captivity, suffering, and ultimately destruction
He will punish them temporarily, but quickly forget their sins
questions.explanation: God says, 'I will tear down their cities,' and mentions, 'They will be among the nations like a vessel no one wants,' and 'They will throw their glory into the nations.' This implies captivity, suffering, and ultimate destruction.

questions.question: What is the most important reminder for us from this passage?
options: God will be pleased if we just serve Him diligently
Choosing our own way to worship God is more important than following His commands
God detests when we break His covenant, pursue idols, or act self-righteously
God will always be patient with our transgressions and never punish us
questions.explanation: This passage strongly indicates that Israel's actions of breaking God's covenant, making idols, and appointing their own kings were detestable to God and would lead to judgment.

en.reflection: Have you ever, without realizing it, strayed from God by pursuing your own desires or relying on worldly things?
reflectionOptions: Admitting to prioritizing money too much
Reflecting on relying on human approval over God's will
Examining if there are hidden idols (e.g., career, pleasure)
en.prayer: Heavenly Father, thank You for being a faithful, covenant-keeping God. Forgive me for times when I, like Israel, act as my own king, pursue my own desires, or treat things other than You as idols in my life. Help me to turn back and make You alone the sovereign Lord of my life. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, spend a few minutes quietly reflecting on what 'idols' in your life you may unknowingly value more than God. Ask God to help you let them go.

en.theme: The Cost of Sin and God's Judgment
en.focus: Israel faces inevitable judgment and displacement due to their unfaithfulness, yet God's heart grieves over them.

questions.question: According to Hosea 9:1, why should Israel not rejoice?
options: They are enjoying the harvest
They have intermarried with foreigners
They have played the whore, deserting their God
They have defeated their enemies in battle
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly states that Israel has played the whore, deserting their God, and therefore should not rejoice.

questions.question: According to Hosea 9:3–6, what significant things will Israel lose?
options: Their throne and wealth
Their land, temple worship, and sacrifices
Their alliances with neighboring countries
Their military strength and fortifications
questions.explanation: Israel will not dwell in the Lord’s land, nor pour out wine offerings to Him. Their sacrifices will not be acceptable, and they will ultimately wander in Egypt and Assyria, to be buried in foreign lands.

questions.type: Observe God's reaction to His people
questions.question: Despite Israel's rebellion, what is God's emotional response towards them?
options: Complete disgust and rejection
Indifference and apathy
Sorrow and abandonment due to their evil
Instant destruction without mercy
questions.explanation: The text implies God's abandonment of them due to their evil (9:15), reflecting His sorrow and anger over their rebellion.

questions.question: What main truth about sin does this passage remind us of?
options: Sin is insignificant as long as there is genuine repentance
Sin leads to broken fellowship with God and inevitable judgment
God will ultimately overlook human transgressions
Sin is an unavoidable destiny for humanity
questions.explanation: Hosea clearly depicts how Israel's sin leads to their broken relationship with God and a series of severe judgments, including loss of land and exile.

en.reflection: This passage reminds us of the seriousness of sin. Today, do you need to repent and turn to God to avoid the bondage and consequences of sin?
reflectionOptions: Confess and abandon a hidden sin
Repent of my selfishness to God
Take my relationship with God more seriously
en.prayer: Heavenly Father, You are a holy and righteous God. Please forgive all the ways I have sinned against You. Help me to recognize the seriousness of sin and grant me the strength to turn away from evil and fully return to You. May my heart belong to You alone. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Spend 5 minutes today quietly reflecting on any areas in your life that displease God, confess them, and repent to Him.

en.focus: Israel reaped the consequences of their unfaithfulness, yet God calls them to return to Him and seek His righteousness.

questions.question: How does the prophet Hosea describe Israel’s initial state?
options: A luxuriant vine that yields its fruit
Barren land that produces nothing
A cut-down olive tree with no hope
An overgrown garden full of weeds
questions.explanation: The passage begins by describing Israel as a luxuriant vine that yielded fruit, but their prosperity led to idolatry.

questions.question: What did the people of Israel do when they prospered, and what were the consequences?
options: They built many altars to worship the LORD, leading to peace and prosperity
They built many altars and sacred pillars for themselves, having a divided heart, leading to the destruction of their land
They sought alliances with foreign nations, gaining strong military power
They kept God's laws, and therefore received God's blessings
questions.explanation: In their prosperity, Israel had a divided heart and built altars and sacred pillars for themselves, resulting in the destruction of their land and the cutting off of their king.

questions.question: According to this chapter, what is God's fundamental requirement for the people of Israel?
options: To build more altars and sacred pillars
To seek help from foreign nations against their enemies
To sow for yourselves righteousness, and seek the LORD
To continue relying on their own strength, chariots, and many warriors
questions.explanation: God calls Israel to stop their wickedness, sow righteousness, and seek the LORD, so that His righteousness may come upon them like a shower.

questions.question: In our walk of faith, what does this passage primarily warn us against today?
options: Working hard to acquire wealth
Neglecting God's grace, having a divided heart, and relying on our own strength or worldly securities instead of Him
Building friendships with non-believers
Planning and saving for the future
questions.explanation: Israel's failure was their divided heart, attributing prosperity to idols rather than God, and relying on their own power. We should avoid a similar mindset and rely solely on God.

en.reflection: Have you ever, in times of success or gain, begun to rely on yourself or other securities instead of God? What 'righteousness' do you most need to sow today?
reflectionOptions: Seek God's righteousness and guidance in an area
en.prayer: Lord, I confess that sometimes, like Israel, when I receive Your grace, I become proud and rely on my own strength or worldly securities. Please forgive me. Help me to seek You alone, to sow righteousness, and to bear fruit that is pleasing to You in my life. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, take a few quiet moments to reflect on anything you have been relying on yourself or external things for, rather than fully on God. Confess it to Him and ask for His help to turn back.

en.focus: God calls His rebellious people back with unfailing love, even as He must discipline them for their sins.

questions.question: How did God treat Israel when they were young?
options: He handed them over to their enemies
He kept them imprisoned
He loved them and called them out of Egypt
He completely ignored them
questions.explanation: God recalls that when Israel was young, He loved them and called them out of Egypt.

questions.question: How does God describe His tender care for Israel?
options: He ruled them with an iron rod
He bound them with ropes
He led them with cords of human kindness, like one who lifts an infant to the cheek
He protected them with high walls
questions.explanation: God says He led them with cords of human kindness, with ties of love, like one who lifts an infant to the cheek, and bent down to feed them.

questions.question: What internal struggle did God experience in response to Israel's rebellion?
options: He immediately decided to destroy them
He was indifferent to their fate
His heart was turned, His compassion grew warm, and He would not carry out His fierce anger
He completely withdrew all grace
questions.explanation: God’s heart was turned within Him, His compassion grew warm, and He would not destroy Israel, because He is God and not a man.

questions.question: How does this chapter encourage us when we face our own weaknesses and failures?
options: Our failures will completely destroy God's love for us
God's love for us has limits and will soon run out
Even when we are rebellious, God's love and compassion endure, and He calls us to return
God's discipline means He has completely given up on us
questions.explanation: Despite Israel's rebellion, God could not bring Himself to destroy them. His love and compassion are eternal, which encourages us to return to Him even in our weaknesses.

en.reflection: Looking back at your life, how has God drawn you to Himself with 'cords of human kindness'?
reflectionOptions: Through a difficult situation or challenge
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for Your unchanging love and compassion. When I, like a child, stray from Your path, draw me back to You with Your cords of love. Help me to always remember Your grace and respond to Your call. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take a moment of quiet reflection to thank God for demonstrating His love and patience in your life, especially when He gently called you back when you strayed.

en.focus: Through His prophet, God reminds His people that their history and future depend on His mercy and faithfulness, not on human efforts or idols.

questions.question: How does Hosea 12 begin by describing Israel's condition?
options: They were rich and powerful, living in comfort
They pursued idols and made alliances with foreign nations
They faithfully served God and pleased Him
They were in famine and in urgent need of help
questions.explanation: The passage states that Israel “tells lies and practices deceit all day long,” making alliances with Assyria and Egypt, and pursuing the empty wind.

questions.question: What historical experience of their ancestor Jacob does God remind His people about in this passage?
options: Jacob met God at Bethel and wrestled with an angel, prevailing
Jacob contended with his brother Esau and seized the birthright
Jacob became a prime minister in Egypt, saving his family
Jacob built a city and became a powerful leader
questions.explanation: God reminds Israel that their ancestor Jacob wrestled with an angel, met God at Bethel, and received the name “Israel.”

questions.question: What is God's main message to the people of Israel through Hosea 12?
options: God has abandoned them and no longer has any relationship with them
They can obtain God's forgiveness by offering more sacrifices
They must return to God, maintain love and justice, and wait continually for Him
They should imitate other nations and seek political and military strength
questions.explanation: God calls His people to “return to your God, maintain love and justice, and wait for your God always.” This is God's expectation for them.

questions.question: How does this chapter remind us of God's faithfulness and human nature?
options: God's faithfulness is limited, depending on human performance
Human nature is to gain blessings by oneself, without needing God
God's faithfulness is eternal, while humans often forget His grace and call
Humans can rely on their own strength and wisdom to solve all problems
questions.explanation: The passage repeatedly reminds the Israelites that even though they turned away from God, He remains their God, calling them to return and recalling His past care for them. Human nature, however, is forgetful and self-reliant.

en.reflection: Reflect on whether you, like the Israelites, have recently forgotten God's grace in some area and turned to rely on yourself or other things?
reflectionOptions: Over-relying on my own abilities in work or studies
Seeking human approval in relationships rather than God's guidance
Turning to others for help before God when facing difficulties
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for Your faithful care in my life. Please forgive me when, like the Israelites, I often forget Your grace and turn to rely on myself or the world. Help me to return to You, to maintain love and justice, and to wait for You always. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, take one minute to quietly reflect on one specific grace of God in your life and offer thanks for it.

en.focus: God's severe judgment aims to turn His people back, for His steadfast love never fails.

questions.question: What happened when Ephraim spoke?
options: Israel grew stronger
Israel sinned out of reverence for God
Ephraim was exalted in Israel
Israel became wealthier
questions.explanation: The passage states that when Ephraim spoke, he was exalted in Israel.

questions.question: What does God compare Himself to in relation to Ephraim?
options: A strong bull
A bear deprived of her cubs
A free bird
A lost sheep
questions.explanation: God describes Himself as a bear deprived of her cubs, ready to ambush and destroy them.

questions.question: Despite Israel's rebellion, what does God still promise to do for them?
options: Abandon them forever
Deliver them to their enemies
Ransom them from the power of death
Leave Samaria utterly desolate
questions.explanation: God promises to ransom them from the power of Sheol and redeem them from death, showing His ultimate mercy.

questions.question: What does this passage primarily teach us about God's character?
options: God is only concerned with punishing sin
God is distant and uninvolved in human affairs
God's wrath is holy and ultimately aims for the redemption of His people
God is powerless against human rebellion
questions.explanation: Though filled with judgment for rebellion, God's ultimate promise is redemption, showing His wrath aims to turn His people back to His lovingkindness.

en.reflection: Is there an area in your life where you need to turn back to God? Do you trust that even in discipline, God's love remains with you?
reflectionOptions: Confess rebellion and seek God's forgiveness
Recommit to God's Word and prayer
Release control of something to God's sovereignty
en.prayer: Faithful God, You are my help. Thank You for Your steadfast love, which disciplines me even in my rebellion to lead me back to You. Help me to see areas in my life that need to change and grant me strength to obey You. May my heart always turn toward You. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take a minute to quietly reflect on God's love and discipline, and offer a short prayer asking Him to guide you back to Him.

en.theme: Return to the Lord, Be Healed
en.focus: God calls His people to return to Him, promising to heal their waywardness and shower them with abundant grace and steadfast love.

questions.question: What does Hosea 14:1 call the people of Israel to do?
options: Build stronger defenses
Seek help from Assyria
Return to the LORD
Prepare for battle
questions.explanation: The passage begins with a direct call for Israel to return to the LORD their God.

questions.question: When Israel returns to God with words of repentance, how does God promise to treat them?
options: Punish them according to their sins
Never acknowledge them again
Heal their waywardness and love them freely
Demand more sacrifices from them
questions.explanation: God promises to heal their waywardness and love them freely, for His anger will turn away from them.

questions.question: What imagery does God use to describe the rich blessings and stability He will give to Israel?
options: Rushing rivers
Morning sunlight
Dew, an olive tree, and a cedar of Lebanon
Towering mountain peaks
questions.explanation: God promises to be like the dew to Israel, causing them to blossom like a lily, take root like a cedar of Lebanon, and flourish like an olive tree.

questions.question: What is the primary message this passage teaches us?
options: People can return to God through their own efforts
God's punishment is unchangeable
Repentance and returning to God lead to His healing, forgiveness, and abundant life
Only through sacrifices can God's anger be appeased
questions.explanation: This passage emphasizes the necessity of repentance and God's promises of healing, forgiveness, steadfast love, and abundant life to those who return to Him.

en.reflection: In what area do you most need to turn back to God more deeply today to experience His healing and renewal?
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for calling me to return to You. I confess my weaknesses and times I have strayed. Please heal my waywardness and fill me with Your steadfast love. May I be rooted in You like a cedar of Lebanon and bear fruit like an olive tree. In Jesus' name, I pray. Amen.
en.action: Take a moment today to quietly confess to God a weakness or transgression you wish to turn from, asking for His forgiveness and healing.

en.focus: In times of disaster, God calls His people to repent and turn wholeheartedly to Him.

questions.question: Who does the prophet Joel primarily call to listen to his message at the beginning of the book?
options: Kings of the nations
Priests in Jerusalem
Elders and all inhabitants of the land
Soldiers of Israel
questions.explanation: Joel begins by appealing to the 'elders' and 'all who live in the land' to pay attention to the prophet's message.

questions.question: What type of severe disaster is described in the passage?
options: Earthquakes and tsunamis
An invasion of locusts
Famine and plague
Floods and landslides
questions.explanation: The chapter vividly details how locusts devour the land's produce, bringing devastating calamity.

questions.question: In response to this disaster, what action does the prophet Joel call the people to take?
options: Organize an army to fight enemies
Seek help from neighboring countries
Fast, weep, wail, and cry out to the LORD
Migrate to more fertile lands
questions.explanation: Joel calls the people to fast, weep, wail, and gather at the house of the LORD to cry out to Him, showing repentance and reliance on God.

questions.question: How does Joel's message help us reflect on current global challenges (e.g., pandemics, economic crises, environmental issues)?
options: They are merely natural phenomena, unrelated to God
We should rely solely on science and human effort to solve problems
It reminds us to humble ourselves, examine our hearts, and wholeheartedly seek God's help
It encourages us to become stronger to control nature
questions.explanation: Joel's message reminds us that when facing uncontrollable disasters, it is important to humble ourselves, examine our hearts, and turn wholeheartedly to God, seeking His mercy and help.

en.reflection: When faced with difficulties and challenges in your life or the world, in what area do you most need to turn more deeply to God for His help?
en.prayer: Almighty Father, when disaster and difficulty strike, help me to see Your will, humble myself, and turn to You with all my heart. Forgive my transgressions, grant me strength and wisdom to face challenges, and lead me to pray for the suffering of the world. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Spend some time today praying about a difficulty or challenge you know of, and ask God how you can rely on Him in it.

en.focus: God calls His people to return to Him with sincere repentance before judgment, for He is a God of grace and compassion.

questions.question: What sound does the prophet Joel use to warn the people at the beginning of the passage?
options: Singing
A trumpet blast
Thunder
Shouting
questions.explanation: Joel calls for a trumpet to be blown in Zion, sounding an alarm about the approaching day of the Lord.

questions.question: How is God's character described when His people turn back to Him?
options: A strict judge
A righteous avenger
Gracious, compassionate, slow to anger, abounding in love
A silent spectator
questions.explanation: The passage clearly states that God is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and abounding in love, and He relents from sending calamity.

questions.question: What is the core of the sincere repentance emphasized in Joel?
options: Merely tearing clothes
Fasting, weeping, mourning, and tearing one's heart
Offering more sacrifices
Promising not to make mistakes in the future
questions.explanation: God calls His people to tear their hearts, not just their garments, indicating that He desires genuine inner repentance, not just outward displays.

questions.question: What is the main message this passage helps us understand about how we should respond to personal or collective challenges?
options: Complain about circumstances and wait for others to solve them
Work harder and rely on our own strength
Turn to God, seeking His mercy and help with a humble and genuinely repentant heart
Ignore the problems and pretend everything is fine
questions.explanation: In the face of God's judgment or difficulties, Joel calls the people to collective fasting and prayer, humbly seeking God's grace and mercy.

en.reflection: In what area do you most need to turn back to God with a 'torn heart' sincerity today?
reflectionOptions: Let go of pride and admit my shortcomings
Forgive someone who has wronged me
en.prayer: Loving Father, thank You for being a God full of grace and compassion. When my heart strays from You, please remind me and give me the strength to return to You with a truly repentant heart. May Your grace cover me, granting me forgiveness and renewal. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Find a quiet moment to confess a weakness in your heart to God and ask Him to help you genuinely turn back.

en.theme: God Responds and Pours Out Grace
en.focus: When God's people genuinely turn back to Him, He responds to their cry and pours out abundant grace and His Spirit.

questions.question: What was the LORD's reaction when His people genuinely turned back in repentance?
options: He abandoned them
He was jealous for His land and took pity on His people
He became angry with them
He pretended not to hear
questions.explanation: The scripture states that the LORD was jealous for His land and took pity on His people.

questions.question: Besides material abundance (like grain, new wine, and oil), what special blessing did God promise to pour out?
options: More enemies
A larger army
His Spirit on all people
Long life and health
questions.explanation: God promised to pour out His Spirit on all people, enabling them to dream dreams and prophesy.

questions.question: What is the core message of Joel 2:28–32?
options: Only certain people can experience God's Spirit
God's promises to Israel are no longer valid
In the last days, God will universally pour out His Spirit and save all who call on His name
One can only call upon God's name in specific locations
questions.explanation: God promises to pour out His Spirit on all people in the last days and emphasizes that everyone who calls on the name of the LORD will be saved.

questions.question: How does this passage encourage our relationship with God today?
options: We should only focus on material blessings
God's grace and the outpouring of His Spirit only happened in ancient times
When we turn back to God, He is eager to show grace and give His Spirit and salvation
God only saves a select few
questions.explanation: The passage clearly shows that when people turn back, God shows grace, provides abundantly, pours out His Spirit, and saves all who call on His name.

en.reflection: Today, do you sense God pouring out His Spirit on you? What do you most need to call upon God for?
reflectionOptions: Ask God to fill me more with His Spirit
Pray for my loved ones, that God would pour out His Spirit on them too
Call on God's name in a specific difficulty
en.prayer: Lord, thank You for being a zealous and compassionate God to Your people. When I turn back to You, You show grace and pour out Your Spirit. Please fill me more today, guide me, and enable me to live according to Your will. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, spend a few minutes in quiet, asking the Holy Spirit to fill you more, and then pray for three people around you, asking God to pour out His Spirit on them too.

en.focus: God's sovereignty is displayed in His judgment of the nations and ultimate restoration of His people.

questions.question: According to the beginning of Joel chapter 3, where does the LORD declare He will gather all nations to judge them?
options: The Valley of Shechem
The Valley of Jehoshaphat
The Valley of Kishon
The Valley of Elah
questions.explanation: The LORD declares He will gather all nations into the Valley of Jehoshaphat to judge them there.

questions.question: What is the primary reason the LORD judges the nations, according to the passage?
options: They did not offer sacrifices to God
They divided God's land and scattered His people
They built the Tower of Babel
They worshipped the sun, moon, and stars
questions.explanation: The LORD judges the nations because they scattered His people among the nations and divided His land, and sold them.

questions.question: What does God promise to do for Judah and Jerusalem?
options: Send them a new famine
Leave them desolate forever
Make them holy, and no foreigners will pass through
Allow more nations to invade them
questions.explanation: God promises to cleanse Judah and Jerusalem, making them holy, and no foreigners will pass through them again.

questions.question: What is the greatest hope Joel chapter 3 offers us?
options: People can overcome all enemies by their own strength
God will ultimately intervene in history to bring righteous judgment and complete restoration
All difficulties will disappear immediately with diligent prayer
Observing the law will prevent all future suffering
questions.explanation: The central message is that God is sovereign, and He will ultimately bring righteous judgment and complete restoration to His people.

en.reflection: When facing injustice or hardship, how do the promises of God's judgment and restoration in Joel 3 strengthen your faith?
reflectionOptions: Reminds me God is in control
Helps me release things to God
Motivates me to pray for justice
en.prayer: Almighty Father, thank You for being a righteous Judge and a faithful Deliverer. When I face injustice in the world or personal difficulties, help me to look to You, trusting that You will bring judgment and restoration in Your perfect time. May my heart find peace and hope in Your promises. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take one minute today to meditate on the phrase, “The LORD is a refuge for His people” (Joel 3:16), resting in Him.

en.focus: Amos prophesies God's judgment upon the surrounding nations for their cruelty and injustice.

questions.question: From which place did the prophet Amos come as a shepherd?
options: Tekoa
Bethlehem
Jerusalem
Samaria
questions.explanation: Amos was a shepherd from Tekoa, called by God to deliver messages to Israel and the surrounding nations.

questions.question: God's judgment on Damascus (Aram) and Gaza (Philistia) was primarily because of what actions?
options: They failed to offer sufficient sacrifices
They built too many altars to idols
They threshed Gilead with iron sledges and exiled whole communities to Edom
They formed alliances with Israel against other nations
questions.explanation: God judged Damascus for threshing Gilead with iron sledges and Gaza for exiling whole communities to Edom.

questions.question: In the passage, what does God repeatedly threaten to send upon the nations as judgment?
options: Locusts
Plague
Fire
Earthquakes
questions.explanation: God repeatedly declares He will send fire to consume the walls and palaces of the nations, symbolizing His fierce wrath and thorough judgment.

questions.question: What is the main message of Amos chapter one's prophecies?
options: God only cares about the Israelites, not foreign nations
God's justice extends not only to His chosen people but to all nations and peoples
Powerful nations are exempt from God's judgment
God's judgment is always immediate, without a period of grace
questions.explanation: Amos clearly shows that God is the Judge of all the earth, and His justice and moral standards apply to all nations, both chosen and Gentile.

en.reflection: What 'small' things in your daily life might be against God's justice and mercy, as highlighted by this passage?
en.prayer: Righteous Lord, I acknowledge You are the God who governs all, and Your judgment extends to all the earth. Help me to see the world through Your eyes and be more sensitive to injustice. Please also illuminate my heart so I may live out Your justice and mercy. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, pray for the nation you live in, asking God to enable it to act justly and love mercy.

en.focus: God judges not only the sins of foreign nations but also the sins of His own people, for He is righteous.
