questions.explanation: The text explicitly states that the word of the LORD came to Zechariah in the second year of Darius.

questions.question: What was the main appeal the LORD made to His people through Zechariah?
options: To seek vengeance on their enemies
To build strong military walls
To return to Him, and He would return to them
To offer more sacrifices
questions.explanation: God’s core message through the prophet was: “Return to me, and I will return to you.”

questions.question: In Zechariah's first vision, what did the man riding the red horse report to the angel of the LORD?
options: The whole earth is at rest and quiet
The whole earth is full of war
The whole earth is rebuilding the temple
The whole earth is suffering from famine
questions.explanation: The man on the red horse reported: “We have gone throughout the earth, and behold, all the earth is at rest and quiet.”

questions.question: What is the main encouragement this passage offers to the returned exiles?
options: God has forgotten them
They should only focus on their personal affairs
God's anger has passed, and He will once again be gracious to them
Their enemies will soon be completely destroyed
questions.explanation: Through the visions, God assures His people that His anger has passed, and He will again choose Jerusalem, showing zeal for her and Zion, promising rebuilding and restoration.

en.reflection: Today, in what area of your life do you most need God to turn to you and show you His grace?
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for being the loving God who calls me to return to You. Help me to turn more deeply towards You today and seek Your face. I trust that Your grace and mercy never change. Strengthen me with Your presence and Your promises. In Jesus' name, I pray, Amen.
en.action: Find a quiet moment and meditate on Zechariah 1:3: “'Return to me,' declares the LORD Almighty, 'and I will return to you.'”

en.focus: God promises to personally protect His people and to greatly expand Jerusalem among all nations.

questions.question: What did Zechariah see in his vision?
options: A temple being built
A man with a measuring line
Farmers working in the fields
A marching army
questions.explanation: Zechariah looked up and saw a man with a measuring line, going to measure Jerusalem.

questions.question: How did God promise Jerusalem would develop?
options: It would have stronger walls built
Its population would decrease but become purer
It would be inhabited without walls because of its great numbers of people and livestock
It would become a small, remote town
questions.explanation: The Lord declared that Jerusalem would be inhabited like unwalled villages, because of its great number of people and livestock.

questions.question: What did God promise to be for Jerusalem's walls?
options: Walls built of gold
The Lord Himself would be a wall of fire around it
Walls guarded by angels
Impenetrable stone walls
questions.explanation: The Lord declares that He will be a wall of fire around Jerusalem and its glory within it.

questions.question: Why did God call His people to flee from Babylon?
options: Babylon was about to be destroyed by an earthquake
Babylon was destined for judgment
There would be a famine in Babylon
Babylon would be flooded
questions.explanation: God refers to Babylon as 'the land of the north' and 'daughter of Babylon,' calling His people to flee because He would rise to judge the nations that plundered them.

en.reflection: What is the greatest comfort and hope this passage brings you today?
reflectionOptions: God's promise of expansion and glory
en.prayer: Almighty Father, thank You for promising to be a wall of fire around me and my glory within. When I feel alone, weak, or afraid, please remind me that You personally protect me. Expand my heart to know Your love and faithfulness more deeply. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Pray a one-sentence prayer: “Lord, thank You for being my wall of fire and my glory.”

en.theme: Clothed in Righteousness, Accepted by God
en.focus: God graciously removes our iniquity and clothes us in clean garments.

questions.question: In Zechariah 3:1–2, who stands before the Angel of the LORD to be judged, and who stands at his right hand to accuse him?
options: Joshua the High Priest and Satan
Zechariah the prophet and the archangel
Zerubbabel the governor of Judah and foreign enemies
The people of Israel and the king of Assyria
questions.explanation: The passage clearly states that Joshua the High Priest stood before the Angel of the LORD, and Satan stood at his right hand to accuse him.

questions.question: What kind of clothes was Joshua the High Priest wearing when he stood before the Angel of the LORD?
options: Splendid priestly garments
Filthy clothes
Brand-new white robes
Old, worn-out everyday clothes
questions.explanation: The text vividly describes Joshua wearing filthy clothes, symbolizing his iniquity.

questions.question: How did God deal with Joshua's filthy clothes and his iniquity?
options: He commanded Joshua to wash his clothes himself
He required Joshua to offer a sin offering
He commanded those standing by to take off his filthy clothes and clothe him with rich robes and a clean turban
He punished him and removed him from his position as High Priest
questions.explanation: The Angel of the LORD commanded those present to remove Joshua's filthy clothes and to clothe him with rich robes and a clean turban, symbolizing God's forgiveness of his iniquity and his cleansing.

questions.question: What is the main message about God's salvation conveyed in this passage?
options: People must remove their own iniquity through their own efforts
God will unconditionally forgive everyone's sins
God actively and completely forgives iniquity and restores His servants to purity and honor
Only the High Priest can be accepted by God
questions.explanation: The core message is that God actively removes Joshua's iniquity (filthy clothes) and grants him purity and honor (rich robes and a clean turban), all out of His grace.

en.reflection: Today's scripture reminds us that God actively removes our iniquity. Reflect on a time in your life when you experienced God's gracious forgiveness. How did that make you feel?
reflectionOptions: Motivated to live a holier life
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for removing my iniquity, just as You removed Joshua's filthy clothes, making me clean through the precious blood of Jesus Christ. Help me to always live in Your grace and to serve You with a grateful heart. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, take a moment to meditate on the salvation accomplished for you by Jesus Christ and offer Him thanks.

en.theme: Not by Might, Nor by Power
en.focus: God's power and the work of His Spirit, not human strength or skill, are key to accomplishing His mission.

questions.question: What did Zechariah see in his vision?
options: A golden lampstand and two olive trees
A burning bush and a rock
A fallen wall and two angels
A high priest and a judgment seat
questions.explanation: Zechariah saw a solid gold lampstand with a bowl on top and seven lamps on it, with seven channels to each lamp. And there were two olive trees beside it.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the statement, “’Not by might nor by power, but by my Spirit,’ says the LORD Almighty”?
options: People don't need to try, just wait for miracles
Human effort is completely irrelevant in God’s work
God’s plans are accomplished through His Spirit's power, not human strength or wisdom
God’s work can be done with enough resources and talent
questions.explanation: This statement emphasizes that God's work is accomplished through His Spirit, and human strength and ability are secondary.

questions.question: What does the 'great mountain' symbolize in the passage?
options: Great wealth
Insurmountable obstacles
Powerful enemies
Steadfast faith
questions.explanation: The 'great mountain' symbolizes the immense, seemingly insurmountable obstacles before Zerubbabel, which God promises will become level ground.

questions.question: What does this passage remind us about serving in the church today?
options: We should rely more on our own abilities and experience
We should pray more and trust in the Holy Spirit's power to accomplish God's work
We should pursue larger scale and greater influence
We should avoid any ministry that seems difficult
questions.explanation: The passage reminds us that in ministry, ultimate success comes not from human ability, but from the work of the Holy Spirit and God's mighty power.

en.reflection: What 'great mountain' are you currently facing that makes you feel powerless, needing to rely more on the Holy Spirit than your own strength?
en.prayer: Almighty God, I confess my limited strength and abilities. When I face the 'great mountains' in my life, remind me that it is not by might nor by power, but by Your Spirit that things are accomplished. May Your Holy Spirit work within me, enabling me to move forward in faith and fulfill Your will. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Find a quiet moment to pray about one thing currently causing you stress or making you feel powerless, asking the Holy Spirit to guide and empower you.

en.focus: God is determined to remove all wickedness from among His people and establish a holy dwelling place.

questions.question: What did Zechariah first see in his vision?
options: A golden lampstand
A flying scroll
A chariot
A basin full of water
questions.explanation: Zechariah first saw a flying scroll, twenty cubits long and ten cubits wide.

questions.type: Observe the meaning of the vision
questions.question: What did the flying scroll represent?
options: God's blessings coming upon the whole land
The curse of God going out over the whole land against wickedness
God raising up new leaders
God rebuilding the temple
questions.explanation: The flying scroll symbolized the curse of God going out over the whole land against those who steal and swear falsely, cutting off the wicked.

questions.question: What did Zechariah see in the second vision of chapter 5?
options: An ephah basket of grain
A flourishing olive tree
A bronze altar
A basket with a woman inside
questions.explanation: Zechariah saw a basket (or ephah) with a woman sitting inside it, representing wickedness.

questions.question: What common message do these two visions convey about God's character?
options: God is lenient toward sin because He is full of love
God is only concerned with judging pagans, not His own people
God is holy and will thoroughly remove wickedness from among His people
God desires people to atone for sin through sacrifices, not true repentance
questions.explanation: The flying scroll symbolizes God's judgment on sin, and the vision of removing the woman (wickedness) indicates God's determination to completely remove sin from His people, making them holy.

en.reflection: Is there any area of your life that you know is wicked, but you have found it difficult to let go of or deal with?
reflectionOptions: Ask God to reveal hidden sin
Confess sin to God and seek forgiveness
Seek help from a spiritual mentor
en.prayer: Holy Lord, I thank You that You are a righteous God, determined to remove all wickedness from my life. Please search my heart and reveal any sins I have been unwilling to face. Help me to bravely surrender them to You and to live a holy life by Your strength. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Quietly reflect on one sin God revealed to you today that needs to be removed, and pray to God in confession about it.

en.theme: The Crown and the Builder's Hope
en.focus: God promises to raise up 'the Branch' who will build the temple and serve as a priest-king, bringing peaceful governance.

questions.question: What did Zechariah see coming out from between two bronze mountains in his vision?
options: Four chariots
Four angels
Four trees
Four rivers
questions.explanation: Zechariah saw four chariots coming out from between two bronze mountains, each drawn by horses of different colors.

questions.question: What did the LORD command Zechariah to do for the high priest Joshua?
options: Anoint him with oil
Dress him in splendid garments
Make a crown and place it on his head
Offer sacrifices for him
questions.explanation: The LORD commanded Zechariah to take silver and gold from those who had arrived and make crowns to place on the head of the high priest Joshua.

questions.question: Who is referred to as 'the Branch' in this passage, and what will He accomplish?
options: A new high priest who will rebuild the altar
A new king who will lead armies in battle
A Messiah who will build the temple and serve as a priest-king
A prophet who will bring new laws
questions.explanation: 'The Branch' refers to a prophesied Messiah who will build the temple of the LORD and sit on His throne, combining the roles of king and priest, bringing about peaceful rule.

questions.question: How does the prophecy in Zechariah 6 encourage us today?
options: It reminds us to solely focus on waiting for future judgment
It inspires us to rebuild everything by ourselves without God's help
It shows us that God is in control of history and ultimately fulfills His promises through Christ
It teaches us that offering more donations will accelerate the prophecy's fulfillment
questions.explanation: This passage prophesies the coming of the Messiah who will build the temple (referring to the church) and serve as both King and Priest, bringing peace. This reveals God's sovereignty over history and His redemptive promises fulfilled in Christ.

en.reflection: In your daily life, are you able to see God building His church and governing all things through Jesus Christ?
reflectionOptions: Yes, I see God's work happening
Sometimes I do, sometimes I forget
I need to seek God's guidance more
en.prayer: Almighty God, thank You for revealing Your redemptive plan through Zechariah’s prophecy, pointing to Jesus Christ as 'the Branch' who would build the temple and serve as the King of Peace and Priest. Help me to grasp more deeply all that You have accomplished in Christ, and may my life be a testament to Your glory. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Spend some time today meditating on Jesus Christ's identity as King and Priest, and how He brings true peace.

en.focus: God calls His people to obey His instructions and to treat each other with mercy and justice.

questions.question: In Zechariah 7:1, in which month did Sharezer and Regem-Melek send men to the house of God to inquire?
options: Passover
Pentecost
The fourth month
The ninth month
questions.explanation: The passage clearly states that it was in the fourth year of King Darius, in the ninth month, Chislev, that they sent men to the house of God.

questions.question: What was the question the people asked the priests and prophets?
options: Should we continue to offer sacrifices?
Should we continue to observe the fasts?
When can we rebuild the temple?
Can we return to Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Their question was: 'Should I mourn and fast in the fifth month, as I have done for so many years?'

questions.question: When God responded through Zechariah to the people's question, what did He emphasize?
options: Fasting is more important than justice and mercy
The tradition of fasting must be strictly followed
They were fasting for themselves, not truly for God
God dislikes all forms of fasting
questions.explanation: God pointed out that their fasting in the fifth and seventh months was not truly for Him, but for themselves, and they had neglected His call for justice, mercy, and compassion.

questions.question: Why did God's people suffer punishment and dispersion?
options: Because they did not fast often enough
Because they refused to listen to God's words and hardened their hearts
Because they did not offer enough sacrifices to God
Because they failed to rebuild the temple
questions.explanation: God said they refused to listen, turning a stubborn shoulder and making their hearts like flint, so that they would not hear the law and the words of the prophets, which is why He scattered them among the nations.

en.reflection: In which areas do I need to re-examine my faith practices today to ensure I am truly doing them for God, and not for myself or out of tradition?
reflectionOptions: My giving of time or money
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding me through Zechariah that You value not just outward religious rituals, but my inner obedience to You and my love for others. Please help me to examine my heart, ensuring that every act of worship and service is sincerely for You. May I treat those around me with justice and mercy. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, try to express love or compassion to a fellow believer with a specific action.

en.focus: God promises to return to His people, rebuild their city, bless them, and make them a blessing to the nations.

questions.question: What does the Lord state twice as His intention for Zion (Jerusalem)?
options: To make Zion the center of all nations
To fill Zion with gold and silver
To be zealous for Zion with great wrath
To destroy all of Zion's enemies
questions.explanation: The Lord declares, “I am jealous for Zion with great jealousy; with great wrath I am jealous for her.” This shows His intense love and protective heart for Jerusalem.

questions.type: Observe the future scene of Jerusalem
questions.question: What scenes are described for the future of Jerusalem?
options: Only old people sitting in the streets, with young people on battlefields
Both old people and children dwelling safely in the city
The city being full of pagan idols
Only priests and Levites serving in the city
questions.explanation: The scripture prophesies that old men and women will again sit in the streets of Jerusalem, and boys and girls will play there.

questions.question: What changes will God’s people experience when they return and rebuild?
options: They will no longer need to obey the law
They will no longer suffer from famine and poverty
They will be transformed from a curse into a blessing, with abundant produce, and all nations seeking the Lord
They can do as they please, without God's discipline
questions.explanation: God promises they will no longer be a curse but a blessing, with the land yielding its produce and the heavens giving their dew; and many nations will come to Jerusalem to seek the Lord.

questions.question: In light of God's promised blessings, what does He command His people to do?
options: To only enjoy their wealth selfishly
To speak the truth to one another and judge justly at the city gates
To only offer sacrifices to God, ignoring their neighbours
To wait for God to do everything on His own
questions.explanation: God commands them to speak the truth to one another, render true and righteous judgment in their gates, and not to devise evil in their hearts or love a false oath.

en.reflection: How do the promises in Zechariah 8 give you new hope for God's plans for your life and the church?
reflectionOptions: Trusting God to rebuild broken parts of my life
Becoming more actively involved in church ministry
Anticipating God's work manifesting around me
en.prayer: Faithful Lord, thank You for Your unwavering zeal and promises for Your people. I pray that You will accomplish Your work of restoration and blessing in my life and in our church. Help me to live in truth and righteousness, becoming a channel of Your blessing. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, speak an honest and encouraging word to someone around you, reflecting God's command to 'speak the truth'.

en.focus: God's promised King will come riding on a donkey, bringing righteousness and salvation, and establishing true peace and freedom.

questions.question: How is the King described in Zechariah 9:9 as coming?
options: Riding on a warhorse with an army
Riding on a donkey, humbly
In a splendid carriage, displaying power
Walking barefoot, in ragged clothes
questions.explanation: The scripture clearly states that this King is 'humble and mounted on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.'

questions.question: What will this King bring to His people upon His arrival?
options: Increased wealth and expanded territory
Abolition of chariots and bows, declaration of peace
Establishment of a mighty army to conquer nations
Imposition of strict laws to punish sinners
questions.explanation: God promises that this King 'will destroy the chariots from Ephraim and the warhorses from Jerusalem, and the battle bow will be broken. He will proclaim peace to the nations.'

questions.question: In Zechariah 9:11-12, how does God describe His salvation for the captives?
options: Through their own strength to break free
Through His covenant of blood with them
By granting them gold and silver
By sending angels to directly bring them back
questions.explanation: God says: 'As for you, because of the blood of my covenant, I will free your prisoners from the waterless pit. Return to your fortress, you prisoners of hope!'

questions.question: How does this passage encourage you to trust in Jesus Christ, the humble King, today?
options: He will meet all my material needs
He has already brought me true peace and salvation
He will help me achieve greater worldly success
I don't need to do anything, just wait for His coming
questions.explanation: This passage prophesies Jesus Christ, who humbly entered Jerusalem and accomplished salvation and peace through His precious blood. Through Him, we are set free from the bondage of sin and enjoy peace.
questions.evidence: Zechariah 9:9–12 (New Testament scriptures often refer to this passage concerning Jesus)

en.reflection: In the face of life's challenges and anxieties, how will you choose to place your hope in this humble King of Peace?
reflectionOptions: Seek to know His character more deeply
en.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for being the humble King who came to earth riding on a donkey, bringing true righteousness, salvation, and peace to me. Help me to trust You in all circumstances and surrender my inner struggles and anxieties to You. May Your peace fill my heart. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, find a quiet moment to reflect on the humble image of Jesus Christ and offer thanks for the peace He provides.

en.focus: God is the provider and the Shepherd; He will send what is needed and raise up fitting leaders for His people.

questions.question: To whom are the people instructed to ask for rain in Zechariah 10:1?
options: Idols
Diviners
The LORD
Leaders
questions.explanation: The passage clearly states that the people should ask the LORD for rain in the spring, as He is the one who sends rain and gives grain.

questions.type: Observe the consequences of false gods and leaders
questions.question: What was the result for those who consulted idols and diviners, according to the passage?
options: Abundant harvest
Empty comfort
True visions
Wise guidance
questions.explanation: Idols and diviners only offered empty comfort and useless visions, causing the people to suffer like sheep without a shepherd.

questions.question: What is God's attitude towards the 'shepherds' (leaders) and 'male goats' (rulers)?
options: Approval of their wisdom
Anger towards them
Granting them wealth
Indifference
questions.explanation: God explicitly states His anger towards the shepherds and His punishment of the male goats, as they were false leaders causing distress to His people.

questions.type: Understand the qualities of leaders raised by God
questions.question: What kind of leaders does God promise to raise from the house of Judah?
options: Weapons of war and rulers
Messengers of peace and builders
Givers of wealth and merchants
Mighty armies and counselors
questions.explanation: God promises to raise from Judah the cornerstone, the tent peg, the battle bow, and every ruler, symbolizing military strength and governing authority to save and guide His people.

en.reflection: In your life, have you ever sought help and guidance from the wrong sources when in need?
reflectionOptions: Relying on my own abilities and wisdom
Indulging in worldly entertainment and pleasures
en.prayer: Heavenly Father, thank You for being the true God who sends spring rain and provides for all our needs. Help me to look to You alone, not seeking empty idols or relying on human wisdom. Please raise up godly shepherds and leaders in my life to guide me in Your truth. In Jesus’ name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take a minute today to reflect: what 'idols' in your life might be drawing you away from God? Ask God to help you turn back to Him.

en.theme: God Promises to Save His People
en.focus: God Himself will save, strengthen, and gather His people, bringing them to complete restoration.

questions.question: What does God promise to do for the house of Judah and the house of Joseph?
options: Allow them to be oppressed by foreigners
Strengthen and save them
Cause them to be forgotten among the nations
Take away all their possessions
questions.explanation: God promises to strengthen and save both the house of Judah and the house of Joseph, as if He had never rejected them.

questions.question: How does God promise to respond to His people?
options: Send new leaders
Whistle for them to gather them
Send down heavy rain to water the land
Cause their enemies to fight among themselves
questions.explanation: God promises to whistle for them and gather them, for He has redeemed them, and their numbers will increase.

questions.question: From which places does the text mention God will bring His people back?
options: Babylon and Assyria
Egypt and Assyria
Canaan and Moab
Sheba and Cush
questions.explanation: The text explicitly states that God will bring them back from the land of Egypt and gather them from Assyria.

questions.question: What is the main hope this passage offers us?
options: People can return to God by their own strength
God only cares for a portion of His people
God has the power to gather and prosper His people wherever they are scattered
Peace comes simply by having a strong army
questions.explanation: This passage emphasizes God's active power to save, gather, and strengthen His people, ensuring their complete restoration no matter where they are scattered.

en.reflection: Is there an area in your life that needs God's powerful salvation and restoration? How will you respond to this promise from God?
reflectionOptions: Ask God for strength and direction
Trust more deeply in God's faithfulness
Pray for those who are lost
en.prayer: Faithful Father, thank You for Your promise to personally save, strengthen, and gather Your people. Please unleash Your power in my life, freeing me from all bondage and establishing me firmly before You. May Your glory fill my life. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take some time today to quietly reflect on how God has saved you in the past and offer Him thanks.

en.focus: God sends shepherds to care for His flock, but when the flock despises this grace, the consequences are severe.

questions.question: What place is called to wail at the beginning of Zechariah 11?
options: Egypt
Lebanon
Babylon
Jerusalem
questions.explanation: The passage opens by calling on Lebanon and its cedars and oaks of Bashan to wail, symbolizing the destruction of Israel's pride and strength.

questions.question: How did the shepherd symbolically tend the flock marked for slaughter?
options: With a staff of gold and a staff of silver
With two staffs, one called 'Favor' and the other 'Union'
With a trumpet and a drum
With a whip and a rope
questions.explanation: The shepherd tended the flock marked for slaughter with two staffs, one named 'Favor' and the other 'Union'.

questions.question: What did the breaking of the two staffs, 'Favor' and 'Union', by the shepherd symbolize?
options: God's covenant with all peoples and the brotherhood between Judah and Israel were broken
The shepherd decided to no longer tend the flock
The flock found a new shepherd
The nation would experience famine and plague
questions.explanation: Breaking 'Favor' symbolized the annulling of the covenant God made with all peoples, and breaking 'Union' symbolized the breaking of the brotherhood between Judah and Israel, signifying the breakdown of God's covenant relationship with His people and the disintegration of unity within Israel.

questions.question: How does this passage remind us to treat the spiritual leaders (shepherds) God has appointed?
options: We can criticize and reject them freely, as they are only human
We should respect and obey them because they are sent by God, even if imperfect
We should only listen to leaders who are flawless
We are only responsible for ourselves and do not need to heed leaders' teachings
questions.explanation: The passage reveals the flock's (Israel's) disdain and rejection of the shepherd sent by God (a prefigurement of the Messiah), which ultimately led to dire consequences. This reminds us to treat God-appointed leaders with reverence.

en.reflection: Have you ever disregarded or rejected God's warnings or guidance given through His servants (pastors or leaders)? How are you willing to respond?
reflectionOptions: Listen more humbly to spiritual leaders
Pray for the pastors and leaders of the church
en.prayer: Loving Heavenly Father, thank You for providing shepherds to guide me. Please forgive me for times when my heart has been hard and unwilling to submit to Your guidance through them. Help me to receive teaching with a humble heart and to pray for my shepherds, that they may faithfully tend Your flock. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, offer a short prayer for your pastor (or a spiritual leader), asking God to grant them strength and wisdom.

en.focus: God will fight for Jerusalem and cause His people to mourn and repent over the pierced Messiah.

questions.question: What three creative powers of the LORD are described in Zechariah 12:1?
options: Stretches out the heavens, lays the foundation of the earth, creates all things
Stretches out the heavens, lays the foundation of the earth, forms the spirit of man within him
Creates heaven and earth, separates day and night, creates man to rule the earth
Creates light and darkness, places the sun and moon, establishes the seasons
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that the LORD is the one who 'stretches out the heavens, lays the foundation of the earth, and forms the spirit of man within him'.

questions.question: How does the LORD describe Jerusalem's role in the eyes of the surrounding nations?
options: A precious jewel coveted by nations
A cup that makes the surrounding peoples reel and a burdensome stone
An impenetrable fortress
A lighthouse that emits light
questions.explanation: The LORD says that Jerusalem will become 'a cup that makes the surrounding peoples reel' and 'a burdensome stone'.

questions.question: What experience will the house of Israel have after God fights and wins for Jerusalem?
options: They will become more arrogant and conceited
They will utterly destroy all their enemies
They will look on Him whom they have pierced, and mourn for Him
They will build a grander temple to commemorate the victory
questions.explanation: God promises, 'And I will pour out on the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem a spirit of grace and pleas for mercy, so that, when they look on Me, on Him whom they have pierced, they shall mourn for Him, as one mourns for an only son.'

questions.question: From this passage, how do we understand God's forgiveness of sin and the change in human hearts?
options: People will naturally repent once they experience God's salvation
God actively grants the spirit of grace, enabling people to mourn and repent for their sins
Repentance is purely human effort, unrelated to God's grace
God is only concerned with external victory in battle, not the inner state of people
questions.explanation: God promises to 'pour out on the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem a spirit of grace and pleas for mercy', enabling them to repent and mourn.

en.reflection: This passage reminds us that God is not only the Deliverer but also the source of repentance. Which 'spirit of grace and pleas for mercy' do you most need God to pour out on you today?
reflectionOptions: A deeper understanding of Christ's suffering
Empathy for the suffering of others
en.prayer: Almighty Father, thank You for being the Creator of heaven and earth and the Lord of history. Please pour out on me a spirit of grace and pleas for mercy, that I may know You more deeply and mourn and repent for the sins in my life that have grieved Your heart. May my heart be turned back to You, to love You more. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take some time today to genuinely repent before God and ask for forgiveness for a sin or transgression you have committed.

en.focus: God promises to open a fountain to cleanse His people from sin and impurity, refining them to be His own.

questions.question: Zechariah 13:1 speaks of a fountain opened for “sin and uncleanness.” For whom is this fountain opened?
options: All Gentile nations
The house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem
The prophets of Israel
The priests and Levites
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states this fountain is for “the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem” to cleanse them from sin and impurity.

questions.question: Besides sin and uncleanness, what else does God promise to remove from the land in the following verses?
options: All sickness and poverty
The names of idols and false prophets
Armies of enemy nations
Drought and famine
questions.explanation: God promises, “On that day I will banish the names of the idols from the land, and they will be remembered no more. I will also remove from the land the prophets and the spirit of impurity.”

questions.question: How does the passage describe God’s process of refining His people?
options: He will burn them completely with fire
He will strike two-thirds, leaving one-third to be refined
He will make them wander in the wilderness for forty years
He will scatter them among all the nations
questions.explanation: God says, “In the whole land, declares the LORD, two-thirds will be struck down and perish; yet one-third will be left in it. This third I will put into the fire; I will refine them like silver and test them like gold.”

questions.question: After the refining process, what kind of relationship will God establish with the remnant of His people?
options: They will become rulers over other nations
They will be His people, and He will be their God
They will no longer need God and become fully independent
They will become priests to speak on God's behalf
questions.explanation: God declares, “They will call on my name and I will answer them; I will say, ‘They are my people,’ and they will say, ‘The LORD is our God.’” This signifies a close, covenantal relationship.

en.reflection: What areas of sin or impurity in your life do you need to bring before God for cleansing and refinement today?
en.prayer: Dear Lord, thank You for opening a fountain to cleanse me from sin and impurity. I confess my imperfections and ask You to wash away all my sins with Your precious blood. I also ask You to refine me, like silver is refined and gold is tested, so that I may become a people pleasing to You. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take a moment today to quietly reflect on the blood Jesus shed for you, and ask Him again to cleanse you from all sin.

en.focus: God will ultimately come to dwell with His people and reign as King over all the earth, bringing complete redemption and holiness.

questions.question: What event does Zechariah 14 describe at its beginning?
options: A grand festival celebration
Jerusalem being besieged by all nations
The construction of a new temple
A great flood covering the world
questions.explanation: The chapter begins by describing the day of the LORD coming, when all nations gather against Jerusalem.

questions.question: How will the LORD respond when the nations attack Jerusalem?
options: He will stand by and watch Jerusalem be destroyed
He will send a prophet to intercede for His people
He will go out and fight against those nations Himself
He will ask the Israelites to resist the enemies on their own
questions.explanation: The LORD will go out and fight against those nations, and His feet will stand on the Mount of Olives.

questions.question: What will the Day of the LORD ultimately bring to the whole earth?
options: Continuous war and conflict
Great abundance of wealth and material possessions
The LORD will be one, and His name the only name, bringing living waters
Humanity will take control of its own ultimate destiny
questions.explanation: On that day, the LORD will be king over the whole earth, His name the only name, and living waters will flow from Jerusalem to nourish the land.

questions.question: What is the significance of the ultimate hope described in Zechariah 14 for our lives today?
options: We should focus on accumulating worldly wealth, as the world will ultimately be destroyed
We don't need to care about the world's suffering, as God will eventually intervene
We can trust in God's sovereignty and ultimate victory, even when facing difficulties and hardships
We should strive to build a perfect human-led society
questions.explanation: Even amidst the world's suffering and injustice, Zechariah 14 reminds us that the LORD God is the King who controls all things, and His kingdom will ultimately come in its fullness, bringing holiness and complete redemption, giving us ultimate hope and strength.

en.reflection: What concerns or discouragements are you facing in your life today? How does this chapter help you to reframe these challenges?
reflectionOptions: I am worried about future uncertainties
I am struggling with a relationship
I feel weak in my faith journey
en.prayer: Almighty LORD God, thank You that You are the King over all the earth, and Your kingdom will surely come in its fullness. When I face challenges and anxieties in this world, help me to look to Your ultimate victory and glory. May Your name be honored in my life, and may Your will be done on earth as it is in heaven. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take a minute today to consider: If the LORD is King over all the earth, what worry do you most need to surrender to Him?

en.focus: God reminds His people that He is the Lord of all, worthy of all honour and holy offerings.

questions.question: How does the book of Malachi begin by describing God's feelings towards Israel?
options: His anger
His love
His judgment
His righteousness
questions.explanation: Malachi opens with a declaration of God's love for Israel, despite their questioning of this love.

questions.question: What sin did the priests commit in their offerings?
options: Stealing gold from the altar
Not offering enough sacrifices according to the law
Offering defiled, blemished sacrifices
Preventing the people from offering sacrifices
questions.explanation: The priests offered blind, lame, and sick animals as sacrifices, despising God's altar.

questions.question: Why was God displeased with the offerings brought by the priests?
options: Because the animals offered were too few
Because they offered sacrifices to please people
Because they considered God's table contemptible and offered polluted sacrifices
Because they did not offer sacrifices on time
questions.explanation: God was displeased because they showed disrespect for His altar, considering it contemptible, and offered unclean animals.

questions.question: What is the primary message this passage reminds us of?
options: The ritual of sacrifice is more important than the heart
God does not care what we offer, only that we offer
God is worthy of our wholehearted honour and best offerings
As long as we serve, God will not question our motives
questions.explanation: God is the LORD of hosts, a great King, and He deserves His people's sincere honour and the best, most holy offerings.

en.reflection: In your life, have you ever treated God's grace or service with a casual attitude?
en.prayer: Lord, You are a great King, worthy of all my honour and my best. Forgive me for any casualness or half-heartedness in my attitude towards You. Help me to offer my best to You with a holy and grateful heart, whether in worship, service, or daily life. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, genuinely thank God for one blessing you have (e.g., health, family, work) and consider how you can respond to His love in the best possible way.

en.theme: Revering God's Name and Returning to the Covenant
en.focus: God calls His priests and people to return to His covenant, revere His name, and deal righteously with one another.

questions.question: In Malachi 2:1–9, what warning does God issue to the priests?
options: He will punish their families
He will curse their blessings and bring dishonor upon them
He will withdraw the sacrifices from the temple
He will cause them to lose authority before the people
questions.explanation: God warns the priests that if they do not listen and give glory to His name, He will curse their blessings and spread refuse on their faces.

questions.question: In Malachi 2:10–16, which two specific sins does God condemn among the people?
options: Not observing the Sabbath and idolatry
Not offering sacrifices and despising the poor
Intermarrying with foreigners and divorcing their wives
Stealing and lying
questions.explanation: God specifically condemns the people for intermarrying with foreigners, defiling what is holy, and dealing treacherously with their wives through divorce.

questions.question: Why does God detest divorce so strongly?
options: Because divorce reduces the population
Because God is 'a righteous judge'
Because divorce is an act of treachery that causes a wife to weep
Because God wants to protect women's rights
questions.explanation: God detests divorce because it is an act of treachery that causes wives to weep before Him and defiles the marriage covenant.

questions.question: Today's passage reminds us to be more vigilant in which areas, treating God and others with sincerity and righteousness?
options: Revering God more in worship and being more faithful in relationships
Being more generous financially and more careful with our words
Being more diligent in service and more urgent in prayer
Being more disciplined in solitude and more submissive in community
questions.explanation: The passage emphasizes priests revering God's name and people being faithful to the covenant, not dealing treacherously with their spouses, all pointing to sincerity and righteousness in worship and relationships.

en.reflection: Is there an area in your life where you need to return to God's heart, treating Him or an important relationship with greater sincerity and reverence?
reflectionOptions: Seek to repair a strained relationship
Re-evaluate your marriage or family life
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for being a covenant-keeping God. Please forgive me for sometimes treating Your name lightly or for lacking sincerity and righteousness in my relationships. Help me to resolve today to worship You with reverence and to treat everyone around me with faithfulness and love. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, specifically pray for your spouse (if married) or an important family member, asking God to help you treat them with love and faithfulness.

en.theme: The Lord Will Suddenly Come to His Temple
en.focus: God promises to send a messenger to prepare the way, and then He Himself will come to His people to judge and purify.

questions.question: According to Malachi 3:1, who will God send before Him to prepare the way before the Lord comes?
options: A new prophet
My messenger
An archangel
A king
questions.explanation: The text clearly states that God will send 'my messenger' to prepare the way before Him, which is often understood as a prophecy of John the Baptist.

questions.question: When the Lord suddenly comes to His temple, what will He be like in purifying His people?
options: A refiner's fire
A farmer's sickle
A shepherd's staff
A craftsman's hammer
questions.explanation: The passage uses the imagery of 'a refiner's fire' and 'fullers' soap' to describe the Lord's action of purifying His people, removing impurities to make them pure.

questions.question: In Malachi 3:7-12, God rebukes the people for withholding their tithes and offerings. What does He promise if they return to Him?
options: A stronger army
Pour out a blessing until there is no more need
Protection from foreign invaders
Rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem
questions.explanation: God promises that if His people bring the whole tithe into the storehouse, He will open the floodgates of heaven and pour out so much blessing that there will not be room enough to store it.

questions.question: According to today's scripture, what does God promise to those who fear Him and esteem His name?
options: They will become world leaders
They will receive great wealth
They shall be mine, says the LORD of hosts, in the day when I make up my treasured possession
They will never experience suffering
questions.explanation: God promises that those who fear Him and esteem His name will be His treasured possession on the day He acts, and He will spare them.

en.reflection: Today's scripture reminds us of God's judgment and grace. In what areas of your life do you feel God's purification and turning are needed so you can better honor Him?
en.prayer: Righteous Lord, thank You for being a faithful God who keeps His covenant, promising to come among us with purification and grace. Please refine anything in my life that is not pleasing to You, and help me to faithfully offer what is due to You and to fear Your name. May I be Your treasured possession. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Consider one small thing you can do today to express your reverence and obedience to God.

en.theme: The Day of the LORD is Coming
en.focus: God’s righteous judgment will come upon all wickedness, but He also provides healing and salvation for those who fear His name.

questions.question: How is the coming day described in Malachi 4:1?
options: A day of great joy and harvest
A day that will burn like an oven
A day when all people will reconcile
A day of continuous signs and wonders
questions.explanation: The scripture explicitly states that the coming day will burn like an oven, consuming all the arrogant and evildoers.

questions.type: Observe God's promise to those who fear His name
questions.question: What does God promise to those who fear His name?
options: To gain great wealth
Their enemies will be defeated
The sun of righteousness will rise with healing in its rays
They will become rulers of the world
questions.explanation: The scripture promises that for those who fear God's name, the sun of righteousness will rise with healing in its rays, and they will go out and leap like calves released from the stall.

questions.question: Before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the LORD, whom will God send, and what is his mission?
options: Moses, to give new laws
Elijah, to turn the hearts of the fathers to their children and the hearts of the children to their fathers
Joshua, to lead the people into a new promised land
David, to rebuild the kingdom of Israel
questions.explanation: Before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the LORD, God will send the prophet Elijah, and his mission is to turn the hearts of the fathers to their children and the hearts of the children to their fathers.

questions.question: How does the end of Malachi encourage us in our lives today?
options: To focus only on earthly pleasures
To ignore God's righteous judgment and only focus on healing
To fear God's name and seek reconciliation in our relationships with Him and others
To avoid all calamity by only doing good deeds
questions.explanation: The passage calls us to fear God and emphasizes the importance of relational reconciliation (between fathers and children, and between God and people) before God's judgment arrives.

en.reflection: Today's scripture reminds us that God is both a righteous judge and a loving healer. How can you live more deeply in the fear of God today, and seek to mend any broken relationships in your life?
reflectionOptions: Initiate an apology to a family member or friend
Spend time in prayer seeking God's healing
en.prayer: Righteous Sun, my Lord, thank You for being a God who brings forth righteous judgment yet also offers healing and hope. Help me to always fear Your name and grant me the courage and wisdom to mend broken relationships. May my life glorify You and be prepared for Your coming day. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, proactively send a blessing or greeting to someone you may have misunderstood or hurt, even if it's just a message, to let the seed of reconciliation begin to sprout.

en.theme: The Genealogy of Jesus Christ: God's Faithful Plan of Salvation
en.focus: Jesus' genealogy is more than a list of names; it is a testament to God's faithful fulfillment of His promises for humanity's redemption.

questions.question: How is Jesus addressed at the very beginning of Matthew's genealogy?
options: Son of God
Son of David, Son of Abraham
King of Israel
Savior of all nations
questions.explanation: The genealogy immediately emphasizes Jesus' lineage from David and Abraham, highlighting key Old Testament messianic promises.

questions.question: How many generations are there from Abraham to David, from David to the exile to Babylon, and from the exile to the Christ?
options: 12 generations
14 generations
16 generations
18 generations
questions.explanation: Matthew structures the genealogy into three distinct sets of fourteen generations, emphasizing divine design and control.

questions.question: Besides Mary, which other women are mentioned in the genealogy?
options: Sarah, Rebekah, Rachel
Ruth, Tamar, Rahab, the wife of Uriah
Eve, Deborah, Esther
Miriam, Dinah, Leah
questions.explanation: The genealogy uniquely includes Tamar, Rahab, Ruth, and the wife of Uriah (Bathsheba), each with significant spiritual implications.

questions.question: What is the main message this seemingly long genealogy intends to convey to us?
options: Jesus came from a very prominent family
Israelites valued family lineage greatly
God faithfully worked through history to fulfill His promises and prepare for the Messiah's coming
Recording genealogies was a common ancient cultural practice
questions.explanation: The genealogy serves as a testament to God's faithfulness, showing how, over a long history, He meticulously brought about the birth of Jesus according to His promises to Abraham and David.

en.reflection: How does this genealogy help you see God's faithfulness and His long-term plan in your own life?
reflectionOptions: Recognize God's constant presence with me
Trust God to fulfill His promises to me
Learn to surrender in times of waiting
en.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for Your genealogy, which reminds me that You are the faithful God who meticulously fulfills Your plan of salvation throughout history. Please help me to see Your faithful guidance and beautiful purpose in my own life as well. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take a quiet moment to recall one or two instances of God's faithfulness in your life and give Him thanks.

en.focus: Jesus' birth is God's faithful promise, fulfilling His plan of salvation in a supernatural way.

questions.question: How does Matthew describe the birth of Jesus Christ?
options: His birth caused great commotion
This is how the birth of Jesus Christ came about
His birth was anticipated by many
His birth was a secret
questions.explanation: The text directly begins with “This is how the birth of Jesus Christ came about,” followed by a detailed narration.

questions.question: What was Joseph's initial reaction upon learning of Mary's pregnancy?
options: He immediately married her publicly
He decided to divorce her quietly
He became very angry
He sought advice from the priests
questions.explanation: Joseph, being a righteous man, did not want to publicly disgrace Mary, so he intended to divorce her quietly.

questions.question: What was the main message conveyed by the angel to Joseph?
options: To leave Mary
To inform him of impending difficulties
To explain that Mary's pregnancy was from the Holy Spirit and to announce the child's mission
To ask him to prepare expensive gifts for the child
questions.explanation: The angel explained the truth of Mary's pregnancy, stating that the child would save His people from their sins and be called Immanuel.

questions.question: Joseph obeyed the angel's command and took Mary as his wife. What reminder does this bring to our lives today?
options: We should always follow guidance from dreams
When God's word comes to us, we should obey in faith even if we don't fully understand
When making important decisions, we can ignore others' opinions
As long as the outcome is good, the process doesn't matter
questions.explanation: Joseph chose to trust and obey God's will even when he didn't fully understand, serving as an example of faith.

en.reflection: Is there an area in your life today where you need to obey God by faith, even if the circumstances seem difficult or unreasonable?
reflectionOptions: A worry that needs to be released
A new beginning that requires a step of faith
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for sending Jesus as promised, bringing about wonderful salvation. Help me, like Joseph, to choose to trust and obey You even amidst confusion and challenges. May my life bring glory to Your name. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Find a quiet moment to reflect on an area in your life that requires more trust and obedience to God, and pray about it.

en.focus: True worship involves setting aside everything to humbly seek and honour God's King.

questions.question: Who came from the East to Jerusalem, seeking Jesus after His birth?
options: Some shepherds
Some wise men
Some Roman soldiers
Some Pharisees
questions.explanation: The text states that wise men from the East came to Jerusalem, asking about “the one who has been born king of the Jews.”

questions.question: How did King Herod and all Jerusalem react when the wise men inquired about the new king?
options: They were all very joyful
They all immediately went to Bethlehem
Herod was disturbed, and all Jerusalem with him
They all disbelieved the wise men
questions.explanation: When Herod heard this, he was “disturbed, and all Jerusalem with him.”

questions.question: After finding Jesus, what did the wise men do?
options: They reported back to King Herod
They rejoiced greatly, bowed down, worshipped Him, and presented gifts
They demanded Jesus perform a miracle immediately
They instructed Joseph and Mary on how to raise Jesus
questions.explanation: After finding Jesus, the wise men “rejoiced exceedingly with great joy,” bowed down, worshipped Him, and presented gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh.

questions.question: What lesson about true worship can we learn from the wise men's actions in seeking and worshipping Jesus?
options: Worship is merely singing in church
True worship requires sacrifice and a humble heart to honour Jesus as King
Worship is for gaining material rewards
Only certain people are meant to worship God
questions.explanation: The wise men's long journey, facing Herod's threat, and ultimately bowing down to worship and presenting precious gifts, demonstrate that true worship involves self-sacrifice, cost, and a humble, reverent acknowledgement of Jesus' kingship.

en.reflection: In what ways do you need to more deeply acknowledge Jesus as your King and offer Him your worship today?
reflectionOptions: Surrender my plans and seek His will
Dedicate my time and energy to God
Trust in His guidance amidst difficulties
en.prayer: Dear Lord Jesus, thank You for being born to be my King. Help me, like the wise men, to single-mindedly seek and worship You, no matter what difficulties or challenges I may face. May I honour You with all my heart and offer You all that is precious to me. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Spend a moment today quietly considering what 'gold, frankincense, and myrrh' you can offer to Jesus in your life, even if it's just a prayer or a heartfelt intention.

en.focus: Even amidst danger and uncertainty, God sovereignly protects and guides His people.

questions.question: Where did Joseph and Mary flee with the child Jesus to escape King Herod?
options: Samaria
Egypt
Galilee
Rome
questions.explanation: An angel appeared to Joseph in a dream, instructing him to take the child and Mary and flee to Egypt.

questions.question: After Herod's death, Joseph received another angelic instruction in a dream. To which land were they told to return?
options: Judea
Syria
the land of Israel
Lebanon
questions.explanation: After Herod died, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt, telling him that those who were trying to take the child's life were dead, and they could return to the land of Israel.

questions.question: Joseph ultimately chose to live in Nazareth, fulfilling what prophecy?
options: “He will be called a great prophet”
“He will be called a Nazarene”
“He will be called Prince of Peace”
“He will be called King of Kings”
questions.explanation: Joseph settled in Nazareth, in the district of Galilee, which fulfilled what was said through the prophets: “He will be called a Nazarene.”

questions.question: What attribute of God does this passage primarily reveal?
options: God’s righteousness
God’s love
God’s wisdom and sovereignty
God’s holiness
questions.explanation: Despite immense danger, God miraculously protected and guided Jesus’ family through angelic instructions, demonstrating His sovereignty and wisdom in all circumstances.

en.reflection: Think of a recent time when you felt lost or worried. How did God guide or protect you?
en.prayer: Dear Lord, thank You for being the God who controls all things, and who lovingly protects and guides me. When I face the unknown and challenges, please grant me faith to trust in Your wisdom and sovereignty, and to willingly follow Your leading. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take some time today to write down or reflect on an experience where God has shown His guidance or protection in your life.

en.theme: Repent, for the Kingdom of Heaven Is Near
en.focus: The nearness of the Kingdom of Heaven demands genuine repentance and actions that demonstrate a changed heart.

questions.question: What was the core message preached by John the Baptist?
options: God's love never changes
Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is near
You must love one another
The law's requirements are strict
questions.explanation: John the Baptist's message directly called people to repent because the Kingdom of Heaven was at hand.

questions.question: What did John the Baptist consider to be true evidence of repentance?
options: Being a descendant of Abraham
Being baptized in the Jordan River
Producing fruit in keeping with repentance
Knowing all the rules of the Law
questions.explanation: John emphasized that mere lineage or external rituals were insufficient; true repentance must be demonstrated by a changed life.

questions.question: Why did John the Baptist sternly rebuke the Pharisees and Sadducees?
options: Because they lived in poverty
Because they did not keep the Law of Moses
Because they lacked genuine repentance and were self-righteous
Because they opposed the Roman government
questions.explanation: John called them a 'brood of vipers' because they had an outward religious appearance but lacked true repentance, relying instead on their ancestry.

questions.question: From John the Baptist's message, what lesson about repentance can we learn today?
options: Repentance only requires verbal admission of wrongdoing
Repentance is a miracle unrelated to human action
True repentance involves not just a change of mind, but practical actions in one's life
Only certain people need to repent
questions.explanation: John's message clearly shows that true repentance is an inner change that manifests through actions, producing 'fruit in keeping with repentance.'

en.reflection: In what areas of your life do you need to examine yourself more deeply today and produce fruit in keeping with repentance?
reflectionOptions: Acknowledge and correct a specific wrong
Apologize to someone you have wronged or seek reconciliation
en.prayer: Dear Lord, I thank You for reminding me of the nearness of Your kingdom through John the Baptist's message. Help me to genuinely repent, not just in words, but by allowing my life to produce fruit in keeping with repentance. May my thoughts, intentions, and actions be pleasing to You. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, choose one specific area in your life that needs repentance and change, and take a first step towards it.

en.theme: Prepare the Way of the Lord, Experience the Holy Spirit's Baptism
en.focus: John the Baptist prepared the way for Jesus, who would baptize us with the Holy Spirit and fire, bringing renewal and God's presence into our lives.

questions.question: What difference did John the Baptist highlight between his baptism and the baptism of the one who was to come?
options: John’s baptism was for repentance, the other’s for forgiveness of sins
John baptized with living water, the other with stagnant water
John baptized with water, the other would baptize with the Holy Spirit and fire
John’s baptism was public, the other’s was secret
questions.explanation: John clearly stated that he baptized with water for repentance, but the one coming after him would baptize with the Holy Spirit and fire.

questions.question: How did John the Baptist view his own status in comparison to the coming Lord?
options: Equal to the Lord, both servants of God
Greater than the Lord, as His forerunner
Unworthy to carry His sandals
A disciple of the Lord, who would later become an apostle
questions.explanation: John humbly declared that he was not even worthy to carry the sandals of the one coming after him, showing his reverence for the Lord and his own humility.

questions.question: How did God the Father and the Holy Spirit manifest themselves during Jesus' baptism?
options: The Father appeared as a great light, the Spirit as a consuming fire
The Father spoke with thunder, the Spirit descended as a dove
The Father's voice came from heaven, the Spirit descended like a dove
The Father appeared in a vision, the Spirit as a gentle breeze
questions.explanation: After Jesus was baptized, heaven was opened, the Spirit of God descended like a dove, and a voice from heaven said, “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased.”

questions.question: How does today's passage encourage us when facing new beginnings or challenges?
options: We can overcome all difficulties by relying solely on our own abilities
We can trust that God will prepare the way and be with us in the power of the Holy Spirit
We should avoid all challenges and maintain the status quo
We should wait for a direct divine manifestation before taking action
questions.explanation: The passage shows God actively preparing Jesus' path and supporting him with the Holy Spirit and the Father's affirmation. This encourages us to trust God's leading and His provision of strength.

en.reflection: Is there an area in your life today where you need the Holy Spirit's renewal or guidance?
en.prayer: Dear Lord Jesus, thank You for baptizing me with the Holy Spirit and fire, granting me new life. Please renew my heart today, allowing me to experience Your presence and power more deeply. Help me to prepare myself and walk in Your will. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take one minute today to quietly pray, asking the Holy Spirit to fill you and guide your words and actions.

en.focus: Jesus' experience in the wilderness teaches us that God's Word is the most powerful weapon against the devil's temptations.

questions.question: Who led Jesus into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil?
options: His disciples
An angel
The Spirit
His family
questions.explanation: The passage clearly states that Jesus was led by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil.

questions.question: How did Jesus respond to the devil's three temptations?
options: He performed miracles to prove His identity
He consumed the devil with heavenly fire
He quoted from the Old Testament Scriptures
He fasted and prayed for His Father's will
questions.explanation: Each time, Jesus responded to the devil's temptation by quoting from the Old Testament Scriptures.

questions.question: From Jesus' experience with temptation, what is most important for us when facing temptation?
options: Resisting by our own willpower
Relying on help from friends
Skillfully using God's Word
Avoiding all environments that might lead to temptation
questions.explanation: Jesus used God's Word as His weapon, teaching us that knowing and using Scripture can help us resist temptation.

questions.question: When Jesus refused the third temptation, what did He command the devil to do?
options: To leave Him
To worship Him
To acknowledge Him as the Son of God
To prepare food for Him
questions.explanation: Jesus refused the third temptation and commanded the devil, 'Away from me, Satan!'

en.reflection: In which area of your life are you most susceptible to temptation, and how can you use God's Word to strengthen yourself there?
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for sending the Spirit to lead Jesus in temptation and for giving Him Your Word as a weapon. Please help me too, in daily temptations, to always remember and quote Your Word, standing firm by the power of the Holy Spirit. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, choose a familiar Scripture (e.g., Psalm 23 or Philippians 4:6-7), memorize it, and meditate on it when you feel tempted.

en.theme: Jesus Begins His Ministry: Light in Darkness
en.focus: Jesus came to Galilee, bringing the good news of the kingdom and healing, shining light into the lives of people living in darkness.

questions.question: After John was arrested, where did Jesus go to begin His ministry?
options: Jerusalem
Samaria
Galilee
Judean wilderness
questions.explanation: The text clearly states that after John was arrested, Jesus withdrew to Galilee.

questions.question: What was the main message Jesus proclaimed when He began His ministry in Galilee?
options: Complex teachings about the Law
A call to repent, for the kingdom of heaven is near
Prophecies about the fall of the Roman Empire
Encouragement to pursue wealth and success
questions.explanation: Jesus' public message was “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near.”

questions.question: What were Peter, Andrew, James, and John doing when Jesus called them?
options: Studying in the synagogue
Working in the fields
Casting or mending nets
Doing business in the marketplace
questions.explanation: When Jesus called them, Peter and Andrew were casting a net, and James and John were mending nets.

questions.question: What are the main works of Jesus highlighted in this passage?
options: Political revolution and military conquest
Establishing new religious rituals
Preaching the good news of the kingdom, healing diseases, and casting out demons
Only teaching moral ethics
questions.explanation: The passage summarizes that Jesus “went throughout Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, proclaiming the good news of the kingdom, and healing every disease and sickness among the people,” and “driving out demons.”

en.reflection: Jesus' arrival brought light and hope. Today, in which area of your life do you most need Jesus' light and healing?
en.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for coming to earth and bringing the true light of the kingdom to us who live in darkness. Please shine Your light today into every corner of my life that needs You, heal my weaknesses, remove my anxieties, and enable me to follow You wholeheartedly. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Pray for the area of your life that most needs Jesus' light today, trusting in His presence.

en.theme: The Beatitudes: The Beginning of True Blessedness
en.focus: Jesus begins His teaching by identifying those who are humble, mournful, meek, and hungry for righteousness as truly blessed.

questions.question: Where did Jesus go to begin teaching His disciples?
options: On a boat
In the synagogue
In the wilderness
On a mountain
questions.explanation: The scripture clearly states that Jesus went up on a mountain and sat down before He began to teach His disciples.

questions.question: According to the passage, why are those who mourn blessed?
options: Because they will receive wealth
Because they will be comforted
Because they will gain power
Because they will see God
questions.explanation: Jesus states, 'Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted.'

questions.question: What does Jesus mean by being 'blessed' in this passage?
options: Having worldly wealth and success
Being favored by God and experiencing true inner joy
Avoiding all suffering and misfortune
Receiving praise and respect from others
questions.explanation: The 'blessedness' Jesus speaks of is not worldly success but a spiritual state before God, bringing inner joy and satisfaction from Him.

questions.question: Based on these verses, how can we practice being 'poor in spirit' today?
options: Striving to acquire more knowledge
Acknowledging our shortcomings and seeking God's help
Acting as if we know everything in front of others
Avoiding sharing our weaknesses with anyone
questions.explanation: Being poor in spirit means recognizing our spiritual need and humbly seeking God's help.

en.reflection: Today's scripture reminds us that true blessedness is not found in external circumstances but in our relationship with God. Are you willing to lay down your pride, and come to God in humility and mourning, to experience His comfort and the riches of His kingdom?
reflectionOptions: Acknowledge an area where you are spiritually poor
Mourn over your own sins or the suffering of others
Seek God's comfort and presence more deeply
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for revealing true blessedness through Jesus' teachings. Help me to have a humble heart that seeks You, to recognize my spiritual poverty, and to mourn over sin and the world's suffering. May I experience Your comfort and live out the character of a citizen of Your kingdom. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Find a quiet moment to acknowledge one area of weakness or need before God, asking Him for humility and comfort.

en.theme: Blessed Are Those Who Hunger and Thirst for Righteousness
en.focus: When we deeply long for God's righteousness and actively seek His will, He will fully satisfy our souls.

questions.question: What kind of people are described as blessed in this verse?
options: Those who are wealthy
Those who hunger and thirst for righteousness
Those who are respected by others
Those who are physically healthy
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly states, “Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness.”

questions.question: What kind of state does 'hunger and thirst' describe?
options: An occasional desire
A strong, urgent need
A casual thought, not essential
Just saying it verbally
questions.explanation: 'Hunger and thirst' is a metaphor for a strong, urgent need for food and water, used here to describe an intense longing for God's righteousness.

questions.question: What does 'righteousness' refer to in this context?
options: Obeying legal codes
Personal flawlessness
God's perfect character and will
Gaining a good reputation in society
questions.explanation: Here, 'righteousness' refers to God's perfect character and His just will reigning on earth, including humanity being reconciled to Him and living lives that please Him.

questions.question: Why will those who hunger and thirst for righteousness 'be filled'?
options: Because they work harder than others
Because they will receive God's satisfaction and blessing
Because they only pursue material wealth
Because they will eventually become perfect
questions.explanation: 'Be filled' is God's promise that He will satisfy those who genuinely seek His righteousness, bringing contentment and abundance to their souls.

en.reflection: What are you most hungry for today? Do you have an urgent longing for God's righteousness and His will, like hunger and thirst?
reflectionOptions: To live a life pleasing to God
To see God's righteousness manifested in the world
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for Your promise to fill those who hunger and thirst for righteousness. Please open my heart to have a deeper and more urgent longing for Your righteousness and Your will, like hunger and thirst. May my life bring You glory and reflect Your pleasing ways. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take a minute today to reflect: How can I specifically seek God's righteousness today? Write down one thing you can do.

en.theme: The Lifestyle of God's Kingdom Citizens
en.focus: Citizens of God's kingdom are called to live by standards that surpass worldly norms, reflecting God's goodness.

questions.question: Who were the first people Jesus taught on the mountain?
options: The Pharisees
His disciples
The scribes
The crowds
questions.explanation: The passage states that Jesus “went up on a mountainside and sat down. His disciples came to him, and he began to teach them.”

questions.question: What two things did Jesus use to describe the role and influence of His disciples in the world?
options: Light and salt
Trees and fruit
Wheat and weeds
Sheep and wolves
questions.explanation: Jesus taught that His disciples are “the salt of the earth” and “the light of the world,” indicating their vital influence.

questions.question: What important characteristic of a kingdom citizen's life does Matthew 5 emphasize?
options: To pursue earthly wealth and success
To follow the letter of the law without seeking inner change
To live out a righteousness that surpasses that of the Pharisees, focusing on inner attitude and outward action
To avoid all contact with the world
questions.explanation: Jesus said, “unless your righteousness surpasses that of the Pharisees and the teachers of the law, you will certainly not enter the kingdom of heaven.” He emphasized the importance of inner attitudes and raised the standard of the law.

questions.question: According to Matthew 5, how should we, as citizens of the kingdom, treat those who hate us?
options: An eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth
Only associate with those who love us
Love our enemies and pray for those who persecute us
Stay away from them and have no dealings with them
questions.explanation: Jesus taught His disciples to “love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you,” demonstrating the kingdom's transcendent love.

en.reflection: Today, in your daily life, in what specific way can you live out the 'light and salt' of a kingdom citizen, surpassing worldly standards?
reflectionOptions: Be honest and integrous at work
Show more patience and forgiveness to family and friends
Actively care for and help those in need around you
en.prayer: Dear Lord Jesus, thank You for teaching us the lifestyle of Your kingdom citizens. Help me, not only in my outward actions but also in my innermost being, to live out the righteousness that pleases You. May I be salt and light in the world, so that others may see Your goodness through me. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, specifically look for an opportunity to respond to a situation or a person with the 'surpassing righteousness' that Jesus taught.

en.theme: Salt and Light of the World
en.focus: As followers of Christ, we are called to be influential in the world, reflecting His truth and love.

questions.question: What two metaphors does Jesus use to describe His disciples?
options: Light of the world and a vine
Salt of the earth and a lamp in the city
Salt of the earth and light of the world
Salt of the earth and a city on a hill
questions.explanation: Jesus explicitly states that His disciples are both the 'salt of the earth' and the 'light of the world'.

questions.type: Observe the function of the metaphors
questions.question: If salt loses its saltiness, what is its use?
options: It can still flavour food
It can be used to spread on roads
It can be used to preserve food
It is useless and can only be thrown out and trampled
questions.explanation: Jesus states that if salt loses its saltiness, it is 'no longer good for anything, except to be thrown out and trampled underfoot'.

questions.question: What does Jesus mean by calling His disciples 'the light of the world'?
options: Disciples should wear glowing clothes
Disciples should hide their good deeds
Disciples should live in a way that reflects Christ, guiding people to God
Disciples should become the center of attention
questions.explanation: As the light of the world, disciples' good deeds should be seen, so that people will glorify their Father in heaven.

questions.question: According to this passage, what are we, as believers, called to do?
options: Only shine within the church walls
Work hard to promote our own reputation
Glorify our Heavenly Father through our good deeds
Isolate ourselves from the world and non-believers
questions.explanation: Jesus' teaching is for disciples' good deeds to be seen, so that 'they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven'.

en.reflection: In what specific ways can you better live out your role as the 'salt of the earth' or 'light of the world' to glorify God?
reflectionOptions: Bringing positive influence in my family
Caring for and serving others in my community
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for calling me to be the salt and light of the world. Please help me to live out Christ's likeness in my daily life, so that my words and actions may glorify Your name and lead more people to know Your love. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, intentionally do one small act of kindness to bless someone around you, and pray silently that God may be glorified through it.

en.theme: Fulfilling the Law, Not Abolishing It
en.focus: Jesus came not to abolish the Old Testament law, but to fully accomplish and bring deeper meaning to it.

questions.question: What did Jesus say He did not come to do?
options: To establish a new kingdom
To abolish the Law or the Prophets
To bring peace
To judge the world
questions.explanation: Jesus clearly states that He did not come to abolish the Law or the Prophets, but to fulfill them.

questions.type: Observe Jesus' emphasis on the Law
questions.question: How did Jesus emphasize that not the smallest letter or stroke of the Law would disappear?
options: Until the earth shakes
Until everyone obeys it
Until heaven and earth pass away, not the smallest letter or stroke of the Law will disappear
Until all prophecies are fulfilled
questions.explanation: Jesus emphasized that until heaven and earth pass away, not the smallest letter or stroke of the Law will disappear, but will all be accomplished.

questions.question: According to Jesus, what will someone be called in the kingdom of heaven if they break one of the least of these commandments and teach others to do the same?
options: Called the greatest
Called the least
Called wise
Called authoritative
