questions.explanation: Jesus explicitly states that anyone who sets aside one of the least of these commandments and teaches others to do likewise will be called least in the kingdom of heaven.

questions.question: Jesus said that unless our righteousness surpasses that of the Pharisees and the teachers of the law, we will certainly not enter the kingdom of heaven. What does this challenge us to pursue?
options: More knowledge and skills
Deeper inner obedience and righteousness
Stricter external rules
Broader social influence
questions.explanation: The Pharisees and teachers of the law focused on external adherence, but Jesus' teaching calls us to a righteousness and obedience that goes beyond the surface, originating from the heart, which is truly what leads to the kingdom of heaven.

en.reflection: How does today's passage challenge you to move beyond mere external obedience to God's Word, and to delve into your inner motives?
reflectionOptions: Seek God's help for more genuine obedience
Stop just going through the motions
en.prayer: Dear Lord Jesus, thank You for coming not to abolish the Law, but to fulfill it. Please help me understand the true meaning of Your Word, to obey You not just in outward actions, but from the depths of my heart. May my life reflect Your righteousness that surpasses that of the Pharisees. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, consider one area of your faith practice where you might be just going through the motions, and ask God to help you practice it from the heart.

en.focus: Jesus teaches that true righteousness is not merely about outward obedience to the law, but about inward devotion to God and love for others.

questions.question: Which two aspects of the Old Testament law did Jesus mention at the beginning of His teaching?
options: You shall not murder; You shall not commit adultery
Honor your father and mother; You shall not steal
You shall not bear false witness; You shall not covet
Love your neighbor; Love your enemies
questions.explanation: Jesus first referenced the commandments against murder and adultery, then deepened their meaning.

questions.question: How did Jesus deepen the meaning of the commandment 'You shall not murder'?
options: It's only a sin if you physically kill someone
Everyone should attend psychology courses
Any anger, insult, or cursing toward a brother is considered a sin
Being friendly at church is sufficient
questions.explanation: Jesus emphasized that anger, insults, and curses toward a brother are as serious in God's eyes as murder, because they stem from hatred in the heart.

questions.question: According to Jesus, what should a person do if, while offering a gift at the altar, they remember that their brother has something against them?
options: Complete the offering first, then consider reconciliation later
Continue the offering, as God will forgive everything
Leave the gift and first be reconciled to their brother, then come back and offer the gift
Ask someone else to offer the gift on their behalf and leave
questions.explanation: Jesus taught that reconciliation with a brother is more important than offering a sacrifice and is a prerequisite for being accepted by God.

questions.question: What is the main message Jesus wants us to understand about the law?
options: Outward behavioral compliance is enough
The Old Testament law is completely abolished and no longer relevant
God's standard goes far beyond outward actions, focusing more on inner motives and attitudes
We should avoid all human relationships to prevent sinning
questions.explanation: Jesus' teaching reveals the depth of the law, emphasizing that God cares not only about actions but also about the thoughts, motives, and attitudes deep within the heart.

en.reflection: In what area today do you need to examine your heart more deeply to align it with Jesus' requirements?
reflectionOptions: Address anger or bitterness towards someone
Be more careful with words, avoiding insults or judgments
Seek to repair a broken relationship
en.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for teaching me that true righteousness begins in the heart. Please help me examine my heart and remove all anger, bitterness, or impure thoughts that are displeasing to You. May my mind be renewed and transformed, to better reflect Your love and holiness. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, specifically pray for someone you might have negative feelings toward. Ask God to bless them and to renew your heart.

en.theme: The Higher Standard of God's Kingdom
en.focus: Jesus teaches that the righteousness of God's kingdom goes beyond outward actions to inner motives.

questions.question: In His teaching on oaths, what does Jesus tell His disciples not to swear by?
options: Their own lives
Heaven and earth
The names of their friends
The temple in Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Jesus specifically instructs not to swear by heaven, earth, or Jerusalem, as these are under God's authority.

questions.question: Beyond the law of 'an eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth,' what does Jesus teach His disciples to do?
options: Seek greater retaliation
Suffer silently without any response
Not resist an evil person, and to love their enemies
Only be at peace with those who treat them well
questions.explanation: Jesus' teaching transcends the Old Testament principle of retaliation, calling disciples not to resist evil and even to love their enemies.

questions.question: What is Jesus' ultimate purpose in teaching His disciples to love their enemies and pray for those who persecute them?
options: To show the world their weakness
To avoid greater harm to themselves
So that they may be children of their Father in heaven
To gain praise and respect from others
questions.explanation: Jesus' purpose is for disciples to imitate the perfection of their Father, who causes His sun to rise on the evil and the good.

questions.question: According to today's passage, how does the righteousness of a kingdom citizen differ from that of the world?
options: Only loving those who love them
Merely following the letter of the law
Living in a way that imitates the Father's perfection and kindness
Avoiding contact with any sinful people
questions.explanation: Kingdom citizens are called to imitate the Father's perfection by loving enemies and praying for persecutors, which goes beyond the world's standard of loving only those who love them.

en.reflection: Which aspect of today's teaching challenges you the most, and where do you need God's help to live up to a higher standard?
reflectionOptions: Loving those who are difficult to love
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for revealing the higher standard of life for Your kingdom citizens through Jesus' teaching. Help me not to just focus on outward actions, but to examine my inner motives. Grant me strength to obey the command to love my enemies and pray for those who persecute me, so that my life may reflect Your perfection and kindness. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, intentionally pray for someone you find difficult to love or who has wronged you.

en.focus: All our good deeds should be done with a sincere heart, not to gain human praise, but to please God.

questions.question: What warning does Jesus give His disciples at the beginning of Matthew 6:1?
options: To strive for wealth
To avoid doing good deeds in front of others
To be careful about performing your righteous acts before others
To showcase your good deeds more to people
questions.explanation: Jesus warns His disciples not to perform their righteous acts publicly with the intention of being seen and praised by people.

questions.question: Which three acts of piety does Jesus mention as examples of practices not to do hypocritically?
options: Giving to the needy, praying, fasting
Reading the Bible, worshiping, fellowship
Evangelizing, teaching, serving
Offering, praising, giving thanks
questions.explanation: Jesus uses giving to the needy, prayer, and fasting as specific examples of spiritual disciplines where hypocrisy should be avoided.

questions.question: According to this passage, what should be our true motivation for doing good and praying?
options: To earn respect and recognition from others
To secure our reputation and status
To seek reward from our Father in heaven
To compete with other believers to appear more devout
questions.explanation: Jesus teaches that the true motivation for good deeds and prayer should be to seek God, our Father who sees in secret and will reward us.

questions.question: How does this passage remind us about the nature of prayer?
options: The longer the prayer, the more powerful it is
Prayer must be done in public settings
Prayer is an intimate conversation with a Father who knows our needs
Prayer is merely presenting demands to God
questions.explanation: Jesus emphasizes that prayer is an intimate conversation with our heavenly Father who already knows our needs before we ask, thus we do not need to use many empty words.

en.reflection: Is there any 'good deed' or 'spiritual discipline' in your life where you sometimes find yourself more concerned with what others think than with God's will?
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for being the One who sees the heart. Please help me so that all my good deeds and prayers are solely to please You, and not to seek praise from people. May my heart always draw near to You and worship You in sincerity. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Do a small act of kindness today that no one else will know about, simply to honor God.

en.theme: The Beginning of Prayer: Hallowing God
en.focus: When we pray, we are to first honor God's name and seek the fulfillment of His will.

questions.question: How does Jesus teach His disciples to address God at the beginning of prayer?
options: Our Creator
Our Father in heaven
King of the universe
Almighty God
questions.explanation: Jesus instructs His disciples to begin their prayer by addressing God as 'Our Father in heaven'.

questions.question: After addressing God, what is the first petition in this prayer?
options: May our days be peaceful
May Your kingdom come
Hallowed be Your name
May we receive abundant provision
questions.explanation: After addressing God as Father, the first petition is 'Hallowed be Your name'.

questions.question: What is the main message conveyed by the phrase, 'Your kingdom come, Your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven'?
options: God will one day destroy all unbelievers
The main purpose of prayer is to ask God to satisfy our personal desires
We long for God's reign and His good will to be fully realized on earth
We pray to make the world perfect, without needing God's intervention
questions.explanation: This phrase expresses a deep longing for God's sovereign rule to come and for His good will to be fully accomplished on earth, just as it is in heaven.

questions.question: According to this passage, what should be our priority in prayer?
options: Our own needs and desires
The faults and shortcomings of others
God's glory and the accomplishment of His will
The suffering and injustice in the world
questions.explanation: This passage teaches us that the focus of prayer should first be on honoring God's holy name, seeking the coming of His kingdom, and the fulfillment of His will.

en.reflection: In your prayer life, how often do you pray for God's glory and will before your own needs?
reflectionOptions: I always pray for my own needs first
I try to seek God's kingdom and righteousness first
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for allowing me to call You Father. May Your holy name be honored, may Your kingdom come, and may Your good will be done in my life and on this earth, as it is in heaven. Help me to seek Your glory more, rather than focusing solely on my own needs. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, before starting any prayer, begin by speaking a sentence to praise God's name and reflect on His glory.

en.focus: God not only provides for our physical needs but also our spiritual needs, including forgiveness and peace.

questions.question: What does the Lord’s Prayer teach us to ask God for?
options: Wealth and fame
Forgiveness of our debts (sins)
Revenge on our enemies
Removal of all temptation
questions.explanation: The Lord's Prayer teaches us to ask God to forgive our 'debts,' which refer to our sins.

questions.question: How does the Lord’s Prayer connect God’s forgiveness with our forgiveness of others?
options: God forgives us only after we forgive others
God's forgiveness is unrelated to our forgiveness of others
If we do not forgive others, God will not forgive us
We forgive others to gain their praise
questions.explanation: Jesus clearly states that if we do not forgive others their trespasses, our heavenly Father will not forgive ours.

questions.question: What is the primary message of “Give us this day our daily bread”?
options: We should worry about tomorrow's food
We should only pray for material luxuries
We should trust God for daily provision
We should rely solely on our own hard work
questions.explanation: This phrase teaches us to trust God for daily provision and to ask Him for it, rather than worrying excessively about the future.

questions.question: According to this passage, what attitude should we have towards conflict in relationships?
options: Insist on our rights and refuse to yield
Wait for the other person to apologize before forgiving
Actively seek reconciliation and willingly forgive others
Hand over all conflicts to God without personal involvement
questions.explanation: Jesus teaches us to forgive others their trespasses, which requires us to actively seek reconciliation and willingly offer forgiveness.

en.reflection: What 'debt' in your life do you need to ask God for forgiveness for? Whose 'debt' do you need to willingly forgive?
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for being the One who provides for all my needs. Please forgive all my trespasses, and help me to forgive those who have wronged me with Your love and grace. May my heart always be reconciled with You and live in peace with others. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, intentionally pray for someone who has wronged you, asking God to bless them.

en.theme: Treasures in Heaven and Earthly Worries
en.focus: When we seek God's kingdom and His righteousness, all our needs will be provided, for our Heavenly Father knows what we need.

questions.question: What kind of treasures did Jesus tell His disciples not to store up for themselves?
options: Gold and silver
Treasures on earth
Tall buildings
Valuable antiques
questions.explanation: Jesus explicitly said not to store up 'treasures on earth,' because these can decay or be stolen.

questions.question: What did Jesus teach us not to worry about concerning our lives?
options: Having no friends
Having no status
What we will eat, drink, or wear
Having no hobbies
questions.explanation: Jesus repeatedly emphasized not to worry about what to eat or drink for our life, or what to wear for our body.

questions.question: What did Jesus use as an analogy for God's care for our daily needs?
options: The wild flowers and the birds of the air
The fish in the lake and the crops in the field
The wild animals in the forest and the streams in the mountains
The livestock in the house and the fruit trees in the garden
questions.explanation: Jesus pointed out how God cares for the birds of the air and the flowers of the field, to illustrate that our Heavenly Father will care for us even more.

questions.question: What is Jesus' core teaching for us when facing daily anxieties?
options: Work harder to earn money
Seek first His kingdom and His righteousness
Solve problems by our own strength
Wait for others to help us
questions.explanation: Jesus taught us not to worry, but to seek first His kingdom and His righteousness, and all these things will be given to us as well.

en.reflection: What worry are you most prone to be troubled by today, which you need to surrender more to God?
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for being the God who cares for sparrows and lilies. Please help me to stop worrying about earthly things and instead seek Your kingdom and Your righteousness above all else. Renew my mind and heart, so I may deeply trust that You will provide all I need. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take one minute today to be still and surrender one of your deepest worries to God, trusting that He will take care of it.

en.focus: We are called to treat others with grace and mercy, recognising our own imperfections and need for God's grace.

questions.question: What clear instruction does Jesus give at the beginning of the passage regarding judging others?
options: Judge strictly, for God is righteous
Do not judge, or you too will be judged
Judge cautiously, but ultimately judge
Only judge those who are clearly in error
questions.explanation: Jesus clearly instructs us not to judge, because we ourselves will be judged in the same way.

questions.question: What metaphor does Jesus use to emphasise the need to examine ourselves before pointing out others' faults?
options: A plank and a speck in the eye
A stain and dust on clothes
Weeds and flowers in a garden
Cracks and plaster on a wall
questions.explanation: Jesus uses the metaphor of a plank in one's own eye before offering to remove a speck from a brother's eye.

questions.question: What is the core message of this passage?
options: We should avoid interacting with everyone
We are responsible for correcting everyone's mistakes
We must first address our own sins and shortcomings before lovingly helping others
We should not discern right from wrong at all
questions.explanation: The passage emphasizes that we must first examine and deal with our own issues before we can genuinely and lovingly help others.

questions.question: According to this passage, what attitude should we have when pointing out others' faults?
options: Harshly criticize and immediately point out errors
Approach with humility and self-reflection, addressing our own issues first, then helping with love and wisdom
Be indifferent and avoid any conflict
Wait for others to proactively seek help
questions.explanation: We are to first examine ourselves, acknowledge our own imperfections, and then approach others in a more humble and constructive way.

en.reflection: Are you finding yourself judging someone today? Is there a 'plank' in your own eye that needs to be dealt with first?
reflectionOptions: Confess your judgment and repent to God
Pray for the person you were judging
Seek God's help to see and address your own shortcomings
en.prayer: Dear Lord Jesus, thank You for teaching me not to judge. Please enlighten me to see the plank in my own eye and help me to deal with my own sins and shortcomings first. Grant me a humble heart to treat those around me with Your love and mercy. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Pray for one person you are tempted to judge today, asking God to bless them and to help you see them through His eyes.

en.focus: God delights in our asking and grants us wisdom to discern and cherish spiritual truths.

questions.question: In Matthew 7:6, who does Jesus instruct His disciples not to give what is holy to?
options: Unbelieving neighbours
Those who do not understand truth
Dogs and pigs
Those unworthy to receive
questions.explanation: Jesus specifically mentions not giving what is holy to dogs or casting pearls before pigs, emphasizing wisdom in discerning and protecting spiritual truths.

questions.question: What action does Jesus repeat three times in Matthew 7:7–8?
options: Repenting
Praying
Listening
Giving
questions.explanation: Jesus emphasizes the action of prayer: 'Ask,' 'seek,' and 'knock,' promising that these actions will be answered.

questions.question: What is Jesus illustrating with the example of fathers giving gifts to their children (7:9-11)?
options: Human love is greater than God's love
God's love and provision for us far exceed that of human parents
Only perfect parents can love their children
Children should be thankful for their parents
questions.explanation: Jesus contrasts human parents, who know how to give good gifts, with the Heavenly Father, who much more knows how to give good gifts to those who ask Him, highlighting God's goodness and abundant provision.

questions.question: How can the 'Golden Rule' – 'So whatever you wish that others would do to you, do also to them' – best be applied in our daily lives?
options: Only associate with those who treat us well
Treat others with love and respect, expecting them to do the same
Do not give to others until they have given to us
Only be kind to people in church
questions.explanation: The Golden Rule teaches us to treat others with love and respect as we would wish to be treated, reflecting a core Christian ethic.

en.reflection: In which areas do you most need to seek God's wisdom today to better discern truth or interact with others?
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for teaching me to pray and seek You. Grant me wisdom to discern truth and to treat everyone around me with Your love and respect. Help me to live out Your Golden Rule and glorify Your name. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, intentionally show kindness or offer help to someone you might usually overlook, practicing the Golden Rule.

en.focus: Jesus reminds us that the path to true life is narrow, requiring careful choice and steadfast obedience to the truth.

questions.question: What two kinds of gates does Jesus use to describe the paths leading to life or destruction?
options: Big gate and small gate
Wide gate and narrow gate
High gate and low gate
Wooden gate and stone gate
questions.explanation: Jesus clearly speaks of a wide gate and a narrow gate, leading to different outcomes.

questions.question: What kind of people does Jesus warn His disciples to beware of?
options: Gentiles
False prophets
Roman soldiers
Sadducees
questions.explanation: Jesus warns His disciples to beware of false prophets, who come in sheep's clothing but are inwardly ravenous wolves.

questions.question: What is the ultimate basis for determining if someone truly belongs to Christ?
options: The sweet words they speak
The miraculous deeds they perform
The fruit they bear, meaning their actions and life
The wealth and status they possess
questions.explanation: Jesus emphasizes that by their fruits, you will recognize them. A true believer's life will bear fruit consistent with their faith.

questions.question: What important reminder does this passage give us today about choosing the path of life?
options: Simply confessing the Lord's name is enough
Be wary of eloquent words and superficial success, valuing the substance of life and actions
Everyone will eventually enter the kingdom of heaven
Faith is just a personal feeling, no action is needed
questions.explanation: Jesus teaches us not to just listen to words, but to look at the actions and the fruit borne in one's life, and to truly do the will of the Father.

en.reflection: Today, what path are you walking in your life? Are you striving to enter the narrow gate and bear good fruit?
reflectionOptions: Check if my words and actions align
Seek God's help to stay on the right path
en.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for showing me the narrow path to life. Please help me to make right choices every day, to discern truth from falsehood, and to bear fruit that glorifies Your name. May my life not be merely outward appearance, but truly doing the will of the Father. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take a moment today to quietly reflect: In a specific decision, am I choosing the wide path or the narrow path? Pray about it.

en.focus: Jesus demonstrates divine compassion and authority by healing various diseases and suffering, fulfilling Old Testament prophecy.

questions.question: After Jesus came down from the mountain, and many followed Him, who was the first person to come and ask for healing?
options: A paralyzed man
A centurion
A man with leprosy
Peter's mother-in-law
questions.explanation: As Jesus came down from the mountain, a man with leprosy came and knelt before Him, asking to be cleansed.

questions.question: What specific action did Jesus take when the man with leprosy approached Him?
options: He commanded him from a distance
He reached out and touched him
He sent His disciples to heal him
He told him to go to the priests for healing
questions.explanation: Jesus reached out His hand and touched the man, saying, “I am willing; be cleansed!”

questions.question: What did the centurion's words to Jesus reveal about his understanding of Jesus' authority?
options: He believed Jesus' authority was limited to Jewish people
He believed Jesus only needed to speak a word to heal his servant
He thought Jesus had to physically come to his house to heal
He believed Jesus' authority was less than a Roman officer's
questions.explanation: The centurion said, “Lord, I am not worthy to have you come under my roof, but only say the word, and my servant will be healed.” He understood that Jesus' authority transcended physical presence and could be exercised through a spoken command.

questions.question: What is the primary emphasis of Matthew 8:17, which quotes an Old Testament passage?
options: That Jesus was a new prophet
That Jesus' healing power fulfilled divine prophecy
That Jesus came to abolish the Law
That Jesus only healed Israelites
questions.explanation: The passage quotes Isaiah to show that Jesus' healing of the sick and bearing of our diseases fulfilled the prophet Isaiah's words, demonstrating His identity as the Messiah with divine authority and compassion.

en.reflection: What 'sickness' or 'suffering' in your life today do you need Jesus' compassion and authority to touch and heal?
en.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for Your profound compassion and authority. You touched and healed so many physically and spiritually. Today, I bring my pains and needs before You. Please touch me with Your mighty power and heal me. Help me to trust more deeply in Your authority, knowing You can do all things. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Reflect on Jesus' act of touching the leper. Silently ask Jesus to specifically touch one area in your life today where you most need His healing.

en.focus: Jesus reminds us that following Him requires a cost and prioritizes Him above all worldly concerns.

questions.question: What situation did Jesus observe when He decided to cross to the other side?
options: He saw that the crowds had left Him
He saw the Pharisees coming to Him
He saw a large crowd around Him
He saw that His disciples were asleep
questions.explanation: The passage states that when Jesus saw a large crowd around Him, He gave orders to go over to the other side.

questions.question: What did the scribe say to Jesus?
options: “Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go.”
“Lord, I want to build a temple for you.”
“Please heal my family first.”
“I want to go home and bury my father first.”
questions.explanation: A scribe came up and said to Jesus, “Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go.”

questions.question: What did Jesus say to the scribe who wanted to follow Him, hinting at the difficulties of discipleship?
options: “There are many treasures in the kingdom of heaven.”
“Foxes have dens and birds of the air have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to lay His head.”
“You must first learn to pray.”
“You will receive authority and power.”
questions.explanation: Jesus warned the scribe that following Him might mean having no fixed home or even a place to rest, implying a life of uncertainty and hardship.

questions.type: Understand Jesus' reply to the disciple
questions.question: Why did Jesus say, “Let the dead bury their own dead” to the disciple who wanted to go and bury his father first?
options: Jesus did not care about the deceased or funerals
Jesus believed physical death was unimportant
Jesus emphasized that the call to follow Him is a more urgent and important priority
Jesus wanted the disciple to go and preach immediately
questions.explanation: Jesus meant that spiritual life (following Him) takes precedence over worldly duties (burying the dead), calling disciples to prioritize the kingdom of God.

en.reflection: What in your life today might be hindering you from fully following Jesus Christ, as prompted by this passage?
en.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for calling me to follow You. Please help me examine my heart and release any worries or attachments that hinder me from following You wholeheartedly. May Your kingdom and Your righteousness be the priority of my life. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Pause for a moment today and reflect: “Lord, what do You want me to lay aside to follow You more deeply?”

en.theme: Even the Winds and the Waves Obey Him
en.focus: Jesus has sovereign power over creation, a power beyond anything we can imagine.

questions.question: What natural phenomenon occurred after Jesus and His disciples got into the boat?
options: A gentle breeze began to blow
A furious storm came up on the lake, so that the waves swept over the boat
The lake was perfectly calm, ideal for sailing
A rainbow appeared in the sky
questions.explanation: The passage clearly states, “Suddenly a furious storm came up on the lake, so that the waves swept over the boat.”

questions.question: What did the disciples say to Jesus when they faced the storm?
options: Teacher, are you asleep?
Lord, save us! We’re going to drown!
Please get off the boat immediately!
What should we do?
questions.explanation: The disciples woke Jesus up, crying out in fear and helplessness, “Lord, save us! We’re going to drown!”

questions.question: How did Jesus respond to the disciples' fear before calming the storm?
options: He rebuked them for waking Him
He asked them why they were so afraid and called them “you of little faith”
He immediately jumped into the water to repair the boat
He expressed understanding of their fear
questions.explanation: Jesus said to the disciples, “You of little faith, why are you so afraid?”

questions.question: What is the main characteristic of Jesus revealed in this story?
options: He is an excellent sailor
He cares about the disciples' physical health
He has authority and power over the natural world
He is always tired and needs rest
questions.explanation: With a word, Jesus calmed the wind and the waves, leading the disciples to exclaim, “What kind of man is this? Even the winds and the waves obey him!” This shows His divine authority.

en.reflection: Are there any 'storms' or 'waves' in your life right now that make you feel afraid and helpless, unable to face them alone?
en.prayer: Lord Jesus, You are the Lord of all creation. Please help me not to be afraid or have little faith in the storms of life. I know You are with me, and You have the power to calm the storms in my life and grant me peace. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, write down one 'storm' you are currently worrying about, then pray and commit it to the Lord Jesus, trusting in His authority.

en.focus: Jesus Christ possesses absolute authority over the spiritual realm and creation, bringing power and transformation.

questions.question: When Jesus arrived in the region of the Gadarenes, whom did He meet?
options: A group of sick people
One demon-possessed man
Two demon-possessed men
A beggar
questions.explanation: The text clearly states that Jesus met 'two demon-possessed men'.

questions.question: What did the demons say when they saw Jesus?
options: “Please do not harm us”
“What do you want with us, Son of God?”
“We know who you are, the Holy One”
“Please do not send us away”
questions.explanation: Upon seeing Jesus, the demons cried out, “What do you want with us, Son of God? Have you come here to torture us before the appointed time?”

questions.question: How does this story demonstrate Jesus' authority over demons?
options: The demons left voluntarily without Jesus' command
Jesus needed to pray for a long time to cast out the demons
The demons recognized Jesus as the Son of God and obeyed His command
The demons resisted Jesus' authority through argument
questions.explanation: The demons not only recognized Jesus as the Son of God but also begged Him to allow them to go into the pigs, and as soon as Jesus 'gave them permission,' they came out and went into the pigs.

questions.question: What does this story remind us about our lives today?
options: We should avoid places with pigs
We should be afraid of demon-possessed people
Jesus' authority transcends all evil forces and difficult situations
We should rely more on our own strength to solve problems
questions.explanation: Even in the darkest and most chaotic circumstances, Jesus' authority is supreme, and He has the power to bring deliverance and change.

en.reflection: What 'demon-possessed' situation in your life today (e.g., an unbreakable bondage, fear, or confusion) needs Jesus' authority to intervene and set you free?
en.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You that You are the God who has authority over all things. I ask You to step into the dark, chaotic, and bound areas of my life with Your authority. I surrender my burdens and struggles to You, trusting that You can bring freedom and healing. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take a quiet moment to tell Jesus about one area in your life where you want Him to intervene with His authority.

en.focus: Jesus has the authority to forgive sins, and His healing is holistic, encompassing both body and soul.

questions.question: What was the first thing Jesus said to the paralytic man in Capernaum?
options: Your sins are forgiven
Get up, pick up your mat and go
Your faith has healed you
Go and sin no more
questions.explanation: When Jesus saw the paralytic, He first declared that his sins were forgiven.

questions.question: What was the scribes' reaction when Jesus forgave the paralytic?
options: They were amazed and praised God
They secretly thought Jesus was blaspheming
They demanded that Jesus prove His authority
They immediately believed Jesus was the Son of God
questions.explanation: The scribes inwardly thought that Jesus was blaspheming, as only God can forgive sins.

questions.question: What was Jesus' purpose in healing the paralytic?
options: To show people a miracle
To prove to the scribes that He had authority to forgive sins
To allow the paralytic to go home
To attract more followers
questions.explanation: Jesus healed the paralytic to demonstrate to the scribes that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins.

questions.question: How does this story help us understand Jesus' identity and power?
options: Jesus was just a prophet with healing abilities
Jesus was only a moral teacher
Jesus is God, with the authority to forgive sins and heal diseases
Jesus' power only applies to people in ancient times
questions.explanation: Through the miracle of forgiving sins and healing, Jesus revealed Himself as God incarnate, possessing complete authority over sin and sickness.

en.reflection: What area of your life do you most need Jesus to forgive and heal today?
en.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for not only healing our bodies but also forgiving our sins and healing our souls. I confess the areas in my life that need Your forgiveness and healing. Please touch me with Your mighty power, bringing freedom and wholeness to my entire being. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take one minute today to quietly reflect: How does Jesus reveal His love and power to you through this miracle?

en.focus: Jesus came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.

questions.question: Where did Jesus see Matthew, the tax collector?
options: In a marketplace
By the sea
At the tax collector's booth
In a synagogue
questions.explanation: As Jesus passed by, He saw Matthew sitting at the tax collector's booth.

questions.question: What did Matthew do immediately after Jesus called him?
options: He hesitated and thought about it
He refused, as he was busy collecting taxes
He got up and followed Jesus
He asked Jesus to heal him first
questions.explanation: Matthew immediately got up and followed Jesus after hearing His call, “Follow me.”

questions.question: How did Jesus respond to the Pharisees' questioning about Him eating with tax collectors and sinners?
options: I desire sacrifice, not mercy
I desire mercy, not sacrifice
Healthy people need a doctor, sick people do not
I have come to call the righteous, not sinners
questions.explanation: Jesus quoted Hosea 6:6, saying, “I desire mercy, not sacrifice.”

questions.question: According to Jesus' teaching, what was His primary purpose in coming to the world?
options: To build relationships with powerful people
To teach the law to those who already obeyed it
To call sinners to repentance and salvation
To help only those who were already perfect
questions.explanation: Jesus clearly stated, “I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners.”

en.reflection: Have you ever felt 'not good enough' to approach Jesus? How does today's passage encourage you?
reflectionOptions: It reminds me that Jesus welcomes sinners, including me
It motivates me to confess my shortcomings to Jesus
It helps me understand Jesus' love and compassion more deeply
en.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for coming not to call the righteous, but sinners. Thank You for looking beyond my past and inviting me to follow You. Help me to come to You boldly, no matter my weaknesses or failures, and to respond to Your call. In Jesus' name, I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, take a moment to quietly reflect on Jesus’ call to you, and respond to Him in a single sentence.

en.focus: Jesus' arrival brought a new spiritual reality that requires a heart prepared to receive new life.

questions.question: What was the concern of John the Baptist's disciples when they came to Jesus?
options: Why Jesus' disciples did not pray often?
Why Jesus' disciples did not fast?
Why Jesus' disciples did not pay taxes?
Why Jesus' disciples did not observe the Sabbath?
questions.explanation: John's disciples questioned why Jesus' disciples did not fast like them and the Pharisees.

questions.question: What did Jesus explain with the parable of the bridegroom and the wedding guests?
options: Fasting is an expression of sorrow, not suitable for joyful occasions
Wedding guests should always stay with the bridegroom
Fasting is a wedding tradition
The bridegroom will be with them forever
questions.explanation: Jesus explained that while the bridegroom (Himself) was with them, the wedding guests (disciples) should not fast in sorrow, as it was a time of joy.

questions.question: What is the main point Jesus wanted to convey with the parables of new cloth on old garments and new wine in old wineskins?
options: Change is difficult
Old and new rules cannot be mixed, as the new spiritual reality requires new ways to be contained and experienced
Old traditions are always the best
New things are always better than old things
questions.explanation: Both parables emphasize that the new era and spiritual reality Jesus brought are incompatible with old traditions and practices, requiring a completely new way of reception.

questions.question: How can we better receive the 'new wine' that Jesus brings today?
options: By adhering to all old religious traditions
By opening our hearts, willing to let go of outdated ideas and habits, and experiencing Him in new ways
By completely rejecting everything from the past
By focusing only on outward actions rather than inner transformation
questions.explanation: Receiving the new life Jesus brings requires an open heart, willing to let go of old constraints and ideas, and to experience and obey Him in fresh, vibrant ways.

en.reflection: Are you willing to let Jesus' 'new wine' challenge and renew any 'old wineskins' in your life? What area is it?
reflectionOptions: My old ideas about God or faith
My old ways of handling relationships
A certain habit or attitude in my life
en.prayer: Dear Lord Jesus, thank You for bringing new life and salvation. Please help me to have an open and flexible heart, willing to let go of old ideas and habits that no longer serve. May my heart be a new wineskin, capable of containing Your fresh grace and truth. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, think of one 'old wineskin' you are willing to surrender for the Lord to renew, and pray to Him for help to change.

en.focus: Jesus has the authority to heal physical ailments and forgive sins, and His compassion transcends all limitations.

questions.question: As Jesus was speaking, what did a synagogue leader come to ask Him to do?
options: Baptize him
Heal his daughter
Build him a house
Cast out a demon
questions.explanation: A synagogue leader came to beg Jesus to lay His hand on his recently deceased daughter so that she would live.

questions.question: What did the woman who had been bleeding for twelve years think would heal her?
options: If I only touch His cloak, I will be healed
If I only cry out to Jesus loudly, I will be healed
If I only give money to Jesus, I will be healed
If I only see Jesus, I will be healed
questions.explanation: She thought, 'If I only touch his cloak, I will be healed.'

questions.question: In this passage, what aspects of His power did Jesus demonstrate?
options: Walking on water and turning water into wine
Calming the storm and feeding five thousand
Raising the dead, healing diseases, and casting out demons
Building a temple and calling disciples
questions.explanation: Jesus raised the synagogue leader's daughter, healed the bleeding woman and two blind men, and cast out a demon from a mute man.

questions.question: What insight does this passage offer us today regarding seeking God's help?
options: Only those with great faith can receive God's help
We should only seek physical healing
God's compassion and power surpass our imagination, and He is willing to respond to prayers of faith
God only helps those who are in high positions or have influence
questions.explanation: Whether it was the synagogue leader, the woman with the flow of blood, or the blind men, their faith and pleas were met with Jesus' compassion and healing, showing that God's grace and power are open to all who seek Him.

en.reflection: What 'impossible' situation in your life do you need to surrender to Jesus in faith today, asking for His powerful intervention?
en.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for being a God of great power and abundant compassion. My life also has areas that need Your touch and healing. Strengthen my faith, so I can boldly come before You and surrender all my weaknesses, struggles, and impossibilities to You. May Your power be manifested in my life once again. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, tell Jesus in one sentence the 'impossible' situation you most need His healing or help with.

en.focus: Jesus, seeing the distress of the people, had compassion on them and instructed His disciples to pray for more workers.

questions.question: What three main things did Jesus do as He went through all the cities and villages?
options: Taught, healed, and cast out demons
Taught, preached the gospel, and healed every disease
Performed miracles, distributed food, and called disciples
Cleansed the temple, rebuked the Pharisees, and instituted the Lord's Supper
questions.explanation: The passage states that Jesus taught in their synagogues, preached the good news of the kingdom, and healed every disease and sickness among the people.

questions.question: What was Jesus' reaction when He saw the crowds?
options: He was annoyed
He was sorrowful
He had compassion on them
He was angry
questions.explanation: Seeing the crowds, Jesus had compassion on them because they were like sheep without a shepherd.

questions.question: When Jesus said, 'The harvest is plentiful but the workers are few,' what did 'the harvest' refer to?
options: Crops in the field
Sick people waiting to be healed
People in need of salvation
Wealthy individuals willing to donate
questions.explanation: The 'harvest' here metaphorically refers to the distressed and scattered people who need to hear the gospel and receive spiritual care.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is the most important thing we should do when facing the many people in need in the world?
options: Immediately donate a lot of money
Criticize their circumstances
Ask the Lord of the harvest to send out workers into His harvest
Wait for others to help them
questions.explanation: Jesus instructed His disciples that in the face of great need, the first thing to do is pray to the Lord of the harvest to send out more workers.

en.reflection: Today, around you, who are the people you see who are 'like sheep without a shepherd'?
reflectionOptions: Elderly living alone in your community
en.prayer: Compassionate Lord Jesus, thank You for seeing my weaknesses and needs, and for having compassion on me. Please open my eyes to see those around me who are like sheep without a shepherd. Move me to pray for them and to ask the Lord of the harvest to send out more workers, and prepare me to be a worker in Your hands. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Pray for one person you know who is currently feeling lost or distressed.

en.focus: Jesus empowers His disciples with authority and a mission to proclaim the Kingdom of Heaven and to serve others with love.

questions.question: After calling His disciples, what did Jesus first give them?
options: Wealth and fame
Authority over unclean spirits and to heal diseases
A command to preach in Rome
Strategies to build large churches
questions.explanation: Jesus called His twelve disciples together and gave them authority to drive out evil spirits and to heal every disease and sickness.

questions.question: When Jesus sent His disciples out, what specifically did He tell them not to take?
options: Gold, silver, or copper
Extra clothes
A staff or sandals
All of the above
questions.explanation: Jesus instructed His disciples not to take any gold, silver, or copper, no bag, no extra shirt, no sandals, and no staff for the journey.

questions.question: What was the main message Jesus told His disciples to preach when He sent them out?
options: Complex teachings about the Law
The Kingdom of Heaven has come near
How to become rich
The necessity of political reform
questions.explanation: Jesus sent His disciples out to preach the message: “The Kingdom of Heaven has come near.”

questions.question: What can we learn from Jesus empowering and sending out His disciples?
options: We should only focus on our spiritual growth
We should wait for a special vision before serving
We are also given the mission to proclaim the Gospel and serve others
Christians do not need to share their faith with others
questions.explanation: The disciples were sent to proclaim the Kingdom and serve others. Today's Christians also receive this mission, using God-given abilities to love and help those around them.

en.reflection: How will you respond to Jesus' commission today, to proclaim the Kingdom and serve others in your sphere of influence?
reflectionOptions: Share the Gospel with a friend
Show care and help someone in need
Pray for spiritual revival in your community
en.prayer: Dear Lord Jesus, thank You for giving me a precious mission and authority. Help me to courageously respond to Your sending, proclaiming the good news of Your Kingdom through my words and actions, and serving those around me with love. May my life bring glory to You. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Intentionally pray today for someone you know who does not yet know Jesus, asking God to open their heart.

en.theme: Disciples of Jesus: Challenges and Promises
en.focus: As disciples of Jesus, we will face challenges, but God promises to be with us, give us the words to speak, and care for us.

questions.question: When Jesus sent out His disciples, which animal did He use to describe their situation?
options: Sheep
Doves
Snakes
Wolves
questions.explanation: Jesus said He was sending them out 'as sheep among wolves,' indicating they would face danger and hostility.

questions.question: What did Jesus tell the disciples not to worry about when they were handed over to authorities?
options: How to defend themselves
Food and lodging
Their personal safety
The safety of their families
questions.explanation: Jesus told them not to worry about what to say, because the Holy Spirit would give them the words at that time.

questions.question: Which fear did Jesus primarily want to dispel for His disciples in this passage?
options: Fear of evangelism
Fear of rejection by others
Fear of persecution and even death
Fear of lacking daily necessities
questions.explanation: Jesus repeatedly mentioned that His disciples would face persecution, hatred, and even death, but He urged them not to fear those who can kill the body but not the soul.

questions.question: What comfort and promise did Jesus give His disciples in this passage?
options: They would never encounter difficulties
They would gain respect and love from the world
God knows and cares for them, even counting the hairs on their heads
They would possess supernatural power to defeat all enemies
questions.explanation: Jesus promised His disciples that if God cares for sparrows, He will certainly care for them, even counting the hairs on their heads, so they have no need to fear.

en.reflection: Today, in your faith journey, what fear do you most need to release to God?
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for calling me to be a disciple of Your Son, Jesus. Please help me to bravely face challenges and release all my fears. I know You care for me, even counting the hairs on my head. May I always trust in Your presence and provision. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Spend one minute today meditating on the phrase 'Do not be afraid,' and surrender one of your biggest worries to God.

en.theme: The Cost and Reward of Following Christ
en.focus: Following Christ may bring conflict, but those who faithfully serve Him will receive rich rewards.

questions.question: Jesus said He came not to bring peace on earth, but what instead?
options: Harmony and unity
A sword
Wealth and prosperity
Wisdom and knowledge
questions.explanation: Jesus clearly states that He did not come to bring peace, but a sword.

questions.question: What is the main point of Jesus saying, “Anyone who loves their father or mother more than me is not worthy of me”?
options: Disciples must abandon love for their families
Disciples’ love for Jesus must surpass all other relationships
Disciples can only love Jesus, not their parents
Disciples’ families will hinder their relationship with God
questions.explanation: This statement emphasizes that loyalty and love for Jesus must be supreme in life, transcending all other human relationships, including the closest family members.

questions.question: What does Jesus mean by “taking up their cross”?
options: Bearing family burdens
Accepting God’s call to evangelize
Being willing to endure suffering and sacrifice for following Christ
Working hard in ministry
questions.explanation: Taking up one's cross means being willing to deny oneself, endure hardship, and even death for the sake of following Christ, which signifies complete commitment and sacrifice.

questions.question: What is the result for those who receive disciples in their capacity as disciples, or give them a cup of cold water?
options: They will receive financial rewards
They will be praised by the world
They will certainly be rewarded
They will immediately become healthy
questions.explanation: Jesus promises that anyone who receives or serves His disciples for His sake will certainly receive a reward, which comes from love and obedience to Christ.

en.reflection: Today's scripture challenges us to consider: in your life of following Christ, what loves and loyalties might you need to release or reorder?
en.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for giving up everything for me. Help me to love You above all else and be willing to pay the cost for Your gospel. Strengthen me to take up my cross and follow You. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, consider one small thing you are willing to sacrifice for Christ, and bring it to Him in prayer.

en.focus: Even in moments of doubt, we can find Jesus' affirmation and through it, rediscover His identity and mission.

questions.question: What did John the Baptist's disciples ask Jesus when John heard about Jesus' deeds?
options: Are you the one who is to come?
Why do you not fast as we do?
When will your kingdom come?
Can you perform greater miracles?
questions.explanation: John the Baptist's disciples asked Jesus, 'Are you the one who is to come, or should we expect someone else?' This indicates John's doubt about Jesus' identity.

questions.question: How did Jesus respond to John the Baptist's question?
options: He directly declared himself to be the Messiah
He referred to Old Testament prophecies and pointed to the miracles he was performing
He rebuked John for his doubt
He told John that he didn't need to know the answer
questions.explanation: Jesus did not answer directly but told the disciples to report back to John what they had seen and heard: the blind receive sight, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor have good news preached to them, all fulfilling Old Testament prophecies of the Messiah.

questions.question: How did Jesus praise John the Baptist?
options: A great philosopher
A prophet, and more than a prophet
A king's advisor
An excellent teacher
questions.explanation: Jesus said, 'Truly, I say to you, among those born of women there has arisen no one greater than John the Baptist. Yet the one who is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.' He also called him 'more than a prophet.'

questions.question: What do we learn about Jesus' identity from His response to John's question?
options: Jesus was a leader focused on political change
Jesus' identity is to be recognized through the miracles He performs and the gospel He proclaims
Jesus only cared about those who were physically healthy
Jesus' mission was to establish a military superpower
questions.explanation: By listing the miracles He performed and the good news He proclaimed, Jesus confirmed that He was the Messiah prophesied in the Old Testament. His identity was revealed through His actions, not just direct declaration.

en.reflection: Have you ever doubted God's work due to life's difficulties or lack of understanding? How are you willing to respond to Jesus' affirmation today?
reflectionOptions: Renew my faith in God's grace and power
Seek to know more about Jesus' identity and mission
Lay down my doubts and trust God
en.prayer: Lord Jesus, when I face confusion or doubt, help me to fix my eyes on Your wonderful works. Thank You for revealing to me through Your words and deeds that You are the Messiah who is to come, my Savior. May my heart find peace and hope in knowing You. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take some time today to recall the wonderful works Jesus has done in your life, and thank Him for them.

en.focus: Are we like the children in the marketplace, blind to God's calling and salvation because of our own expectations?

questions.question: What parable did Jesus use to describe the people of His generation?
options: Children playing in the marketplace
Farmers working in the field
Craftsmen building houses
Fishermen catching fish at sea
questions.explanation: Jesus compared His generation to children playing in the marketplace who complained that their companions would not dance when they played the flute, nor mourn when they sang a dirge.

questions.type: Observe people's reaction to John the Baptist
questions.question: How did people describe John the Baptist?
options: He has a demon
He is a messenger of God
He is a great prophet
He is the Messiah
questions.explanation: The passage states that John came neither eating nor drinking, and people said he had a demon.

questions.question: How did people describe the Son of Man (Jesus)?
options: He is an ascetic
He is a strict teacher
He is a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners
He is a political leader
questions.explanation: People saw the Son of Man eating and drinking, and they said he was a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners.

questions.question: What is the main point Jesus is making in this passage?
options: John the Baptist and Jesus had very different teaching styles
People often approach God's call with preconceived notions and biases
Wisdom is foolishness in the eyes of the world
Repentance and believing the gospel are difficult
questions.explanation: Jesus uses this parable to show that regardless of whether John the Baptist preached through asceticism or He Himself preached by being approachable, people refused to accept the message due to their own preconceived notions and biases.

en.reflection: Have you ever, like the people in the passage, ignored God's grace and truth because of your own preferences or prejudices?
reflectionOptions: Admit to prejudice against certain people
Release my expectations and seek God's will
en.prayer: Dear Lord Jesus, forgive me for the times I have been like the discontented children, blind to Your call and truth. Open my eyes, Lord, that I may receive Your wisdom and grace with a humble heart. Help me to lay aside my prejudices and preferences and truly seek Your will. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, think of a person or situation you have rejected due to prejudice and try to look at it with new eyes.

en.theme: Come to Me and Find Rest
en.focus: Jesus invites all who are weary and burdened to come to Him and find true rest.

questions.question: To whom does Jesus give thanks at the beginning of this passage?
options: The kings of the earth
The wise and learned
His Father
His disciples
questions.explanation: At the beginning of this passage, Jesus gives thanks to His Father because He has hidden these things from the wise and learned and revealed them to little children.

questions.question: What authority does Jesus say He has received from the Father?
options: Authority to judge the earth
Authority over all things
Authority to know the Father
Authority to forgive sins
questions.explanation: Jesus states, 'All things have been handed over to me by my Father, and no one knows the Son except the Father, and no one knows the Father except the Son and anyone to whom the Son chooses to reveal him.' This shows His unique authority to know and reveal the Father.

questions.question: What kind of people does Jesus invite to come to Him?
options: All the rich and powerful
All who are weary and burdened
All who are self-righteous
All who are healthy and strong
questions.explanation: Jesus extends His invitation to 'all who are weary and burdened,' promising them rest.

questions.question: How does Jesus describe His yoke?
options: Heavy and difficult
Easy and light
Complex and confusing
Challenging and demanding
questions.explanation: Jesus declares, 'For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.' His yoke stands in contrast to the heavy burdens of the world.

en.reflection: What weariness or burdens in your life do you need to bring to Jesus today to find rest?
en.prayer: Dear Lord Jesus, thank You for inviting me to come to You, for Your yoke is easy and Your burden is light. Help me to lay down the heavy loads of my life and learn from You, finding true rest in Your presence. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take a moment today to quietly tell Jesus about one burden on your heart and ask Him to give you His rest.

en.theme: Lord of the Sabbath and Compassion
en.focus: Jesus is the Lord of the Sabbath, and His compassion and healing transcend the letter of the law.

questions.question: Why did the Pharisees accuse Jesus' disciples?
options: They were working on the Sabbath
They were not praying on the Sabbath
They were picking heads of grain to eat on the Sabbath
They were healing on the Sabbath
questions.explanation: The Pharisees accused the disciples of picking heads of grain on the Sabbath, considering it a violation of the Sabbath law.

questions.question: How did Jesus respond to the Pharisees' accusation against His disciples?
options: By quoting other examples from the Law
By directly rebuking them as hypocrites
By telling the disciples to stop picking grain
By pointing out their lack of understanding of God's love
questions.explanation: Jesus cited the examples of David and his companions eating the consecrated bread, and priests performing work in the temple on the Sabbath without being guilty of breaking the law.

questions.question: What did Jesus say He desires, rather than sacrifice?
options: I desire mercy, not sacrifice
I desire knowledge, not foolishness
I desire righteousness, not wickedness
I desire the law, not tradition
questions.explanation: Jesus quoted Hosea, emphasizing that God desires mercy, not just the mere observance of sacrificial rituals.

questions.question: What is the main teaching of this chapter?
options: The Sabbath is no longer important and can be spent as one pleases
God's law is rigid with no exceptions
Compassion and human need take precedence over the literal observance of the law
Only priests and prophets can work on the Sabbath
questions.explanation: Through His actions and teachings, Jesus demonstrated that God's heart is for mercy and helping people, which is more important than mechanically following rules.

en.reflection: Is there an area in your life where you tend to prioritize rules over love and compassion?
en.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for being the Lord of the Sabbath and the Lord of compassion. Help me to see beyond the letter of the law and to understand Your heart of love and mercy. May my life increasingly reflect Your compassion. In Jesus' name, I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, intentionally find an opportunity to show tender compassion to someone around you, even if it causes you slight inconvenience.

en.focus: Jesus' authority comes from God, and rejecting His work is resisting the Holy Spirit with severe consequences.

questions.question: What was the crowd's reaction after the demon-possessed man, who was blind and mute, was healed?
options: They became afraid and immediately fled
They questioned Jesus' power and demanded more signs
They were astonished and began to wonder if Jesus was the Son of David
They immediately believed Jesus was the Messiah and worshipped Him
questions.explanation: The crowd was astonished by Jesus' miracle and began to consider if He was the expected Messiah, the Son of David.

questions.question: How did the Pharisees explain Jesus' ability to cast out demons?
options: They said Jesus cast out demons by the Spirit of God
They accused Jesus of casting out demons by Beelzebul, the prince of demons
They believed Jesus was using some form of sorcery
They thought the man was not truly demon-possessed
questions.explanation: The Pharisees attributed Jesus' power to cast out demons to Beelzebul, the prince of demons, attempting to deny His divine nature.

questions.question: How did Jesus refute the Pharisees' accusation?
options: He performed another greater miracle to prove Himself
He condemned the Pharisees for their evil hearts, unworthy of knowing the truth
He pointed out the illogical nature of their accusation, stating that a kingdom or house divided against itself cannot stand
He directly denied knowing Beelzebul
questions.explanation: Jesus refuted the Pharisees' accusation with a simple logical argument: a kingdom or house divided against itself cannot stand, and evil spirits would not cast out evil spirits.

questions.question: What is the main point Jesus wanted to emphasize regarding the sin of 'blasphemy against the Holy Spirit'?
options: All sins can be forgiven except for using profanity
Willfully attributing the work of the Holy Spirit to Satan is a rejection of God's forgiving grace
Saying one wrong word means one can never be saved
The Holy Spirit only works at specific times and cannot be questioned
questions.explanation: Jesus emphasized that to knowingly attribute the work of the Holy Spirit to Satan is to refuse repentance and reject God's forgiving grace, making it unforgivable.
questions.evidence: Matthew 12:30–32 (While the passage given is 22-30, verses 31-32 are directly related and provide essential context for understanding this point.)

en.reflection: Have you ever, due to prejudice or unwillingness to acknowledge God's true work, missed an opportunity to draw closer to Him?
reflectionOptions: Seek the Holy Spirit's guidance more humbly
Repent for past rejections of truth
en.prayer: Lord Jesus, forgive me for times when, due to my own prejudice, unbelief, or ignorance, I have failed to fully recognize and accept Your work. Help me to have a humble and teachable heart, to be sensitive to the Holy Spirit's leading, and not to attribute Your glory to Satan. May I always walk in Your light and with You. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take some quiet time today to reflect on moments you might not have fully acknowledged or accepted the Holy Spirit's work, and repent before God.

en.focus: Our words not only reflect our hearts but also reveal the direction of our lives and our relationship with God.

questions.question: Which sin does Jesus say will not be forgiven?
options: Blasphemy against the Holy Spirit
Murder
Theft
Lying
questions.explanation: Jesus clearly states that blasphemy against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.

questions.question: What analogy does Jesus use to describe the relationship between a person and their words?
options: A good tree bears good fruit, and a bad tree bears bad fruit
Salt seasons, light illuminates
Lost sheep need a shepherd
The foundation of a house
questions.explanation: Jesus uses the analogy of 'a good tree bears good fruit, and a bad tree bears bad fruit' to illustrate that words are a true outflow of the heart.

questions.question: According to this passage, what does Jesus teach us about our words?
options: Words are unimportant; only the heart matters
It doesn't matter what you say, as long as you don't curse
Our words reflect the condition of our hearts, and we are accountable for them
Words are just a form of expression without real power
questions.explanation: Jesus teaches that our words come from the heart, and we will be held accountable for every word we speak.

questions.question: How does this passage remind you to be careful with your words in daily life?
options: It reminds me to speak less to avoid mistakes
It reminds me to speak more positive words
It reminds me that words are a window to the soul, prompting me to examine my heart
It reminds me that verbal confession is sufficient
questions.explanation: Words are an outpouring of the heart. When we examine our hearts and ask God to cleanse them, our words will naturally be pleasing to Him.

en.reflection: Which aspect of your heart do you feel your words most truly reflect?
en.prayer: Dear Lord, thank You for reminding me of the power of words. Please cleanse my heart and let the words I speak be pleasing to You and build others up. Help me to constantly examine myself, so that my words may be a beautiful testimony to You. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, try to replace one complaint with one word of gratitude.

en.focus: Jesus teaches that true spiritual kinship transcends blood ties and is defined by doing the will of His Father.

questions.question: What did the scribes and Pharisees ask Jesus for?
options: A sign
An explanation of the Law
A question about taxes
Healing for the sick
questions.explanation: The scribes and Pharisees asked Jesus to show them a sign.

questions.question: What sign did Jesus give them in response?
options: Turning water into wine
Raising the dead
The sign of Jonah
Calming the storm
questions.explanation: Jesus referred to Jonah being in the belly of the great fish for three days and three nights as a sign, foreshadowing the Son of Man being in the heart of the earth for the same duration.

questions.question: Who did Jesus say were His brothers, sisters, and mother?
options: Those who were related to Him by blood
Those who lived in Nazareth
Those who do the will of His Father in heaven
Those who served in the temple
questions.explanation: Jesus clearly stated that whoever does the will of His Father in heaven is His brother, sister, and mother.

questions.question: How does this passage challenge our traditional understanding of 'family'?
options: Blood relations are no longer important
Spiritual connection takes precedence over blood relations
Only believers can be true family
We should abandon all family responsibilities
questions.explanation: Jesus emphasizes that spiritual connection—doing God's will—is more significant than earthly blood relations, defining true 'family'.

en.reflection: Which relationships in your life truly reflect the 'family' of those who do the Father's will? How can you strengthen these connections?
reflectionOptions: Intentionally care for non-blood spiritual family
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for making me a part of Your family through faith in Jesus. Please help me to know Your will more deeply each day and to live it out by the power of Your Holy Spirit. May my life glorify You and grow alongside my spiritual family. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, intentionally pray for a brother or sister in Christ with whom you have no blood relation, and send them an encouraging message.

en.theme: The Parable of the Sower: Mysteries of the Kingdom
en.focus: God's Word is like a seed, and its growth and fruitfulness depend on the preparation of our hearts.

questions.question: Where did Jesus tell the parable of the sower to the crowd?
options: In the synagogue
On a mountain
In a house
By the sea
questions.explanation: The passage states that Jesus went out of the house and sat by the lake to teach the large crowd.

questions.question: In the parable of the sower, where did the seeds fall?
options: Stony ground, fertile ground, sandy ground, muddy ground
Path, rocky places, thorns, good soil
Field edge, ditch, hillside, valley
Barren land, saline land, wetland, cultivated land
questions.explanation: The parable mentions seeds falling on the path, on rocky places, among thorns, and on good soil.

questions.question: What is the main point this parable illustrates?
options: Sowers must be very diligent
The type of soil determines if seeds will grow
God's Word is precious, but people receive it differently
As long as seeds are sown, there will always be a good harvest
questions.explanation: The parable's focus is on how different hearers respond to God's Word, leading to varying outcomes.

questions.question: What does the statement, 'Whoever has ears, let them hear!' remind us?
options: To attend more concerts
To be aware of ambient noise
To carefully consider and respond to God's Word
To follow everyone's advice
questions.explanation: This statement is a call to be attentive and to thoughtfully receive and respond to what the Lord is saying.

en.reflection: Which type of soil in the parable does your heart most resemble right now? How are you willing to respond to God's Word?
reflectionOptions: Confess spiritual hardness, ask God to soften
Remove 'thorns' from my life to focus more on God
Seek to be more deeply rooted in God's Word
en.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for teaching me through the parable of the sower. Please help me to prepare my heart, removing any obstacles that hinder me from receiving Your Word. May my heart be good soil, so that Your Word may take root, grow, and bear abundant fruit in my life. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take a moment today to quietly reflect on a Bible verse you've recently read, and ask the Holy Spirit to help you understand and apply it.

en.focus: Jesus taught in parables to reveal truth to those seeking it and to conceal it from those with hardened hearts.

questions.question: What was the first question the disciples asked Jesus?
options: Why do You speak to them in parables?
What are the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven?
Who can understand Your parables?
Can we understand Your parables?
questions.explanation: The disciples directly asked Jesus why He spoke to them in parables.

questions.question: According to Jesus, what was the purpose of His teaching in parables?
options: To make the truths of the kingdom easily accessible to everyone
To encourage people to use their wisdom to explore profound truths
To reveal the mysteries of the kingdom to His disciples but hide them from outsiders
To test the listeners' understanding and level of faith
questions.explanation: Jesus explained that the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven were given to the disciples to know, but not to others. This is an act of God's sovereignty.

questions.question: Which prophet did Jesus quote to explain His method of teaching?
options: Isaiah
Jeremiah
Ezekiel
Micah
questions.explanation: Jesus quoted the prophet Isaiah to explain that 'seeing they do not see, and hearing they do not hear, nor do they understand.'

questions.question: Jesus said His disciples were blessed because of what?
options: They were wiser than the prophets and righteous people of old
They saw and heard what many prophets and righteous people longed to see and hear
They would become the sole inheritors of the kingdom's mysteries
They could fully understand all of Jesus' parables
questions.explanation: Jesus declared His disciples blessed because they saw and heard what many prophets and righteous people in the past desired to see and hear but could not.

en.reflection: Today, do you feel the mysteries of the kingdom revealed to you? Are you seeking God's Word with a humble and teachable heart?
reflectionOptions: I long to understand God's Word more deeply
I need more quiet time for reading and prayer
I sometimes feel confused by God's Word
en.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for revealing the mysteries of the kingdom to me. Please open my spiritual eyes and ears so that I may see, hear, and understand Your Word. Help me to always have a humble and teachable heart, not being stiff-necked, but hungering for Your truth. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, spend five minutes quietly rereading today's scripture, asking the Holy Spirit to illuminate you and help you understand its truth more deeply.

en.focus: God tolerates evil in the world until the harvest, when He will personally judge and separate.

questions.question: Who is described as sowing good seed in the field?
options: A farmer
A good sower
A man
A master
questions.explanation: The parable begins by stating, 'The kingdom of heaven is like a man who sowed good seed in his field,' highlighting 'a man' as the sower.

questions.question: What did the enemy do after the master sowed good seed?
options: Pulled up the good seed
Sowed weeds among the wheat
Set fire to the field
Stole the good seed
questions.explanation: While everyone was sleeping, his enemy came and sowed weeds among the wheat and went away.

questions.question: When the servants asked if they should pull up the weeds, how did the master respond?
options: Let them both grow together until the harvest
Go and pull them up immediately
Only pull up the large weeds
Let the servants decide what to do
questions.explanation: The master instructed his servants to let both the wheat and the weeds grow together until the harvest, when they would be separated.

questions.question: What is the most important lesson this parable teaches us?
options: We should immediately distinguish and judge everyone around us
God allows evil to exist according to His own timing and ultimate purpose
We must strive to eliminate all evil in the world ourselves
The lines between good and evil are too blurred to distinguish
questions.explanation: This parable reminds us that God has His patience and ultimate judgment for evil, and we should trust in His timing and wisdom.

en.reflection: Are there any 'weeds' in your life that cause you confusion or a sense of injustice? How can you entrust these concerns to God, who is in control of all things?
reflectionOptions: Pray for those in difficult situations
Release your judgment and trust God's justice
Seek wisdom to do good where you can
en.prayer: Heavenly Father, thank You for being a just and patient God. Help me, when facing injustice and evil in the world, not to act out of my own impatience, but to trust in Your wisdom and ultimate judgment. May I be like Your good wheat, bearing beautiful fruit for Your glory. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, try to silently pray for someone you usually disapprove of or feel is unjust.

en.theme: Parables of the Mustard Seed and Leaven
en.focus: Though the Kingdom of God starts small, it possesses astonishing power to grow and ultimately fill the earth.

questions.question: To what does Jesus compare the Kingdom of Heaven?
options: A precious gem and a grand castle
A mustard seed and some yeast
A towering mountain and a vast ocean
A large tree and a flock of birds
questions.explanation: Jesus uses the mustard seed and leaven to illustrate the Kingdom of Heaven, highlighting its humble beginnings and profound impact.

questions.question: Which characteristic of the Kingdom of Heaven does the parable of the mustard seed emphasize?
options: It is only accessible to a select few
It remains hidden underground, unknown to people
It starts small but grows to be immense
It requires constant watering to survive
questions.explanation: The mustard seed is the smallest of seeds but grows into a large tree, showing that God's Kingdom begins insignificantly but will greatly expand.

questions.question: What is the main characteristic of the Kingdom of Heaven illustrated by the parable of the leaven?
options: It requires a long time to ferment
It only causes superficial changes
It silently and completely permeates and transforms
It only affects a few individuals
questions.explanation: A small amount of leaven can work through an entire batch of dough, symbolising the Kingdom's intrinsic, pervasive, and transformative power.

questions.question: What truth about God's Kingdom do these two parables collectively reveal?
options: God's Kingdom only attracts wealthy people
God's Kingdom is an immediately visible and mighty force
God's Kingdom starts humbly but has inherent vitality and influence, eventually expanding fully
God's Kingdom exists only on a spiritual level and does not affect the real world
questions.explanation: Both parables emphasize that while God's Kingdom may start unnoticed, its life and permeating power will ultimately lead to its full expansion and transformation of the world.

en.reflection: In what area of your life is the Kingdom of God quietly growing and transforming you?
en.prayer: Dear Lord Jesus, thank You for the parables of the mustard seed and leaven, showing me that Your Kingdom, though it begins small, has incredible life and transformative power. Please let this Kingdom grow within me, permeating every aspect of my life, so that I may live more like You. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, specifically give thanks for something you consider 'insignificant' but related to God's Kingdom, such as a small act of kindness or a quiet prayer.

en.theme: The Value and Cost of the Kingdom
