en.focus: The Kingdom of Heaven is so precious that it is worth selling everything to possess it.

questions.question: In Matthew 13:44–46, which two parables does Jesus use to describe the Kingdom of Heaven?
options: The parable of the net and the weeds
The parable of the mustard seed and the yeast
The parable of the hidden treasure and the pearl of great value
The parable of the wise builder and the two sons
questions.explanation: Jesus uses the parables of the 'treasure hidden in a field' and the 'pearl of great value' to describe the Kingdom of Heaven, emphasizing its incomparable worth.

questions.question: What common characteristic of the Kingdom of Heaven do the parables of the hidden treasure and the pearl emphasize?
options: The Kingdom is easily accessible to everyone
The Kingdom is hidden and requires effort to find
The Kingdom is so valuable that it is worth selling everything for
The Kingdom is only given to the wealthy
questions.explanation: Both parables show that whether discovered by chance or sought diligently, when one recognizes the value of the Kingdom, they are willing to give up everything to possess it.

questions.question: What was the reaction of the people in Jesus' hometown when he taught there?
options: They warmly welcomed and believed him
They were astonished but refused to believe him
They demanded that Jesus perform more miracles
They did not recognize Jesus at all
questions.explanation: The people in Jesus' hometown were amazed by his wisdom and power, but they took offense at him because of his background and refused to believe.

questions.question: Why did Jesus not do many miracles in his hometown?
options: Because his power was limited
Because he did not want to show miracles to familiar people
Because their lack of faith limited the occurrence of miracles
Because miracles only happen in unfamiliar places
questions.explanation: The scripture clearly states that Jesus did not do many miracles there 'because of their lack of faith.' Unbelief became a barrier to receiving God's grace.

en.reflection: What value does the Kingdom of Heaven hold for you? Are you willing to pay the cost for it?
reflectionOptions: Willing to give up some hobbies
Willing to invest more time in service
Willing to sacrifice some material comforts
en.prayer: Dear Lord Jesus, thank You for revealing the preciousness of the Kingdom of Heaven through Your parables. Open my eyes to understand its true value more deeply, and grant me the courage and faith to be willing to give up everything to follow You and inherit Your Kingdom. Help me to live by faith and not be stumbled by the world's opinions. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, take a few minutes to consider if there is anything in your life that you value more than the Kingdom of Heaven. Ask God to help you adjust your priorities.

en.focus: Even in times of injustice and difficulty, God remains sovereign, and we can choose to trust Him and focus on His work.

questions.question: Who ordered the arrest and imprisonment of John the Baptist?
options: Pontius Pilate, the Roman governor
The Jewish Sanhedrin
Herod Antipas
Caiaphas, the high priest
questions.explanation: The text clearly states that Herod Antipas, the tetrarch, ordered John the Baptist to be arrested and put in prison.

questions.question: What ultimately led Herod to decide to kill John?
options: John incited the people to rebel against Herod's rule
Herodias, Herod's wife, strongly demanded it
Herod's daughter danced at a banquet, causing Herod to make an oath
John cursed Herod's family, enraging Herod
questions.explanation: Herod's daughter danced at the banquet, pleasing Herod, who then swore to give her whatever she asked. Prompted by Herodias, she requested John's head.

questions.question: What action did John the Baptist's disciples take after his death?
options: They gathered to rebel against King Herod
They complained to the Roman government about Herod's injustice
They came and took John's body, buried him, and then went and told Jesus
They scattered in fear and stopped preaching
questions.explanation: John's disciples came, took his body, buried it, and then went and told Jesus what had happened.

questions.question: What can we learn from John's disciples when facing injustice or suffering?
options: Immediately seek revenge, an eye for an eye
Remain silent and pretend nothing happened
Bring our difficulties to Jesus, seeking His comfort and guidance
Trust in our own abilities to solve all problems independently
questions.explanation: John's disciples, after losing their teacher, chose to tell Jesus about this painful event, teaching us to seek Jesus in times of distress.

en.reflection: Is there a situation in your life right now that feels unjust or causes you pain, which you need to bring before Jesus?
en.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for being sovereign over all things. Even in seemingly unjust and dark moments, You are our hope. Help me to bring all my difficulties and heartaches before You, trusting in Your comfort and guidance. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take some time today to tell Jesus in prayer about one thing that has been troubling or feeling unjust to you recently.

en.focus: Even in seemingly impossible situations, Jesus provides for every need through His compassion and miraculous power.

questions.question: What did Jesus do after hearing about John the Baptist's death?
options: He immediately condemned King Herod
He withdrew by Himself to a solitary place
He gathered His disciples to plan a strategy
He publicly preached the kingdom message to the crowds
questions.explanation: Upon hearing of John the Baptist's death, Jesus chose to withdraw by boat to a solitary place to be alone.

questions.question: How did the crowds respond when Jesus withdrew to a solitary place?
options: They followed the disciples home
They eagerly followed Him on foot from the towns
They sent representatives to ask Him to return
They complained that Jesus had abandoned them
questions.explanation: When the crowds heard where Jesus had gone, they followed Him on foot from the towns.

questions.question: When faced with 5,000 hungry men (besides women and children), what did the disciples suggest, and what did Jesus do instead?
options: The disciples suggested sending the crowds away, but Jesus told them to feed the people
The disciples suggested seeking help from nearby villages, but Jesus told them to collect offerings from the crowds
The disciples suggested buying food themselves, but Jesus told them to pray and wait
The disciples suggested feeding only the children and elderly, but Jesus told them to feed everyone
questions.explanation: The disciples suggested sending the crowds away to buy food for themselves, but Jesus told them, “They do not need to go away. You give them something to eat.”

questions.type: Understand the meaning of the miracle
questions.question: What is the most significant lesson we learn from the miracle of feeding the five thousand with five loaves and two fish?
options: Having enough resources solves all problems
We should rely on ourselves, not God, to solve difficulties
Even small offerings, in God's hands, can accomplish great things
God only helps those who are well-off
questions.explanation: This miracle shows that even insignificant resources like five loaves and two fish can miraculously feed a multitude and have leftovers when in Jesus' hands.

en.reflection: What are your 'five loaves and two fish' today – something seemingly small that you can offer to the Lord for Him to use for great things?
en.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for Your compassion and Your mighty power. When I see my own inadequacies and the limitations of my circumstances, help me to turn to You, trusting that You can do the miraculous in the impossible. May I be willing to offer all that I have for Your use. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, intentionally pray about something you consider 'too small to be useful,' asking the Lord to use it.

en.theme: Faith and Peace in the Storm
en.focus: Even when facing life's storms with fear or confusion, we can trust in Jesus, for He is in control and offers true peace.

questions.question: Under what circumstances did Jesus make His disciples get into the boat and go ahead of Him?
options: After He had just performed the miracle of feeding the five thousand
After He had spent the entire night in prayer on the mountain
While He was arguing with the Pharisees
As He was preparing to go to Jerusalem
questions.explanation: After feeding the five thousand, Jesus made His disciples get into the boat.

questions.question: What was the disciples' initial reaction when they saw Jesus walking on the water?
options: They immediately recognised Him as the Lord
They were greatly overjoyed
They thought He was a ghost and were terrified
They debated who He was
questions.explanation: When the disciples saw Jesus walking on the lake, they were terrified and cried out, 'It's a ghost!'

questions.question: How did Jesus respond when Peter began to sink?
options: He immediately rebuked Peter for his lack of faith
He reached out His hand and caught him, asking why he doubted
He let Peter struggle to learn a lesson
He told other disciples to help Peter
questions.explanation: When Peter, with little faith, began to sink, Jesus immediately reached out His hand and caught him, saying, 'You of little faith, why did you doubt?'

questions.question: What is the main message this passage teaches us?
options: With enough faith, we will never encounter difficulties
Jesus' power is only revealed on calm waters
Even in our deepest fears and difficulties, Jesus is with us and can save us
We can overcome all challenges by our own strength
questions.explanation: This passage shows that even amidst the storm and the disciples' fear and little faith, Jesus is present and has the power to save them from danger.

en.reflection: What are the 'storms' in your life today? In what area do you most need to hear Jesus say to you, 'It is I; don't be afraid'?
en.prayer: Dear Lord Jesus, thank You for controlling the storms and for being in control of my life. When my heart is overwhelmed by fear or worry, help me to hear Your voice saying, 'It is I; don't be afraid!' Help me to fix my eyes on You alone and experience the peace You give. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Close your eyes and quietly say to yourself three times: 'Lord Jesus, I believe You are with me; do not be afraid.'

en.focus: True cleansing and worship are not about external rituals, but about a pure heart and obedience to God's commands.

questions.question: What did the Pharisees and scribes question Jesus' disciples about?
options: Why they did not pay the temple tax?
Why they did not wash their hands before eating?
Why they did not observe the Sabbath?
Why they ate with sinners?
questions.explanation: The Pharisees and scribes asked Jesus why His disciples broke the tradition of the elders by not washing their hands before eating.

questions.question: How did Jesus refute the Pharisees and scribes, pointing out their problem?
options: He said they did not understand the true meaning of the Law.
He said they nullified God's command by their tradition.
He said they did not know the Law of Moses.
He said their hearts were far from God, honoring Him only with their lips.
questions.explanation: Jesus accused the Pharisees of nullifying the word of God for the sake of their tradition, giving the example of 'Corban'.

questions.question: What did Jesus say truly defiles a person?
options: Unwashed food
Evil thoughts and words coming out of a person's mouth
Contact with Gentiles
Not offering enough sacrifices
questions.explanation: Jesus taught that what comes out of the mouth—evil thoughts, murder, adultery, sexual immorality, theft, false witness, slander—these are what defile a person.

questions.question: What does this passage teach us about living a godly life today?
options: External religious rituals are more important than the heart.
Only outward actions matter, not inner thoughts.
We should focus more on inner purity and obedience to God's Word.
We can interpret the Bible however we want, as long as our intentions are good.
questions.explanation: Jesus emphasized the importance of the heart, showing that true godliness comes from inner obedience and purity towards God, not external rituals.

en.reflection: Am I giving more importance to external religious forms today, neglecting true worship and obedience to God from my heart?
reflectionOptions: Ask God to cleanse my thoughts and words
Let go of some man-made rules
en.prayer: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for teaching me that true cleansing comes from within. Please forgive me for sometimes prioritizing external religious acts over inner purity. Help me, Lord, that what I say and think may be pleasing to You, and enable me to worship You in spirit and truth. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Before speaking to someone today, take a few seconds to pray for God to cleanse your heart and mouth, so that your words may be edifying.

en.focus: True faith perseveres in prayer even amidst testing, trusting in God's mercy and power.

questions.question: How did the Canaanite woman address Jesus when she cried out to Him?
options: Son of God
Son of David
King of Israel
Lord of Heaven
questions.explanation: The woman immediately addressed Jesus as 'Lord, Son of David,' showing her understanding of His identity.

questions.question: What was Jesus' initial reaction to the woman's plea?
options: He healed her daughter immediately
He rebuked her harshly
He did not answer her a word
He told her to repent first
questions.explanation: The scripture states, 'He did not answer her a word,' which was a test of her faith.

questions.question: What is the main lesson from Jesus' interaction with the Canaanite woman?
options: God only cares about Israelites, not Gentiles
If we are persistent enough, we can force God to do what we want
We should persevere in faith in prayer to God, even when facing apparent rejection
Humble people do not need to ask for anything for themselves
questions.explanation: Despite Jesus' initial silence and the seemingly dismissive analogy, the woman persisted with humility and unwavering faith, ultimately receiving healing.

questions.question: What can we learn about prayer from the example of the Canaanite woman?
options: We must first prove our worthiness to God in prayer
Prayer doesn't need to be persistent; once is enough
Even when we don't feel an immediate response, we should continue to entrust our needs to God in faith
Only flawless people receive answers to their prayers
questions.explanation: The woman did not give up, even when faced with Jesus' silence and a seemingly dismissive analogy. Her persistent faith was ultimately commended by Jesus and her request granted.

en.reflection: Is there a situation in your life where you have been praying persistently but have not yet seen an answer?
reflectionOptions: Praying for an unbelieving family member
en.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for teaching me the value of faith through the story of the Canaanite woman. Help me to be persistent and humble in my prayers, trusting in Your love and power even when facing challenges or apparent silence. May my faith be pleasing to You. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, offer a prayer of faith again for a need you have been consistently praying about.

en.focus: Jesus not only heals all kinds of diseases, but He also feeds the hungry with His power and compassion.

questions.question: When Jesus came to the Sea of Galilee, what kind of sick people did the crowd bring to Him?
options: Blind, lame, mute, disabled
Sick, demon-possessed, epileptic
Feverish, lepers, paralytics
Elderly, children, women
questions.explanation: The passage clearly lists that people brought the blind, the lame, the mute, the crippled and many others to Jesus, and He healed them.

questions.question: What was the crowd's reaction after Jesus healed everyone?
options: They were surprised and left
They were afraid and kept their distance
They were angry and did not believe Him
They were amazed and glorified the God of Israel
questions.explanation: The crowds were amazed when they saw the mute speaking, the crippled made whole, the lame walking, and the blind seeing, and they glorified the God of Israel.

questions.question: Why did Jesus decide to feed the crowd?
options: They had been with Him for three days and had nothing to eat
They asked Jesus to give them food
Jesus wanted to demonstrate His miraculous power
Jesus wanted them not to leave
questions.explanation: Jesus had compassion on the crowd because they had been with Him for three days and had nothing to eat, and He did not want to send them away hungry lest they collapse on the way.

questions.question: In the miracle of feeding the four thousand, what did Jesus do after the disciples gave Him their limited food?
options: Jesus instantly created more food
Jesus took the food, gave thanks, broke it, and gave it to the disciples to distribute to the crowd
Jesus told the disciples to buy food
Jesus let the crowd figure it out themselves
questions.explanation: Jesus took the seven loaves and a few small fish that the disciples had, gave thanks, broke them, and gave them to the disciples, who then distributed them to the crowds.

en.reflection: Today's passage reminds us of Jesus' compassion and power. In what area of your life do you most need Jesus to show you compassion and demonstrate His power today?
en.prayer: Loving Lord Jesus, thank You for Your compassion and power. You healed the sick and fed the hungry, showing that You are a God who cares for us. Please extend Your grace into my life today, whether it's a physical, spiritual, or daily need. Sustain and provide for me with Your mighty power. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Find a quiet moment to reflect on Jesus' actions in the passage, and tell Him your deepest need today.

en.focus: Jesus refused to perform a sign to satisfy unbelievers' demands, as they sought not truth but to test Him.

questions.question: What did the Pharisees and Sadducees demand from Jesus?
options: A miracle to heal the sick
A sign from heaven
A prophecy about the end times
A miracle to raise the dead
questions.explanation: They demanded a sign from heaven to test Him.

questions.question: Why did Jesus rebuke the Pharisees and Sadducees?
options: They were not dressed according to the law
They did not know the Law of Moses
They could interpret the weather but not the signs of the times
They did not give their offerings on time
questions.explanation: Jesus pointed out that they could discern the weather by looking at the sky, but they could not understand the signs of what God was doing through Him.

questions.question: What sign did Jesus say would be given to this wicked and adulterous generation?
options: The sign of Moses
The sign of Elijah
The sign of Jonah
The sign of Isaiah
questions.explanation: Jesus stated that no sign would be given to them except the sign of Jonah, which foreshadowed His death and resurrection.

questions.question: What lesson can we learn about seeking signs from this passage?
options: Signs are the foundation of faith, and we must constantly seek them
Signs are the only way God answers prayer
Signs are not meant to satisfy unbelievers' curiosity or to test God
Signs are only revealed to those who have no faith at all
questions.explanation: Jesus refused to perform a sign to satisfy the testing of the Pharisees and Sadducees, indicating that the purpose of signs is to reveal God's kingdom and authority, not to fulfill human desires or unbelief.

en.reflection: In your life, have you ever sought evidence or confirmation from God with an improper attitude?
en.prayer: Lord Jesus, please help me to have a pure heart that seeks truth. When I face challenges or doubts, may I humbly seek Your will instead of testing You or demanding inappropriate signs. May I discern Your work and trust You wholeheartedly. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, when in doubt, pause to pray quietly, asking God for wisdom and faith, rather than rushing to seek external 'signs' for confirmation.

en.focus: Jesus warns His disciples to be wary of the teachings of the Pharisees and Sadducees, as false doctrine can permeate like leaven.

questions.question: What were the disciples discussing when they realized they had forgotten bread?
options: How Jesus would make bread
Where they could buy bread
Why they had not brought bread
The relationship between Jesus' teaching and bread
questions.explanation: The disciples were focused on the fact that they had forgotten to bring bread, leading to their discussion.

questions.question: When Jesus warned the disciples to “beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees,” what was the “leaven” referring to?
options: The bread they made
Their wealth
Their false teaching
Their authority
questions.explanation: Jesus clarified that the 'leaven' was the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees, which could subtly influence people.

questions.question: The disciples initially misunderstood Jesus' teaching about 'leaven.' What does this indicate?
options: They completely failed to understand Jesus' parables
Their concern for physical food outweighed their understanding of spiritual teaching
They thought Jesus was criticizing their memory
They believed Jesus was particular about food
questions.explanation: The disciples' discussion centered on forgetting bread, showing their focus on physical needs rather than Jesus' spiritual warning.

questions.question: What is an important reminder from this passage for us today?
options: We should avoid sharing food with everyone
We must only eat unleavened bread
We need to be alert to false teachings and focus on Jesus' truth
We should not worry about daily physical needs
questions.explanation: Jesus' warning is for us to be cautious of false teachings that can corrupt our faith and thoughts, and to hold fast to His truth.

en.reflection: Today, what 'leaven' might be subtly influencing your thoughts or faith?
en.prayer: Dear Lord Jesus, thank You for reminding me to be vigilant against the 'leaven' that can corrupt my thoughts and faith. Grant me wisdom to discern, and help me to hold fast to Your truth, not being swayed by the various teachings of the world. May my heart follow You alone. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Take some time today to examine the information you've been exposed to recently, and ask God to help you discern what is truth and what is 'leaven'.

en.theme: You Are the Christ, the Son of the Living God
en.focus: Jesus is the Christ, the Son of the Living God – this is a truth revealed by God and the foundation upon which the church is built.

questions.question: When Jesus asked His disciples who people said He was, what answers did they give?
options: John the Baptist, Elijah, Jeremiah
Moses, David, Solomon
The prophet Samuel, Isaiah
A great teacher, a healer
questions.explanation: The disciples reported that some people believed Jesus was John the Baptist, Elijah, Jeremiah, or one of the prophets.

questions.question: How did Peter answer Jesus' question, 'But who do you say I am?'
options: You are our Master, a great teacher
You are the Messiah, who will restore the kingdom of Israel
You are the Christ, the Son of the living God
You are a powerful prophet
questions.explanation: Peter clearly declared, 'You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.'

questions.question: Jesus commended Peter's answer and indicated that Peter's insight did not come from where?
options: From his own wisdom
From human teaching
From flesh and blood
From listening to other disciples
questions.explanation: Jesus explicitly stated that Peter's insight did not come from 'flesh and blood' but was revealed to him by His Father in heaven.

questions.question: Jesus said He would build His church on this 'rock.' What does this 'rock' refer to?
options: Peter himself
Peter's faith and loyalty
The truth that Peter confessed: 'You are the Christ, the Son of the living God'
The teachings of all the apostles
questions.explanation: The 'rock' Jesus referred to is the truth Peter confessed—that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of the living God. The church is built upon this core truth.

en.reflection: Like Peter, do you recognize and confess Jesus as the Christ, the Son of the living God? How does this truth impact your life today?
reflectionOptions: It reminds me to trust in the Lord Jesus daily
It gives me deeper hope in eternal life and God's presence
It motivates me to share Jesus more actively with others
en.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You that You are the Christ, the Son of the living God. Thank You, Father, for revealing this precious truth to me. Help me to build my life on this rock, to trust in You steadfastly, and to live a life worthy of this truth. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Today, take a moment to meditate on the statement 'Jesus is the Christ, the Son of the living God' and offer thanks to God for it.

en.focus: Following Jesus means denying oneself, taking up one’s cross, and living for eternal rewards.

questions.question: When Jesus first predicted His suffering, where did He say He must go?
options: Samaria
Jericho
Jerusalem
Galilee
questions.explanation: Jesus clearly told His disciples that He must go to Jerusalem and suffer many things from the elders, chief priests, and scrib there.

questions.question: How did Jesus respond to Peter when Peter tried to dissuade Him from suffering?
options: Commended Peter for his concern
Rebuked Peter, calling him 'Satan'
Calmly explained God's will to him
Asked Peter to remain silent
questions.explanation: Jesus turned and said to Peter, 'Get behind me, Satan! You are a hindrance to me. For you are not setting your mind on the things of God, but on the things of man.'

questions.question: What did Jesus say a person must do if they want to follow Him?
options: Accumulate much wealth
Deny themselves, and take up their cross and follow Him
Avoid all difficulties and challenges
Seek the praise of the world
questions.explanation: Jesus clearly stated that the condition for following Him is to deny oneself, take up one's cross, and follow Him.

questions.question: How does this passage prompt us to view the true value of life?
options: The value of life is in accumulating worldly wealth and fame
The value of life is in enjoying the present and avoiding all suffering
The true value of life is in giving up worldly gains and losses to live for eternal rewards
The value of life depends on how others perceive us
questions.explanation: Jesus taught that gaining the whole world but forfeiting one's soul, or exchanging one's soul for anything, is profitless. This reminds us that the true value of life is found in Christ and eternity.

en.reflection: In what area do you most need to 'deny yourself and take up your cross' to follow Jesus today?
reflectionOptions: Surrender my plans and submit to God's will
Forgive someone who has hurt me
Sacrifice my time or resources to serve others
en.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for laying down Your life for me and bearing the cross. Please help me to be willing to deny myself and take up my cross to follow You today. May my actions reflect Your will, not human desires. In Jesus' name I pray, Amen.
en.action: Make a small effort or sacrifice today for an action you might not want to do, but know is pleasing to God.
